source_blocks.source_text_en: When Your Benefits Start
source_blocks.text: 您的福利何时开始

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your application is approved, your first Social Security benefit will be paid for the sixth full month after the date we find that your disability began.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的申请获得批准，您的第一笔社会保障福利将在我们认定您的残疾开始的日期之后的第六个完整月份支付。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For example, if your disability began on June 15, 2018, your first benefit would be paid for the month of December 2018, the sixth full month of disability.
source_blocks.text: 例如，如果您的残疾始于2018年6月15日，您的第一笔福利将在2018年12月支付，即残疾的第六个完整月份。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Social Security benefits are paid in the month following the month for which they're due. This means that the benefit due for December would be paid to you in January 2019, and so on.
source_blocks.text: 社会保障福利在应支付月份的下一个月支付。这意味着12月应支付的福利将在2019年1月支付给您，以此类推。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How Much You Will Receive
source_blocks.text: 您将收到多少金额

source_blocks.source_text_en: The amount of your monthly disability benefit is based on your lifetime average earnings covered by Social Security.
source_blocks.text: 您每月残疾福利的金额基于您受社会保障覆盖的终身平均收入。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you don't already have an estimate, you can get your online with your personal my Social Security account or use our Benefit Calculators to determine how much you would get if you became disabled right now.
source_blocks.text: 如果您还没有估算，您可以使用您的个人我的社会保障账户在线获取，或使用我们的福利计算器来确定如果您现在残疾，您将获得多少。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Other Payments May Affect Your Disability Benefits
source_blocks.text: 其他付款可能影响您的残疾福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you receive certain other government benefits, such as workers' compensation, public disability benefits, or pensions based on work not covered by Social Security (for example, some government or foreign employment), the Social Security benefits payable to you and your family may be reduced.
source_blocks.text: 如果您领取某些其他政府福利，如工伤赔偿、公共残疾福利或基于未受社会保障覆盖的工作的养老金（例如，一些政府或外国就业），您和您的家人可领取的社会保障福利可能会减少。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For more information about how these benefits can affect your Social Security payments, refer to the following publications:
source_blocks.text: 有关这些福利如何影响您的社会保障付款的更多信息，请参阅以下出版物：

source_blocks.source_text_en: How Workers' Compensation And Other Disability Payments May Affect Your Benefit; Windfall Elimination Provision; or Government Pension Offset.
source_blocks.text: 工伤赔偿和其他残疾付款如何影响您的福利； 意外收益消除条款；或 政府养老金抵消。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Related Information
source_blocks.text: 相关信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: Income Taxes And Your Social Security Benefits.
source_blocks.text: 所得税和您的社会保障福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Medicare Coverage If You're Disabled
source_blocks.text: 如果您残疾，医疗保险覆盖

source_blocks.source_text_en: We automatically enroll you in Medicare after you get disability benefits for two years. The two parts of Medicare we enroll you in are hospital insurance and medical insurance.
source_blocks.text: 在您获得残疾福利两年后，我们会自动为您注册医疗保险。我们为您注册的医疗保险的两个部分是医院保险和医疗保险。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Hospital insurance (Part A) helps pay for inpatient hospital bills and some follow-up care. The taxes you paid while you were working financed this coverage, so it is provided at no cost to you. Medical insurance (Part B) helps pay doctors' bills, outpatient hospital care, and other medical services. You will need to pay a monthly premium for this coverage if you want it.
source_blocks.text: 医院保险（A部分）帮助支付住院医院账单和一些后续护理费用。您在工作期间缴纳的税款资助了这项覆盖，因此您无需支付费用。 医疗保险（B部分）帮助支付医生账单、门诊医院护理和其他医疗服务。如果您需要这项覆盖，您需要每月支付保费。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Most people have both parts of Medicare. If you have questions about this coverage, you can contact Medicare toll-free at 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) to speak to a Medicare Customer Service Representative. TTY users should call 1-877-486-2048.
source_blocks.text: 大多数人拥有医疗保险的两个部分。如果您对此覆盖有疑问，您可以拨打医疗保险免费电话 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) 与医疗保险客户服务代表交谈。TTY用户应拨打1-877-486-2048。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Other Parts of Medicare
source_blocks.text: 医疗保险的其他部分

source_blocks.source_text_en: Medicare Advantage (Part C). People with Medicare Parts A and Part B can choose to receive all of their health care services through plans that are offered by private companies and approved by Medicare. For more information, we recommend you read Medicare's
source_blocks.text: 医疗保险优势计划（C部分）。拥有医疗保险A部分和B部分的人可以选择通过由私营公司提供并经医疗保险批准的保险计划来接受所有医疗服务。如需更多信息，我们建议您阅读医疗保险的

source_blocks.source_text_en: Prescription Drug Coverage (Part D) helps pay for medications doctors prescribe for treatment. For more information on the enrollment periods for Part D, we recommend you read Medicare's page.
source_blocks.text: 处方药保险（D部分）帮助支付医生为治疗而开具的药物费用。有关D部分注册期的更多信息，我们建议您阅读医疗保险的页面。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you receive Medicare and have limited resources and income, you may be eligible for Extra Help with Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Costs.
source_blocks.text: 如果您享受医疗保险但资源和收入有限，您可能有资格获得医疗保险处方药计划费用的额外补助。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Help For Low-Income Medicare Beneficiaries
source_blocks.text: 针对低收入医疗保险受益人的帮助

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you get Medicare and have low-income and few resources, your state may pay your Medicare premiums and, in some cases, other Medicare costs for which you are normally responsible such as deductibles and coinsurance.
source_blocks.text: 如果您享受医疗保险且收入低、资源少，您的州可能会为您支付医疗保险保费，在某些情况下，还会支付您通常需要负责的其他医疗保险费用，如免赔额和共付保险。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Only your state can decide if you qualify for this assistance. To find out if you do, contact your state or local welfare office or Medicaid agency.
source_blocks.text: 只有您的州才能决定您是否符合此援助的资格。要了解您是否符合条件，请联系您所在州或地方的福利办公室或医疗补助机构。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For additional information about the program, please go to the Medicare's page.
source_blocks.text: 有关该计划的更多信息，请访问医疗保险的页面。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you need additional information about the other parts of Medicare, please read the "Who Can Get Medicare?" section of our Medicare booklet or visit Medicare.gov.
source_blocks.text: 如果您需要有关医疗保险其他部分的更多信息，请阅读我们医疗保险手册中的“谁能获得医疗保险？”部分或访问Medicare.gov。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits Planner: Disability \| Your Continuing Eligibility
source_blocks.text: Benefits Planner: Disability \| Your Continuing Eligibility

source_blocks.source_text_en: In most cases, you will continue to receive benefits as long as you are disabled. However, there are certain circumstances that may change your continuing eligibility for disability benefits. For example, your health may improve to the point where you are no longer disabled or you go back to work.
source_blocks.text: In most cases, you will continue to receive benefits as long as you are disabled. However, there are certain circumstances that may change your continuing eligibility for disability benefits. For example, your health may improve to the point where you are no longer disabled or you go back to work.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The law requires that we review your case from time to time to verify that you are still disabled. We tell you if it is time to review your case and we also keep you informed about your benefit status.
source_blocks.text: The law requires that we review your case from time to time to verify that you are still disabled. We tell you if it is time to review your case and we also keep you informed about your benefit status.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You should be aware that you are responsible for letting us know if your health improves or you go back to work.
source_blocks.text: You should be aware that you are responsible for letting us know if your health improves or you go back to work.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reviewing Your Disability
source_blocks.text: Reviewing Your Disability

source_blocks.source_text_en: In general, your benefits will continue as long as you are disabled. How often we review your case depends on whether your condition is expected to improve.
source_blocks.text: In general, your benefits will continue as long as you are disabled. How often we review your case depends on whether your condition is expected to improve.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If medical improvement is:
source_blocks.text: If medical improvement is:

source_blocks.source_text_en: "Expected," your case will normally be reviewed within six to 18 months after your benefits start. "Possible," your case will normally be reviewed no sooner than three years. "Not expected," your case will normally be reviewed no sooner than seven years.
source_blocks.text: "Expected," your case will normally be reviewed within six to 18 months after your benefits start. "Possible," your case will normally be reviewed no sooner than three years. "Not expected," your case will normally be reviewed no sooner than seven years.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What Can Cause Benefits to Stop?
source_blocks.text: What Can Cause Benefits to Stop?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Two things can cause us to decide that you are no longer disabled and to stop your benefits:
source_blocks.text: Two things can cause us to decide that you are no longer disabled and to stop your benefits:

source_blocks.source_text_en: if you work at a level we consider "substantial."
source_blocks.text: if you work at a level we consider "substantial."

source_blocks.source_text_en: In 2019, average earnings of \$1,220 or more per month (\$2,040 or more per month if you are blind) are usually considered substantial.
source_blocks.text: In 2019, average earnings of \$1,220 or more per month (\$2,040 or more per month if you are blind) are usually considered substantial.

source_blocks.source_text_en: if we decide that your medical condition has improved to the point that you are no longer disabled.
source_blocks.text: if we decide that your medical condition has improved to the point that you are no longer disabled.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Remember, you are responsible for promptly reporting any improvement in your condition, or if you return to work. The booklet we send you when your application is approved explains what you need to report to us.
source_blocks.text: Remember, you are responsible for promptly reporting any improvement in your condition, or if you return to work. The booklet we send you when your application is approved explains what you need to report to us.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If You Go Back To Work
source_blocks.text: If You Go Back To Work

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you're like most people, you would rather work than try to live on disability benefits.
source_blocks.text: If you're like most people, you would rather work than try to live on disability benefits.

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are special rules that help you keep your cash benefits and Medicare while you test your ability to work. We call these rules "work incentives." For more information about Social Security work incentives, read Working While Disabled: How We Can Help.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits Planner: Disability | Family Benefits | Social Security Administration
source_blocks.text: 福利规划器：残疾 | 家庭福利 | 社会保障管理局

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits Planner: Family Benefits
source_blocks.text: 福利规划器：家庭福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: When you start receiving disability benefits, certain members of your family may also qualify for benefits on your record. Benefits may be paid to your:
source_blocks.text: 当您开始领取残疾福利时，您的某些家庭成员也可能有资格根据您的记录领取福利。福利可以支付给您的：

source_blocks.source_text_en: spouse; divorced spouse; children; disabled child; and adult child disabled before age 22.
source_blocks.text: 配偶； 离婚配偶； 子女； 残疾子女；以及 22岁前残疾的成年子女。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If any of your qualified family members apply for benefits, we will ask for their Social Security numbers and their birth certificates.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的任何合格家庭成员申请福利，我们将要求提供他们的社会保障号码和出生证明。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your spouse is applying for benefits, we may also ask for proof of marriage and dates of prior marriages, if applicable.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的配偶申请福利，我们也可能要求提供婚姻证明以及之前婚姻的日期（如适用）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Maximum Family Amount
source_blocks.text: 最高家庭金额

source_blocks.source_text_en: Each family member may be eligible for a monthly benefit of up to 50 percent of your disability benefit amount. However, there is a limit to the amount we can pay your family.
source_blocks.text: 每位家庭成员每月可能有资格领取高达您残疾福利金额50%的福利。但是，我们可以支付给您家庭的金额有限制。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The total depends on your benefit amount and the number of family members who also qualify on your record. The total varies, but generally the total amount you and your family can receive is between 150 and 180 percent of your disability benefit.
source_blocks.text: 总额取决于您的福利金额以及根据您的记录也有资格领取福利的家庭成员人数。总额各不相同，但通常您和您的家庭可以领取的总金额在您残疾福利的150%到180%之间。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If the sum of the benefits payable on your account is greater than the family limit, the benefits to the family members will be reduced proportionately. Your benefit will not be affected.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的账户上应支付的福利总和大于家庭限额，则支付给家庭成员的福利将按比例减少。您的福利不会受到影响。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have a divorced spouse who qualifies for benefits, it will not affect the amount of benefits you or your family may receive.
source_blocks.text: 如果您有一位符合福利资格的离婚配偶，这不会影响您或您的家庭可能领取的福利金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits For Your Spouse
source_blocks.text: 您配偶的福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: When benefits are payable to your spouse:
source_blocks.text: 当您的配偶有资格领取福利时：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Age 62 or older, unless he or she collects a higher Social Security benefit based on his or her earnings record. The spouse benefit amount will be permanently reduced by a percentage based on the number of months until his or her full retirement age.
source_blocks.text: 年满62岁或以上，除非他或她根据其收入记录领取更高的社会保障福利。配偶福利金额将根据距离其全额退休年龄的月数按百分比永久减少。

source_blocks.source_text_en: At any age if he or she is caring for your child under age 16 or disabled.
source_blocks.text: 任何年龄，如果他或她在照顾您未满16岁或残疾的子女。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your spouse would receive these benefits until the child reaches age 16. At that time, the child's benefits continue, but your spouse's benefits stop unless he or she is old enough to receive retirement benefits (age 62 or older) or survivor benefits as a widow or widower (age 60).
source_blocks.text: 您的配偶将领取这些福利，直到子女年满16岁。届时，子女的福利继续，但您配偶的福利停止，除非他或她年龄足够领取退休福利（62岁或以上）或作为遗孀或鳏夫领取遗属福利（60岁）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If Your Spouse Also Worked Under Social Security
source_blocks.text: 如果您的配偶也在社会保障下工作过

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your spouse is eligible for retirement benefits on his or her own record, we will always pay that amount first. But if the spouse benefit that is payable on your record is a higher amount, he or she will get a combination of benefits that equals that higher amount.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的配偶有资格根据其自己的记录领取退休福利，我们将始终首先支付该金额。但是，如果根据您的记录应支付的配偶福利金额更高，他或她将获得等于该更高金额的福利组合。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your spouse will also receive a pension based on work not covered by Social Security, such as government or foreign work, his or her Social Security benefit on your record may be affected.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的配偶也将根据未纳入社会保障的工作（如政府或外国工作）领取养老金，那么他或她基于您记录获得的社会保障福利可能会受到影响。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits For Your Divorced Spouse
source_blocks.text: 您离婚配偶的福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are divorced, even if you have remarried, your ex-spouse may qualify for benefits on your record.
source_blocks.text: 如果您已离婚，即使您再婚，您的前配偶也可能有资格基于您的记录获得福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: (If your ex-spouse will also receive a pension based on work not covered by Social Security, such as government or foreign work, his or her Social Security benefit on your record may be affected.)
source_blocks.text: （如果您的前配偶也将根据未纳入社会保障的工作（如政府或外国工作）领取养老金，那么他或她基于您记录获得的社会保障福利可能会受到影响。）

source_blocks.source_text_en: To qualify on your record, your ex-spouse must:
source_blocks.text: 要基于您的记录获得资格，您的前配偶必须：

source_blocks.source_text_en: have been married to you for at least 10 years; be at least 62 years old; be unmarried; and not be eligible for an equal or higher benefit on his or her own Social Security record, or on someone else's Social Security record.
source_blocks.text: 与您结婚至少10年； 年满62岁； 未婚；且 没有资格基于其自身或其他人的社会保障记录获得同等或更高的福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The amount of benefits payable to your divorced spouse has no effect on the amount of benefits you or your current spouse may receive.
source_blocks.text: 支付给您离婚配偶的福利金额不会影响您或您现任配偶可能获得的福利金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits For Your Children
source_blocks.text: 您子女的福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: When you qualify for Social Security disability benefits, your children may also qualify to receive benefits on your record. Your eligible child can be your biological child, adopted child, or stepchild. A dependent grandchild may also qualify.
source_blocks.text: 当您符合社会保障残疾福利的资格时，您的子女也可能有资格基于您的记录领取福利。您符合条件的子女可以是您的亲生子女、收养子女或继子女。受抚养的孙辈也可能符合资格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To receive benefits, the child must be unmarried and be:
source_blocks.text: 要领取福利，子女必须未婚且符合以下条件之一：

source_blocks.source_text_en: under age 18; or 18-19 years old and a full-time student (no higher than grade 12); or 18 or older and have a disability that started before age 22.
source_blocks.text: 未满18岁；或 18至19岁，且为全日制学生（不超过12年级）；或 年满18岁或以上，且在22岁之前开始有残疾。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Normally, benefits stop when children reach age 18 unless they are disabled. However, if the child is still a full-time student at a secondary (or elementary) school at age 18, benefits will continue until the child graduates or until two months after the child becomes age 19, whichever is first.
source_blocks.text: 通常，福利在子女年满18岁时停止，除非他们残疾。但是，如果子女在18岁时仍在中学（或小学）全日制就读，福利将持续到子女毕业或年满19岁后两个月，以先到者为准。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To qualify for Social Security disability benefits, you must first have worked in jobs covered by Social Security. Then you must have a medical condition that meets Social Security's definition of disability. In general, we pay monthly benefits to people who are unable to work for a year or more because of a disability.
source_blocks.text: To qualify for Social Security disability benefits, you must first have worked in jobs covered by Social Security. Then you must have a medical condition that meets Social Security's definition of disability. In general, we pay monthly benefits to people who are unable to work for a year or more because of a disability.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits usually continue until you are able to work again on a regular basis. There are also a number of special rules, called "work incentives," that provide continued benefits and health care coverage to help you make the transition back to work.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are receiving Social Security disability benefits when you reach full retirement age, your disability benefits automatically convert to retirement benefits, but the amount remains the same.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How Much Work Do You Need?
source_blocks.text: How Much Work Do You Need?

source_blocks.source_text_en: In addition to meeting our definition of disability, you must have worked long enough and recently enough under Social Security to qualify for disability benefits.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Social Security work credits are based on your total yearly wages or self-employment income. You can earn up to four credits each year.
source_blocks.text: Social Security work credits are based on your total yearly wages or self-employment income. You can earn up to four credits each year.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The amount needed for a work credit changes from year to year. In 2019, for example, you earn one credit for each \$1,360 in wages or self-employment income. When you've earned \$5,440, you've earned your four credits for the year.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What We Mean By Disability
source_blocks.text: What We Mean By Disability

source_blocks.source_text_en: The definition of disability under Social Security is different than other programs. Social Security pays only for total disability. No benefits are payable for partial disability or for short-term disability.

source_blocks.source_text_en: We consider you disabled under Social Security rules if:

source_blocks.source_text_en: You cannot do work that you did before; We decide that you cannot adjust to other work because of your medical condition(s); and Your disability has lasted or is expected to last for at least one year or to result in death.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Are you working?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are not working, we will send your application to the Disability Determination Services (DDS) office that will make the decision about your medical condition. The DDS uses Steps 2-5 below to make the decision.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your condition must significantly limit your ability to do basic work such as lifting, standing, walking, sitting, and remembering for at least 12 months. If it does not, we will find that you are not disabled.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Special Rules For People Who Are Blind Or Have Low Vision
source_blocks.text: Special Rules For People Who Are Blind Or Have Low Vision

source_blocks.source_text_en: We consider you to be legally blind under Social Security rules if your vision cannot be corrected to better than 20/200 in your better eye or if your visual field is 20 degrees or less, even with a corrective lens. Many people who meet the legal definition of blindness still have some sight and may be able to read large print and get around without a cane or a guide dog.

Many people who meet the legal definition of blindness still have some sight and may be able to read large print and get around without a cane or a guide dog.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you do not meet the legal definition of blindness, you may still qualify for disability benefits if your vision problems alone or combined with other health problems prevent you from working.

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are a number of special rules for people who are blind that recognize the severe impact of blindness on a person's ability to work. For example, the monthly earnings limit for people who are blind is generally higher than the limit that applies to non-blind disabled workers.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If something happens to a worker, benefits may be payable to their widow, widower, or surviving divorced spouse with a disability if the following conditions are met:

source_blocks.source_text_en: He or she is between ages 50 and 60; Their condition meets the definition of disability for adults; and The disability started before or within seven years of the worker's death.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits For A Disabled Child
source_blocks.text: Benefits For A Disabled Child

source_blocks.source_text_en: A child under age 18 may be disabled, but we don't need to consider the child's disability when deciding if he or she qualifies for benefits as your dependent. The child's benefits normally stop at age 18 unless he or she is a full-time student in an elementary or high school (benefits can continue until age 19) or is disabled.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Adults Disabled Before Age 22
source_blocks.text: Adults Disabled Before Age 22

source_blocks.source_text_en: An adult disabled before age 22 may be eligible for child's benefits if a parent is deceased or starts receiving retirement or disability benefits. We consider this a "child's" benefit because it is paid on a parent's Social Security earnings record.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The "adult child" including an adopted child, or, in some cases, a stepchild, grandchild, or step grandchild must be unmarried, age 18 or older, have a disability that started before age 22, and meet the definition of disability for adults.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The definition of disability under Social Security is different than other programs. Social Security pays only for total disability. No benefits are payable for partial disability or for short-term disability.

source_blocks.source_text_en: We consider you disabled under Social Security rules if:

source_blocks.source_text_en: You cannot do work that you did before; We decide that you cannot adjust to other work because of your medical condition(s); and Your disability has lasted or is expected to last for at least one year or to result in death.
source_blocks.text: 您无法从事您以前做过的工作； 我们认定由于您的医疗状况，您无法适应其他工作；且 您的残疾已经持续或预计将持续至少一年或导致死亡。

source_blocks.source_text_en: This is a strict definition of disability. Social Security program rules assume that working families have access to other resources to provide support during periods of short-term disabilities, including workers' compensation, insurance, savings, and investments.
source_blocks.text: 这是一个严格的残疾定义。社会保障计划规则假定工作家庭在短期残疾期间可以获得其他资源来提供支持，包括工伤赔偿、保险、储蓄和投资。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How We Decide If You Are Disabled
source_blocks.text: 我们如何决定您是否残疾

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have enough work to qualify for disability benefits, we use a step-by-step process involving five questions. They are:
source_blocks.text: 如果您有足够的工作来符合残疾福利的资格，我们会使用一个涉及五个问题的分步流程。它们是：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Are you working?
source_blocks.text: 您是否在工作？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are working in 2019 and your earnings average more than \$1,220 a month, you generally cannot be considered disabled.
source_blocks.text: 如果您在2019年工作，且您的月平均收入超过\$1,220，通常您不能被视为残疾。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are not working, we will send your application to the Disability Determination Services (DDS) office that will make the decision about your medical condition. The DDS uses Steps 2-5 below to make the decision.
source_blocks.text: 如果您没有工作，我们会将您的申请发送至残疾决定服务处（DDS），该机构将就您的医疗状况做出决定。DDS使用以下第2至第5步来做出决定。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Is your condition "severe"?
source_blocks.text: 您的状况是否“严重”？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your condition must significantly limit your ability to do basic work such as lifting, standing, walking, sitting, and remembering for at least 12 months. If it does not, we will find that you are not disabled.
source_blocks.text: 您的状况必须显著限制您从事基本工作的能力，如提举、站立、行走、坐立和记忆，且至少持续12个月。如果不是，我们将认定您不残疾。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your condition does interfere with basic work-related activities, we go to Step 3.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的状况确实干扰了与工作相关的基本活动，我们将进入第3步。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Is your condition found in the list of disabling conditions?
source_blocks.text: 您的状况是否在致残疾病清单中？

source_blocks.source_text_en: For each of the major body systems, we maintain a list of medical conditions that we consider so severe that it prevents a person from completing substantial gainful activity. If your condition is not on the list, we have to decide if it is as severe as a medical condition that is on the list. If it is, we will find that you are disabled. If it is not, we then go to Step 4.
source_blocks.text: 针对每个主要身体系统，我们维护一份医疗状况清单，这些状况被认为严重到足以阻止一个人从事实质性有酬活动。如果您的状况不在清单上，我们必须判断其是否与清单上的医疗状况一样严重。如果是，我们将认定您残疾。如果不是，我们则进入第4步。

source_blocks.source_text_en: We have two initiatives designed to expedite our processing of new disability claims:
source_blocks.text: 我们有两项旨在加快处理新残疾索赔的举措：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Compassionate Allowances: Certain cases that usually qualify for disability can be allowed as soon as the diagnosis is confirmed. Examples include acute leukemia, Lou Gehrig s disease (ALS), and pancreatic cancer. Quick Disability Determinations: We use sophisticated computer screening to identify cases with a high probability of allowance.
source_blocks.text: 同情性津贴：某些通常符合残疾资格的病例，一旦诊断确认即可获准。例如急性白血病、肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）和胰腺癌。 快速残疾决定：我们使用复杂的计算机筛选来识别高概率获准的病例。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For more information about our disability claims process, visit our Benefits For People With Disabilities website.
source_blocks.text: 有关我们残疾索赔流程的更多信息，请访问我们的“残疾人福利”网站。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can you do the work you did previously?
source_blocks.text: 您能否从事之前的工作？

source_blocks.source_text_en: At this step, we decide if your medical impairment(s) prevents you from performing any of your past work. It is doesn t, we ll decide you don t have a qualifying disability. If it does, we proceed to Step 5.
source_blocks.text: 在此步骤中，我们判断您的医疗损伤是否阻止您从事任何过去的工作。如果不是，我们将决定您没有符合条件的残疾。如果是，我们将进入第5步。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can you do any other type of work?
source_blocks.text: 您能否从事任何其他类型的工作？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you can t do the work you did in the past, we look to see if there is other work you could do despite your impairment(s).
source_blocks.text: 如果您无法从事过去的工作，我们会查看是否有其他您尽管有损伤但仍能从事的工作。

source_blocks.source_text_en: We consider your medical conditions and your age, education, past work experience, and any transferable skills you may have. If you can t do other work, we ll decide you are disabled. If you can do other work, we ll decide that you don t have a qualifying disability and your claim will be denied.
source_blocks.text: 我们会考虑您的医疗状况以及您的年龄、教育背景、过去的工作经验以及您可能拥有的任何可转移技能。如果您无法从事其他工作，我们将决定您残疾。如果您能从事其他工作，我们将决定您没有符合条件的残疾，您的索赔将被拒绝。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Special Situations
source_blocks.text: 特殊情况

source_blocks.source_text_en: Most people who receive disability benefits are workers who qualify on their own records and meet the work and disability requirements we have just described. However, there are some situations you may not know about:
source_blocks.text: 大多数领取残疾福利的人是依据自身记录符合资格并满足我们刚才所述的工作和残疾要求的工人。然而，有些情况您可能不知道：

source_blocks.source_text_en: If You're Blind Or Have Low Vision - How We Can Help If You Are The Worker's Widow Or Widower Benefits For A Disabled Child Benefits for Wounded Warriors & Veterans
source_blocks.text: 如果您失明或视力低下 - 我们能如何帮助 如果您是工人的遗孀或鳏夫 残疾儿童福利 受伤战士与退伍军人福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: Special Rules For People Who Are Blind Or Have Low Vision
source_blocks.text: 针对失明或视力低下人士的特殊规则

source_blocks.source_text_en: We consider you to be legally blind under Social Security rules if your vision cannot be corrected to better than 20/200 in your better eye or if your visual field is 20 degrees or less, even with a corrective lens. Many people who meet the legal definition of blindness still have some sight and may be able to read large print and get around without a cane or a guide dog.
source_blocks.text: 根据社会保障规则，如果您的视力无法矫正至较好眼睛优于20/200，或即使佩戴矫正镜片，您的视野仍为20度或更小，我们便认为您在法律上属于失明。许多符合法律失明定义的人仍有一些视力，可能能够阅读大号字体，并且无需拐杖或导盲犬即可出行。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you do not meet the legal definition of blindness, you may still qualify for disability benefits if your vision problems alone or combined with other health problems prevent you from working.
source_blocks.text: 如果您不符合法律上的失明定义，但您的视力问题单独或与其他健康问题结合使您无法工作，您仍可能有资格获得残疾福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are a number of special rules for people who are blind that recognize the severe impact of blindness on a person's ability to work. For example, the monthly earnings limit for people who are blind is generally higher than the limit that applies to non-blind disabled workers.
source_blocks.text: 针对失明人士有许多特殊规则，这些规则承认失明对个人工作能力的严重影响。例如，失明人士的每月收入限额通常高于适用于非失明残疾工人的限额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: In 2019, the monthly earnings limit is \$2,040.
Benefits For Disabled Widows Or Widowers
source_blocks.text: 针对残疾遗孀或鳏夫的福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: If something happens to a worker, benefits may be payable to their widow, widower, or surviving divorced spouse with a disability if the following conditions are met:
source_blocks.text: 如果工人发生意外，其遗孀、鳏夫或尚存离婚配偶若符合以下条件，可能有资格获得福利：

source_blocks.source_text_en: He or she is between ages 50 and 60; Their condition meets the definition of disability for adults; and The disability started before or within seven years of the worker's death.
source_blocks.text: 年龄在50岁至60岁之间； 其状况符合成人残疾的定义；且 残疾始于工人去世之前或之后七年内。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If a widow or widower who is caring for the worker's children receives Social Security benefits, he or she is still eligible for disabled widow s or widower s benefits if their disability starts before those payments end or within seven years after they end.
source_blocks.text: 如果照顾工人子女的遗孀或鳏夫领取社会保障福利，只要其残疾在那些付款结束之前或结束后七年内开始，他或她仍有资格获得残疾遗孀或鳏夫福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Widows, widowers, and surviving divorced spouses cannot apply online for survivors benefits. However, if they want to apply for benefits, they should contact Social Security immediately at 1-800-772-1213 to request an appointment. (If they are deaf or hard of hearing, they should call our TTY number at 1-800-325-0778.)
source_blocks.text: 遗孀、鳏夫和尚存离婚配偶无法在线申请遗属福利。但是，如果他们想申请福利，应立即联系社会保障局，拨打 1-800-772-1213 预约。 （如果他们失聪或有听力障碍，应拨打我们的TTY号码 1-800-325-0778。）

source_blocks.source_text_en: If they are disabled, they can speed up the application process if they complete an Adult Disability Report and have it available at the time of their appointment.
source_blocks.text: 如果他们残疾，他们可以填写成人残疾报告并在预约时提供该报告，以加快申请流程。

source_blocks.source_text_en: We use the same definition of disability for widows and widowers as we do for workers.
source_blocks.text: 我们对遗孀和鳏夫使用与工人相同的残疾定义。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits For A Disabled Child
source_blocks.text: 针对残疾儿童的福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: A child under age 18 may be disabled, but we don't need to consider the child's disability when deciding if he or she qualifies for benefits as your dependent. The child's benefits normally stop at age 18 unless he or she is a full-time student in an elementary or high school (benefits can continue until age 19) or is disabled.
source_blocks.text: 18岁以下的儿童可能残疾，但在决定他或她是否有资格作为您的受抚养人获得福利时，我们无需考虑该儿童的残疾状况。儿童的福利通常在其18岁时停止，除非他或她是小学或高中的全日制学生（福利可持续至19岁）或残疾。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Adults Disabled Before Age 22
source_blocks.text: 22岁前残疾的成年人

source_blocks.source_text_en: An adult disabled before age 22 may be eligible for child's benefits if a parent is deceased or starts receiving retirement or disability benefits. We consider this a "child's" benefit because it is paid on a parent's Social Security earnings record.
source_blocks.text: 如果父母去世或开始领取退休或残疾福利，22岁前残疾的成年人可能有资格获得子女福利。我们将其视为“子女”福利，因为它是根据父母的社保收入记录支付的。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The "adult child" including an adopted child, or, in some cases, a stepchild, grandchild, or step grandchild must be unmarried, age 18 or older, have a disability that started before age 22, and meet the definition of disability for adults.
source_blocks.text: “成年子女”（包括收养子女，或在某些情况下，继子女、孙子女或继孙子女）必须未婚、年满18岁或以上、残疾始于22岁之前，并符合成人残疾的定义。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Example: A worker starts collecting Social Security retirement benefits at age 62. He has a 38-year old son who has had cerebral palsy since birth. The son will start collecting a disabled "child's" benefit on his father's Social Security record.
source_blocks.text: 示例：一名工人在62岁时开始领取社会保障退休福利。他有一个38岁的儿子，自出生起就患有脑性瘫痪。这个儿子将根据其父亲的社保记录开始领取残疾“子女”福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: It is not necessary that the adult child ever worked. Benefits are paid based on the parent's earnings record.
source_blocks.text: 成年子女不必曾经工作过。福利是根据父母的收入记录支付的。

source_blocks.source_text_en: An adult child must not have substantial earnings. The amount of earnings we consider "substantial" increases each year. In 2019, this means working and earning more than \$1,220 a month.
source_blocks.text: 成年子女不得有可观的收入。我们认为“可观”的收入金额每年都会增加。2019年，这意味着每月工作收入超过\$1,220美元。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Certain expenses the adult child incurs in order to work may be excluded from these earnings. For more information about work and disability, refer to .
source_blocks.text: 成年子女为工作而产生的某些费用可以从这些收入中扣除。有关工作和残疾的更多信息，请参阅。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if the adult child is already receiving SSI benefits or disability benefits on his or her own record?
source_blocks.text: 如果成年子女已经根据其自身记录领取SSI福利或残疾福利怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: An adult child already receiving SSI benefits or disability benefits on his or her own record should still check to see if benefits may be payable on a parent's earnings record. Higher benefits might be payable and entitlement to Medicare may be possible.
source_blocks.text: 已经根据自身记录领取SSI福利或残疾福利的成年子女仍应检查是否可以根据父母的收入记录领取福利。可能可以领取更高的福利，并且可能有权享受Medicare。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do we decide if an adult "child" is disabled for SSDI benefits?
source_blocks.text: 我们如何判断成年“子女”是否符合SSDI福利的残疾标准？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If a child is age 18 or older, we will evaluate his or her disability the same way we would evaluate the disability for any adult. We send the application to the Disability Determination Services in your state that completes the disability decision for us.
source_blocks.text: 如果子女年满18岁或以上，我们将以评估任何成年人残疾的相同方式评估其残疾。我们将申请发送给您所在州的残疾鉴定服务部门，该部门为我们完成残疾决定。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What happens if the adult child gets married?
source_blocks.text: 如果成年子女结婚会怎样？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If he or she receives benefits as an adult disabled since childhood, the benefits generally end if he or she gets married. However, some marriages (for example, to another adult disabled child) are considered protected.
source_blocks.text: 如果他或她作为自幼残疾的成年人领取福利，通常结婚后福利会终止。但是，某些婚姻（例如，与另一位自幼残疾的成年人结婚）被视为受保护的。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The rules vary depending on the situation. Contact a Social Security representative at 1-800-772-1213 (If you are deaf or hard of hearing, call TTY number at 1-800-325-0778) to find out if the benefits can continue.
source_blocks.text: 规则因情况而异。请联系社会保障代表，电话1-800-772-1213（如果您失聪或听力困难，请拨打TTY号码1-800-325-0778），以了解福利是否可以继续。

source_blocks.source_text_en: At this time, you cannot apply for disabled adult child's benefits online. If you wish to file for benefits, contact Social Security immediately at 1-800-772-1213 to request an appointment. (If you are deaf or hard of hearing, call our TTY number at 1-800-325-0778.) If you delay, some potential benefits could be lost.
source_blocks.text: 目前，您无法在线申请残疾成年子女福利。如果您希望申请福利，请立即联系社会保障局，电话1-800-772-1213，预约时间。（如果您失聪或听力困难，请拨打我们的TTY号码1-800-325-0778。）如果您拖延，可能会失去一些潜在的福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If they are disabled, they can speed up the application process if they complete an Adult Disability Report and have it available at the time of their appointment.
source_blocks.text: 如果他们残疾，他们可以填写《成人残疾报告》并在预约时准备好，以加快申请流程。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Disability is a subject you may read about in the newspaper, but not think of as something that might actually happen to you. But your chances of becoming disabled are probably greater than you realize.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Studies show that just over one in four of today's 20-year-olds will become disabled before reaching age 67.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Disability and Supplemental Security Income
source_blocks.text: Disability and Supplemental Security Income

source_blocks.source_text_en: We pay disability benefits under two programs:
source_blocks.text: We pay disability benefits under two programs:

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Social Security disability insurance program pays benefits to you and certain family members if you worked long enough and paid Social Security taxes. (Your adult child also may qualify for benefits on your earnings record if he or she has a disability that started before age 22.) The Supplemental Security Income (SSI) program pays benefits to disabled adults and children who have limited income and resources.

(Your adult child also may qualify for benefits on your earnings record if he or she has a disability that started before age 22.) The Supplemental Security Income (SSI) program pays benefits to disabled adults and children who have limited income and resources.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For most people, the medical requirements are the same under both programs and disability is determined by the same process.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Whether you apply for Social Security disability or SSI, we ask you for information about your medical condition, work, and education history to help us decide if you are disabled under our rules.

source_blocks.source_text_en: We pay disability benefits under two programs:
source_blocks.text: We pay disability benefits under two programs:

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Social Security disability insurance program pays benefits to you and certain family members if you worked long enough and paid Social Security taxes. (Your adult child also may qualify for benefits on your earnings record if he or she has a disability that started before age 22.) The Supplemental Security Income (SSI) program pays benefits to disabled adults and children who have limited income and resources.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For most people, the medical requirements are the same under both programs and disability is determined by the same process.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Apply for benefits before full retirement age, your benefits will be reduced because you are taking them earlier. (Full retirement age is 66 for people born between 1943 and 1954. Beginning with 1955, two months are added for every birth year until the full retirement age reaches 67 for people born in 1960 or later.) If your full retirement age is 66 and you decide to start your retirement benefits at age 65, your benefit will be 93.33 percent of your full benefit amount.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Hospital insurance (Part A) helps pay for inpatient care in a hospital or skilled nursing facility (following a hospital stay), some home health care, and hospice care.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Most people age 65 or older are eligible for free Medicare hospital insurance (Part A) if they have worked and paid Medicare taxes long enough. source_blocks.source_text_en: Apply for benefits before full retirement age, your benefits will be reduced because you are taking them earlier. source_blocks.source_text_en: No matter what your full retirement age (also called "normal retirement age") is, you may start receiving benefits as early as age 62 or as late as age 70.
source_blocks.text: 无论你的 full retirement age（也称为 "normal retirement age"）是多少，你都可以最早在 62 岁或最晚在 70 岁开始领取福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If You Retire Early
source_blocks.text: 如果你提前退休

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can retire at any time between age 62 and full retirement age. However, if you start benefits early, your benefits are reduced a fraction of a percent for each month before your full retirement age.
source_blocks.text: 你可以在 62 岁到 full retirement age 之间的任何时间退休。然而，如果你提前开始领取福利，你的福利将根据你提前的月份数按百分比减少。

source_blocks.text: 下表列出了 62 岁时的减少金额，并基于 full retirement age 时估计每月福利 \$1000 的示例。选择你的出生年份，了解如果你在 62 岁到 full retirement age 之间退休，你的福利将减少多少。

source_blocks.text: 如果你的生日是 1 月 1 日，我们会按照你的生日在上一年来计算你的福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are advantages and disadvantages to taking your benefit before your full retirement age. The advantage is that you collect benefits for a longer period of time. The disadvantage is your benefit is reduced. Each person's situation is different. It is important to remember:
source_blocks.text: 在 full retirement age 之前领取福利有优点也有缺点。优点是你领取福利的时间更长。缺点是福利会减少。每个人的情况不同。重要的是要记住：

source_blocks.source_text_en: if you delay your benefits until after full retirement age, you may be eligible for delayed retirement credits that would increase your monthly benefit; that there are other things to consider when making the correct decision about your retirement benefits; and to contact Social Security before you decide when to retire.
source_blocks.text: 如果你将福利延迟到 full retirement age 之后，你可能符合 delayed retirement credits 的条件，这会增加你的每月福利； 在做出关于退休福利的正确决定时，还有其他因素需要考虑；以及 在决定何时退休之前，请联系 Social Security。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you decide to delay your benefits until after age 65, you should still for Medicare benefits within three months of your 65th birthday. If you wait longer, your Medicare medical insurance (Part B) and prescription drug coverage (Part D) may cost you more money.
source_blocks.text: 如果你决定将福利延迟到 65 岁之后，你仍应在 65 岁生日后的三个月内申请 Medicare 福利。如果你等待更长时间，你的 Medicare 医疗保险（Part B）和处方药保险（Part D）可能会花费更多。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits For Your Family
source_blocks.text: 您的家庭福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: When you start receiving Social Security retirement benefits, some members of your family may also qualify to receive benefits on your record.
source_blocks.text: 当您开始领取社会保障退休福利时，您的部分家庭成员也可能有资格根据您的记录领取福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If they qualify, your spouse or child may receive a monthly payment of up to one-half of your full retirement benefit amount. These payments will not decrease your retirement benefit. In fact, the value of the benefits your family may receive, added to your own, may help you decide if taking your benefits sooner may be more advantageous.
source_blocks.text: 如果他们符合资格，您的配偶或子女每月可能收到高达您全额退休福利金额一半的付款。这些付款不会减少您的退休福利。事实上，您的家庭可能获得的福利价值加上您自己的福利，可能有助于您决定提前领取福利是否更有利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits paid to your spouse will not decrease your retirement benefit. In fact, the value of the benefits they may receive, added to your own, may help you decide if taking your benefits sooner may be more advantageous.
source_blocks.text: 支付给您配偶的福利不会减少您的退休福利。事实上，他们可能获得的福利价值加上您自己的福利，可能有助于您决定提前领取福利是否更有利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Maximum Family Benefits
source_blocks.text: 最高家庭福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: If one of your children also qualifies for benefits, there is a limit to the amount we can pay your family. The total depends on your benefit amount and the number of family members who also qualify on your record.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的子女之一也符合资格领取福利，我们能够支付给您家庭的金额是有限制的。总额取决于您的福利金额以及根据您的记录也符合资格的家庭成员人数。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The total varies, but generally the total amount you and your family can receive is about 150 to 180 percent of your full retirement benefit.
source_blocks.text: 总额各不相同，但通常您和您的家庭能够收到的总金额约为您全额退休福利的150%至180%。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have a divorced spouse who qualifies for benefits, it will not affect the amount of benefits you or your family may receive.
source_blocks.text: 如果您有一位符合福利资格的前配偶，这不会影响您或您的家庭可能收到的福利金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If any of your qualified family members apply for benefits with you, we will ask you for their Social Security numbers and their birth certificates.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的任何合格家庭成员与您一起申请福利，我们将要求您提供他们的社会保障号码和出生证明。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits For Your Spouse
source_blocks.text: 您的配偶的福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: Even if they have never worked under Social Security, your spouse may be able to get benefits if they are at least 62 years of age and you are receiving or eligible for retirement or disability benefits. Your spouse can also qualify for Medicare at age 65.
source_blocks.text: 即使您的配偶从未在社会保障制度下工作过，只要他们年满62岁，并且您正在领取或有资格领取退休或残疾福利，他们也可能获得福利。您的配偶在65岁时也有资格加入Medicare。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How Much Will My Spouse Receive?
source_blocks.text: 我的配偶将收到多少？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your spouse qualifies for benefits on their own record, we will pay that amount first. If the benefit on your record is higher, they will get an additional amount on your record so that the combination of benefits equals that higher amount.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的配偶根据他们自己的记录有资格领取福利，我们将首先支付该金额。如果根据您的记录的福利更高，他们将根据您的记录获得额外金额，以便福利组合等于该更高金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The benefits for your spouse do not include any delayed retirement credits you may receive.
source_blocks.text: 您配偶的福利不包括您可能获得的任何延迟退休积分。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If they begin receiving benefits:
source_blocks.text: 如果他们开始领取福利：

source_blocks.source_text_en: between age 62 and their full retirement age, the amount will be permanently reduced by a percentage based on the number of months up to their full retirement age. If your spouse is under full retirement age and: - works while receiving benefits, their benefits may be affected by the retirement earnings test. - also qualifies on their own record, their application will include both benefits. at their full retirement age, the spouse s benefit cannot exceed one-half of your full retirement amount.
source_blocks.text: 在62岁至其全额退休年龄之间，金额将根据距离其全额退休年龄的月数按百分比永久减少。如果您的配偶未达到全额退休年龄并且： - 在领取福利期间工作，他们的福利可能会受到退休收入测试的影响。 - 也根据他们自己的记录符合资格，他们的申请将包括两种福利。 在其全额退休年龄时，配偶的福利不能超过您全额退休金额的一半。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Delayed Retirement Credits
source_blocks.text: 延迟退休积分

source_blocks.source_text_en: Social Security retirement benefits are increased by a certain percentage (depending on date of birth) if you delay your retirement beyond full retirement age.
source_blocks.text: 如果您在达到完全退休年龄后延迟退休，社会保障退休福利将按一定百分比增加（取决于出生日期）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The benefit increase no longer applies when you reach age 70, even if you continue to delay taking benefits.
source_blocks.text: 当您达到70岁时，福利增加不再适用，即使您继续延迟领取福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Increase for Delayed Retirement
source_blocks.text: 延迟退休的增加

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you've already reached full retirement age, you can choose to start receiving benefits before the month you apply. However, we cannot pay retroactive benefits for any month before you reached full retirement age or more than 6 months in the past.
source_blocks.text: 如果您已经达到完全退休年龄，您可以选择在申请月份之前开始领取福利。但是，我们不能支付您达到完全退休年龄之前或超过过去6个月的追溯福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you decide to delay your retirement, be sure to sign up for just Medicare at age 65.
source_blocks.text: 如果您决定延迟退休，请务必在65岁时仅注册Medicare。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you do not sign up, in some circumstances your Medicare coverage may be delayed and cost more .
source_blocks.text: 如果您不注册，在某些情况下，您的Medicare保险可能会被延迟并花费更多。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you do not sign up, in some circumstances your Medicare coverage may be delayed and cost more.
source_blocks.text: 如果您不注册，在某些情况下，您的Medicare保险可能会被延迟并花费更多。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Additional Information
source_blocks.text: 附加信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: What's the best time to start your retirement benefits? We're not recommending that you start at age 62, your full retirement age, age 70, or any age in between. Here's some additional information that may help you decide what's right for you:
source_blocks.text: 什么时候开始领取退休福利最合适？我们并不建议您在62岁、完全退休年龄、70岁或任何中间年龄开始领取。以下是一些附加信息，可能有助于您决定什么最适合您：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Early or Late Retirement? Retirement Information for Medicare Beneficiaries Other Things To Consider
source_blocks.text: 提前还是延迟退休？ 针对Medicare受益人的退休信息 其他需要考虑的事项

source_blocks.source_text_en: Getting Benefits While Working
source_blocks.text: 工作期间领取福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can work while you receive Social Security retirement (or survivors) benefits. When you do, it could mean a higher benefit for you in the future.
source_blocks.text: 您可以在领取社会保障退休（或遗属）福利的同时工作。这样做，未来您可能会获得更高的福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Each year we review the records for all working Social Security recipients. If your earnings for the prior year are higher than one of the years we used to compute your retirement benefit, we will recalculate your benefit amount. We pay the increase retroactive to January the year after you earned the money.
source_blocks.text: 每年我们都会审查所有在职社会保障受益人的记录。如果您上一年的收入高于我们计算您退休福利时所使用的某一年份，我们将重新计算您的福利金额。我们会将增加的部分追溯支付至您赚取该收入之后的次年一月。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Higher benefits can be important to you later in life and increase the future benefit amounts your family and your survivors could receive.
source_blocks.text: 更高的福利对您晚年生活可能很重要，并会增加您的家人和遗属未来可能获得的福利金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you receive survivors benefits, the additional earnings could help make your retirement benefit higher than your current survivors benefit.
source_blocks.text: 如果您领取遗属福利，额外的收入可能有助于使您的退休福利高于您当前的遗属福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How Much Can I Earn And Still Get Benefits?
source_blocks.text: 我能赚多少钱还能领取福利？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are younger than full retirement age and make more than the yearly earnings limit, your earnings may reduce your benefit amount. (Full retirement age is 66 for people born between 1943 and 1954. Beginning with 1955, two months are added for every birth year until the full retirement age reaches 67 for people born in 1960 or later.)
source_blocks.text: 如果您未达到完全退休年龄，并且收入超过年度收入限额，您的收入可能会减少您的福利金额。（对于1943年至1954年出生的人，完全退休年龄为66岁。从1955年开始，每出生一年增加两个月，直到1960年或以后出生的人完全退休年龄达到67岁。）

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are under full retirement age for the entire year, we deduct \$1 from your benefit payments for every \$2 you earn above the annual limit. For 2019, that limit is \$17,640.
source_blocks.text: 如果您全年未达到完全退休年龄，我们将从您的福利金中扣除您超过年度限额部分每赚取2美元中的1美元。2019年，该限额为17,640美元。

source_blocks.source_text_en: In the year you reach full retirement age, we deduct \$1 in benefits for every \$3 you earn above a different limit. In 2019, the limit on your earnings is \$46,920 but we only count earnings before the month you reach your full retirement age.
source_blocks.text: 在您达到完全退休年龄的那一年，对于您超过另一限额的收入，每赚取3美元，我们将扣除1美元的福利。2019年，您的收入限额为46,920美元，但我们只计算您达到完全退休年龄之前那个月的收入。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is Government Pension Offset (GPO)?
source_blocks.text: 什么是政府养老金抵销（GPO）？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you will receive a pension for work not covered by Social Security (such as government employment), any Social Security benefits you may be eligible to receive on your spouse's record may be reduced. This type of benefit reduction is called GPO.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The estimated "gross" monthly amount of your pension from your government job not covered by Social Security. The estimated monthly amount of your Social Security benefit as a spouse, widow, or widower before the effect of GPO.
source_blocks.text: 您未纳入社会保障的政府工作养老金的估计“毛”月金额。 在GPO影响之前，您作为配偶、遗孀或鳏夫的社会保障福利的估计月金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you will be eligible for spouse's benefits and have access to your spouse's estimate:
source_blocks.text: 如果您将有资格获得配偶福利，并且可以访问您配偶的估算：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Find the estimated amount of the retirement benefit your spouse would be eligible to receive at full retirement age. If your spouse already receives benefits, ask them what their benefit would be if it started at their full (or normal) retirement age. Divide this amount in half and round down to the nearest dollar. This is your estimated spouse's benefit if you retire at full retirement age.
source_blocks.text: 找到您的配偶在完全退休年龄有资格获得的退休福利的估计金额。如果您的配偶已经在领取福利，请询问他们，如果福利在其完全（或正常）退休年龄开始，金额会是多少。 将此金额除以二，并向下取整到最接近的美元。这是您在完全退休年龄退休时的估计配偶福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you will be eligible for a Social Security retirement benefit based on your own earnings:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your benefit as a divorced spouse is equal to one-half of your ex-spouse's full retirement amount (or disability benefit) if you start receiving benefits at your full retirement age. The benefits do not include any delayed retirement credits your ex-spouse may receive.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Medicare Premiums: Rules For Higher-Income Beneficiaries
source_blocks.text: Medicare Premiums: Rules For Higher-Income Beneficiaries

source_blocks.source_text_en: The law requires an adjustment to your monthly Medicare Part B (medical insurance) and Medicare prescription drug coverage premiums. This affects less than five percent of people with Medicare. Most people don t pay higher premiums.
source_blocks.text: The law requires an adjustment to your monthly Medicare Part B (medical insurance) and Medicare prescription drug coverage premiums. This affects less than five percent of people with Medicare. Most people don t pay higher premiums.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If You Have a Higher Income
source_blocks.text: If You Have a Higher Income

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have higher income, you ll pay an additional premium amount for Medicare Part B and Medicare prescription drug coverage. We call the additional amount the income-related monthly adjustment amount. Here s how it works:
source_blocks.text: If you have higher income, you ll pay an additional premium amount for Medicare Part B and Medicare prescription drug coverage. We call the additional amount the income-related monthly adjustment amount. Here s how it works:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Part B helps pay for your doctors services and outpatient care. It also covers other medical services, such as physical and occupational therapy, and some home health care. For most beneficiaries, the government pays a substantial portion about 75 percent of the Part B premium, and the beneficiary pays the remaining 25 percent.
source_blocks.text: Part B helps pay for your doctors services and outpatient care. It also covers other medical services, such as physical and occupational therapy, and some home health care. For most beneficiaries, the government pays a substantial portion about 75 percent of the Part B premium, and the beneficiary pays the remaining 25 percent.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If we determine you re a higher-income beneficiary, you ll pay a larger percentage of the total cost of Part B based on the income you normally report to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). You ll pay monthly Part B premiums equal to 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost, depending on what you report to the IRS.
source_blocks.text: If we determine you re a higher-income beneficiary, you ll pay a larger percentage of the total cost of Part B based on the income you normally report to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). You ll pay monthly Part B premiums equal to 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost, depending on what you report to the IRS.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Medicare prescription drug coverage helps pay for your prescription drugs. For most beneficiaries, the government pays a major portion of the total costs for this coverage, and the beneficiary pays the rest. Prescription drug plan costs vary depending on the plan, and whether you get the Extra Help, also known as the subsidy, with your portion of the Medicare prescription drug coverage costs.
source_blocks.text: Medicare prescription drug coverage helps pay for your prescription drugs. For most beneficiaries, the government pays a major portion of the total costs for this coverage, and the beneficiary pays the rest. Prescription drug plan costs vary depending on the plan, and whether you get the Extra Help, also known as the subsidy, with your portion of the Medicare prescription drug coverage costs.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re a higher-income beneficiary with Medicare prescription drug coverage, you ll pay monthly premiums plus an additional amount, which is based on what you report to the IRS. Because individual plan premiums vary, the law specifies that the amount is determined using a base premium. We tie the additional amount you pay to the base beneficiary premium, not your own premium amount. If you re a higher-income beneficiary, we deduct this amount from your monthly Social Security payments regardless of how you usually pay your monthly prescription plan premiums. If the amount is greater than your monthly payment from Social Security, or you don t get monthly payments, you ll get a separate bill from another federal agency, such as the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services or the Railroad Retirement Board.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The law requires an adjustment to your monthly Medicare Part B (medical insurance) and Medicare prescription drug coverage premiums. This affects less than five percent of people with Medicare. Most people don t pay higher premiums.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If You Have a Higher Income
source_blocks.text: If You Have a Higher Income

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have higher income, you ll pay an additional premium amount for Medicare Part B and Medicare prescription drug coverage. We call the additional amount the income-related monthly adjustment amount. Here s how it works:
source_blocks.text: If you have higher income, you ll pay an additional premium amount for Medicare Part B and Medicare prescription drug coverage. We call the additional amount the income-related monthly adjustment amount. Here s how it works:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Part B helps pay for your doctors services and outpatient care. It also covers other medical services, such as physical and occupational therapy, and some home health care. For most beneficiaries, the government pays a substantial portion about 75 percent of the Part B premium, and the beneficiary pays the remaining 25 percent.
source_blocks.text: Part B helps pay for your doctors services and outpatient care. It also covers other medical services, such as physical and occupational therapy, and some home health care. For most beneficiaries, the government pays a substantial portion about 75 percent of the Part B premium, and the beneficiary pays the remaining 25 percent.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If we determine you re a higher-income beneficiary, you ll pay a larger percentage of the total cost of Part B based on the income you normally report to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). You ll pay monthly Part B premiums equal to 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost, depending on what you report to the IRS.
source_blocks.text: If we determine you re a higher-income beneficiary, you ll pay a larger percentage of the total cost of Part B based on the income you normally report to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). You ll pay monthly Part B premiums equal to 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost, depending on what you report to the IRS.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Medicare prescription drug coverage helps pay for your prescription drugs. For most beneficiaries, the government pays a major portion of the total costs for this coverage, and the beneficiary pays the rest. Prescription drug plan costs vary depending on the plan, and whether you get the Extra Help, also known as the subsidy, with your portion of the Medicare prescription drug coverage costs.
source_blocks.text: Medicare prescription drug coverage helps pay for your prescription drugs. For most beneficiaries, the government pays a major portion of the total costs for this coverage, and the beneficiary pays the rest. Prescription drug plan costs vary depending on the plan, and whether you get the Extra Help, also known as the subsidy, with your portion of the Medicare prescription drug coverage costs.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re a higher-income beneficiary with Medicare prescription drug coverage, you ll pay monthly premiums plus an additional amount, which is based on what you report to the IRS. Because individual plan premiums vary, the law specifies that the amount is determined using a base premium. We tie the additional amount you pay to the base beneficiary premium, not your own premium amount. If you re a higher-income beneficiary, we deduct this amount from your monthly Social Security payments regardless of how you usually pay your monthly prescription plan premiums. If the amount is greater than your monthly payment from Social Security, or you don t get monthly payments, you ll get a separate bill from another federal agency, such as the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services or the Railroad Retirement Board.

source_blocks.text: 下面显示的计算器允许您估算您的社会保障福利。但是，为了获得最准确的估算，请使用详细计算器。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You need to enter all your past earnings , which are shown on your online .
source_blocks.text: 您需要输入所有过去的收入，这些收入显示在您的在线记录中。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Please Note:
source_blocks.text: 请注意：

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Online Calculator is updated periodically\ with new benefit increases and other benefit amounts. Therefore, it is likely that your benefit estimates in the future will differ from those calculated today. The Online Calculator works on PCs and Macs with Javascript enabled. Some browsers may not allow you to print the table below.
source_blocks.text: 在线计算器会定期更新\，以反映新的福利增加和其他福利金额。因此，您未来的福利估算很可能与今天计算的结果不同。 在线计算器适用于启用Javascript的PC和Mac。 某些浏览器可能不允许您打印下面的表格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Online Calculator temporarily stores information on your local computer while your browser is open. To protect your personal information, you should close your browser after you have finished your estimate.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: If your birthday is on January 1st, we figure your benefit as if your birthday was in the previous year.
source_blocks.text: 注意：如果您的生日是1月1日，我们会将您的福利计算视为您的生日是在上一年。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What Is The Best Age To Start Your Benefits?
source_blocks.text: What Is The Best Age To Start Your Benefits?

source_blocks.source_text_en: The answer is that there is no one "best age" for everyone and, ultimately, it is your choice. You should make an informed decision about when to apply for benefits based on your individual and family circumstances.
source_blocks.text: The answer is that there is no one "best age" for everyone and, ultimately, it is your choice. You should make an informed decision about when to apply for benefits based on your individual and family circumstances.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your monthly benefit amount can differ substantially based on the age when you start receiving benefits. If you decide to start benefits:
source_blocks.text: Your monthly benefit amount can differ substantially based on the age when you start receiving benefits. If you decide to start benefits:

source_blocks.source_text_en: before your full retirement age, your benefit will be smaller but you will receive it for a longer period of time. at your full retirement age or later, you will receive a larger monthly benefit for a shorter period of time.
source_blocks.text: before your full retirement age, your benefit will be smaller but you will receive it for a longer period of time. at your full retirement age or later, you will receive a larger monthly benefit for a shorter period of time.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The amount you receive when you first get benefits sets the base for the amount you will receive for the rest of your life.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may want to consider the following when you make that decision:
source_blocks.text: You may want to consider the following when you make that decision:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Are you still working?
source_blocks.text: Are you still working?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you plan to continue working, there are limits on how much you can earn each year between age 62 and full retirement age and still get all your benefits.
source_blocks.text: If you plan to continue working, there are limits on how much you can earn each year between age 62 and full retirement age and still get all your benefits.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Depending on the amount of your benefit and your earnings for the year, you may have to give up some of your benefits. If your earnings will be high, you may decide to wait until full retirement age to start your benefits.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Once you reach full retirement age, there is no limit on how much you can earn.
source_blocks.text: Once you reach full retirement age, there is no limit on how much you can earn.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reminders:
source_blocks.text: Reminders:

source_blocks.source_text_en: After you reach full retirement age, we recalculate your benefit amount to give you credit for any months in which you did not receive a benefit because of your earnings. When additional earnings appear on your record, we check whether they will increase your monthly benefit. If they do, we will send you a letter telling you your new benefit amount. You can apply for just Medicare at age 65 and start receiving retirement benefits later.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Do you come from a long-lived family?
source_blocks.text: Do you come from a long-lived family?

source_blocks.source_text_en: When you think about retirement, be sure to plan for the long term.
source_blocks.text: When you think about retirement, be sure to plan for the long term.

source_blocks.source_text_en: A man who turned 65 in 2014 can expect to live about another 19.3 years. A woman who turned 65 the same year can expect to live about another 21.6 years.

source_blocks.source_text_en: And those are just averages. About one out of every four 65-year-olds today will live past age 90. One out of 10 will live past age 95.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How long do you expect to live?
source_blocks.text: How long do you expect to live?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Did your parents and grandparents all live into their 80s or 90s? If the answer is yes, and you have every reason to believe you will too, you may want to delay starting your benefits until full retirement age or later. If they didn't, you may choose to start receiving retirement benefits earlier.

If they didn't, you may choose to start receiving retirement benefits earlier.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you come from a long-lived family, you may need the extra money more in later years, particularly if you may outlive pensions or annuities with limits on how long they are paid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Will you still have health insurance?
source_blocks.text: Will you still have health insurance?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you stop working, not only will you lose your paycheck, but you may also lose valuable employer provided health insurance. Although there are exceptions, most people will not be covered by Medicare until they reach age 65.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your employer should be able to tell you if you will have retiree health benefits or if you can temporarily extend your health insurance coverage after you retire. Also, if you are married and your spouse is employed, you may be able to switch to their health insurance.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Should I apply for Medicare?
source_blocks.text: Should I apply for Medicare?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Remember, Medicare usually starts when you reach age 65.
source_blocks.text: Remember, Medicare usually starts when you reach age 65.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you decide to delay starting your benefits, be sure to contact Social Security about 3 months before you turn age 65 to check about applying for Medicare.
source_blocks.text: If you decide to delay starting your benefits, be sure to contact Social Security about 3 months before you turn age 65 to check about applying for Medicare.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Even if you have health insurance through a current or former employer or as part of your severance package, you should still check to see whether you need to sign up for Medicare. Some health insurance plans change automatically at age 65.
source_blocks.text: Even if you have health insurance through a current or former employer or as part of your severance package, you should still check to see whether you need to sign up for Medicare. Some health insurance plans change automatically at age 65.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you need to sign up for Medicare but you do not, your Medicare coverage may be delayed and cost more. Please read the general and special enrollment period information on page 12 of our Medicare booklet to find out what may happen if you delay.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are eligible on another record, you may have additional options:
source_blocks.text: If you are eligible on another record, you may have additional options:

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you qualify for benefits as a widow, widower, or surviving divorced spouse on another record, you may choose to apply for survivors benefits now and delay your retirement benefit until later.
source_blocks.text: If you qualify for benefits as a widow, widower, or surviving divorced spouse on another record, you may choose to apply for survivors benefits now and delay your retirement benefit until later.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you delay receiving your retirement benefit until your full retirement age or later, your retirement benefit will be higher.
source_blocks.text: If you delay receiving your retirement benefit until your full retirement age or later, your retirement benefit will be higher.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you were born before January 2, 1954 and have already reached your full retirement age, and are eligible for a spouse s or divorced-spouse s benefit and your own retirement benefit, you can choose to receive only the spouse s benefit and delay receiving your retirement benefit until a later date. If your birthday is January 2, 1954 or later, the option to take only one benefit at full retirement age no longer exists. If you file for one benefit, you will be effectively filing for all retirement or spousal benefits.

If your birthday is January 2, 1954 or later, the option to take only one benefit at full retirement age no longer exists. If you file for one benefit, you will be effectively filing for all retirement or spousal benefits.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Do you have other income to support you if you decide to delay taking your benefits?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you don't need your benefits immediately, you may decide to:
source_blocks.text: If you don't need your benefits immediately, you may decide to:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Wait beyond full retirement age to receive delayed retirement credits.
source_blocks.text: Wait beyond full retirement age to receive delayed retirement credits.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reminder: If you are within 4 months of age 65, or older, and you have health insurance through an employer or former employer, you should check to see whether you need to sign up for Medicare.
source_blocks.text: Reminder: If you are within 4 months of age 65, or older, and you have health insurance through an employer or former employer, you should check to see whether you need to sign up for Medicare.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Some health insurance plans change automatically at age 65.
source_blocks.text: Some health insurance plans change automatically at age 65.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Choose early retirement and increase the value of your benefits by investing them instead of spending them.
source_blocks.text: Choose early retirement and increase the value of your benefits by investing them instead of spending them.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reminder: If you're receiving early retirement from your employer, keep in mind that some company pensions include a Social Security-equivalent supplement that stops automatically at age 62.
source_blocks.text: Reminder: If you're receiving early retirement from your employer, keep in mind that some company pensions include a Social Security-equivalent supplement that stops automatically at age 62.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The supplement stops because they assume you will apply for your retirement benefits at age 62.
source_blocks.text: The supplement stops because they assume you will apply for your retirement benefits at age 62.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Will other family members qualify for benefits on your record?
source_blocks.text: Will other family members qualify for benefits on your record?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your spouse or minor or disabled children will also qualify for benefits from your record, the value of their benefits, added to your own, may help you decide if taking your benefits sooner is your best choice.
source_blocks.text: If your spouse or minor or disabled children will also qualify for benefits from your record, the value of their benefits, added to your own, may help you decide if taking your benefits sooner is your best choice.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your spouse or ex-spouse s date of birth is January 2, 1954 or later and they become eligible to receive a higher benefit on your record while receiving retirement benefits, they can no longer delay filing for the additional benefit. If your spouse files for one benefit, they will be effectively filing for all retirement or spousal benefits.
source_blocks.text: If your spouse or ex-spouse s date of birth is January 2, 1954 or later and they become eligible to receive a higher benefit on your record while receiving retirement benefits, they can no longer delay filing for the additional benefit. If your spouse files for one benefit, they will be effectively filing for all retirement or spousal benefits.

source_blocks.source_text_en: However, when you start your retirement benefits also affects the amount your surviving spouse may receive. If you start your benefits:
source_blocks.text: However, when you start your retirement benefits also affects the amount your surviving spouse may receive. If you start your benefits:

source_blocks.source_text_en: before full retirement age, we cannot pay your surviving spouse the full benefit amount from your record. Generally, if you were receiving reduced benefits, we base the survivors benefit on that amount. after full retirement age, your surviving spouse may receive your full benefit amount plus any accumulated delayed retirement credits.
