source_blocks.source_text_en: Aid for Military Families | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 军人家庭援助 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may be able to get money for college or career school for your or your family member s military service.
source_blocks.text: 您或您的家庭成员可能因服兵役而获得上大学或职业学校的资助。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Scholarships and loan repayment assistance are available from a number of sources.
source_blocks.text: 多项奖学金和贷款偿还援助可从多个来源获得。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Both the federal government and nonprofit organizations offer money for college to veterans, future military personnel, active duty personnel, or those related to veterans or active duty personnel.
source_blocks.text: 联邦政府和非营利组织都为退伍军人、未来军人、现役军人或与退伍军人或现役军人相关的人员提供大学资助。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Try This ResourceScholarships for Military Families Provides resources and contact information for finding college scholarships for military families.
source_blocks.text: 尝试此资源军人家庭奖学金 提供寻找军人家庭大学奖学金的资源和联系信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What financial aid does the government offer for military service or for family members of military personnel?
source_blocks.text: 政府为服兵役或军人家庭成员提供哪些经济援助？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Below are a few sources of financial aid that you might want to consider. You also should explore todaysmilitary.com s list of education benefits for service members.
source_blocks.text: 以下是一些您可能想要考虑的经济援助来源。您还应该浏览todaysmilitary.com上为军人列出的教育福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reserve Officers Training Corps (ROTC) Scholarships
source_blocks.text: 预备役军官训练军团（ROTC）奖学金

source_blocks.source_text_en: These scholarships are awarded on the basis of merit rather than financial need:
source_blocks.text: 这些奖学金是根据成绩而非经济需要授予的：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Army ROTC scholarships are offered at more than 1,000 colleges. For application packets, information about eligibility, and the telephone number of an ROTC advisor in your area, call 1-888-550-ARMY (1-888-550-2769) or visit the Army ROTC web page. The Air Force ROTC college scholarship program targets students pursuing certain foreign language and technical degrees, although students entering a wide variety of majors may be accepted. For more information, call 1-866-4-AFROTC (1-866-423-7682) or visit the Air Force ROTC Scholarship web page. The Navy ROTC offers both four-year and partial scholarships. To learn more, call 1-800-NAV-ROTC (1-800-628-7682) or visit the Navy ROTC website. The Navy ROTC Marine Option Scholarship helps you pay your way through college at approved Navy ROTC schools. Learn more about the Navy ROTC Marine Option Scholarship.
source_blocks.text: 陆军ROTC奖学金在超过1,000所大学提供。如需申请资料包、资格信息以及您所在地区ROTC顾问的电话号码，请致电1-888-550-ARMY（1-888-550-2769）或访问陆军ROTC网页。 空军ROTC大学奖学金计划针对攻读某些外语和技术学位的学生，尽管进入各种专业的学生也可能被接受。如需更多信息，请致电1-866-4-AFROTC（1-866-423-7682）或访问空军ROTC奖学金网页。 海军ROTC提供四年制和部分奖学金。要了解更多信息，请致电1-800-NAV-ROTC（1-800-628-7682）或访问海军ROTC网站。 海军ROTC海军陆战队选项奖学金帮助您在经批准的海军ROTC学校支付大学费用。了解更多关于海军ROTC海军陆战队选项奖学金的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Education Benefits
source_blocks.text: 退伍军人事务部（VA）教育福利

source_blocks.source_text_en: The VA offers education benefits for veterans and for their widows and dependents on its GI Bill site.
source_blocks.text: 退伍军人事务部在其GI Bill网站上为退伍军人及其遗孀和家属提供教育福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grant or Additional Federal Pell Grant Funds
source_blocks.text: 伊拉克和阿富汗服务补助金或额外的联邦佩尔助学金

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your parent or guardian died as a result of military service in Iraq or Afghanistan after the events of 9/11, you may be eligible for additional aid. To be eligible, at the time of your parent s or guardian s death, you must have been less than 24 years old or enrolled at least part-time at a college or career school. Payments will be adjusted if you are enrolled less than full-time.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的父母或监护人在9/11事件后因在伊拉克或阿富汗的军事服务而去世，您可能有资格获得额外援助。要符合资格，在您父母或监护人去世时，您必须未满24岁或至少半工半读地就读于学院或职业学校。如果您注册的课程少于全日制，付款将进行调整。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal Pell Grants: If you meet the requirements above and are eligible to receive a Pell Grant, you will receive an Expected Family Contribution (EFC) of zero, which maximizes your Pell Grant eligibility and can increase your eligibility for other federal student aid programs. Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grants: If you meet the requirements above but are not eligible for a Pell Grant based on your EFC, you will be eligible to receive the Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grant. The maximum amount of the Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grant is the same as the maximum Pell Grant award. Your EFC will not be affected, and therefore neither will your eligibility for any need-based federal student aid.
source_blocks.text: 联邦佩尔助学金：如果您满足上述要求并有资格获得佩尔助学金，您的预期家庭贡献（EFC）将为零，这使您的佩尔助学金资格最大化，并可能增加您获得其他联邦学生援助计划的资格。 伊拉克和阿富汗服务补助金：如果您满足上述要求但根据您的EFC没有资格获得佩尔助学金，您将有资格获得伊拉克和阿富汗服务补助金。伊拉克和阿富汗服务补助金的最高金额与佩尔助学金最高奖励相同。您的EFC不会受到影响，因此您对任何基于需求的联邦学生援助的资格也不会受到影响。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Limited Interest Rates, No Accrual of Interest, and Deferment of Student Loans
source_blocks.text: 有限利率、不产生利息和学生贷款延期

source_blocks.source_text_en: To receive the benefits below, contact your loan servicer for information about the documentation you must provide to show that you qualify.
source_blocks.text: 要获得以下福利，请联系您的贷款服务商，了解您必须提供的证明您符合资格的文件信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, if you took out student loans prior to entering the military or being called to active duty, the interest rate on those loans will be limited to 6% during your active duty military service. This applies to both federal and private student loans (and other loans as well). For all Direct Loans first disbursed on or after Oct. 1, 2008, no interest will be charged for a period of no more than 60 months while you are serving on active duty or performing qualifying National Guard duty during a war, other military operation, or national emergency and are serving in an area of hostilities qualifying for special pay. For Direct Consolidation Loans, this benefit applies to the portion of the consolidation loan that repaid loans first disbursed on or after Oct. 1, 2008. You will qualify for deferment of repayment on any of your federal loans while serving on active duty in the military, or performing qualifying National Guard duty, during a war, military operation, or national emergency. If your period of active duty service includes Oct. 1, 2007, or begins on or after that date, your deferment will be extended for an additional 180 days after the demobilization date for each period of qualifying service. If you are a member of the National Guard or other reserve component of the U.S. armed forces (current or retired) and you are called or ordered to active duty while you are enrolled at least half-time at an eligible school or within six months of having been enrolled at least half-time, you qualify for deferment of repayment on your federal student loans during the 13 months following the end of your active duty service, or until you return to school on at least a half-time basis, whichever is earlier.
source_blocks.text: 根据《军人民事救济法案》，如果您在入伍或被征召服现役之前申请了学生贷款，这些贷款的利率在您服现役期间将被限制在6%。这适用于联邦和私人学生贷款（以及其他贷款）。 对于所有在2008年10月1日或之后首次发放的直接贷款，在您服现役或执行符合条件的国民警卫队任务期间（在战争、其他军事行动或国家紧急状态期间，并且在符合特殊报酬条件的敌对地区服役），不超过60个月的期间内不会收取利息。对于直接合并贷款，此福利适用于合并贷款中偿还了在2008年10月1日或之后首次发放的贷款的部分。 在战争、军事行动或国家紧急状态期间，您在服现役或执行符合条件的国民警卫队任务时，将有资格延期偿还您的任何联邦贷款。如果您的现役服务期包括2007年10月1日或在该日期或之后开始，您的延期将在每次合格服务期的复员日期后额外延长180天。 如果您是美国武装部队国民警卫队或其他预备役部队的成员（现役或退役），并且在您至少半工半读地就读于合格学校期间或被征召或命令服现役，或在至少半工半读注册后的六个月内，您有资格在现役服务结束后的13个月内延期偿还您的联邦学生贷款，或直到您至少半工半读地返回学校，以较早者为准。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What financial aid do veterans service organizations offer for military service or for family members of military personnel?
source_blocks.text: 退伍军人服务组织为军人服役或军人家庭成员提供哪些经济援助？

source_blocks.source_text_en: The following major national organizations offer scholarships primarily to active duty military, veterans, and/or their families:
source_blocks.text: 以下主要国家组织主要向现役军人、退伍军人和/或其家属提供奖学金：

source_blocks.source_text_en: American Legion AMVETS Paralyzed Veterans of America Veterans of Foreign Wars
source_blocks.text: 美国退伍军人协会 美国退伍军人组织 美国瘫痪退伍军人协会 海外退伍军人协会

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are many smaller veterans service organizations around the country that might offer scholarships. Check with your local organization or try a scholarship search.
source_blocks.text: 全国各地还有许多较小的退伍军人服务组织可能提供奖学金。请咨询您当地的组织或尝试奖学金搜索。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How can I submit a complaint about how my college or career school is administering my financial aid?
source_blocks.text: 我如何就我的学院或职业学校管理我的经济援助提出投诉？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Do you believe your school is not administering federal student aid funds properly? Here s some information that might help you determine how to solve your problem or submit a complaint.
source_blocks.text: 您是否认为您的学校没有妥善管理联邦学生援助资金？以下信息可能有助于您确定如何解决问题或提交投诉。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your college or career school not the U.S. Department of Education will distribute your financial aid. If you have questions about why your aid hasn t been paid out yet, or why it wasn t the amount you expected, contact your school.
source_blocks.text: 您的学院或职业学校（而非美国教育部）将分发您的经济援助。如果您对援助为何尚未发放或金额为何与预期不符有疑问，请联系您的学校。

source_blocks.source_text_en: IF: You believe your school violated its own policy or federal regulations in its administration of the federal student aid programs for instance, if
source_blocks.text: 如果：您认为您的学校在管理联邦学生援助项目时违反了其自身政策或联邦法规，例如，如果

source_blocks.source_text_en: your school calculated your eligibility for federal student grants, loans, or work-study incorrectly;
source_blocks.text: 您的学校错误计算了您获得联邦学生助学金、贷款或勤工俭学的资格；

source_blocks.source_text_en: your school disbursed (paid out) your aid or your credit balance incorrectly (in the wrong amount, at the wrong time, or not at all); your school doesn t have a financial aid administrator (yet is participating in the federal student aid programs), doesn t have policies or procedures for administering the federal student aid programs, or has policies but isn t following them; your school or its representative has made false or misleading statements about the school s educational programs, financial charges, employability of graduates, etc.;
source_blocks.text: 您的学校错误地发放（支付）了您的援助或贷方余额（金额错误、时间错误或根本没有发放）； 您的学校没有经济援助管理员（但参与了联邦学生援助项目），没有管理联邦学生援助项目的政策或程序，或者有政策但未遵守； 您的学校或其代表对学校的教育项目、财务收费、毕业生就业能力等做出了虚假或误导性陈述；

source_blocks.source_text_en: and if you have tried to work things out with the school but have been unable to THEN: You may contact the Federal Student Aid Feedback Center or call 1-844-651-0077.
source_blocks.text: 并且如果您已尝试与学校解决问题但未能成功，那么：您可以联系联邦学生援助反馈中心或致电1-844-651-0077。

source_blocks.source_text_en: IF: You think your school awarded aid to someone else in your name THEN: Learn about identity theft and how to report it to our Office of Inspector General Hotline.
source_blocks.text: 如果：您认为您的学校以您的名义向他人授予了援助，那么：了解身份盗窃以及如何向我们的监察长办公室热线举报。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How can I learn more about military service?
source_blocks.text: 我如何了解更多关于军事服役的信息？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Contact a recruiter to learn more about service with the following military branches:
source_blocks.text: 联系招聘人员以了解以下军事部门的服役信息：

source_blocks.source_text_en: marines.com navy.com goarmy.com airforce.com gocoastguard.com

source_blocks.text: What is Income-Driven Repayment?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Income-driven repayment (IDR) plans are designed to make your student loan debt more manageable by reducing your monthly payment amount. If you need to make lower monthly payments or if your outstanding federal student loan debt represents a significant portion of your annual income, one of the following income-driven plans may be right for you:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Avoiding Default | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 避免违约 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are steps you can take to repay your federal student loan successfully and avoid going into default.
source_blocks.text: 您可以采取一些步骤来成功偿还联邦学生贷款并避免违约。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understanding your loan agreement, staying on top of your loan information, and making sure to contact your loan servicer if you are having trouble making payments can help you avoid default.
source_blocks.text: 了解您的贷款协议、及时掌握贷款信息，并在还款遇到困难时务必联系您的贷款服务机构，这些都有助于您避免违约。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you don t make a payment on time or if you miss making a payment, your loan is delinquent and late fees may be assessed. Even if you are delinquent on your loan, you may still be able to avoid default, so it s important that you contact your loan servicer immediately.
source_blocks.text: 如果您未能按时还款或错过还款，您的贷款将处于逾期状态，并可能产生滞纳金。即使您的贷款已逾期，您仍有可能避免违约，因此立即联系您的贷款服务机构非常重要。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Take Steps to Avoid Default
source_blocks.text: 采取措施避免违约

source_blocks.source_text_en: Avoid default. Take the time to fully understand your loan agreement and the types of loans you are receiving. It s also important that you not borrow more than you need or more than you expect to be able to repay. Develop a sound and realistic financial plan.
source_blocks.text: 避免违约。花时间充分了解您的贷款协议以及您所获得的贷款类型。同样重要的是，不要借超过您需要的金额，也不要借超过您预期能够偿还的金额。制定一个健全且现实的财务计划。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your federal student loan is delinquent, check out the Student Loan Debt Collection Assistant, which the U.S. Department of Education developed in partnership with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. The tool provides information about how to access the full range of special repayment options available to you.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的联邦学生贷款已逾期，请查看美国教育部与消费者金融保护局合作开发的“学生贷款债务催收助手”。该工具提供有关如何获取您可用的所有特殊还款选项的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understand Your Loan and Loan Agreement
source_blocks.text: 了解您的贷款和贷款协议

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understand the type of aid you are receiving. Loans, unlike most grants, scholarships, or work-study funds, must be repaid.
source_blocks.text: 了解您所获得的援助类型。与大多数助学金、奖学金或勤工助学资金不同，贷款必须偿还。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Know the type of loan you are receiving. Understand the costs of getting the loan, the interest rate, and the repayment terms for the loan. Read Know Before You Owe from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Read your promissory note. It is a legal document. Signing a promissory note means you agree to repay the loan according to the terms of the note. You must repay all the loans you receive, even if you don t complete your education.
source_blocks.text: 了解您所获得的贷款类型。了解获得贷款的成本、利率以及贷款的还款条款。 阅读消费者金融保护局发布的《欠债前须知》。 阅读您的本票。这是一份法律文件。签署本票意味着您同意根据本票条款偿还贷款。您必须偿还所获得的所有贷款，即使您未完成学业。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Manage Your Borrowing
source_blocks.text: 管理您的借款

source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrow only what you need to pay for your college expenses.
source_blocks.text: 只借您需要支付大学费用所需的金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Create a budget to determine how much you really need to borrow. Contact your school s financial aid office to request a lower loan amount instead of borrowing the maximum amount you might be eligible to receive. Complete Financial Awareness Counseling.
source_blocks.text: 制定预算以确定您实际需要借多少钱。 联系您学校的财务援助办公室，要求降低贷款金额，而不是借入您可能有资格获得的最高金额。 完成财务意识咨询。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Track Your Loans Online
source_blocks.text: 在线跟踪您的贷款

source_blocks.source_text_en: Find information about all of your federal student loans from the U.S. Department of Education by logging in to "My Federal Student Aid."
source_blocks.text: 通过登录“我的联邦学生援助”，查找美国教育部提供的有关您所有联邦学生贷款的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Keep Good Records
source_blocks.text: 妥善保存记录

source_blocks.source_text_en: Keep the following important documents in an organized file:
source_blocks.text: 将以下重要文件整理归档：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Financial aid offers Loan counseling materials (entrance counseling and exit counseling) Your promissory note(s) Amount(s) of all student loans you borrow Account number for each student loan you receive Loan servicer contact information Loan disclosure(s) Payment schedules Record of your monthly payments Notes about any questions you ask about your student loan, the answers, and the name of the person to whom you spoke Deferment or forbearance paperwork and notes of any phone calls to the loan servicer Documentation that you paid your loan in full
source_blocks.text: 财务援助通知 贷款咨询材料（入学咨询和离校咨询） 您的本票 您所借的所有学生贷款的金额 您收到的每笔学生贷款的账号 贷款服务机构联系信息 贷款披露文件 还款计划表 每月还款记录 关于您就学生贷款提出的任何问题、答案以及您与之交谈的人员姓名的记录 延期还款或暂缓还款的文书工作以及致电贷款服务机构的任何电话记录 您已全额还清贷款的证明文件

source_blocks.source_text_en: Notify Your Loan Servicer
source_blocks.text: 通知你的贷款服务商

source_blocks.source_text_en: Tell your loan servicer when you
source_blocks.text: 在以下情况告知你的贷款服务商

source_blocks.source_text_en: need help making your monthly payments; graduate; withdraw from school; drop below half-time enrollment status at school; change your name, address, or Social Security number; transfer to another school; or experience a change in your life that might impact your loan payments.
source_blocks.text: 需要帮助支付每月还款； 毕业； 退学； 在学校注册状态降至半日制以下； 更改姓名、地址或社会安全号码； 转学到另一所学校；或 生活中发生可能影响贷款还款的变化。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I can t make my monthly payment?
source_blocks.text: 如果我无法每月还款怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are having trouble making your monthly payments, contact your loan servicer immediately. Your loan servicer can help you understand your options. You may be able to
source_blocks.text: 如果你在每月还款方面遇到困难，请立即联系你的贷款服务商。你的贷款服务商可以帮助你了解你的选择。你可能能够

source_blocks.source_text_en: switch repayment plans to get a lower monthly payment, consider an income-driven repayment plan, change your payment due date, or get a deferment or forbearance.
source_blocks.text: 更换还款计划以获得较低的每月还款额， 考虑收入驱动还款计划， 更改还款到期日，或 获得延期还款或暂缓还款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: NEVER ignore delinquency or default notices from your loan servicer.
source_blocks.text: 切勿忽视贷款服务商发出的逾期或违约通知。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Consider Simplifying Repayment with Consolidation
source_blocks.text: 考虑通过合并简化还款

source_blocks.source_text_en: You might wish to combine your multiple federal student loans into a single Direct Consolidation Loan to simplify repayment. There may be tradeoffs, so understand the advantages and possible disadvantages of consolidation before you apply.
source_blocks.text: 你可能希望将多笔联邦学生贷款合并为一笔直接合并贷款，以简化还款。合并可能存在权衡，因此在申请前请了解合并的优点和可能的缺点。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reduce Your Risk of Identity Theft When Applying for Aid
source_blocks.text: Reduce Your Risk of Identity Theft When Applying for Aid

source_blocks.source_text_en: Identity theft can occur when criminals access personal data such as names, Social Security numbers, and bank and credit card information. Using the stolen data, the criminal can illegally obtain credit cards, set up mobile phone accounts, and more. Take the following precautions to reduce your risk when applying for federal student aid:
source_blocks.text: Identity theft can occur when criminals access personal data such as names, Social Security numbers, and bank and credit card information. Using the stolen data, the criminal can illegally obtain credit cards, set up mobile phone accounts, and more. Take the following precautions to reduce your risk when applying for federal student aid:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Apply for federal student aid by filling out the FAFSA form at the official website or on our myStudentAid mobile app. After completing the FAFSA form online, exit the application and close the browser; any cookies created during your session will be deleted automatically. Don t tell anyone your FSA ID username or password, even if that person is helping you fill out the FAFSA form. Review your financial aid offers and keep track of the amounts you applied for and received. Never give personal information over the phone or internet unless you made the contact. If you have questions about an offer of aid or about your student loan account, ask your college or contact the Federal Student Aid Information Center. We securely store your information within the National Student Loan Data System (NSLDS) database and provide access to it when you log in to your account. However, if you complete or even request a student loan application from a lender, you may be granting the lender permission to access your file. Before providing personal information to an organization, review its privacy policy. Keep receipts and documents (for example, credit applications or offers, checks and bank statements) with personal information in a safe place, and shred them when you are finished with them. Keep your purse or wallet safe at all times; store it and other items containing personal information in a secure place at home, especially if you have roommates. Immediately report all lost or stolen identification to the issuer (e.g., the credit card company or your state s Department of Motor Vehicles) and to the police, if appropriate.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How ED Keeps Your Information Safe
source_blocks.text: How ED Keeps Your Information Safe

source_blocks.source_text_en: We care about the privacy of your personal information. The information you share with us via our secure websites goes through a process called encryption. Encryption uses a mathematical formula to scramble your data into a format that is unreadable to a hacker. This is how we do our part to keep your information safe but you need to do yours as well.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Identify a Student Loan Scam
source_blocks.text: Identify a Student Loan Scam

source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrowers have reported receiving phone calls, emails, letters, and/or texts offering them relief from their federal student loans or warning them that student loan forgiveness programs would end soon. Usually, the so-called student loan debt relief companies offering these types of services don t offer any relief at all. Often they re just fraudsters who are after your money.
source_blocks.text: Borrowers have reported receiving phone calls, emails, letters, and/or texts offering them relief from their federal student loans or warning them that student loan forgiveness programs would end soon. Usually, the so-called student loan debt relief companies offering these types of services don t offer any relief at all. Often they re just fraudsters who are after your money.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here are some examples of the false claims made in these communications:
source_blocks.text: Here are some examples of the false claims made in these communications:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Act immediately to qualify for student loan forgiveness before the program is discontinued. You are now eligible to receive benefits from a recent law that has passed regarding federal student loans, including total forgiveness in some circumstances. Federal student loan programs may change. Please call within 30 days of receiving this notice. Your student loans may qualify for complete discharge. Enrollments are first come, first served. Student alerts: Your student loan is flagged for forgiveness pending verification. Call now!
source_blocks.text: Act immediately to qualify for student loan forgiveness before the program is discontinued. You are now eligible to receive benefits from a recent law that has passed regarding federal student loans, including total forgiveness in some circumstances. Federal student loan programs may change. Please call within 30 days of receiving this notice. Your student loans may qualify for complete discharge. Enrollments are first come, first served. Student alerts: Your student loan is flagged for forgiveness pending verification. Call now!

source_blocks.source_text_en: Communications using this type of aggressive advertising to lure borrowers are NOT coming from the U.S. Department of Education (ED) or its partners.
source_blocks.text: Communications using this type of aggressive advertising to lure borrowers are NOT coming from the U.S. Department of Education (ED) or its partners.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here are some signs to help you identify a scam by a student loan debt relief company:
source_blocks.text: Here are some signs to help you identify a scam by a student loan debt relief company:

source_blocks.source_text_en: They require you to pay up-front or monthly fees for help. It is illegal to charge an up-front fee for this type of service, so if a company requires a fee before they actually do anything, that s a huge red flag especially if they try to get your credit card number or bank account information. In some cases, they may even step in and ask you to pay them directly, promising to pay your servicer each month when your bill comes due. Free assistance is available through your federal loan servicer. They promise immediate and total loan forgiveness or cancellation. No one can promise immediate and total loan forgiveness or cancellation. Most government forgiveness programs require many years of qualifying payments and/or employment in certain fields before your loans can be forgiven. Also, student loan debt relief companies do not have the ability to negotiate with your federal loan servicer for a special deal under the federal student loan programs. Payment levels under income-driven payment plans are set by federal law. They ask for your FSA ID username and password. ED or its partners will never ask you for your FSA ID password. Your FSA ID is used to sign legally binding documents electronically. It has the same legal status as a written signature. Do not give your FSA ID password to anyone or allow anyone to create an FSA ID for you. If a company has access to your FSA ID information, they can make changes to your account without your permission. They ask you to sign and submit a third-party authorization form or a power of attorney. These are written agreements giving the third party legal permission to talk directly to your federal loan servicer and make decisions on your behalf. Debt relief companies often want these authorizations so that they can change your account and contact information, so you don t realize that they aren t actually paying your monthly student loan bill. They claim that their offer is limited and encourage you to act immediately. Student loan debt relief companies often try to instill a sense of urgency by citing new laws or discontinuing programs as a way to encourage borrowers to contact them immediately. While there are some deadlines you need to meet regarding your student loans for instance, if you re paying under an income-driven repayment plan, you need to recertify annually our programs are limited only by the eligibility requirements. Their communications contain spelling and grammatical errors. While many of the communications sent out by these companies look very formal (for example, fold-and-tear letters with safety patterns), they often contain spelling and grammatical errors. If you notice unusual capitalization, improper grammar, or incomplete sentences in the communication you receive, that s likely a red flag that the company is not affiliated with ED.
source_blocks.text: They require you to pay up-front or monthly fees for help. It is illegal to charge an up-front fee for this type of service, so if a company requires a fee before they actually do anything, that s a huge red flag especially if they try to get your credit card number or bank account information. In some cases, they may even step in and ask you to pay them directly, promising to pay your servicer each month when your bill comes due. Free assistance is available through your federal loan servicer. They promise immediate and total loan forgiveness or cancellation. No one can promise immediate and total loan forgiveness or cancellation. Most government forgiveness programs require many years of qualifying payments and/or employment in certain fields before your loans can be forgiven. Also, student loan debt relief companies do not have the ability to negotiate with your federal loan servicer for a special deal under the federal student loan programs. Payment levels under income-driven payment plans are set by federal law. They ask for your FSA ID username and password. ED or its partners will never ask you for your FSA ID password. Your FSA ID is used to sign legally binding documents electronically. It has the same legal status as a written signature. Do not give your FSA ID password to anyone or allow anyone to create an FSA ID for you. If a company has access to your FSA ID information, they can make changes to your account without your permission. They ask you to sign and submit a third-party authorization form or a power of attorney. These are written agreements giving the third party legal permission to talk directly to your federal loan servicer and make decisions on your behalf. Debt relief companies often want these authorizations so that they can change your account and contact information, so you don t realize that they aren t actually paying your monthly student loan bill. They claim that their offer is limited and encourage you to act immediately. Student loan debt relief companies often try to instill a sense of urgency by citing new laws or discontinuing programs as a way to encourage borrowers to contact them immediately. While there are some deadlines you need to meet regarding your student loans for instance, if you re paying under an income-driven repayment plan, you need to recertify annually our programs are limited only by the eligibility requirements. Their communications contain spelling and grammatical errors. While many of the communications sent out by these companies look very formal (for example, fold-and-tear letters with safety patterns), they often contain spelling and grammatical errors. If you notice unusual capitalization, improper grammar, or incomplete sentences in the communication you receive, that s likely a red flag that the company is not affiliated with ED.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How Student Loan Debt Relief Companies Work
source_blocks.text: How Student Loan Debt Relief Companies Work

source_blocks.source_text_en: Student loan debt relief companies are private companies that provide (or claim to provide) student loan management services for a fee. Often these companies are charging for services you can easily manage yourself. They will say they can help reduce your monthly payment or get your loans forgiven, but after you pay, you might be worse off. You might not get the promised help or your money back, and the company may have made changes to your loan repayment plan that you didn t authorize or want. If you stopped paying your loans, your credit could be damaged and your loan balances could balloon.
