source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrower Defense to Repayment | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 借款人抗辩还款 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrowers may be eligible for forgiveness of the federal student loans used to attend a school if that school misled them or engaged in other misconduct in violation of certain laws.
source_blocks.text: 如果学校误导借款人或在违反某些法律方面有其他不当行为，借款人可能符合免除用于就读该校的联邦学生贷款的条件。

source_blocks.source_text_en: This type of loan forgiveness is called borrower defense to repayment, sometimes abbreviated to borrower defense. Learn more in the sections below to see whether you may qualify.
source_blocks.text: 这种贷款免除称为借款人抗辩还款，有时简称为借款人抗辩。在以下部分了解更多信息，看看您是否符合资格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrower Defense Application
source_blocks.text: 借款人抗辩申请

source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrowers who attended Corinthian Colleges (Everest, Heald, and WyoTech) with a first date of attendance between July 1, 2010, and Sept. 30, 2014, and are seeking federal student loan forgiveness through borrower defense will complete a Corinthian-specific application. For more information about forgiveness of federal student loan(s) used to attend Corinthian Colleges, go to the Information about Debt Relief for Corinthian Colleges Students page.
source_blocks.text: 就读于科林斯学院（Everest、Heald 和 WyoTech）且首次入学日期在2010年7月1日至2014年9月30日之间，并寻求通过借款人抗辩获得联邦学生贷款免除的借款人，将填写一份针对科林斯学院的特定申请。有关用于就读科林斯学院的联邦学生贷款免除的更多信息，请访问“科林斯学院学生债务减免信息”页面。

source_blocks.source_text_en: All other borrowers applying for borrower defense MUST submit their application using one of the U.S. Department of Education (ED) borrower defense application forms provided in the sections below. Please read the instructions provided within the application before filling out the application form. Please note that the instructions also include information for parent PLUS borrowers.
source_blocks.text: 所有其他申请借款人抗辩的借款人必须使用以下部分提供的美国教育部（ED）借款人抗辩申请表之一提交申请。请在填写申请表前阅读申请中提供的说明。请注意，说明中还包括家长PLUS借款人的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To apply for federal student loan forgiveness based on borrower defense, complete an online application form. Within the online application form, you will be required to provide your signature digitally. It is helpful to include additional documentation as part of your application by uploading additional electronic documents (for example, scanned PDF documents). ED recommends you prepare the additional documentation prior to starting the application process.
source_blocks.text: 要基于借款人抗辩申请联邦学生贷款免除，请填写在线申请表。在在线申请表中，您需要以数字方式提供签名。通过上传额外的电子文档（例如，扫描的PDF文档）作为申请的一部分，有助于提供额外的证明材料。ED建议您在开始申请流程之前准备好额外的证明材料。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you choose to submit additional documents as part of your borrower defense application, the following types of documents are among those that may be helpful to your application:
source_blocks.text: 如果您选择提交额外文件作为借款人抗辩申请的一部分，以下类型的文件可能对您的申请有帮助：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Documentation to confirm the school for which you are applying for borrower defense, your program of study, and your dates of enrollment such as transcripts, enrollment agreements, and registration documents Promotional materials from the school Emails with school officials Your school s manual or course catalog
source_blocks.text: 用于确认您申请借款人抗辩的学校、学习课程和入学日期的文件，如成绩单、入学协议和注册文件 学校的宣传材料 与学校官员的电子邮件 您学校的手册或课程目录

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED and/or your federal student loan servicer(s) will contact you once the review of your application is complete to inform you of whether your application was successful or denied.
source_blocks.text: ED和/或您的联邦学生贷款服务机构将在您的申请审查完成后与您联系，告知您的申请是成功还是被拒绝。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To apply via email or physical mail, complete a fillable PDF application form, print it, and sign it (view a nonfillable HTML version of the application form). Send your completed form to the U.S. Department of Education by email to BorrowerDefense@ed.gov or by regular mail to U.S. Dept. of Education Borrower Defense to Repayment, P.O. Box 1854, Monticello, KY 42633. If you submit your PDF application by email, you are required to upload an electronic version of your signature. You can upload a picture file of your signature (for example, taken with a smart phone or digital camera). If you have additional documents that you would like to include as part of your emailed application, please include the documents with your email (for example, by attaching scanned PDF documents).
source_blocks.text: 要通过电子邮件或普通邮件申请，请填写可填写的PDF申请表，打印并签名（查看申请表的非可填写HTML版本）。将填好的表格通过电子邮件发送至BorrowerDefense@ed.gov，或通过普通邮件寄至U.S. Dept. of Education Borrower Defense to Repayment, P.O. Box 1854, Monticello, KY 42633。如果您通过电子邮件提交PDF申请，您需要上传电子版签名。您可以上传签名的图片文件（例如，用智能手机或数码相机拍摄的）。如果您有其他文件希望作为电子邮件申请的一部分包含，请将文件附在电子邮件中（例如，通过附加扫描的PDF文档）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED recommends you prepare the additional documentation prior to starting the application process.
source_blocks.text: ED建议您在开始申请流程之前准备好额外的证明材料。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Who Qualifies for Borrower Defense to Repayment Loan Forgiveness
source_blocks.text: 谁符合借款人抗辩还款贷款免除的资格

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under the law, you may be eligible for borrower defense to repayment forgiveness of the federal student loans that you took out to attend a school if that school misled you, or engaged in other misconduct in violation of certain state laws. Specifically, you may assert borrower defense by demonstrating that the school, through an act or omission, violated state law directly related to your federal student loan or to the educational services for which the loan was provided. You may be eligible for borrower defense regardless of whether your school closed or you are otherwise eligible for loan forgiveness under other laws.
source_blocks.text: 根据法律，如果学校误导您或违反某些州法律有其他不当行为，您可能符合免除用于就读该校的联邦学生贷款的借款人抗辩还款资格。具体来说，您可以通过证明学校通过作为或不作为违反了与您的联邦学生贷款或贷款所支付的教育服务直接相关的州法律来主张借款人抗辩。无论您的学校是否关闭，或者您是否根据其他法律有资格获得贷款免除，您都可能符合借款人抗辩的资格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are eligible to receive federal student loan forgiveness, you may be able to have all or part of your outstanding federal student loan debt forgiven, and you also may be reimbursed for amounts you have already paid on those loans.
source_blocks.text: 如果您有资格获得联邦学生贷款免除，您可能能够免除全部或部分未偿还的联邦学生贷款债务，并且您还可能获得已偿还这些贷款的金额的补偿。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You will only be eligible for this type of federal student loan forgiveness if your school s misleading activities or other misconduct directly relate to the loan or to the educational services for which the loan was provided. You will not be eligible for this type of forgiveness based on claims that are not directly related to your loan or the educational services provided by the school. For example, personal injury claims or claims based on allegations of harassment are not bases for a borrower defense application.
source_blocks.text: 只有当学校的误导活动或其他不当行为与贷款或贷款所支付的教育服务直接相关时，您才有资格获得此类联邦学生贷款免除。您将没有资格基于与您的贷款或学校提供的教育服务不直接相关的索赔获得此类免除。例如，人身伤害索赔或基于骚扰指控的索赔不能作为借款人抗辩申请的依据。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Please note that eligibility for federal student loan forgiveness is limited to federal student loans taken out for payment to the school relating to your borrower defense application. If you would like to apply for borrower defense against multiple schools that you attended and for which you took out federal student loans, you must submit separate applications for each school of attendance.
source_blocks.text: 请注意，联邦学生贷款免除的资格仅限于用于支付与您的借款人抗辩申请相关的学校费用的联邦学生贷款。如果您想针对您就读并借款的多所学校申请借款人抗辩，您必须为每所就读学校提交单独的申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For the purposes of borrower defense discharge only, we interpret the term Direct Loan in 34 CFR 685.206(c) to include Direct Consolidation loans. This interpretation enables borrowers with loans eligible for Direct Loan consolidation, including Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program loans or Federal Perkins Loans, to avail themselves of the borrower discharge process provided here by consolidating such loans into the Direct Loan Program.
source_blocks.text: 仅就借款人抗辩免除而言，我们将34 CFR 685.206(c)中的“直接贷款”解释为包括直接合并贷款。这一解释使拥有符合直接贷款合并条件的贷款（包括联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划贷款或联邦帕金斯贷款）的借款人能够通过将此类贷款合并到直接贷款计划中来利用此处提供的借款人免除流程。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Forbearance/Stopped Collections Status
source_blocks.text: 宽限/停止催收状态

source_blocks.source_text_en: Within the application, you may select to have your federal student loans placed into forbearance or stopped collections status while your application is reviewed by ED. If you choose for your loans to be placed into forbearance or stopped collections status, shortly after we receive your application, your loans will be placed in forbearance, and collections will cease on any of your loans that are in default while your application is evaluated.
source_blocks.text: 在申请中，您可以选择让您的联邦学生贷款在教育部审核您的申请期间进入宽限期或停止催收状态。如果您选择让您的贷款进入宽限期或停止催收状态，在我们收到您的申请后不久，您的贷款将被置于宽限期，并且任何处于违约状态的贷款的催收活动将在您的申请评估期间停止。

source_blocks.source_text_en: NOTE: If you do not select one of the forbearance or stopped collection options within the application, your federal student loans will be placed into forbearance or stopped collection, and ED will request forbearance or stopped collection for any commercially held Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program loans that you have currently. Interest will continue to accrue for the loans in forbearance while your application is evaluated.
source_blocks.text: 注意：如果您在申请中未选择宽限期或停止催收选项，您的联邦学生贷款将被置于宽限期或停止催收状态，教育部将请求对您目前持有的任何商业持有的联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划贷款进行宽限或停止催收。在您的申请评估期间，处于宽限期的贷款将继续产生利息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: More information on forbearance and stopped collections is available immediately below in the Common Questions and Answers Regarding Forbearance/Stopped Collections section.
source_blocks.text: 有关宽限期和停止催收的更多信息，请参见下方“关于宽限期/停止催收状态的常见问题与解答”部分。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Automatic Administrative Forbearance and Temporary 0% Interest as a Result of the COVID-19 National Emergency
source_blocks.text: 因COVID-19国家紧急状态而自动实施的行政宽限期和临时0%利率

source_blocks.source_text_en: To provide relief to student loan borrowers during the COVID-19 national emergency, federal student loan borrowers are automatically being placed in an administrative forbearance, which allows you to temporarily stop making your monthly loan payments. In addition, interest is being temporarily set at 0% on federal student loans. This 0% interest and suspension of payments will last from March 13, 2020, through Sept. 30, 2020, but you can still make payments if you choose.
source_blocks.text: 为了在COVID-19国家紧急状态期间为学生贷款借款人提供救济，联邦学生贷款借款人被自动置于行政宽限期，这允许您暂时停止每月贷款还款。此外，联邦学生贷款的利率被临时设定为0%。这一0%利率和暂停还款将从2020年3月13日持续到2020年9月30日，但如果您选择，您仍然可以还款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Have questions? Find out what loans qualify, and get additional information about the 0% interest period, administrative forbearance, and other student loan flexibilities due to the COVID-19 national emergency.
source_blocks.text: 有问题吗？了解哪些贷款符合条件，并获取有关0%利率期、行政宽限期以及因COVID-19国家紧急状态而提供的其他学生贷款灵活性的更多信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Common Questions and Answers Regarding Forbearance/Stopped Collections Status
source_blocks.text: 关于宽限期/停止催收状态的常见问题与解答

source_blocks.source_text_en: By completing and submitting a borrower defense application, you may have all of your federal student loans in repayment placed into forbearance status and have debt collections on any federal student loans in default stopped ( stopped collections status ) while ED reviews your application. However,please note interest will continue to accumulate on federal student loans regardless of what status they are in, including for subsidized loans. If your application for borrower defense is denied or partially approved, then when you are taken out of forbearance or stopped collections, the interest that accumulated will be added to the amount you owed when you entered forbearance or stopped collections, and the total amount you owe in the future may be higher.
source_blocks.text: 通过填写并提交借款人辩护申请，您可以让所有处于还款期的联邦学生贷款进入宽限期，并让任何处于违约状态的联邦学生贷款的债务催收停止（停止催收状态），而教育部将审核您的申请。但是，请注意，无论贷款处于何种状态，联邦学生贷款将继续累积利息，包括补贴贷款。如果您的借款人辩护申请被拒绝或部分批准，那么当您被解除宽限期或停止催收状态时，累积的利息将加到您进入宽限期或停止催收状态时所欠的金额上，您未来所欠的总金额可能会更高。

source_blocks.source_text_en: NOTE: You do not have to place your loans in forbearance or stopped collections to apply for borrower defense forgiveness. If you do not select one of the forbearance or stopped collection options within the application, your ED-held Federal Student Aid loans will automatically be placed into forbearance and stopped collections, and ED will request forbearance and debt collection to stop for any commercially held FFEL Program loans that you have currently (as applicable).
source_blocks.text: 注意：您不必将贷款置于宽限期或停止催收状态即可申请借款人辩护免除。如果您在申请中未选择宽限期或停止催收选项，您由教育部持有的联邦学生援助贷款将自动进入宽限期和停止催收状态，教育部将请求对您目前持有的任何商业持有的FFEL计划贷款（如适用）进行宽限和停止债务催收。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Please read the following question and answer (Q & A) section carefully before you choose whether you want the U.S. Department of Education to place your loans into forbearance or stopped collections.
source_blocks.text: 在您选择是否希望美国教育部将您的贷款置于宽限期或停止催收状态之前，请仔细阅读以下问答部分。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What does forbearance status mean?
source_blocks.text: 问：宽限期状态是什么意思？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. During any period that your federal student loans are in forbearance, you do not have to make payments on those loans, and the loans will not go into default. This will continue until the borrower defense review process of your application is completed. Your loan servicer will notify you when your federal student loan(s) have been placed into forbearance status. Until you receive that notice, you must continue to make payments.
source_blocks.text: 答：在您的联邦学生贷款处于宽限期的任何期间，您无需偿还这些贷款，并且贷款不会进入违约状态。这种情况将持续到您的借款人辩护审查过程完成。您的贷款服务商将在您的联邦学生贷款被置于宽限期状态时通知您。在您收到该通知之前，您必须继续还款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What does stopped collections status mean?
source_blocks.text: 问：停止催收状态是什么意思？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. During any period that your loans are in default, if you choose to enter stopped collections status, collections on your loans will stop. For federal student loans that are placed into stopped collections status, the federal government or debt collection companies will stop attempting to collect on the loan, including by not withholding money from your wages or income tax refunds. This will continue until the borrower defense review process of your application is completed.
source_blocks.text: 答：在您的贷款处于违约状态的任何期间，如果您选择进入停止催收状态，您的贷款催收将停止。对于被置于停止催收状态的联邦学生贷款，联邦政府或债务催收公司将停止尝试催收该贷款，包括不扣留您的工资或所得税退税。这种情况将持续到您的借款人辩护审查过程完成。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you previously defaulted on your federal student loan(s) and have entered a rehabilitation plan, please contact the collection agency that you have been working with to set up that plan in order to determine whether there may be any negative consequences if you choose to enter stopped collections status.
source_blocks.text: 如果您之前拖欠了联邦学生贷款并已进入康复计划，请联系您为制定该计划而合作的催收机构，以确定如果您选择进入停止催收状态是否可能产生任何负面后果。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Which of my federal student loans are eligible to go into forbearance or stopped collections status?
source_blocks.text: 问：我的哪些联邦学生贷款有资格进入宽限期或停止催收状态？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Initially, if you choose forbearance or stopped collections status, it will affect all of your federal student loans that are owned by ED and are being serviced by your federal student loan servicer, including loans that are not eligible for borrower defense loan forgiveness, such as (1) loans taken out to attend another institution, and (2) any loans you have for which you are not asserting borrower defense. If you select forbearance and you have commercially held FFEL Program loans, ED will request forbearance on your behalf.
source_blocks.text: 答：最初，如果您选择宽限期或停止催收状态，这将影响您所有由教育部拥有并由您的联邦学生贷款服务商服务的联邦学生贷款，包括不符合借款人辩护贷款免除资格的贷款，例如（1）为就读另一所学校而借的贷款，以及（2）您未主张借款人辩护的任何贷款。如果您选择宽限期并且您有商业持有的FFEL计划贷款，教育部将代表您请求宽限期。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Can I remove some or all of my federal student loans from forbearance or stopped collections status?
source_blocks.text: 问：我可以将我的一些或全部联邦学生贷款从暂缓还款或停止催收状态中移除吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. If you want the forbearance or stopped collections status to apply only to those federal student loans related to your borrower defense application, you must contact your loan servicer after you hear from your loan servicer and your servicer confirms the forbearance or stopped collection status. After your loans enter forbearance or stopped collection status, if at any time you want to remove all of your federal student loans from forbearance or stopped collections, you must also contact your loan servicer.
source_blocks.text: 答：如果您希望暂缓还款或停止催收状态仅适用于与您的借款人抗辩申请相关的联邦学生贷款，您必须在收到贷款服务机构的通知并确认暂缓还款或停止催收状态后，联系您的贷款服务机构。在您的贷款进入暂缓还款或停止催收状态后，如果您在任何时候想要将所有联邦学生贷款从暂缓还款或停止催收状态中移除，您也必须联系您的贷款服务机构。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Can I make payments on my federal student loans that are in forbearance or stopped collections?
source_blocks.text: 问：我可以对处于暂缓还款或停止催收状态的联邦学生贷款进行还款吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Yes. While your federal student loans are in forbearance or stopped collections, you are not required to pay your loans. However, you are allowed to make payments on any of your loans that are in forbearance or stopped collections, including payments for accrued interest. As noted above, interest will continue to accrue on all of these loans while they are in forbearance or stopped collections.
source_blocks.text: 答：可以。当您的联邦学生贷款处于暂缓还款或停止催收状态时，您无需偿还贷款。但是，您可以对处于暂缓还款或停止催收状态的任何贷款进行还款，包括支付应计利息。如上所述，在这些贷款处于暂缓还款或停止催收状态期间，所有此类贷款的利息将继续累积。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What happens if my borrower defense application against the school is successful?
source_blocks.text: 问：如果我对学校的借款人抗辩申请成功，会发生什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Your federal student loans related to your application may be discharged partially or completely. If you receive a partial discharge, you will be responsible for repaying any amounts that are not discharged through borrower defense including any interest that accumulated. Also, at that time, the forbearance or stopped collections period for any of your other federal student loans will end. You will be responsible for repaying those other loans, if applicable, including interest that accrued during the forbearance or stopped collections period.
source_blocks.text: 答：与您的申请相关的联邦学生贷款可能会被部分或全部免除。如果您获得部分免除，您将负责偿还任何未通过借款人抗辩免除的金额，包括累积的任何利息。此外，届时，您其他任何联邦学生贷款的暂缓还款或停止催收期将结束。您将负责偿还这些其他贷款（如适用），包括在暂缓还款或停止催收期间累积的利息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What happens if my borrower defense application against the school is denied?
source_blocks.text: 问：如果我对学校的借款人抗辩申请被拒绝，会发生什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. You will not receive a discharge of any of your federal student loans and the forbearance or stopped collections period will end for all of your loans. You will be responsible for repaying these loans, including interest that accrued during the forbearance or stopped collections period.
source_blocks.text: 答：您将不会获得任何联邦学生贷款的免除，并且所有贷款的暂缓还款或停止催收期将结束。您将负责偿还这些贷款，包括在暂缓还款或停止催收期间累积的利息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. I believe I may be a member of the class that has been certified in the case, Manriquez v. DeVos, because my borrower defense application includes a claim that is based upon job placement rate misrepresentations made by a Corinthian Colleges school. What happens with my repayment status, and what should I do if I am in the wrong repayment status?
source_blocks.text: 问：我认为我可能是Manriquez诉DeVos案中已认证集体的一员，因为我的借款人抗辩申请包含基于科林斯学院学校所作就业安置率虚假陈述的索赔。我的还款状态会怎样，如果我处于错误的还款状态，我该怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. For more information about the Manriquez v. DeVos case and the class that has been certified in that case, go to the Information About Debt Relief for Corinthian Colleges Students page, under the Information on Pending Litigation for Students at Corinthian Colleges (Everest, Heald, and WyoTech) Under Borrower Defense to Repayment Rule section. The Frequently Asked Questions About Manriquez v. DeVos subsection provides additional information on how forbearance and stopped collections may apply to your situation due to the pending litigation and court injunction and on what to do if you have questions about your repayment status.
source_blocks.text: 答：有关Manriquez诉DeVos案及该案已认证集体的更多信息，请访问“科林斯学院学生债务减免信息”页面，在“根据借款人抗辩还款规则，针对科林斯学院（Everest、Heald和WyoTech）学生的未决诉讼信息”部分下。关于Manriquez诉DeVos的常见问题解答子部分提供了更多信息，说明由于未决诉讼和法院禁令，暂缓还款和停止催收可能如何适用于您的情况，以及如果您对自己的还款状态有疑问该怎么办。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Notifications Regarding Manriquez v. DeVos Lawsuit section on this page provides information about notifications ED began emailing and mailing to borrowers on Dec. 26, 2019.
source_blocks.text: 此页面上的“关于Manriquez诉DeVos诉讼的通知”部分提供了有关教育部于2019年12月26日开始通过电子邮件和邮寄方式向借款人发送通知的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Common Questions and Answers Regarding Borrower Defense Decision Notifications
source_blocks.text: 关于借款人抗辩决定通知的常见问题与解答

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. Department of Education (ED) notifies borrower defense applicants of ED s determination about borrower defense discharge eligibility. The notifications are emailed to borrowers.
source_blocks.text: 美国教育部（ED）通知借款人抗辩申请人有关教育部关于借款人抗辩免除资格的决定。通知通过电子邮件发送给借款人。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have questions about your notification email that aren t answered below, call our borrower defense hotline: 1-855-279-6207. Representatives are available Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern time (ET).
source_blocks.text: 如果您对通知电子邮件有疑问，但以下未解答，请拨打我们的借款人抗辩热线：1-855-279-6207。代表的工作时间为周一至周五东部时间上午8点至晚上8点。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. I received an email saying that my borrower defense claim is approved. Is this email legitimate?
source_blocks.text: 问：我收到一封电子邮件，说我的借款人抗辩申请已获批准。这封电子邮件是合法的吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Yes. ED completed its review of your application for a borrower defense discharge of your Direct Loans under the applicable borrower defense to repayment rules and determined that your claim associated with your enrollment (or your child s enrollment) at the school identified in that notification email is approved.
source_blocks.text: 答：是的。教育部已完成对您根据适用的借款人抗辩还款规则申请免除直接贷款的审查，并确定与您在该通知电子邮件中确定的学校入学（或您子女的入学）相关的索赔已获批准。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your borrower defense application was evaluated based on the applicable state law and the circumstances identified in your notification email.
source_blocks.text: 您的借款人抗辩申请是根据适用的州法律和您的通知电子邮件中确定的情况进行评估的。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your notification email identified the percentage of the total amount of the Direct Loans you took out to pay for your program that will be discharged. You should receive notification of your discharge from your federal loan servicer within 90 120 days after you received your notification email.
source_blocks.text: 您的通知电子邮件确定了您为支付课程费用而获得的直接贷款总额中将被免除的百分比。您应在收到通知电子邮件后的90至120天内收到联邦贷款服务机构关于免除的通知。

source_blocks.source_text_en: As explained in the What happens next? section of your email notification, wait to receive notification of your discharge from your federal loan servicer.
source_blocks.text: 正如您的电子邮件通知中的“后续步骤”部分所述，请等待收到您的联邦贷款服务机构的解除贷款通知。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Does the borrower defense discharge apply to all loans I took out to pay for my program?
source_blocks.text: 问：借款人抗辩解除是否适用于我为了支付我的专业课程而借的所有贷款？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. No. This borrower defense discharge applies only to your Direct Loans. This borrower defense discharge does not apply to private student loans or other loans you may have received from programs administered by federal or state agencies, including other programs administered by ED.
source_blocks.text: 答：不适用。此借款人抗辩解除仅适用于您的直接贷款。此借款人抗辩解除不适用于私人学生贷款或您可能从联邦或州机构管理的项目中获得的其他贷款，包括教育部管理的其他项目。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED will proceed with the applicable discharge of your Direct Loans. If some of your federal student loans are Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program loans and/or Federal Perkins Loan Program loans, they are not eligible for discharge under the Borrower Defense to Repayment law or regulations.
source_blocks.text: 教育部将着手对您的直接贷款进行适用的解除。如果您的一些联邦学生贷款是联邦家庭教育贷款计划贷款和/或联邦帕金斯贷款计划贷款，则这些贷款不符合根据借款人抗辩还款法律或法规进行解除的条件。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you want to have your borrower defense discharge apply to your FFEL and/or Federal Perkins loans, you can consolidate your loans into a Direct Consolidation Loan and obtain the discharge. To apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan, go to StudentAid.gov/app/launchConsolidation.action. Once you have your Direct Consolidation Loan, contact our borrower defense hotline at 1-855-279-6207 from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET on Monday through Friday to proceed with discharge.
source_blocks.text: 如果您希望您的借款人抗辩解除适用于您的联邦家庭教育贷款和/或联邦帕金斯贷款，您可以将您的贷款合并为直接合并贷款并获得解除。要申请直接合并贷款，请访问 StudentAid.gov/app/launchConsolidation.action。一旦您获得直接合并贷款，请在美国东部时间周一至周五上午8点至晚上8点拨打我们的借款人抗辩热线 1-855-279-6207，以继续进行解除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. How did ED determine my discharge percentage?
source_blocks.text: 问：教育部如何确定我的解除百分比？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. For approved borrower discharge claims, ED calculated the amount of borrower defense discharge relief by comparing the earnings of those who completed the same or a similar program at a borrower s school ( median program earnings ) to the earnings of those who completed the same or a similar program at other schools ( median comparison earnings ).
source_blocks.text: 答：对于已批准的借款人抗辩解除申请，教育部通过比较在借款人所在学校完成相同或类似专业课程的人员的收入（中位专业收入）与在其他学校完成相同或类似专业课程的人员的收入（中位比较收入），来计算借款人抗辩解除救济的金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Specifically, ED used a statistical tool called standard deviation to identify the range of program earnings that would qualify for loan relief, and then divided that range into quartiles to determine the amount of relief a borrower would be provided. If your program earnings exceeded the comparison earnings, then, even if you filed an approved claim, you will not receive a discharge unless your approved application is associated with Corinthian Colleges, Inc. (CCI). If your approved application is associated with CCI, you will receive at least a 10% discharge. The larger the negative gap between your program earnings and comparison earnings, the greater the amount of loan discharge you received.
source_blocks.text: 具体来说，教育部使用一种称为标准差的统计工具来确定有资格获得贷款减免的专业收入范围，然后将该范围划分为四分位数，以确定借款人将获得的救济金额。如果您的专业收入超过了比较收入，那么即使您提交了已批准的申请，您也不会获得解除，除非您已批准的申请与科林斯学院有关。如果您已批准的申请与科林斯学院有关，您将获得至少10%的解除。您的专业收入与比较收入之间的负差距越大，您获得的贷款解除金额就越大。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Borrower Defense Partial Relief Methodology tables used by ED to determine relief percentages are provided for your reference. When viewing the earnings charts, note the following:
source_blocks.text: 教育部用于确定救济百分比的《借款人抗辩部分救济方法》表格供您参考。查看收入图表时，请注意以下几点：

source_blocks.source_text_en: No Data Available appears when there was no data available to complete a calculation. The wording under Program Name may not match exactly to the program name used by your school. There can be slight wording differences in the program name used by the school and the program name shown in the earnings chart. The word Diploma under the Credential column, means the same as Certificate Program, which is often used by schools.
source_blocks.text: 当没有可用于完成计算的数据时，会显示“无可用数据”。 “专业名称”下的措辞可能与您学校使用的专业名称不完全一致。学校使用的专业名称与收入图表中显示的专业名称可能存在细微的措辞差异。 “证书”列下的“文凭”一词与学校经常使用的“证书课程”含义相同。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Will prior payments be refunded after my discharge is applied?
source_blocks.text: 问：在应用我的解除后，之前的付款会被退还吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. A time limitation applies on receiving a refund of payments made on your federal student loans when a borrower defense claim is approved. We will inform your loan servicer whether you filed your borrower defense to repayment application within the applicable number of years of separating from (leaving) your school.
source_blocks.text: 答：当借款人抗辩申请获得批准时，关于收到联邦学生贷款付款退款存在时间限制。我们将告知您的贷款服务机构，您是否在离开学校的适用年限内提交了借款人抗辩还款申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: One of two things will happen.
source_blocks.text: 将发生以下两种情况之一。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you filed your application within the applicable limitation period and your loan payments exceed the amount owed after your discharge is applied, you will be eligible for a refund of payments. Your loan servicer will apply the borrower defense discharge to your student loan account and then determine whether you still have an outstanding amount (balance) due on any Direct Loans. If a balance remains on your account after your discharge is applied, your servicer will apply any prior payments made on the discharged loans first to the remaining balance of your discharged loans and then to the balance of other Direct Loans on your account. If no balance remains on your account, your servicer will return the refund amount to you. If you filed your application outside the applicable limitation period or your loan payments are less than the amount owed after your discharge is applied, you will not be eligible for a refund of payments. Your loan servicer will not apply any prior payments made on the discharged loans or return any refund amount to you.
source_blocks.text: 如果您在适用的限制期内提交了申请，并且您的贷款付款超过了应用解除后所欠的金额，您将有资格获得付款退款。您的贷款服务机构将把借款人抗辩解除应用于您的学生贷款账户，然后确定您是否仍有任何直接贷款的未偿余额。如果在应用解除后您的账户仍有余额，您的服务机构将首先将您对已解除贷款所做的任何先前付款应用于已解除贷款的剩余余额，然后应用于您账户上其他直接贷款的余额。如果您的账户没有余额，您的服务机构将把退款金额退还给您。 如果您在适用的限制期之外提交了申请，或者您的贷款付款少于应用解除后所欠的金额，您将没有资格获得付款退款。您的贷款服务机构将不会应用您对已解除贷款所做的任何先前付款，也不会向您退还任何退款金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your loan servicer will let you know if you are eligible or ineligible for a refund of payments.
source_blocks.text: 您的贷款服务机构将告知您是否有资格获得付款退款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Will interest be waived in addition to my discharge?
source_blocks.text: 问：除了解除之外，利息也会被免除吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. For borrower defense applications received by ED on or before Jan. 1, 2020, ED will waive interest on the federal student loans that it holds for the period between the date you submitted your borrower defense application and the date of your notification email. ED is waiving interest in these cases because of the extended period of time it took to review claims.
source_blocks.text: 答：对于教育部在2020年1月1日或之前收到的借款人抗辩申请，教育部将免除其持有的联邦学生贷款在您提交借款人抗辩申请之日与您收到通知电子邮件之日之间的利息。教育部在这些情况下免除利息，是因为审查申请花费了较长时间。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your federal loan servicer will let you know what your remaining balance is after the interest waiver has been applied.
source_blocks.text: 您的联邦贷款服务机构将在应用利息免除后告知您剩余余额是多少。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: If you receive a 100% discharge, you do not receive a separate interest waiver because your entire loan balance, including any interest, is discharged.
source_blocks.text: 注意：如果您获得100%的免除，您不会收到单独的利息豁免，因为您的全部贷款余额（包括任何利息）已被免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. I m a CCI borrower and received an email saying that my borrower defense claim is ineligible for relief. Is this email legitimate?
source_blocks.text: 问：我是CCI借款人，收到一封电子邮件，称我的借款人辩护索赔不符合救济条件。这封电子邮件是合法的吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Yes. ED completed its review of your application under the applicable Borrower Defense to Repayment regulations for discharge of your Direct Loans made in connection with your or your child s enrollment at a school operated by CCI, including Everest Institute, Everest College, Everest University, Heald College, and WyoTech. ED has determined that your application is ineligible for relief based on review of the facts of your claim and the regulatory criteria for relief; this decision means that your Direct Loans will not be discharged.
source_blocks.text: 答：是的。教育部已根据适用的《借款人辩护偿还条例》完成了对您申请的审查，以确定是否免除与您或您的子女在CCI运营的学校（包括Everest Institute、Everest College、Everest University、Heald College和WyoTech）就读相关的直接贷款。教育部根据对您索赔事实和救济监管标准的审查，确定您的申请不符合救济条件；这一决定意味着您的直接贷款将不会被免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED s reasons for this determination are as follows:
source_blocks.text: 教育部作出此决定的原因如下：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Applicable Law
source_blocks.text: 适用法律

source_blocks.source_text_en: For Direct Loans first disbursed prior to July 1, 2017, a borrower may be eligible for a discharge (forgiveness) of part or all of one or more Direct Loans if the borrower s school engaged in acts or omissions that would give rise to a cause of action against the school under applicable state law. See 455(h) of the Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended, 20 U.S.C. 1087e(h), and 34 CFR 685.206(c) and 685.222 (the Borrower Defense regulations). ED recognizes a borrower s defense to repayment of a Direct Loan only if the cause of action directly relates to the Direct Loan or to the school s provision of educational services for which the Direct Loan was provided. 34 CFR 685.206(c)(1), 685.222(a)(5); U.S. Department of Education, Notice of Interpretation, 60 Fed. Reg. 37,769 (July 21, 1995).
source_blocks.text: 对于2017年7月1日之前首次发放的直接贷款，如果借款人的学校从事了根据适用的州法律可能对学校提起诉讼的作为或不作为，借款人可能有资格获得部分或全部直接贷款的免除（宽恕）。参见经修订的《1965年高等教育法》第455(h)条，20 U.S.C. 1087e(h)，以及34 CFR 685.206(c)和685.222（借款人辩护条例）。只有当诉讼原因直接与直接贷款或学校提供教育服务（该直接贷款是为这些服务提供的）相关时，教育部才承认借款人对直接贷款偿还的辩护。34 CFR 685.206(c)(1), 685.222(a)(5)；美国教育部，解释通知，60 Fed. Reg. 37,769（1995年7月21日）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrower Defense Claims Based on CCI Job Placement Rates
source_blocks.text: 基于CCI就业安置率的借款人辩护索赔

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED has determined that students who first enrolled in certain programs at certain schools operated by CCI between 2010 and 2014 have borrower defense claims arising from the publication of misleading job placement rates for many of their programs of study and are eligible for a discharge of part or all of their loans under ED s Borrower Defense regulation. Lists of covered programs and time periods are available for Everest/WyoTech and Heald (the covered programs ).
source_blocks.text: 教育部已确定，在2010年至2014年间首次注册CCI运营的某些学校的某些课程的学生，因其许多学习课程发布了误导性的就业安置率而提出借款人辩护索赔，并有资格根据教育部的借款人辩护条例获得部分或全部贷款的免除。涵盖课程和时间段的列表可在Everest/WyoTech和Heald（涵盖课程）部分获得。

source_blocks.source_text_en: In order to have a successful borrower defense claim based on ED s CCI findings, you must have enrolled in one of the covered programs during a listed time period. ED has established a process for the review of borrower defense to repayment claims for job placement rates asserted by borrowers enrolled in the covered programs at CCI schools during the eligibility period. Each CCI borrower s application is reviewed under the same process to determine whether the borrower qualifies for borrower defense to payment relief based on a CCI school job placement rate claim.
source_blocks.text: 为了根据教育部的CCI调查结果提出成功的借款人辩护索赔，您必须在列出的时间段内注册了其中一个涵盖课程。教育部已建立了一个流程，用于审查在资格期内注册CCI学校涵盖课程的借款人基于就业安置率提出的借款人辩护偿还索赔。每位CCI借款人的申请都按照相同的流程进行审查，以确定借款人是否有资格基于CCI学校就业安置率索赔获得借款人辩护还款救济。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Why was my CCI application determined to be ineligible?
source_blocks.text: 问：为什么我的CCI申请被确定不符合资格？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. ED reviewed your application regarding the campuses you attended, the programs in which you enrolled, and the dates that you enrolled. ED also reviewed data from the National Student Loan Data System (NSLDS) database and, if available, school-provided data regarding your programs and enrollment dates, in addition to the enrollment information on any official school documents that you provided with your application. You includes your child if you are a Direct PLUS Loan borrower who requested a discharge for loans taken out to pay for a child s enrollment at a CCI-operated institution.
source_blocks.text: 答：教育部审查了您关于所就读校区、注册课程和注册日期的申请。教育部还审查了国家学生贷款数据系统（NSLDS）数据库中的数据，以及（如果可用）学校提供的关于您课程和注册日期的数据，以及您随申请提供的任何官方学校文件中的注册信息。如果您是直接PLUS贷款借款人，为支付子女在CCI运营机构的注册费用而申请免除贷款，则“您”包括您的子女。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Based on that review, ED has determined that you did not enroll in a covered program at a CCI school during the eligibility period. Either (a) the initial enrollment dates or programs you provided in your application fell outside the eligibility period for a covered program at one or more of the CCI campuses or (b) both NSLDS data and the school s data demonstrated that you were not enrolled in a covered program at one or more of the CCI schools during the eligibility period.
source_blocks.text: 基于该审查，教育部确定您未在资格期内注册CCI学校的涵盖课程。要么（a）您在申请中提供的初始注册日期或课程在CCI一个或多个校区的涵盖课程资格期之外，要么（b）NSLDS数据和学校数据均表明您在资格期内未在CCI一所或多所学校的涵盖课程中注册。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Moreover, your borrower defense application did not describe any other act or omission by the CCI schools that related to the making of your Direct Loans for enrollment or the provision of educational services for which the Direct Loan was made and that would be actionable under state law. Accordingly, ED has determined that your borrower defense to repayment application is ineligible and will not discharge your Direct Loans.
source_blocks.text: 此外，您的借款人辩护申请未描述CCI学校与您的直接贷款发放或提供教育服务（该直接贷款是为这些服务提供的）相关的任何其他作为或不作为，这些作为或不作为根据州法律可提起诉讼。因此，教育部确定您的借款人辩护偿还申请不符合资格，并且不会免除您的直接贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your borrower defense application was evaluated based on California state law and the circumstances identified in your notification email.
source_blocks.text: 您的借款人辩护申请是根据加利福尼亚州法律和您通知电子邮件中确定的情况进行评估的。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For borrower defense applications received by ED on or before Jan. 1, 2020, ED will waive interest on the federal student loans that it holds for the period between the date you submitted your borrower defense application and the date of your notification email. ED is waiving interest in these cases because of the extended period of time it took to review claims.
source_blocks.text: 对于教育部在2020年1月1日或之前收到的借款人辩护申请，教育部将免除其持有的联邦学生贷款在您提交借款人辩护申请之日与通知电子邮件日期之间的利息。教育部在这些情况下免除利息，是因为审查索赔花费了较长时间。

source_blocks.source_text_en: As explained in the What should I do now? section of your email notification, wait to receive notification from your federal loan servicer.
source_blocks.text: 如您电子邮件通知中的“我现在应该做什么？”部分所述，请等待您的联邦贷款服务机构的通知。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you disagree with this decision, you can ask ED to reconsider your borrower defense application.
source_blocks.text: 如果您不同意此决定，您可以要求教育部重新考虑您的借款人辩护申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. I m a non-CCI borrower and received an email saying that my borrower defense claim is ineligible for relief. Is this email legitimate?
source_blocks.text: 问：我是非CCI借款人，收到一封电子邮件，称我的借款人辩护索赔不符合救济条件。这封电子邮件是合法的吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Yes. ED completed its review of your application under the applicable Borrower Defense to Repayment regulations for discharge of your Direct Loans made in connection with your or your child s enrollment at the school identified in that notification email. ED has determined that your application is ineligible for relief based on review of the facts of your claim and the regulatory criteria for relief; this decision means that your Direct Loans will not be discharged.
source_blocks.text: A. 是的。教育部已根据适用的借款人防御还款规定，完成了对您申请的审查，以确定是否免除您或您的子女在该通知电子邮件中确定的学校就读期间所获得的直接贷款。教育部根据对您索赔事实的审查和救济的监管标准，确定您的申请不符合救济条件；这一决定意味着您的直接贷款将不会被免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Applicable Law
source_blocks.text: 适用法律

source_blocks.source_text_en: For Direct Loans first disbursed prior to July 1, 2017, a borrower may be eligible for a discharge (forgiveness) of part or all of one or more Direct Loans if the borrower s school engaged in acts or omissions that would give rise to a cause of action against the school under applicable state law. See 455(h) of the Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended, 20 U.S.C. 1087e(h), and 34 CFR 685.206(c) and 685.222 (the Borrower Defense regulations). ED recognizes a borrower s defense to repayment of a Direct Loan only if the cause of action directly relates to the Direct Loan or to the school s provision of educational services for which the Direct Loan was provided. 34 CFR 685.206(c)(1), 685.222(a)(5); U.S. Department of Education, Notice of Interpretation, 60 Fed. Reg. 37,769 (July 21, 1995).
source_blocks.text: 对于2017年7月1日之前首次发放的直接贷款，如果借款人的学校从事了根据适用的州法律可能对学校提起诉讼的作为或不作为，借款人可能有资格获得部分或全部直接贷款的免除（宽恕）。参见经修订的《1965年高等教育法》第455(h)条，20 U.S.C. 1087e(h)，以及34 CFR 685.206(c)和685.222（借款人防御规定）。教育部仅在诉讼原因直接与直接贷款或学校提供教育服务（该直接贷款是为这些服务提供的）相关时，才承认借款人对偿还直接贷款的防御。34 CFR 685.206(c)(1)，685.222(a)(5)；美国教育部，解释通知，60 Fed. Reg. 37,769（1995年7月21日）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Why was my non-CCI application determined to be ineligible?
source_blocks.text: 问：为什么我的非CCI申请被认定为不符合条件？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. ED reviewed your borrower defense claim based on any evidence submitted by you in support of your application, your loan data from the NSLDS database, as well as evidence gathered from the sources identified in your notification email. Each allegation of misconduct you claimed is identified in your email along with the reason that claim failed.
source_blocks.text: 答：教育部根据您提交的支持申请的任何证据、NSLDS数据库中您的贷款数据以及从您通知电子邮件中确定的来源收集的证据，审查了您的借款人防御索赔。您声称的每项不当行为指控均在您的电子邮件中列出，并附有该索赔失败的原因。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For borrower defense applications received by ED on or before Jan. 1, 2020, ED will waive interest on the federal student loans that it holds for the period between the date you submitted your borrower defense application and the date of your notification email. ED is waiving interest in these cases because of the extended period of time it took to review claims.
source_blocks.text: 对于教育部在2020年1月1日或之前收到的借款人防御申请，教育部将免除其在您提交借款人防御申请之日至通知电子邮件之日期间持有的联邦学生贷款的利息。教育部在这些案件中免除利息，是因为审查索赔花费了较长时间。

source_blocks.source_text_en: As explained in the What should I do now? section of your email notification, wait to receive notification from your federal loan servicer.
source_blocks.text: 如您通知电子邮件的“我现在应该做什么？”部分所述，请等待您的联邦贷款服务机构的通知。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you disagree with the percentage discharge determined under the formula or with other parts of this decision, you can ask ED to reconsider your borrower defense application.
source_blocks.text: 如果您不同意根据公式确定的免除百分比或本决定的其他部分，您可以要求教育部重新考虑您的借款人防御申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. I received more than one notification email about my borrower defense claim. Should this have happened?
source_blocks.text: 问：我收到了多封关于我的借款人防御索赔的通知电子邮件。这应该发生吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. There are two circumstances that would result in your receipt of more than one notification email.
source_blocks.text: 答：有两种情况会导致您收到多封通知电子邮件。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have two email addresses associated with your borrower defense application, ED sent a notification email to both addresses. If you have a borrower defense application that was approved and a different borrower defense application that was determined to be ineligible, ED sent you a notification email specific to each application.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的借款人防御申请关联了两个电子邮件地址，教育部会向两个地址发送通知电子邮件。 如果您有一份借款人防御申请被批准，而另一份不同的借款人防御申请被认定为不符合条件，教育部会针对每份申请分别发送通知电子邮件。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To check the notification emails you received, contact our borrower defense hotline at 1-855-279-6207 from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET on Monday through Friday.
source_blocks.text: 要检查您收到的通知电子邮件，请于周一至周五东部时间上午8点至晚上8点拨打我们的借款人防御热线1-855-279-6207。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What if I don t agree with the decision made regarding my borrower defense claim?
source_blocks.text: 问：如果我不同意关于我的借款人防御索赔的决定怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. If you disagree with ED s decision, you can ask ED to reconsider your borrower defense application. You can do so in one of two ways:
source_blocks.text: 答：如果您不同意教育部的决定，您可以要求教育部重新考虑您的借款人防御申请。您可以通过以下两种方式之一进行：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Send a new email with the subject line Request for Reconsideration to BorrowerDefense@ed.gov. Include the number that appears with the words Request for Reconsideration in the What if I don t agree with this decision? section of your notification email.
source_blocks.text: 发送一封新电子邮件，主题行注明“Request for Reconsideration”，发送至BorrowerDefense@ed.gov。请在邮件中包含您通知电子邮件中“如果我不同意此决定怎么办？”部分中出现的带有“Request for Reconsideration”字样的编号。

source_blocks.source_text_en: OR
source_blocks.text: 或

source_blocks.source_text_en: Mail your request to U.S. Department of Education, P.O. Box 1854, Monticello, KY 42633.
source_blocks.text: 将您的请求邮寄至：美国教育部，P.O. Box 1854, Monticello, KY 42633。

source_blocks.source_text_en: In your request for reconsideration, provide the following information:
source_blocks.text: 在您的重新考虑请求中，请提供以下信息：

source_blocks.source_text_en: What you think was decided incorrectly Why you believe the decision was incorrect Any evidence that you believe establishes that you are eligible for a different decision
source_blocks.text: 您认为哪些决定是错误的 为什么您认为该决定是错误的 您认为能够证明您有资格获得不同决定的任何证据

source_blocks.source_text_en: We will not accept any request for reconsideration that includes new allegations of misconduct by your school. If you include new allegations of misconduct by your school in your reconsideration request, the request will be rejected. You must file a new application regarding acts or omissions by your school other than those described in the borrower defense application identified in your notification email, by submitting an application. In the new application, you should explain in the relevant sections the basis for any new borrower defense claims and submit all supporting evidence.
source_blocks.text: 我们不会接受任何包含对您学校不当行为新指控的复审请求。如果您在复审请求中包含对您学校不当行为的新指控，该请求将被拒绝。您必须通过提交申请，就通知电子邮件中确定的借款人辩护申请中所述以外的学校行为或不作为提出新的申请。在新申请中，您应在相关部分说明任何新的借款人辩护索赔的依据，并提交所有支持证据。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED will not place your federal student loans into forbearance or stopped collection activity when you file a request for reconsideration. In addition, if your borrower defense claim was approved, ED will not begin its review of your request for reconsideration until your federal loan servicer notifies you that the discharge has been completed.
source_blocks.text: 当您提交复审请求时，教育部不会将您的联邦学生贷款置于宽限期或停止催收活动。此外，如果您的借款人辩护索赔已获批准，教育部将不会开始审查您的复审请求，直到您的联邦贷款服务机构通知您免除已完成。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For more information about reconsideration, contact our borrower defense hotline at 1-855-279-6207 from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET on Monday through Friday.
source_blocks.text: 有关复审的更多信息，请于周一至周五东部时间上午8点至晚上8点拨打借款人辩护热线1-855-279-6207。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Can I apply for borrower defense if I have additional allegations?
source_blocks.text: 问：如果我有额外的指控，我可以申请借款人辩护吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Yes. If you wish to file a new application regarding acts or omissions by your school other than those described in the borrower defense application identified in your notification email, submit an application. In the new application, you should explain in the relevant sections the basis for any new borrower defense claims and submit all supporting evidence.
source_blocks.text: 答：可以。如果您希望就通知电子邮件中确定的借款人辩护申请中所述以外的学校行为或不作为提交新的申请，请提交申请。在新申请中，您应在相关部分说明任何新的借款人辩护索赔的依据，并提交所有支持证据。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What should I know about repayment?
source_blocks.text: 问：关于还款，我应该了解什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. ED offers a variety of loan repayment options, including standard, graduated, and extended repayment plans, which base your payment on your loan balance and interest rate, as well as income driven repayment plans, which base your payment on your income. Remember, that while you can choose a repayment plan that lowers your monthly payment amount, it may also increase the amount of interest you pay over time which sometimes is significantly more. For more information about student loan repayment options, visit StudentAid.gov/plans.
source_blocks.text: 答：教育部提供多种贷款还款方案，包括标准、 Graduated 和延长还款计划，这些计划根据您的贷款余额和利率计算还款额，以及基于收入的还款计划，根据您的收入计算还款额。请记住，虽然您可以选择降低每月还款额的还款计划，但这也可能增加您随时间支付的利息总额，有时会显著增加。有关学生贷款还款方案的更多信息，请访问 StudentAid.gov/plans。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you don t begin or resume repayment when required, your loans may be placed into default. Defaulting on your loans subjects you to collection activity that includes
source_blocks.text: 如果您未按要求开始或恢复还款，您的贷款可能会被置于违约状态。贷款违约将使您面临催收活动，包括

source_blocks.source_text_en: administrative wage garnishment (taking money out of your pay); offset of state and federal payments you may be owed (taking money owed to you by the government); and litigation (taking legal action against you).
source_blocks.text: 行政工资扣押（从您的工资中扣除款项）； 抵消您可能有权获得的州和联邦付款（扣除政府欠您的款项）；以及 诉讼（对您采取法律行动）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrower Defense Discharge Earnings Information
source_blocks.text: 借款人辩护免除收入信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. Department of Education (ED) notifies borrower defense applicants about its review of their claims for discharge. Some claims are approved for discharge and other claims are determined to be ineligible for discharge. For approved borrower discharge claims, ED calculates the amount of borrower defense discharge relief by comparing the earnings of those who completed the same or a similar program at a borrower s school ( median program earnings ) to the earnings of those who completed the same or a similar program at other schools ( median comparison earnings ).
source_blocks.text: 美国教育部（ED）通知借款人辩护申请人其审查免除索赔的情况。一些索赔被批准免除，而其他索赔被确定为不符合免除条件。对于已批准的借款人免除索赔，ED通过比较借款人所在学校完成相同或类似课程者的收入（中位课程收入）与其他学校完成相同或类似课程者的收入（中位比较收入）来计算借款人辩护免除救济金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Specifically, ED uses a statistical tool called standard deviation to identify the range of program earnings that would qualify for loan relief, and then divides that range into quartiles to determine the amount of relief a borrower would be provided. If your program earnings exceed the comparison earnings, then, even if you filed an approved claim, you will not receive a discharge unless your approved application is associated with Corinthian Colleges, Inc. (CCI). If your approved application is associated with CCI, you will receive at least a 10% discharge. The larger the negative gap between your program earnings and comparison earnings, the greater the amount of loan discharge you receive.
source_blocks.text: 具体而言，ED使用称为标准差的统计工具来确定有资格获得贷款减免的课程收入范围，然后将该范围划分为四分位数，以确定借款人将获得的救济金额。如果您的课程收入超过比较收入，那么即使您提交的索赔已获批准，您也不会获得免除，除非您批准的申请与 Corinthian Colleges, Inc. (CCI) 相关。如果您批准的申请与 CCI 相关，您将获得至少10%的免除。您的课程收入与比较收入之间的负差距越大，您获得的贷款免除金额就越大。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Borrower Defense Partial Relief Methodology tables used by ED to determine relief percentages are provided for your reference. When viewing the earnings charts, note the following:
source_blocks.text: ED用于确定救济百分比的借款人辩护部分救济方法表供您参考。查看收入图表时，请注意以下事项：

source_blocks.source_text_en: No Data Available appears when there was no data available to complete a calculation. The wording under Program Name may not match exactly to the program name used by your school. There can be slight wording differences in the program name used by the school and the program name shown in the earnings chart. The word Diploma under the Credential column, means the same as Certificate Program, which is often used by schools.
source_blocks.text: 当没有可用于完成计算的数据时，会出现“无可用数据”。 课程名称下的措辞可能与您学校使用的课程名称不完全匹配。学校使用的课程名称与收入图表中显示的课程名称可能存在细微的措辞差异。 证书列下的“文凭”一词与学校经常使用的“证书课程”含义相同。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Notifications Regarding Sweet v. DeVos Lawsuit
source_blocks.text: 关于 Sweet v. DeVos 诉讼的通知

source_blocks.source_text_en: In June and early July 2020, the U.S. Department of Education (ED) will email and mail notifications about the Sweet v. DeVos lawsuit to borrower defense applicants who are potential members of the group of borrowers to whom the lawsuit applies to inform them that there is a proposed settlement of the lawsuit. The settlement will not become final until it is approved by the court as fair, adequate, and reasonable. The notification describes how borrowers legal rights may be affected by the settlement.
source_blocks.text: 2020年6月和7月初，美国教育部（ED）将通过电子邮件和邮件向借款人防御申请者发送关于Sweet诉DeVos诉讼的通知，这些申请者是该诉讼可能涉及的借款人群体成员，告知他们该诉讼有一项拟议和解方案。该和解方案在法院认定其公平、充分且合理并批准之前不会最终生效。通知描述了借款人的法律权利可能受到和解方案影响的方式。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED will send borrowers two notifications one by email and one by mail. The email notifications will be sent to borrowers from the email address noreply@studentaid.gov. The mailed notifications will be sent to borrowers in an envelope marked with Federal Student Aid s return address.
source_blocks.text: ED将向借款人发送两份通知，一份通过电子邮件，一份通过邮寄。电子邮件通知将从邮箱地址noreply@studentaid.gov发送给借款人。邮寄通知将装在标有联邦学生援助回信地址的信封中寄给借款人。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have questions about notifications you receive that aren t answered below, there s more information about the Sweet v. DeVos lawsuit on Class Counsel s website at predatorystudentlending.org/sweet-v-devos-class-members/.
source_blocks.text: 如果您对收到的通知有疑问，且以下未解答，可在班级律师网站predatorystudentlending.org/sweet-v-devos-class-members/上找到有关Sweet诉DeVos诉讼的更多信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. I received an email from noreply@studentaid.gov and/or a letter saying that I may be part of a group of borrowers under a lawsuit called Sweet v. DeVos. Are these communications legitimate?
source_blocks.text: 问：我收到了来自noreply@studentaid.gov的电子邮件和/或一封信，说我可能是Sweet诉DeVos诉讼中借款人群体的一员。这些通信是否合法？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Yes. The case Sweet v. DeVos, No. 19-cv-3674 (N.D. Cal.), is a lawsuit that was filed in a federal court in California by seven borrower defense applicants who represent, with certain exceptions, all borrowers with pending borrower defense applications as of April 7, 2020. The lawsuit challenges the fact that ED did not issue a final decision on any borrower defense applications from any school between June 2018 and December 2019.
source_blocks.text: 答：是的。Sweet诉DeVos案，案号19-cv-3674（北加州地区法院），是由七名借款人防御申请者在加利福尼亚州联邦法院提起的诉讼，他们代表（除某些例外情况外）截至2020年4月7日所有有待决借款人防御申请的借款人。该诉讼质疑ED在2018年6月至2019年12月期间未对任何学校的任何借款人防御申请作出最终决定的事实。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The lawsuit is ONLY about the fact that final decisions were not issued during that period of time, NOT whether those applications should result in loan cancellation or not. Now, both parties are proposing to settle this lawsuit. This proposed settlement is a compromise of disputed claims, and ED continues to deny that it has acted unlawfully.
source_blocks.text: 该诉讼仅涉及在该时间段内未作出最终决定的事实，而非这些申请是否应导致贷款取消。现在，双方提议和解此诉讼。此拟议和解是对争议索赔的折中，ED继续否认其行为违法。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Who is included in the group of people (the class ) represented by Sweet v. DeVos?
source_blocks.text: 问：Sweet诉DeVos案所代表的群体（“类别”）包括哪些人？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. The case Sweet v. DeVos includes all people who borrowed a Direct Loan or FFEL loan to pay for a program of higher education, who have asserted a borrower defense to repayment to the U.S. Department of Education, whose borrower defense has not been granted or denied on the merits, and who is not a class member in Manriquez v. DeVos, No. 17-cv-7210 (N.D. Cal.).
source_blocks.text: 答：Sweet诉DeVos案包括所有借款Direct Loan或FFEL贷款以支付高等教育课程的人，他们已向美国教育部提出借款人防御还款主张，其借款人防御主张尚未在实质上被批准或拒绝，且不是Manriquez诉DeVos案（案号17-cv-7210（北加州地区法院））的类别成员。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What are the terms of the proposed settlement?
source_blocks.text: 问：拟议和解的条款是什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. In the proposed settlement, ED agrees to resolve pending borrower defense applications of people who have borrower defense applications pending as of April 7, 2020, on the following terms:
source_blocks.text: 答：在拟议和解中，ED同意按以下条款解决截至2020年4月7日有待决借款人防御申请的人的借款人防御申请：

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED will approve or deny all Sweet class members pending borrower defense applications within 18 months of when the settlement agreement is approved by the court. ED will notify you of whether your claim was approved, whether you will receive any loan cancellation, and if so, how much loan cancellation you will receive. If your application is approved and you are entitled to any loan discharge, ED will complete the process of canceling some or all of your outstanding loan debt within 21 months of the date on which the settlement agreement is approved by the court. ED will provide your lawyers with information about its progress making borrower defense decisions every three months, including how many decisions ED has made, how many borrowers have received a loan discharge, and any new borrower defense findings ED has made. ED confirms, consistent with governing law and existing policies, that if you are in default, it will not take action to collect your debt, such as by garnishing your wages (that is, taking part of your paycheck) or taking portions of your tax refund, while your application is pending.
source_blocks.text: ED将在法院批准和解协议后18个月内批准或拒绝所有Sweet类别成员待决的借款人防御申请。ED将通知您您的索赔是否被批准，您是否会获得任何贷款取消，以及如果获得，您将获得多少贷款取消。 如果您的申请被批准且您有权获得任何贷款免除，ED将在法院批准和解协议之日起21个月内完成取消您部分或全部未偿贷款债务的过程。 ED将每三个月向您的律师提供其作出借款人防御决定进展的信息，包括ED已作出多少决定、多少借款人已获得贷款免除，以及ED作出的任何新的借款人防御认定。 ED确认，根据适用法律和现行政策，如果您违约，在您的申请待决期间，它不会采取行动收取您的债务，例如通过扣押您的工资（即从您的工资中扣除一部分）或扣留您的部分退税。

source_blocks.source_text_en: A copy of the proposed settlement is available online at predatorystudentlending.org/cases/sweet-v-devos.
source_blocks.text: 拟议和解的副本可在predatorystudentlending.org/cases/sweet-v-devos在线获取。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What will happen next?
source_blocks.text: 问：接下来会发生什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. The court will need to approve the proposed settlement before it becomes final. The court will hold a public hearing, called a fairness hearing, to decide if the proposed settlement is fair. The hearing will be held on Oct. 1, 2020, beginning at 8 a.m. Pacific time at the following address:
source_blocks.text: 答：法院需要批准拟议和解才能使其最终生效。法院将举行公开听证会，称为公平听证会，以决定拟议和解是否公平。听证会将于2020年10月1日上午8点（太平洋时间）在以下地址举行：

source_blocks.source_text_en: United States District Court Northern District of California 450 Golden Gate Avenue, Courtroom 12, 19th Floor San Francisco, CA 94102
source_blocks.text: 美国加利福尼亚北区联邦地区法院，地址：450 Golden Gate Avenue, Courtroom 12, 19th Floor, San Francisco, CA 94102

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What should I do in response to this notice?
source_blocks.text: 问：我应如何回应此通知？

source_blocks.source_text_en: IF YOU AGREE with the proposed settlement, you do not have to do anything. You have the right to attend the fairness hearing, at the time and place above, but you are not required to do so.
source_blocks.text: 如果您同意拟议和解，则无需采取任何行动。您有权在上述时间和地点出席公平听证会，但并非必须出席。

source_blocks.source_text_en: IF YOU DISAGREE WITH OR HAVE COMMENTS on the proposed settlement, you can write to the court or ask to speak at the hearing. You must do this by writing to the Clerk of the Court, at the following mailing address:
source_blocks.text: 如果您不同意拟议和解或有意见，您可以写信给法院或要求在听证会上发言。您必须通过写信给法院书记官，邮寄地址如下：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Clerk of the Court United States District Court Northern District of California 450 Golden Gate Avenue San Francisco, CA 94102
source_blocks.text: 美国加利福尼亚北区联邦地区法院法院书记官 450 Golden Gate Avenue San Francisco, CA 94102

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your written comments or request to speak at the fairness hearing must be postmarked by Aug. 20, 2020. The Clerk of the Court will provide copies of the written comments to the lawyers who brought the lawsuit.
source_blocks.text: 您的书面评论或在公平听证会上发言的请求必须在2020年8月20日前盖上邮戳。法院书记官将向提起诉讼的律师提供书面评论的副本。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. Who are the lawyers for the Sweet v. DeVos class and how can I contact them?
source_blocks.text: 问：Sweet v. DeVos 集体诉讼的律师是谁？我如何联系他们？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. The class is represented by the Legal Services Center at Harvard Law School and Housing & Economic Rights Advocates. If you have questions about this lawsuit or about the proposed settlement, please visit their Frequently Asked Questions page at predatorystudentlending.org/sweet-v-devos-class-members/, which also has contact information for the lawyers who brought the lawsuit.
source_blocks.text: 答：该集体由哈佛法学院法律服务中心和住房与经济权利倡导者代表。如果您对此诉讼或拟议和解有疑问，请访问他们在 predatorystudentlending.org/sweet-v-devos-class-members/ 的常见问题页面，该页面也提供了提起诉讼律师的联系信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Notifications Regarding Manriquez v. DeVos Lawsuit
source_blocks.text: 关于 Manriquez v. DeVos 诉讼的通知

source_blocks.source_text_en: Beginning Dec. 26, 2019, the U.S. Department of Education (ED) will email notifications about the Manriquez v. DeVos lawsuit to borrower defense applicants who are potential members of the group of borrowers to whom the lawsuit applies. The email notifications will be sent to borrowers from the email address noreply@studentaid.gov. For borrowers without a good email address, ED will mail notifications. The mailed notifications will be sent to borrowers in an envelope marked with Federal Student Aid s return address. Each borrower will receive either an emailed notification or a mailed notification.
source_blocks.text: 从2019年12月26日开始，美国教育部（ED）将向可能属于该诉讼适用借款人群体成员的借款人防御申请人发送关于 Manriquez v. DeVos 诉讼的电子邮件通知。电子邮件通知将从 noreply@studentaid.gov 发送给借款人。对于没有有效电子邮件地址的借款人，ED将邮寄通知。邮寄通知将装在带有联邦学生援助回信地址的信封中发送给借款人。每位借款人将收到电子邮件通知或邮寄通知。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have questions about notifications you receive that aren t answered below, there s more information about the Manriquez v. DeVos lawsuit on Class Counsel s website at harvardlaw.github.io/ppsldropdown/index.
source_blocks.text: 如果您对收到的通知有疑问，而以下未解答，可在集体律师网站 harvardlaw.github.io/ppsldropdown/index 上找到有关 Manriquez v. DeVos 诉讼的更多信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can contact the lawyers representing the covered class in the Manriquez v. DeVos lawsuit by emailing CMclass@law.harvard.edu or calling 617-390-2612.
source_blocks.text: 您可以通过发送电子邮件至 CMclass@law.harvard.edu 或致电 617-390-2612 联系代表 Manriquez v. DeVos 诉讼中覆盖集体的律师。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. I received an email from noreply@studentaid.gov saying that I may be part of a group of borrowers protected under a lawsuit called Manriquez v. DeVos. Is this email legitimate?
source_blocks.text: 问：我收到来自 noreply@studentaid.gov 的电子邮件，说我可能是 Manriquez v. DeVos 诉讼保护下的借款人群体的一部分。这封电子邮件合法吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Yes. You may be part of a group referred to as a class that is protected in certain ways because of a lawsuit called Manriquez v. DeVos.
source_blocks.text: 答：是的。您可能是一个被称为集体的群体的一部分，该群体因一项名为 Manriquez v. DeVos 的诉讼而在某些方面受到保护。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. Department of Education (ED) contacted you to make sure you know
source_blocks.text: 美国教育部（ED）联系您是为了确保您知道

source_blocks.source_text_en: how to determine if you are part of the class, what protections you have, that ED made mistakes recently that may have applied to you, what ED has done to fix the mistakes, and where to find more information about the lawsuit and your federal student loans.
source_blocks.text: 如何确定您是否属于该集体， 您拥有哪些保护， ED最近犯了一些可能适用于您的错误， ED已采取哪些措施来纠正这些错误，以及 在哪里可以找到有关该诉讼和您的联邦学生贷款的更多信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED contacted you because its records show that you borrowed one or more Direct Loans to attend (or for your child to attend) Heald College, Everest Institute, or WyoTech, operated by Corinthian Colleges, Inc.
source_blocks.text: ED联系您是因为其记录显示您借了一笔或多笔直接贷款，用于就读（或让您的孩子就读）由Corinthian Colleges, Inc.运营的Heald College、Everest Institute或WyoTech。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED s records also show that you asked to cancel some or all of your federal student loan debt because the school you attended (or that your child attended) did something wrong. This is known as a borrower defense application.
source_blocks.text: ED的记录还显示，您要求取消部分或全部联邦学生贷款债务，因为您就读（或您的孩子就读）的学校做错了事。这被称为借款人防御申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The intent of the email was to inform you generally about the lawsuit and give you contact information for obtaining additional information if needed.
source_blocks.text: 该电子邮件的目的是向您大致介绍该诉讼，并提供联系信息，以便您在需要时获取更多信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. How do I find out if I m part of the group/class and get more information?
source_blocks.text: 问：我如何知道我是否属于该群体/集体，并获取更多信息？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. To determine if you re a member of the class in the Manriquez v. DeVos lawsuit, visit the website set up by the class lawyers.
source_blocks.text: 答：要确定您是否是 Manriquez v. DeVos 诉讼中集体的成员，请访问集体律师设立的网站。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can contact the lawyers representing the covered class in the Manriquez v. DeVos lawsuit by emailing CMclass@law.harvard.edu or calling 617-390-2612.
source_blocks.text: 您可以通过发送电子邮件至 CMclass@law.harvard.edu 或致电 617-390-2612 联系代表 Manriquez v. DeVos 诉讼中覆盖集体的律师。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED will still review and decide your borrower defense even if you are not a member of the class.
source_blocks.text: 即使您不是集体诉讼的成员，教育部仍将审查并决定您的借款人辩护。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What protections does the class get?
source_blocks.text: 问：集体诉讼成员获得哪些保护？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. A June 2018 court order in the lawsuit stops ED from collecting federal student loan payments from members of the class until the lawsuit is over. Since June 2018, class members have not been required to make any payments on their loans related to Everest, Heald, or WyoTech.
source_blocks.text: 答：2018年6月的一项法院命令在诉讼结束前阻止教育部向集体成员收取联邦学生贷款付款。自2018年6月以来，集体成员无需对其与Everest、Heald或WyoTech相关的贷款进行任何付款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Loans that were not in default as of June 2018 should be placed into something called forbearance or another appropriate repayment status, such as an income-driven repayment plan that requires a payment of zero dollars or in-school deferment status. These statuses mean no payments are required, and your loans cannot go into default.
source_blocks.text: 截至2018年6月未违约的贷款应置于所谓的暂缓还款或其他适当的还款状态，例如要求每月还款为零美元的收入驱动还款计划或在校延期状态。这些状态意味着无需付款，您的贷款不会违约。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Loans that were in default as of June 2018 should be placed in what is known as a stopped collections status. This status means ED must stop collecting money from you, such as by taking part of your paycheck or tax refund.
source_blocks.text: 截至2018年6月已违约的贷款应置于所谓的停止催收状态。此状态意味着教育部必须停止向您收取款项，例如通过扣除您的部分工资或退税。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What mistakes have been made?
source_blocks.text: 问：出现了哪些错误？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. Many people in the class did not receive these protections. Specifically, since June 2018, ED and companies that work for ED mistakenly
source_blocks.text: 答：集体中的许多人未获得这些保护。具体而言，自2018年6月以来，教育部及其合作公司错误地

source_blocks.source_text_en: sent bills to students and parents for money they were not required to pay, collected money from students and parents that they were not required to pay, reduced tax refunds or paychecks from students and parents, and made negative reports to credit reporting agencies.
source_blocks.text: 向学生和家长发送了他们无需支付的账单， 收取了学生和家长无需支付的款项， 减少了学生和家长的退税或工资，以及 向信用报告机构做出了负面报告。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED sincerely regrets these mistakes.
source_blocks.text: 教育部对这些错误深表歉意。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q. What has ED done to fix its errors?
source_blocks.text: 问：教育部已采取哪些措施纠正错误？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A. ED has confirmed that potential class members are in the correct repayment status.
source_blocks.text: 答：教育部已确认潜在的集体成员处于正确的还款状态。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED is working with the Department of the Treasury to make sure that other payments that should not have been made, or that you would not have made otherwise, are given back.
source_blocks.text: 教育部正在与财政部合作，确保退还其他不应支付或您本不会支付的款项。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED has also worked to fix any bad credit reporting that came from its mistakes.
source_blocks.text: 教育部还努力修复因其错误导致的任何不良信用报告。

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED will work harder to make sure further mistakes do not happen. ED will review accounts of all potential people in the class to make sure there are no additional problems.
source_blocks.text: 教育部将更加努力确保不再发生进一步错误。教育部将审查所有潜在集体成员的账户，以确保没有其他问题。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Not sure what college or career school might be right for you?
source_blocks.text: 不确定哪所学院或职业学校适合你？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn about steps you can take to research possible colleges or career schools.
source_blocks.text: 了解你可以采取的步骤，研究可能的学院或职业学校。

source_blocks.source_text_en: While getting the right education and training will help you get a better-paying job, going to college or career school is a big investment in time, money, and effort. Make sure to take your time and research your options.
source_blocks.text: 虽然获得正确的教育和培训将帮助你找到薪水更高的工作，但上大学或职业学校在时间、金钱和精力上都是一项重大投资。确保你花时间研究你的选择。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I find the right college or career school for me?
source_blocks.text: 如何找到适合我的学院或职业学校？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Types of Schools
source_blocks.text: 学校类型

source_blocks.source_text_en: There is a wide array of schools available for higher education. Options include two- and four-year colleges and universities, vocational, trade, and career schools, online schools, and graduate schools. Different schools serve different purposes. Make sure you choose the type of school that helps you achieve your goals.
source_blocks.text: 高等教育有各种各样的学校可供选择。选项包括两年制和四年制学院和大学、职业技术学校、在线学校和研究生院。不同的学校服务于不同的目的。确保你选择有助于实现目标的学校类型。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Remember that financial assistance programs and requirements can vary from school to school. Plus, not all colleges and career schools participate in the federal student aid programs. Always check with a school to find out what financial aid is available there.
source_blocks.text: 请记住，经济援助计划和要求可能因学校而异。此外，并非所有学院和职业学校都参与联邦学生援助计划。始终向学校咨询，了解那里有哪些经济援助可用。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Assess Yourself
source_blocks.text: 自我评估

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understanding your career goals and options (and their earning potential) will help you find a college or career school that meets your needs. The Career Search will help you match your skills and interests with potential careers.
source_blocks.text: 了解你的职业目标和选择（及其收入潜力）将帮助你找到满足需求的学院或职业学校。职业搜索将帮助你将自己的技能和兴趣与潜在职业相匹配。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Use the College Search Tool
source_blocks.text: 使用学院搜索工具

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. Department of Education s college search tool, College Navigator, is a way to find colleges and career schools that may fit your needs. You can search for schools by location, degrees offered, programs and majors, tuition and fees, setting, size, and much more. College Navigator allows you to compare schools, save your session, and export your results into a spreadsheet.
source_blocks.text: 美国教育部的学院搜索工具 College Navigator 是找到可能适合你需求的学院和职业学校的一种方式。你可以按地点、提供的学位、课程和专业、学费和费用、环境、规模等搜索学校。College Navigator 允许你比较学校、保存会话并将结果导出到电子表格中。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Check Out Schools (In Person or Remotely)
source_blocks.text: 考察学校（亲自或远程）

source_blocks.source_text_en: To help you narrow down your college or career school options, try the following:
source_blocks.text: 为了帮助你缩小学院或职业学校的选择范围，请尝试以下方法：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Check out the school s website. Lots of colleges and career schools offer virtual tours, so you can still see the campus, even if you can t visit in person. Attend college fairs. College fairs give you the chance to talk to representatives from multiple colleges and career schools. For instance, you can visit the National Association for College Admission Counseling college fairs. A great way to get a feel for a school is to contact the school and schedule a visit, preferably while classes are in session. Be sure to bring a list of questions to ask. If you re in high school, ask your school counselor what information he or she has about the schools that interest you. Visit your state higher education agency s website to learn more about colleges and universities in your state.
source_blocks.text: 查看学校的网站。许多学院和职业学校提供虚拟参观，因此即使你不能亲自访问，你仍然可以看到校园。 参加大学博览会。大学博览会让你有机会与多所学院和职业学校的代表交谈。例如，你可以访问全国大学入学咨询协会的大学博览会。 了解学校的一个好方法是联系学校并安排参观，最好是在上课期间。一定要带上要问的问题清单。 如果你在高中，请向你的学校辅导员询问他或她关于你感兴趣的学校的信息。 访问你所在州的高等教育机构网站，了解更多关于你所在州的学院和大学的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your education is a major investment, so find out as much information as you can before you enroll. And because each school may offer different financial aid packages, you should consider applying to more than one school. For more information about what you should be doing to get ready for college, use our checklists for help.
source_blocks.text: 你的教育是一项重大投资，所以在入学前尽可能多地了解信息。而且因为每所学校可能提供不同的经济援助方案，你应该考虑申请多所学校。有关你应该为上大学做哪些准备的更多信息，请使用我们的清单寻求帮助。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What should I consider when comparing schools?
source_blocks.text: 比较学校时我应该考虑什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: As you research colleges and career schools, consider such factors as cost, location, accreditation, and more.
source_blocks.text: 在研究学院和职业学校时，要考虑成本、地点、认证等因素。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To find the information listed on this page for a specific school, check the school s website or search for the school using the U.S. Department of Education s college search tool, College Navigator.
source_blocks.text: 要查找此页面上列出的特定学校的信息，请查看学校网站或使用美国教育部的大学搜索工具 College Navigator 搜索该学校。

source_blocks.source_text_en: School Costs and Net Price
source_blocks.text: 学校费用与净价

source_blocks.source_text_en: School costs can be one of the most important factors in choosing potential colleges or career schools and costs can vary significantly from school to school. Learn about what is included in the cost of college and ways to reduce college costs. Any school that participates in the federal student aid programs is required to provide information on its cost of attendance and to offer a net price calculator on its website. Searching for a school s net price calculator is easy. This calculator will give you an idea of how much a program may cost after subtracting any financial aid. You can look up the cost and assess the value of colleges using the College Scorecard.
source_blocks.text: 学校费用可能是选择潜在学院或职业学校时最重要的因素之一，且各校费用差异可能很大。了解大学费用包含哪些内容以及降低大学费用的方法。 任何参与联邦学生资助项目的学校都必须提供其出勤费用信息，并在其网站上提供净价计算器。搜索学校的净价计算器很容易。该计算器将让您了解扣除任何经济资助后，某个项目可能花费多少。 您可以使用 College Scorecard 查询费用并评估大学的价值。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Financial Aid
source_blocks.text: 经济资助

source_blocks.source_text_en: Many students worry that tuition and the other costs of continuing their education will be out of reach. But don t let the potential costs stop you. Most students receive some kind of financial aid, and a few students even get a free ride, with all their costs covered. You should learn about financial aid including grants, scholarships, work-study, and loans. Always apply for all types of aid for which you might qualify, and meet all deadlines! Creating and managing a budget is a way to keep track of your income and expenses and save for your goals.
source_blocks.text: 许多学生担心学费和继续教育的其他费用会超出承受能力。但不要让潜在的费用阻止您。大多数学生都会获得某种形式的经济资助，少数学生甚至能获得全额资助，所有费用都被覆盖。您应该了解经济资助，包括助学金、奖学金、勤工助学和贷款。 始终申请您可能符合资格的所有类型的资助，并赶上所有截止日期！ 制定和管理预算是跟踪您的收入和支出并为您的目标储蓄的一种方式。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Admission Requirements
source_blocks.text: 入学要求

source_blocks.source_text_en: Different schools have different admission requirements. Learn exactly what a school requires by visiting its website or checking in with its admissions office. Many U.S. colleges require that students submit standardized test scores as part of their application packages. For most undergraduate programs, you ll have to take either the SAT or the ACT Test.
source_blocks.text: 不同学校有不同的入学要求。通过访问学校网站或咨询其招生办公室，确切了解学校的要求。 许多美国大学要求学生在申请材料中提交标准化考试成绩。对于大多数本科项目，您需要参加 SAT 或 ACT 考试。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Accreditation
source_blocks.text: 认证

source_blocks.source_text_en: An accredited school meets certain standards set by an independent agency. It helps ensure the training or education you get meets employer standards in a specific field. If you attend a school that isn t accredited, you might not be able to get any financial aid. Use our accreditation search page to check a particular school s standards or to find an accredited school in a particular field or location.
source_blocks.text: 经认证的学校符合独立机构设定的某些标准。这有助于确保您获得的培训或教育符合特定领域雇主的标准。如果您就读的学校未经认证，您可能无法获得任何经济资助。 使用我们的认证搜索页面来检查特定学校的标准，或查找特定领域或地点的经认证学校。

source_blocks.source_text_en: A diploma mill is an unaccredited school (or a business claiming to be a school) that awards a degree without requiring classwork that meets college-level standards. Some will send a diploma without you doing any work at all if you pay a fee. Others assign classwork that is so easy that your resulting degree is worthless, compared to a degree from an accredited school, and it won t help you get a good job. Learn more about diploma mills and how to avoid them.
source_blocks.text: 文凭工厂是一所未经认证的学校（或声称是学校的企业），它颁发学位时不要求达到大学水平标准的课程作业。有些学校只要您付费，甚至不需要您做任何工作就会寄送文凭。其他学校布置的课程作业非常容易，以至于您获得的学位与经认证学校的学位相比毫无价值，并且无法帮助您找到好工作。了解更多关于文凭工厂以及如何避免它们的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Enrollment Contracts
source_blocks.text: 入学合同

source_blocks.source_text_en: Read any school enrollment contract carefully before you sign it. The contract explains what the school will give you for your money. If a school representative promises you something (such as help finding a job) that s not in the contract, ask the representative to write that promise into the contract and have it signed and dated. A promise is usually not enforceable unless it s in writing.
source_blocks.text: 在签署任何学校入学合同之前，请仔细阅读。合同说明了学校将为您提供的服务以换取您的金钱。 如果学校代表向您承诺了合同中未包含的内容（例如帮助找工作），请要求该代表将该承诺写入合同，并签署和注明日期。承诺通常只有在书面形式下才可执行。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Refund Policies
source_blocks.text: 退款政策

source_blocks.source_text_en: Find out the school s tuition refund policy. If you enroll but never begin classes, you should get most of your money back. If you begin attending classes but leave before completing your course work, you might be able to get some of your money back. Also find out the school s return-of-aid policy. If you receive federal student aid (except for Federal Work-Study) and you withdraw from school, some of that money might have to be given back to the source by you or by your school. Even if you don t finish your course work, you ll have to repay the loan funds you received, minus any student loan funds your school has returned to the U.S. Department of Education. Learn more about repaying federal student loans.
source_blocks.text: 了解学校的学费退款政策。如果您已注册但从未开始上课，您应该获得大部分退款。如果您开始上课但在完成课程之前离开，您可能能够获得部分退款。 还要了解学校的资助返还政策。如果您获得联邦学生资助（联邦勤工助学除外）并退学，您或您的学校可能需要将部分资金返还给资助来源。 即使您未完成课程，您仍需偿还所收到的贷款资金，减去您的学校已返还给美国教育部的任何学生贷款资金。了解更多关于偿还联邦学生贷款的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Past Complaints and Reputation
source_blocks.text: 过往投诉与声誉

source_blocks.source_text_en: Just because a school participates in the federal student aid programs doesn t mean we ve endorsed the quality of education the school offers. To find out whether there have been any complaints about the school, contact your local Better Business Bureau , state higher education agency, or the consumer protection division of your state attorney general s office. Check with the agency that licenses or accredits the school to see whether it meets required standards.
source_blocks.text: 学校参与联邦学生资助项目并不意味着我们认可其提供的教育质量。 要了解是否有关于学校的投诉，请联系您当地的商业改进局、州高等教育机构或州总检察长办公室的消费者保护部门。向许可或认证学校的机构查询，以了解其是否符合要求的标准。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Useful Statistics
source_blocks.text: 有用的统计数据

source_blocks.source_text_en: Some numbers can help you evaluate schools.
source_blocks.text: 一些数字可以帮助您评估学校。
