source_blocks.source_text_en: Closed School Discharge | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 学校关闭贷款免除 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your school closes while you re enrolled or soon after you withdraw, you may be eligible for discharge of your federal student loan.
source_blocks.text: 如果你在学校关闭时正在就读，或在你退学后不久学校关闭，你可能符合资格获得联邦学生贷款的免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn about the eligibility requirements for discharge and how you can apply.
source_blocks.text: 了解免除的资格要求以及如何申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are certain eligibility requirements to qualify for a closed school discharge; you must apply to get a discharge.
source_blocks.text: 要符合学校关闭贷款免除的资格，有特定的要求；你必须申请才能获得免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: It s important for you to obtain your academic and financial aid records if your school closes since you might need those records if you plan to attend another school or want your student loans discharged.
source_blocks.text: 如果你的学校关闭，获取你的学业和财务援助记录很重要，因为如果你计划就读另一所学校或希望你的学生贷款被免除，你可能需要这些记录。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Discharge Criteria
source_blocks.text: 免除标准

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may be eligible for a 100 percent discharge of your William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program loans, Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program loans, or Federal Perkins Loans if you were unable to complete your program because your school closed, and if
source_blocks.text: 如果你因学校关闭而无法完成你的课程，并且符合以下条件，你可能符合资格获得威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款（直接贷款）计划贷款、联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划贷款或联邦帕金斯贷款的100%免除：

source_blocks.source_text_en: you were enrolled when your school closed; you were on an approved leave of absence when your school closed; or your school closed within 120 days after you withdrew.
source_blocks.text: 学校关闭时你正在就读； 学校关闭时你正在批准的休假期间；或 学校在你退学后120天内关闭。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You are not eligible for discharge of your loans if your school closes and any of the following is true:
source_blocks.text: 如果学校关闭且以下任何情况属实，你没有资格获得贷款免除：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Except in exceptional circumstances, you withdrew more than 120 days before the school closed. You are completing a comparable educational program at another school - through a teach-out, - by transferring academic credits or hours earned at the closed school to another school, - or by any other comparable means. You completed all the coursework for the program before the school closed, even if you did not receive a diploma or certificate.
source_blocks.text: 除非特殊情况，你在学校关闭前超过120天退学。 你正在另一所学校完成可比的教育课程 - 通过教学转移， - 通过将关闭学校获得的学分或学时转移到另一所学校， - 或通过任何其他可比方式。 你在学校关闭前完成了课程的所有 coursework，即使你没有获得文凭或证书。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Discharge Process
source_blocks.text: 免除流程

source_blocks.source_text_en: Contact your loan servicer about the application process for getting your loan discharged.
source_blocks.text: 联系你的贷款服务机构，了解申请贷款免除的流程。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Be sure to continue to make payments on your loan while your discharge application is being processed. Find out what happens if your loan discharge is approved. Find out what happens if your loan discharge is denied.
source_blocks.text: 在免除申请处理期间，务必继续偿还贷款。 了解如果你的贷款免除获得批准会发生什么。 了解如果你的贷款免除被拒绝会发生什么。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Automatic Closed School Discharge
source_blocks.text: 自动学校关闭贷款免除

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you meet the eligibility requirements for a closed school discharge of your loans obtained to attend a school that closed on or after Nov. 1, 2013, and you have not enrolled at another school that participates in the federal student aid programs within three years of the date your prior school closed, you will receive an automatic closed school discharge. This discharge will be initiated by the U.S. Department of Education (ED), and you will be notified by your loan servicer.
source_blocks.text: 如果你符合学校关闭贷款免除的资格要求，该贷款是为了就读于2013年11月1日或之后关闭的学校而获得的，并且你在原学校关闭之日起三年内未在另一所参与联邦学生援助计划的学校注册，你将获得自动学校关闭贷款免除。此免除将由美国教育部（ED）启动，你的贷款服务机构将通知你。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Although this closed school loan discharge is granted automatically after three years have passed since your school s closure, nothing prevents you from applying for and receiving a closed school discharge as soon as your school s official closure date is confirmed by ED. If you 1) attended a school that closed less than three years ago, 2) meet the eligibility requirements for a closed school discharge, and 3) want your loans discharged, contact your loan servicer about applying for a closed school discharge now instead of waiting for three years to receive an automatic closed school discharge.
source_blocks.text: 尽管在学校关闭三年后会自动授予此学校关闭贷款免除，但没有什么阻止你在ED确认学校官方关闭日期后立即申请并获得学校关闭贷款免除。如果你1）就读的学校在不到三年前关闭，2）符合学校关闭贷款免除的资格要求，并且3）希望你的贷款被免除，请立即联系你的贷款服务机构申请学校关闭贷款免除，而不是等待三年获得自动免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Q&A on Closed School Loan Discharges
source_blocks.text: 关于学校关闭贷款免除的问答

source_blocks.source_text_en: What benefits do I have by receiving a closed school loan discharge?
source_blocks.text: 获得学校关闭贷款免除对我有什么好处？

source_blocks.source_text_en: By receiving a closed school loan discharge,
source_blocks.text: 通过获得学校关闭贷款免除，

source_blocks.source_text_en: you have no further obligation to repay the loan, you will receive reimbursement of payments made voluntarily or through forced collection, and the record of the loan and all repayment history associated with the loan, including any adverse history, will be deleted from your credit report.
source_blocks.text: 您不再有义务偿还该贷款， 您将获得自愿支付或通过强制收款方式支付的款项的退款，并且 该贷款及与之相关的所有还款记录，包括任何不良记录，将从您的信用报告中删除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: I have nonfederal loans through private lenders. Can I get those loans discharged?
source_blocks.text: 我通过私人贷款机构获得了非联邦贷款。我可以免除这些贷款吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: You will need to contact the private lender that made the loan to get that information.
source_blocks.text: 您需要联系发放贷款的私人贷款机构以获取该信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: I received loans for several different programs of study at the same school, but I was unable to complete any of the programs or transfer credits from one program to another before the school closed. Can all the loans be discharged?
source_blocks.text: 我在同一所学校获得了几个不同学习项目的贷款，但在学校关闭前，我未能完成任何项目，也未能将学分从一个项目转到另一个项目。所有这些贷款都可以免除吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Only loans you received for a program that you were unable to complete because of the school s closure are eligible for discharge.
source_blocks.text: 只有您因学校关闭而无法完成的学习项目所获得的贷款才有资格免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For example, if you initially enrolled in Program A, but decided not to continue with that program and transferred to Program B, and you were then unable to complete Program B because the school closed, only loans you received for Program B could potentially be discharged.
source_blocks.text: 例如，如果您最初注册了项目A，但决定不继续该项目并转到了项目B，然后因学校关闭而无法完成项目B，那么只有您为项目B获得的贷款可能被免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: In the example, you would not be eligible for discharge of any loans you received for Program A, because the school s closure did not prevent you from completing that program.
source_blocks.text: 在该示例中，您没有资格免除为项目A获得的任何贷款，因为学校关闭并未阻止您完成该项目。

source_blocks.source_text_en: I did not complete the program, but I received a diploma or certificate. Does that make me ineligible for a loan discharge?
source_blocks.text: 我没有完成项目，但我获得了文凭或证书。这是否会使我没有资格获得贷款免除？

source_blocks.source_text_en: No. Before closing, some schools may issue a diploma or certificate to students who did not complete the program of study. If you did not complete your program of study, the fact that the school gave you a diploma or certificate does not disqualify you for discharge.
source_blocks.text: 不会。在关闭前，一些学校可能会向未完成学习项目的学生颁发文凭或证书。如果您未完成学习项目，学校向您颁发文凭或证书这一事实并不会使您失去免除资格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: I transferred credits from a closed school to a completely different program of study at a new school and completed the new program. Does that make me ineligible for discharge of the loans I received at the closed school?
source_blocks.text: 我将关闭学校的学分转到了新学校的一个完全不同的学习项目，并完成了新项目。这是否会使我没有资格免除在关闭学校获得的贷款？

source_blocks.source_text_en: No. Transfer of credits from the closed school to a completely different program of study at the new school does not disqualify you for discharge.
source_blocks.text: 不会。将关闭学校的学分转到新学校完全不同的学习项目并不会使您失去免除资格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: I attended a school that is now closed. Where can I obtain a copy of my academic transcript?
source_blocks.text: 我上了一所现已关闭的学校。我在哪里可以获得我的学业成绩单副本？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Contact the state licensing agency in the state where the school was located to find out if the state has the records.
source_blocks.text: 联系学校所在州的州许可机构，以了解该州是否保存有这些记录。

source_blocks.source_text_en: My school informed me that they have arranged a teach-out with neighboring schools. What is a teach-out?
source_blocks.text: 我的学校通知我，他们已经与邻近学校安排了教学衔接。什么是教学衔接？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A teach-out is a written agreement between schools that provides for the equitable treatment of students and a reasonable opportunity for students to complete their program of study if a school ceases to operate before all students have completed their program of study.
source_blocks.text: 教学衔接是学校之间签订的书面协议，规定如果学校在全体学生完成学习项目之前停止运营，将公平对待学生，并为学生提供合理的机会完成其学习项目。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If my school closes and I then enroll in a comparable program at another school, can I still receive a discharge of the loans I received at the closed school?
source_blocks.text: 如果我的学校关闭，然后我在另一所学校注册了类似的项目，我仍然可以获得在关闭学校所获贷款的免除吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: It depends. If you completed or are in the process of completing a comparable program of study at another school through a teach-out, by transferring academic credits or hours from the closed school, or by any other comparable means, you are not eligible for a closed school discharge.
source_blocks.text: 这取决于情况。如果您通过教学衔接、从关闭学校转移学分或学时，或通过任何其他类似方式，在另一所学校完成或正在完成类似的学习项目，则您没有资格获得学校关闭贷款免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: However, you may be eligible for discharge if you completed or are in the process of completing a comparable program at another school, but you did not participate in a teach-out, transfer credits or hours from the closed school, or benefit from the training you received at the closed school by any other comparable means, and if you otherwise meet the eligibility requirements for a closed school discharge.
source_blocks.text: 然而，如果您在另一所学校已完成或正在完成类似课程，但您未参与教学收尾、未从关闭学校转学分或学时，也未通过任何其他类似方式受益于在关闭学校所接受的培训，并且您在其他方面满足关闭学校贷款免除的资格要求，则您可能有资格获得贷款免除。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is a Co-Signer?
source_blocks.text: 什么是共同签署人？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A co-signer is the spouse of an applicant who initiated an Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request. As a co-signer you are not obligated to repay this loan by signing a borrower's IDR application.
source_blocks.text: 共同签署人是发起收入驱动还款计划请求的申请人的配偶。作为共同签署人，您不因签署借款人的IDR申请而有义务偿还此贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The IDR applicant should have provided you with a Reference Number/Co-sign Code. If you do not have the Reference Number/Co-sign Code, contact the IDR applicant. An e-mail containing the Reference Number/Co-sign Code was sent to him or her. The IDR applicant can also access the Reference Number/Co-sign Code by logging in to StudentAid.gov and clicking on the appropriate link.
source_blocks.text: IDR申请人应向您提供参考号/共同签署代码。如果您没有参考号/共同签署代码，请联系IDR申请人。包含参考号/共同签署代码的电子邮件已发送给他/她。IDR申请人也可以通过登录StudentAid.gov并点击相应链接来访问参考号/共同签署代码。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Directions to access the Reference Number/Co-sign Code

source_blocks.source_text_en: If the applicant completed an Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request that was not part of a Direct Consolidation Loan Application, he or she will click on "Income-Driven Repayment Plan Requests" under "My Loan Documents" to locate and provide you with the Reference Number you need. If the applicant completed an Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request as part of a Direct Consolidation Loan Application, he or she will click on "Direct Consolidation Loan Applications" under "My Loan Documents" to locate and provide you with the Co-sign Code you need.
source_blocks.text: 如果申请人完成的收入驱动还款计划请求不属于直接合并贷款申请的一部分，他/她将点击“我的贷款文件”下的“收入驱动还款计划请求”来查找并向您提供所需的参考号。 如果申请人完成的收入驱动还款计划请求是直接合并贷款申请的一部分，他/她将点击“我的贷款文件”下的“直接合并贷款申请”来查找并向您提供所需的共同签署代码。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you default on your federal student loan, the loan may be placed with a collection agency, which will then contact you to obtain payment.
source_blocks.text: If you default on your federal student loan, the loan may be placed with a collection agency, which will then contact you to obtain payment.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you default on your federal student loan, the entire balance of the loan (principal and interest) becomes immediately due. This is called acceleration. Once your loan is accelerated, you no longer have access to deferment or forbearance options or to a choice of repayment plans. In addition, if you do not make repayment arrangements with the holder of your loan the U.S. Department of Education (ED), a guaranty agency, or the school that made the loan and comply with the terms of the repayment arrangement, your loan holder may place your loan with a collection agency.
source_blocks.text: If you default on your federal student loan, the entire balance of the loan (principal and interest) becomes immediately due. This is called acceleration. Once your loan is accelerated, you no longer have access to deferment or forbearance options or to a choice of repayment plans. In addition, if you do not make repayment arrangements with the holder of your loan the U.S. Department of Education (ED), a guaranty agency, or the school that made the loan and comply with the terms of the repayment arrangement, your loan holder may place your loan with a collection agency.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your loan is placed with a collection agency, you will be responsible for costs incurred by your loan holder to get payment. These costs amount to 17.92% of your loan amount if your loan is held by ED. Other loan holders may charge a different amount. You should check with them to find out what it is.

These costs amount to 17.92% of your loan amount if your loan is held by ED. Other loan holders may charge a different amount. You should check with them to find out what it is.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The 17.92% is payable in addition to your outstanding principal balance, interest, and fees. For example, if you owe ED \$10,000, you ll owe an additional \$1,792 in collection fees once your loan goes to a collection agency, for a total of \$11,792:

source_blocks.source_text_en: The holder of your loan can take other actions to collect as well.
source_blocks.text: The holder of your loan can take other actions to collect as well.

source_blocks.source_text_en: ED currently contracts with several collection agencies to administer many of the collection activities of our accounts. Many guaranty agencies also contract with collection agencies for the same reason. Collection agency employees are trained to comply with the terms of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, which govern collection practices by debt collectors.
source_blocks.text: ED currently contracts with several collection agencies to administer many of the collection activities of our accounts. Many guaranty agencies also contract with collection agencies for the same reason. Collection agency employees are trained to comply with the terms of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, which govern collection practices by debt collectors.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your defaulted loan is placed with a private collection agency, you can expect the agency to first offer you the option of entering into a voluntary repayment agreement. If you do not agree to enter into a voluntary repayment agreement, or if you enter into a repayment agreement but don t continue making the payments you agreed to make, the collection agency will then begin the process of garnishing your wages (Learn about wage garnishment). If they are unable to garnish your wages (for example, because you are self-employed), they may recommend that ED refer your case to the U.S. Department of Justice for legal action. The Department of Justice may then sue you to collect on your defaulted loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: harassing or abusing any person in connection with the collection of a debt; making false, deceptive, or misleading claims in connection with the collection of a debt; and using unfair or unreasonable means to collect or attempt to collect any debt.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I know if the information on this page applies to me?
source_blocks.text: How do I know if the information on this page applies to me?

source_blocks.source_text_en: The information on this page mostly applies to borrowers who have defaulted loans that are held by ED.

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are three federal student loan programs administered by ED:
source_blocks.text: There are three federal student loan programs administered by ED:

source_blocks.source_text_en: the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program the Federal Perkins Loan Program
source_blocks.text: the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program the Federal Perkins Loan Program

source_blocks.source_text_en: All defaulted Direct Loans are held by ED. Defaulted FFEL Program loans may be held by ED or by a guaranty agency. Defaulted Federal Perkins Loans may be held by a school or by ED. ED s Default Resolution Group, at Federal Student Aid, oversees the collections process for all defaulted loans that are held by ED. Find out how to contact ED s Default Resolution Group.

Find out how to contact ED s Default Resolution Group.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you don t know who your loan holder is, you can find out by logging in to My Federal Student Aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How will my outstanding debt be collected?
source_blocks.text: How will my outstanding debt be collected?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you fail to make (and comply with) other arrangements to repay the debt, which could include entering into a loan rehabilitation agreement, ED can use a variety of methods to collect your defaulted federal student loan. Find out more about getting out of default.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Withholding Money From Your Tax Refund or Other Federal Payments (Treasury Offset)
source_blocks.text: Withholding Money From Your Tax Refund or Other Federal Payments (Treasury Offset)

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal law related to the collection of debts owed to the government requires ED to request that the U.S. Department of the Treasury withhold money from your federal income tax refunds, Social Security payments (including Social Security disability benefits), and other federal payments to be applied toward repayment of your defaulted federal student loan. This withholding is called Treasury offset.
source_blocks.text: Federal law related to the collection of debts owed to the government requires ED to request that the U.S. Department of the Treasury withhold money from your federal income tax refunds, Social Security payments (including Social Security disability benefits), and other federal payments to be applied toward repayment of your defaulted federal student loan. This withholding is called Treasury offset.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have a defaulted FFEL Program loan that is held by a guaranty agency, your state tax refunds may also be withheld and applied toward repayment of your loan. You may also lose your driver's license or other state-issued licenses.
source_blocks.text: If you have a defaulted FFEL Program loan that is held by a guaranty agency, your state tax refunds may also be withheld and applied toward repayment of your loan. You may also lose your driver's license or other state-issued licenses.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Before the offset begins, a notice of intent to offset will be sent to your last-known address to inform you that the offset is scheduled to begin in 65 days. The notice may only be sent once, and offsets will continue until your debt is paid or the default status is resolved.
source_blocks.text: Before the offset begins, a notice of intent to offset will be sent to your last-known address to inform you that the offset is scheduled to begin in 65 days. The notice may only be sent once, and offsets will continue until your debt is paid or the default status is resolved.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You do have the right to request a review of your account to prevent the offset from occurring. If you are successful, then your tax refund and other federal payments will not be offset, or the amount being offset may be reduced. If you are unsuccessful, then your tax refund and other federal payments will be offset.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your Social Security disability benefits are being withheld, the withholding of those benefits will be suspended if the Social Security Administration (SSA) makes a determination that you are totally disabled, with medical improvement not expected. However, if the SSA later converts your disability benefits to retirement benefits, the withholding of your Social Security benefits may resume without notice.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your loan holder can order your employer to withhold up to 15 percent of your disposable pay to collect your defaulted debt without taking you to court. This withholding ( garnishment ) continues until your defaulted loan is paid in full or removed from default.

source_blocks.source_text_en: With garnishment, you have the right to
source_blocks.text: With garnishment, you have the right to

source_blocks.source_text_en: be sent a notice that explains ED s intention to garnish your wages in 30 days, the nature and amount of your debt, your opportunity to inspect and copy records relating to your debt, your right to object to garnishment, and your option to avoid garnishment by voluntary repayment; be given an opportunity to enter into a written agreement under terms agreeable to ED to establish a voluntary repayment agreement; be given an opportunity for a hearing to present and obtain a ruling on - any objection you have to the existence, amount, or enforceability of the debt; - any objection that garnishment of 15 percent of your disposable pay would produce an extreme financial hardship; or - any objection stating that garnishment cannot be used at this time because you ve been employed for less than 12 months after having previously been involuntarily separated from employment; have the garnishment action withheld by filing a timely request for a hearing, until the hearing is completed and a decision issued; not be discharged from employment, refused employment, or subjected to disciplinary action due to the garnishment, and to seek redress in federal or state court if such action occurs; initiate any legal action against your employer if the employer discharges, refuses to hire, or takes disciplinary action against you based on the garnishment action; and not have any information provided to your employer regarding the garnishment other than what is necessary for the employer to comply with the withholding order.

source_blocks.source_text_en: One way to avoid garnishment of 15 percent of your disposable pay is to negotiate repayment terms acceptable to ED or the private collection agency and ensure that ED receives the first payment no later than 30 days from the date the garnishment notice was sent.

(All in-person hearings are held at one of the three regional offices: Atlanta, Chicago, or San Francisco. source_blocks.source_text_en: If my loan is placed with a collection agency, what other costs might I incur?
source_blocks.text: If my loan is placed with a collection agency, what other costs might I incur?

source_blocks.source_text_en: After you default, you are liable for the costs of collecting your defaulted federal student loans. The largest of these costs are usually the costs of placing your loan with a private collection agency. They amount to 17.92% of your outstanding balance, which includes principal, interest, and fees.
source_blocks.text: After you default, you are liable for the costs of collecting your defaulted federal student loans. The largest of these costs are usually the costs of placing your loan with a private collection agency. They amount to 17.92% of your outstanding balance, which includes principal, interest, and fees.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Before a defaulted loan is placed with a private collection agency, ED will explain what you can do to avoid both the assignment to a private collection agency and the reporting of default status to credit agencies.
source_blocks.text: Before a defaulted loan is placed with a private collection agency, ED will explain what you can do to avoid both the assignment to a private collection agency and the reporting of default status to credit agencies.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you do not enter into a repayment agreement for your defaulted federal student loans, ED will refer your loans to a private collection agency. Private collection agencies earn a commission for any payments you make on loans that ED has referred for collection. When you make a payment, the payment is first applied to the collection cost we charge (17.92% of your outstanding balance due), with the remainder of the payment being applied to interest and principal on your loan. This is one reason that defaulting on your federal student loans can significantly increase the total cost of your loans.

This is one reason that defaulting on your federal student loans can significantly increase the total cost of your loans.

source_blocks.source_text_en: On each billing statement, ED projects an estimate of the total amount needed to satisfy the debt on the date of the statement, including collection costs.

source_blocks.source_text_en: While the cost of placing your loan with a private collection agency is usually the largest collection cost you may face if you default, there may be other collection costs, such as Treasury offset processing fees and costs associated with potential civil litigation from the Department of Justice.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What should I do if I am contacted by someone who wants to charge me fees to get my federal student loan out of default?
source_blocks.text: What should I do if I am contacted by someone who wants to charge me fees to get my federal student loan out of default?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Contact the Default Resolution Group. If you are contacted by a company asking you to pay "enrollment," "subscription," or "maintenance" fees to help you get out of default, you should walk away. source_blocks.source_text_en: Figuring Out Net Price
source_blocks.text: Figuring Out Net Price

source_blocks.source_text_en: Follow these easy steps to figure out your net price, or net cost, for each school, and find out which school will be most affordable for you.
source_blocks.text: Follow these easy steps to figure out your net price, or net cost, for each school, and find out which school will be most affordable for you.

source_blocks.source_text_en: First, find the cost of attendance for your program on the aid offer. If the school doesn t list the cost of attendance on the aid offer, ask the financial aid office for this figure. Make sure it includes amounts you will pay to the school directly (such as tuition and fees) as well as other costs (such as living expenses, books and supplies, and transportation). Next, subtract the grant and scholarship amounts on your aid offer from the cost of attendance amount. Also subtract any savings you have available to put toward your school costs for the school year. The remaining amount is your net or out-of-pocket cost. Compare the net costs for the schools you are considering. The net cost is the amount you will have to pay out of your pocket, using earnings from work or loan funds that you borrow.

source_blocks.text: Master Promissory Note (MPN)

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Master Promissory Note (MPN) is a legal document in which you promise to repay your loan(s) and any accrued interest and fees to the U.S. Department of Education. It also explains the terms and conditions of your loan(s).You may receive more than one loan under an MPN over a period of up to 10 years to pay for your or your child s educational costs, as long as the school is authorized to use the MPN in this way and chooses to do so.The school will tell you which loans, if any, you are eligible to receive.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For purposes of applying for federal student aid, what s the difference between a dependent student and an independent student?
source_blocks.text: For purposes of applying for federal student aid, what s the difference between a dependent student and an independent student?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Read the definitions, find out who has to provide parent information on the FAFSA form, and learn what to do if you aren t in contact with your parents.
source_blocks.text: Read the definitions, find out who has to provide parent information on the FAFSA form, and learn what to do if you aren t in contact with your parents.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your dependency status determines whose information you must report on the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form.
source_blocks.text: Your dependency status determines whose information you must report on the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re a dependent student, you will report your and your parents information. If you re an independent student, you will report your own information (and, if you re married, your spouse s).
source_blocks.text: If you re a dependent student, you will report your and your parents information. If you re an independent student, you will report your own information (and, if you re married, your spouse s).

source_blocks.source_text_en: The federal student aid programs are based on the concept that it is primarily your and your family s responsibility to pay for your education. A dependent student is assumed to have the support of parents, so the parents information has to be assessed along with the student s, in order to get a full picture of the family s financial strength. If you re a dependent student, it doesn t mean your parents are required to pay anything toward your education; this is just a way of looking at everyone in a consistent manner.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your legal parents are married to each other, or are not married to each other and live together, you should report information about both of them on your FAFSA form. (Your legal parents are your biological or adoptive parents, or your parents as determined by the state for example, if the parent is listed on your birth certificate.) However, we recognize that many situations are a little more complicated, so we ve provided information on how to figure out which parent(s) should provide information on the FAFSA form.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if my parents aren t going to help me pay for college and refuse to provide information for my FAFSA form?
source_blocks.text: What if my parents aren t going to help me pay for college and refuse to provide information for my FAFSA form?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can t be considered independent of your parents just because they refuse to help you with this process. If you do not provide their information on the FAFSA form, the application will be considered rejected, and you might not be able to receive any federal student aid. The most you would be able to get (depending on what the financial aid office at your college decides) would be a loan called an unsubsidized loan. The FAFSA instructions will tell you what to do if you are in this situation. Learn more about how to fill out the FAFSA form when your parents aren t supporting you and won t provide their information.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You should check with your high school counselor or financial aid office to see whether completing the FAFSA form is the way to apply for state and college student aid. source_blocks.source_text_en: Students with criminal convictions have limited eligibility for federal student aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Make sure you understand your status, and don t assume you can t get aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your eligibility for federal student aid can be affected by incarceration and/or the type of conviction you have.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If I m incarcerated, can I get federal student aid?
source_blocks.text: If I m incarcerated, can I get federal student aid?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You have limited eligibility for federal student aid.
source_blocks.text: You have limited eligibility for federal student aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Once you re released, most eligibility limitations will be removed. In fact, you may apply for aid before you re released so your aid is processed in time for you to start school. However, if your incarceration was for a drug-related offense or if you are subject to an involuntary civil commitment for a sexual offense, your eligibility may be limited.
source_blocks.text: Once you re released, most eligibility limitations will be removed. In fact, you may apply for aid before you re released so your aid is processed in time for you to start school. However, if your incarceration was for a drug-related offense or if you are subject to an involuntary civil commitment for a sexual offense, your eligibility may be limited.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Even if you are ineligible for federal aid, you should complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form, because most schools and states use FAFSA information to award nonfederal aid, and you might be able to get some of those funds.
source_blocks.text: Even if you are ineligible for federal aid, you should complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form, because most schools and states use FAFSA information to award nonfederal aid, and you might be able to get some of those funds.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If I m on probation or parole, can I get federal student aid?
source_blocks.text: If I m on probation or parole, can I get federal student aid?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes; if you are on probation or parole or living in a halfway house, you may be eligible for federal student aid. But remember, if you were convicted of a drug-related offense or if you are subject to an involuntary civil commitment for a sexual offense, your eligibility may be limited.
source_blocks.text: Yes; if you are on probation or parole or living in a halfway house, you may be eligible for federal student aid. But remember, if you were convicted of a drug-related offense or if you are subject to an involuntary civil commitment for a sexual offense, your eligibility may be limited.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Is it true that drug convictions might affect my ability to get federal student aid?
source_blocks.text: Is it true that drug convictions might affect my ability to get federal student aid?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes; your eligibility might be suspended if the offense occurred while you were receiving federal student aid (grants, loans, or work-study). When you complete the FAFSA form, you will be asked whether you had a drug conviction for an offense that occurred while you were receiving federal student aid. If the answer is yes, you will be provided a worksheet to help you determine whether your conviction affects your eligibility for federal student aid.
source_blocks.text: Yes; your eligibility might be suspended if the offense occurred while you were receiving federal student aid (grants, loans, or work-study). When you complete the FAFSA form, you will be asked whether you had a drug conviction for an offense that occurred while you were receiving federal student aid. If the answer is yes, you will be provided a worksheet to help you determine whether your conviction affects your eligibility for federal student aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your eligibility for federal student aid has been suspended due to a drug conviction, you can regain eligibility early by successfully completing an approved drug rehabilitation program or by passing two unannounced drug tests administered by an approved drug rehabilitation program. If you regain eligibility during the award year, notify your financial aid office immediately so you can get any aid you re eligible for.
source_blocks.text: If your eligibility for federal student aid has been suspended due to a drug conviction, you can regain eligibility early by successfully completing an approved drug rehabilitation program or by passing two unannounced drug tests administered by an approved drug rehabilitation program. If you regain eligibility during the award year, notify your financial aid office immediately so you can get any aid you re eligible for.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are convicted of a drug-related offense after you submit the FAFSA form, you might lose eligibility for federal student aid, and you might be liable for returning any financial aid you received during a period of ineligibility.
source_blocks.text: If you are convicted of a drug-related offense after you submit the FAFSA form, you might lose eligibility for federal student aid, and you might be liable for returning any financial aid you received during a period of ineligibility.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What other convictions might affect my aid?
source_blocks.text: What other convictions might affect my aid?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have been convicted of a forcible or nonforcible sexual offense, and you are subject to an involuntary civil commitment upon completion of a period of incarceration for that offense, you cannot receive a Federal Pell Grant.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Our basic eligibility requirements are that you must
source_blocks.text: Our basic eligibility requirements are that you must

source_blocks.source_text_en: demonstrate financial need (for most programs); be a U.S. citizen or an eligible noncitizen; have a valid Social Security number (with the exception of students from the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, or the Republic of Palau); be registered with Selective Service, if you re a male (you must register between the ages of 18 and 25); be enrolled or accepted for enrollment as a regular student in an eligible degree or certificate program; be enrolled at least half-time to be eligible for Direct Loan Program funds; maintain satisfactory academic progress in college or career school; sign the certification statement on the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form stating that - you are not in default on a federal student loan, - you do not owe money on a federal student grant, and - you will use federal student aid only for educational purposes; and show you re qualified to obtain a college or career school education by - having a high school diploma or a recognized equivalent such as a General Educational Development (GED) certificate; - completing a high school education in a homeschool setting approved under state law (or if state law does not require a homeschooled student to obtain a completion credential completing a high school education in a homeschool setting that qualifies as an exemption from compulsory attendance requirements under state law); or - enrolling in an eligible career pathway program and meeting one of the "ability-to-benefit" alternatives described below.

You can call Selective Service toll-free at 1-888-655-1825 for general information about registering, or register online at sss.gov or while completing the FAFSA form.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Exit counseling provides important information to prepare you to repay your federal student loan(s).
source_blocks.text: 离校咨询提供重要信息，帮助您为偿还联邦学生贷款做好准备。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have received a subsidized, unsubsidized or PLUS loan under the Direct Loan Program or the FFEL Program, you must complete exit counseling each time you:
source_blocks.text: 如果您在直接贷款计划或FFEL计划下获得了补贴、非补贴或PLUS贷款，则每次出现以下情况时，您都必须完成离校咨询：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Drop below half-time enrollment Graduate Leave school
source_blocks.text: 注册状态降至半日制以下 毕业 离开学校

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: The FFEL Program ended June 30, 2010 and no new loans have been made under the FFEL Program after that date.
source_blocks.text: 注意：FFEL计划已于2010年6月30日结束，此后未在该计划下发放任何新贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete Exit Counseling
source_blocks.text: 完成离校咨询

source_blocks.source_text_en: LOG IN TO START
source_blocks.text: 登录开始

source_blocks.source_text_en: Who should complete this?
source_blocks.text: 谁应完成此咨询？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Students who have received a subsidized, unsubsidized or PLUS loan(s) under the Direct Loan Program or the FFEL Program, must complete exit counseling each time they drop below half-time enrollment, graduate, or leave school.
source_blocks.text: 在直接贷款计划或FFEL计划下获得补贴、非补贴或PLUS贷款的学生，每次注册状态降至半日制以下、毕业或离开学校时，都必须完成离校咨询。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How long will it take?
source_blocks.text: 需要多长时间？

source_blocks.source_text_en: The entire counseling process must be completed in a single session. Most people complete counseling in 20-30 minutes.
source_blocks.text: 整个咨询过程必须在一次会话中完成。大多数人会在20-30分钟内完成咨询。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What do I need?
source_blocks.text: 我需要什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Verified FSA ID -
source_blocks.text: 已验证的 FSA ID -

source_blocks.source_text_en: Return to the Counseling selection page
source_blocks.text: 返回咨询选择页面

source_blocks.source_text_en: TEACH Grant Exit Counseling
source_blocks.text: TEACH 助学金离校咨询

source_blocks.source_text_en: Students who received a TEACH Grant and are graduating from their program of study or withdrawing from school must complete TEACH Grant Exit Counseling. TEACH Grant Exit Counseling provides information about fulfilling the TEACH Grant service obligation and explains the terms and conditions that will apply if the TEACH Grant is converted to a Direct Unsubsidized Loan.
source_blocks.text: 获得 TEACH 助学金且即将从学习项目毕业或退学的学生必须完成 TEACH 助学金离校咨询。TEACH 助学金离校咨询提供关于履行 TEACH 助学金服务义务的信息，并解释如果 TEACH 助学金转换为直接无补贴贷款时将适用的条款和条件。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Go to TEACH Grant Exit Counseling
source_blocks.text: 前往 TEACH 助学金离校咨询

source_blocks.source_text_en: Extended Plan | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 扩展计划 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Extended Repayment Plan allows you to repay your loans over an extended period of time.
source_blocks.text: 扩展还款计划允许您在较长时间内偿还贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Payments are made for up to 25 years.
source_blocks.text: 还款期限最长可达25年。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you need to make lower monthly payments over a longer period of time than under plans such as the Standard Repayment Plan, then the Extended Repayment Plan may be right for you.
source_blocks.text: 如果您需要在比标准还款计划等计划更长的时间内支付较低的月供，那么扩展还款计划可能适合您。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Eligible Federal Loans
source_blocks.text: 符合条件的联邦贷款

source_blocks.source_text_en: The following loans from the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program and the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program are eligible for the Extended Repayment Plan:
source_blocks.text: 以下来自威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款（直接贷款）计划和联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划的贷款符合扩展还款计划的条件：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct Subsidized Loans Direct Unsubsidized Loans Direct PLUS Loans Direct Consolidation Loans Subsidized Federal Stafford Loans Unsubsidized Federal Stafford Loans FFEL PLUS Loans FFEL Consolidation Loans
source_blocks.text: 直接补贴贷款 直接无补贴贷款 直接PLUS贷款 直接合并贷款 补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款 无补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款 FFEL PLUS贷款 FFEL合并贷款

source_blocks.source_text_en: Eligibility for the Extended Repayment Plan
source_blocks.text: 扩展还款计划的资格

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you're a Direct Loan borrower, you must have had no outstanding balance on a Direct Loan as of October 7, 1998, or on the date you obtained a Direct Loan after October 7, 1998, and you must have more than \$30,000 in outstanding Direct Loans.
source_blocks.text: 如果您是直接贷款借款人，您必须在1998年10月7日或之后获得直接贷款之日没有未偿还的直接贷款余额，并且您必须拥有超过30,000美元的未偿还直接贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you're a FFEL borrower, to qualify for this plan you must have had no outstanding balance on a FFEL Program loan as of October 7, 1998, or on the date you obtained a FFEL Program loan after October 7, 1998, and you must have more than \$30,000 in outstanding FFEL Program loans.
source_blocks.text: 如果您是FFEL借款人，要符合此计划的条件，您必须在1998年10月7日或之后获得FFEL计划贷款之日没有未偿还的FFEL计划贷款余额，并且您必须拥有超过30,000美元的未偿还FFEL计划贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For example, if you have \$35,000 in outstanding FFEL Program loans and \$10,000 in outstanding Direct Loans, you can choose the Extended Repayment Plan for your FFEL Program loans, but not for your Direct Loans.
source_blocks.text: 例如，如果您有35,000美元的未偿还FFEL计划贷款和10,000美元的未偿还直接贷款，您可以为您的FFEL计划贷款选择扩展还款计划，但不能为您的直接贷款选择。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Monthly Payments
source_blocks.text: 每月还款额

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under this plan, your monthly payments are
source_blocks.text: 在此计划下，您的每月还款额为

source_blocks.source_text_en: a fixed or graduated amount, made for up to 25 years, and generally lower than payments made under the Standard and Graduated Repayment Plans.
source_blocks.text: 固定或递增的金额， 最长还款期限为25年，并且 通常低于标准还款计划和递增还款计划下的还款额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Using Loan Simulator to Estimate Your Eligibility and Payment Amount Under the Extended Repayment Plan
source_blocks.text: 使用贷款模拟器估算您在扩展还款计划下的资格和还款金额

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your loan servicer, the company that handles the billing and other services on your federal student loan, can help you choose a loan repayment plan that s best for you. Before you contact your loan servicer to discuss repayment plans, you can use our Loan Simulator to get an early look at what plans you may be eligible for and to receive a comparison of estimated monthly payment amounts for all federal student loan repayment plans. This comparison is important because the Extended Plan may not provide you with the lowest payment amount based on your individual circumstances. You may find that your payment will be lower under another repayment plan.
source_blocks.text: 您的贷款服务机构，即处理您的联邦学生贷款账单和其他服务的公司，可以帮助您选择最适合您的贷款还款计划。在联系您的贷款服务机构讨论还款计划之前，您可以使用我们的贷款模拟器提前了解您可能符合条件的计划，并获得所有联邦学生贷款还款计划的预计月还款额比较。此比较很重要，因为扩展计划可能不会根据您的个人情况提供最低的还款金额。您可能会发现，在另一个还款计划下，您的还款额会更低。

source_blocks.source_text_en: FAFSA Deadlines
source_blocks.text: FAFSA 截止日期

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes, there are FAFSA deadlines, and we ve got them right here. Don t miss out on financial aid opportunities.
source_blocks.text: 是的，FAFSA 有截止日期，我们在这里列出了它们。不要错过经济援助机会。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form allows you to be considered for federal student aid. In addition, states and colleges use FAFSA information to award their own grants, scholarships, and loans. But, since aid is limited, you have to meet the deadlines!
source_blocks.text: 填写免费申请联邦学生援助（FAFSA）表格，您就有资格获得联邦学生援助。此外，各州和学院也使用 FAFSA 信息来颁发自己的助学金、奖学金和贷款。但是，由于援助有限，您必须遵守截止日期！

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal Deadlines
source_blocks.text: 联邦截止日期

source_blocks.source_text_en: 2020 21 Academic Year
Online FAFSA forms must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. Central time (CT), June 30, 2021. Any corrections or updates must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. CT, September 11, 2021.
source_blocks.text: 在线 FAFSA 表格必须在 2021 年 6 月 30 日中部时间（CT）晚上 11:59 之前提交。任何更正或更新必须在 2021 年 9 月 11 日中部时间（CT）晚上 11:59 之前提交。

source_blocks.source_text_en: 2019 20 Academic Year

Online Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) forms must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. Central time (CT), June 30, 2020. Any corrections or updates must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. CT, September 12, 2020.
source_blocks.text: 在线免费申请联邦学生援助（FAFSA）表格必须在 2020 年 6 月 30 日中部时间（CT）晚上 11:59 之前提交。任何更正或更新必须在 2020 年 9 月 12 日中部时间（CT）晚上 11:59 之前提交。

source_blocks.source_text_en: College Deadlines
source_blocks.text: 学院截止日期

source_blocks.source_text_en: Each college may have its own deadline. Check with the college(s) you re interested in attending. You may also want to ask your college about its definition of an application deadline. Is it the date your FAFSA form is processed or the date the college receives your processed FAFSA data?
source_blocks.text: 每所学院可能有自己的截止日期。请与您感兴趣的学院核实。您可能还想询问您的学院关于申请截止日期的定义。是您的 FAFSA 表格被处理的日期，还是学院收到您已处理的 FAFSA 数据的日期？

source_blocks.source_text_en: You might be eligible for a discharge of your federal student loans based on false certification.
source_blocks.text: You might be eligible for a discharge of your federal student loans based on false certification.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn more about false certification discharge to see whether you might qualify.
source_blocks.text: Learn more about false certification discharge to see whether you might qualify.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You might be eligible for a discharge of your loan made under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program or Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program if your school falsely certified your eligibility to receive a loan.
source_blocks.text: You might be eligible for a discharge of your loan made under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program or Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program if your school falsely certified your eligibility to receive a loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What are the eligibility requirements to qualify for a loan discharge based on false certification?
source_blocks.text: What are the eligibility requirements to qualify for a loan discharge based on false certification?

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are three categories of false certification through which you might be eligible for a discharge of your Direct Loans or FFEL Program loans:
source_blocks.text: There are three categories of false certification through which you might be eligible for a discharge of your Direct Loans or FFEL Program loans:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Ability to benefit: The school falsely certified your eligibility to receive the loan based on your ability to benefit from its training, and you didn t meet the ability-to-benefit student eligibility requirements that were in effect at the time the school determined your eligibility. Disqualifying status: The school certified your eligibility to receive the loan, but at the time of the certification, you had a status (physical or mental condition, age, criminal record, or other circumstance) that disqualified you from meeting the legal requirements for employment in your state of residence in the occupation for which the program of study was preparing you. Unauthorized signature or unauthorized payment: The school signed your name on the loan application or promissory note without your authorization or the school endorsed your loan check or signed your authorization for electronic funds transfer without your knowledge, and the loan money wasn t given to you or applied to charges you owed to the school.

If you believe that someone else (other than a school employee) forged your signature on a loan document or a loan was made in your name as a result of the crime of identity theft, contact your loan servicer.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How much of my loan will be discharged if I m approved for a loan discharge?
source_blocks.text: How much of my loan will be discharged if I m approved for a loan discharge?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you meet the eligibility requirements for a discharge, the entire remaining balance of your loan will be discharged, and any payments made on the loan will be refunded.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What happens if my loan discharge is denied?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You will remain responsible for repaying your loan. If you believe that your loan discharge application was denied in error or if you have additional information that you believe would support your eligibility for a false certification discharge, you may ask the U.S. Department of Education to review the denial.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal Versus Private Loans | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 联邦贷款与私人贷款 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: When it comes to paying for college, career school, or graduate school, federal student loans can offer several advantages over private student loans.
source_blocks.text: 在支付大学、职业学校或研究生院费用时，联邦学生贷款相比私人学生贷款可以提供多项优势。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Need a loan to help pay for college? Consider federal loans first!
source_blocks.text: 需要贷款来帮助支付大学费用吗？先考虑联邦贷款！

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you apply for financial aid, your school will likely include student loans as part of your financial aid package. It s important to understand what types of loans you are offered. Generally, there are two types of student loans federal and private.
source_blocks.text: 如果你申请经济援助，你的学校很可能会将学生贷款作为你经济援助计划的一部分。了解你被提供的贷款类型很重要。一般来说，有两种类型的学生贷款：联邦贷款和私人贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal student loans and federal parent loans: These loans are funded by the federal government. Private student loans: These loans are nonfederal loans, made by a lender such as a bank, credit union, state agency, or a school.
source_blocks.text: 联邦学生贷款和联邦家长贷款：这些贷款由联邦政府资助。 私人学生贷款：这些贷款是非联邦贷款，由银行、信用合作社、州机构或学校等贷方提供。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you need to borrow money to pay for college or career school, start with federal loans.
source_blocks.text: 如果你需要借钱支付大学或职业学校费用，从联邦贷款开始。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal student loans are
source_blocks.text: 联邦学生贷款是

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans and Direct PLUS Loans (for graduate and professional students).
source_blocks.text: 直接补贴贷款和直接非补贴贷款，以及 直接PLUS贷款（针对研究生和专业学生）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal parent loans are
source_blocks.text: 联邦家长贷款是

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct PLUS Loans (for parents). Parents are fully responsible for paying these loans, even though they are taken out to benefit students.
source_blocks.text: 直接PLUS贷款（针对家长）。家长对这些贷款负有全部偿还责任，即使这些贷款是为了帮助学生而借的。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What are the differences between federal and private student loans?
source_blocks.text: 联邦学生贷款和私人学生贷款有什么区别？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal student loans are made by the government, with terms and conditions that are set by law, and include many benefits (such as fixed interest rates and income-driven repayment plans) not typically offered with private loans.
source_blocks.text: 联邦学生贷款由政府提供，其条款和条件由法律规定，并包含许多私人贷款通常不提供的福利（如固定利率和基于收入的还款计划）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: In contrast, private loans are made by private organizations such banks, credit unions, and state-based or state-affiliated organizations, and have terms and conditions that are set by the lender. Private student loans are generally more expensive than federal student loans.
source_blocks.text: 相比之下，私人贷款由私人组织提供，如银行、信用合作社以及州级或州附属组织，其条款和条件由贷方设定。私人学生贷款通常比联邦学生贷款更昂贵。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The chart below provides a summary of the differences.
source_blocks.text: 下面的图表提供了差异的摘要。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Private loans differ by lender and by type of loan. Be sure you understand the terms of your loan, and keep in touch with your lender about any questions you may have.
source_blocks.text: 私人贷款因贷方和贷款类型而异。请确保你了解你的贷款条款，并就你可能有的任何问题与你的贷方保持联系。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I get a federal student loan?
source_blocks.text: 我如何获得联邦学生贷款？

source_blocks.source_text_en: To get a federal loan, you must first complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form. Learn more about applying for aid.
source_blocks.text: 要获得联邦贷款，你必须首先完成联邦学生援助免费申请（FAFSA）表格。了解更多关于申请援助的信息。
