source_blocks.source_text_en: Filling Out the FAFSA® Form | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 填写FAFSA®表格 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: You know you have to fill out the FreeApplication for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form, but maybe you re not sure what to do.
source_blocks.text: 你知道你必须填写联邦学生援助免费申请（FAFSA）表格，但也许你不确定该怎么做。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Let s review what to expect.
source_blocks.text: 让我们了解一下预期情况。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Filling out the FAFSA form can be a straightforward and easy process. Select the Fill Out the FAFSA button on the home page, and just follow the directions on the screen. Below are some tips to help you along the way.
source_blocks.text: 填写FAFSA表格可以是一个直接且简单的过程。在主页上选择“填写FAFSA”按钮，然后按照屏幕上的指示操作。以下是一些帮助你顺利进行的提示。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Ready to fill out your FAFSA form now? Go for it!
source_blocks.text: 准备好现在填写你的FAFSA表格了吗？开始吧！

source_blocks.source_text_en: Fill Out the FAFSA
source_blocks.text: 填写FAFSA

source_blocks.source_text_en: Prefer a mobile app? The 2020 21 and 2019 20 FAFSA forms are on the myStudentAid app, available on the App Store (iOS) or on Google Play (Android).
source_blocks.text: 更喜欢移动应用？2020-21和2019-20 FAFSA表格在myStudentAid应用上，可在App Store（iOS）或Google Play（Android）上获取。

source_blocks.source_text_en: FAFSA Topics
source_blocks.text: FAFSA主题

source_blocks.source_text_en: Try This ResourceThe FAFSA Process graphic Walks through the process of preparing for, completing, and submitting a FAFSA form. Includes info on what happens after the form is submitted.
source_blocks.text: 尝试此资源：FAFSA流程图形，引导你完成准备、填写和提交FAFSA表格的过程。包括提交表格后会发生什么的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Creating an FSA ID
source_blocks.text: 创建FSA ID

source_blocks.source_text_en: We strongly recommend you create an FSA ID, a username and password combination that allows you to sign your FAFSA form electronically. Your FSA ID also can be used to access the myStudentAid app, sign loan contracts, and access certain information online. While you can get your FSA ID as you re completing the FAFSA form online, getting it ahead of time and using it to begin your FAFSA form on fafsa.gov or on the myStudentAid mobile app cuts down on errors and delays. Find out how to get an FSA ID and what to do if you forgot your FSA ID.
source_blocks.text: 我们强烈建议你创建一个FSA ID，这是一个用户名和密码组合，允许你以电子方式签署你的FAFSA表格。你的FSA ID还可以用于访问myStudentAid应用、签署贷款合同以及在线访问某些信息。虽然你可以在在线完成FAFSA表格时获取FSA ID，但提前获取并使用它在fafsa.gov或myStudentAid移动应用上开始你的FAFSA表格可以减少错误和延误。了解如何获取FSA ID以及如果你忘记了FSA ID该怎么办。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Important note: If you re a dependent student, one of your parents whose information is reported on the FAFSA form will also need an FSA ID so that he or she can sign your application electronically. If your parent doesn t have a Social Security number (SSN), your parent won t be able to create an FSA ID (which requires an SSN). This means you ll have to select the option to print a signature page when you get to the end of your FAFSA form on fafsa.gov (this option isn t available in the myStudentAid app).
source_blocks.text: 重要提示：如果你是一名受抚养学生，你的信息在FAFSA表格上报告的父母之一也需要一个FSA ID，以便他或她可以以电子方式签署你的申请。如果你的父母没有社会安全号码（SSN），你的父母将无法创建FSA ID（这需要SSN）。这意味着你必须在fafsa.gov上完成FAFSA表格时选择打印签名页的选项（此选项在myStudentAid应用中不可用）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Creating your FSA ID before you begin the FAFSA form only takes a few minutes and could prevent processing delays. (Plus, you can t use the myStudentAid mobile app at all without an FSA ID, so you ll need to create it before filling out the FAFSA form on the app.)
source_blocks.text: 在开始FAFSA表格之前创建你的FSA ID只需几分钟，可以防止处理延迟。（此外，没有FSA ID你根本无法使用myStudentAid移动应用，所以你需要先创建它才能在该应用上填写FAFSA表格。）

source_blocks.source_text_en: Tip: Use your FSA ID to start your FAFSA form. When you create your FSA ID, be careful to enter your name and Social Security number exactly as they appear on your Social Security card. Then, if you go to fafsa.gov to start your application and indicate that you are the student, you will be given the option to enter your FSA ID or to enter your identifiers (your name, date of birth, and SSN).
source_blocks.text: 提示：使用你的FSA ID开始你的FAFSA表格。当你创建FSA ID时，请务必准确输入你的姓名和社会安全号码，就像它们出现在你的社会安全卡上一样。然后，如果你去fafsa.gov开始你的申请并表明你是学生，你将可以选择输入你的FSA ID或输入你的标识符（你的姓名、出生日期和SSN）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you log in with your FSA ID, certain information (including your name, Social Security number, and date of birth) will be automatically loaded into your application. This will prevent you from running into a common error that occurs when your verified FSA ID information doesn t match the information on your FAFSA form. Additionally, you won t have to provide your FSA ID again to sign your FAFSA form electronically or to use the Internal Revenue Service Data Retrieval Tool (IRS DRT) if you re eligible.
source_blocks.text: 如果你使用FSA ID登录，某些信息（包括你的姓名、社会安全号码和出生日期）将自动加载到你的申请中。这将防止你遇到一个常见错误，即你验证的FSA ID信息与FAFSA表格上的信息不匹配。此外，如果你符合条件，你无需再次提供FSA ID即可以电子方式签署你的FAFSA表格或使用美国国税局数据检索工具（IRS DRT）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The student is the one applying for financial aid, so be sure it s the student entering his or her FSA ID in the I am the student tab. Do not start the FAFSA form by supplying the parent s FSA ID.
source_blocks.text: 学生是申请经济援助的人，所以确保是学生在“我是学生”标签下输入他或她的FSA ID。不要通过提供父母的FSA ID来开始FAFSA表格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Gathering the Documents Needed to Apply
source_blocks.text: 收集申请所需的文件

source_blocks.source_text_en: The FAFSA questions ask for information about you (your name, date of birth, address, etc.) and about your financial situation. Depending on your circumstances (for instance, whether you re a U.S. citizen or what tax form you used), you might need the following information or documents as you fill out the application:
source_blocks.text: FAFSA问题询问关于你（你的姓名、出生日期、地址等）以及你的财务状况的信息。根据你的情况（例如，你是否是美国公民或你使用了哪种税表），你在填写申请时可能需要以下信息或文件：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your Social Security number (it s important that you enter it correctly on the FAFSA form!) Your parents Social Security numbers if you are a dependent student Your driver s license number if you have one Your Alien Registration number if you are not a U.S. citizen Federal tax information or tax returns including IRS W-2 information, for you (and your spouse, if you are married), and for your parents if you are a dependent student: - IRS 1040 - Foreign tax return, IRS 1040NR, or IRS 1040NR-EZ - Tax return for Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, the U.S. Virgin Islands, the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, or Palau Records of your untaxed income, such as child support received, interest income, and veterans noneducation benefits, for you, and for your parents if you are a dependent student Information on cash; savings and checking account balances; investments, including stocks and bonds and real estate (but not including the home in which you live); and business and farm assets for you, and for your parents if you are a dependent student
source_blocks.text: 您的社会安全号码（在FAFSA表格上正确输入非常重要！） 如果您是受抚养学生，您父母的社会安全号码 如果您有驾照，您的驾照号码 如果您不是美国公民，您的外国人登记号码 您（以及如果您已婚，您的配偶）和如果您是受抚养学生，您父母的联邦税务信息或纳税申报表，包括IRS W-2信息： - IRS 1040 - 外国纳税申报表、IRS 1040NR或IRS 1040NR-EZ - 波多黎各、关岛、美属萨摩亚、美属维尔京群岛、马绍尔群岛、密克罗尼西亚联邦或帕劳的纳税申报表 您（以及如果您是受抚养学生，您父母）的未征税收入记录，例如收到的子女抚养费、利息收入和退伍军人的非教育福利 您（以及如果您是受抚养学生，您父母）的现金、储蓄和支票账户余额、投资（包括股票、债券和房地产，但不包括您居住的房屋）以及企业和农场资产的信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: Keep these records! You may need them again. Do not mail your records to us.
source_blocks.text: 保留这些记录！您可能再次需要它们。请勿将您的记录邮寄给我们。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Try This Resource2020 21 FAFSA on the Web Worksheet Provides a preview of the questions students and parents may be asked while completing the FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 尝试此资源2020-21 FAFSA在线工作表 提供学生和家长在填写FAFSA表格时可能被问到的问题的预览。

source_blocks.source_text_en: One thing you don t need for the FAFSA form is money! The FAFSA form is FREE, so if a website or mobile app asks you to pay to fill it out, you re not dealing with the official FAFSA site or the official myStudentAid app. Remember, this is a government application, so it s on a .gov website and an official U.S. Department of Education mobile app.
source_blocks.text: 填写FAFSA表格不需要的一件事是钱！FAFSA表格是免费的，所以如果网站或移动应用程序要求您付费填写，您不是在处理官方的FAFSA网站或官方的myStudentAid应用程序。请记住，这是一个政府申请，所以它在.gov网站和官方的美国教育部移动应用程序上。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Getting Help
source_blocks.text: 获取帮助

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you need help filling out the FAFSA form, use these free tools:
source_blocks.text: 如果您在填写FAFSA表格时需要帮助，请使用这些免费工具：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Select the blue and white question mark icon next to a FAFSA question to view a "tool tip" that provides information about how to answer that question. In the online FAFSA form, the tool tip may have a More Help link for additional information. You also can select the Help button at the bottom of the tool tip to reach the FAFSA Help page, where you can browse FAQs, search for more information, or click on Contact Us. Once you click on Contact Us, you ll have the option of emailing us with your question or, during business hours, chatting (in English or Spanish) with live technical support staff. (In the myStudentAid mobile app, you can find the contact information via the hamburger menu the three parallel lines at the top right of the screen.) Contact the financial aid office at the college or career school you plan to attend.
source_blocks.text: 选择FAFSA问题旁边的蓝白问号图标，查看提供有关如何回答该问题的信息的“工具提示”。 在在线FAFSA表格中，工具提示可能有“更多帮助”链接以获取更多信息。您还可以选择工具提示底部的“帮助”按钮进入FAFSA帮助页面，在那里您可以浏览常见问题解答、搜索更多信息或点击“联系我们”。 一旦您点击“联系我们”，您可以选择通过电子邮件向我们提问，或者在工作时间内与实时技术支持人员聊天（英语或西班牙语）。（在myStudentAid移动应用程序中，您可以通过屏幕右上角的三条平行线汉堡菜单找到联系信息。） 联系您计划就读的学院或职业学校的财政援助办公室。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Starting Your FAFSA Form and Providing Your Basic Personal Information
source_blocks.text: 开始填写FAFSA表格并提供您的基本个人信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: The FAFSA form is available on Oct. 1 for the next school year. We encourage you to fill it out as soon as possible on or after Oct. 1 to meet FAFSA deadlines.
source_blocks.text: FAFSA表格于10月1日开放用于下一学年。我们鼓励您在10月1日或之后尽快填写，以满足FAFSA截止日期。

source_blocks.source_text_en: FAFSA Filing Options You may choose any of these methods to file a FAFSA form:
source_blocks.text: FAFSA提交选项 您可以选择以下任何方式提交FAFSA表格：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Log in at fafsa.gov to apply online or Fill out the form in the myStudentAid mobile app, available on the App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android) or Complete a 2020-21 FAFSA PDF or a 2019 20 FAFSA PDF (note: you must print out and mail the FAFSA PDF for processing) or Request a print-out of the FAFSA PDF by calling us at 1-800-4-FED-AID (1-800-433-3243) or 334-523-2691 (TTY for the deaf or hard of hearing 1-800-730-8913); then fill out the form and mail it for processing
source_blocks.text: 登录fafsa.gov在线申请，或 在myStudentAid移动应用程序中填写表格，该应用程序可在App Store（iOS）或Google Play（Android）上获得，或 填写2020-21 FAFSA PDF或2019-20 FAFSA PDF（注意：您必须打印并邮寄FAFSA PDF以供处理），或 致电1-800-4-FED-AID（1-800-433-3243）或334-523-2691（聋人或听力障碍者TTY：1-800-730-8913）索取FAFSA PDF打印件；然后填写表格并邮寄以供处理

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are starting the application for the first time on fafsa.gov, select START HERE. As you begin, keep the following in mind:
source_blocks.text: 如果您是第一次在fafsa.gov上开始申请，请选择“从这里开始”。当您开始时，请记住以下几点：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your name and Social Security number must match those on your Social Security card. Follow this tip to avoid getting a notice that your information doesn t match the Social Security Administration s records (or your FSA ID account). If you re concerned about providing your personal information on the log-in page, choose the virtual keyboard option for additional security. To ensure the application functions properly, make sure the pop-up blocker in your browser allows pop-ups from fafsa.ed.gov. Learn how to enable pop-ups in your browser.
source_blocks.text: 您的姓名和社会安全号码必须与社会安全卡上的信息一致。遵循此提示，以避免收到您的信息与社会安全管理局记录（或您的FSA ID账户）不匹配的通知。 如果您担心在登录页面上提供个人信息，请选择虚拟键盘选项以增加安全性。 为确保应用程序正常运行，请确保浏览器中的弹出窗口阻止程序允许来自fafsa.ed.gov的弹出窗口。了解如何在浏览器中启用弹出窗口。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re starting for the first time on the myStudentAid mobile app, you will select START HERE and then be required to enter your FSA ID. You cannot fill out the FAFSA form on the mobile app without an FSA ID.
source_blocks.text: 如果您是第一次在myStudentAid移动应用程序上开始，您将选择“从这里开始”，然后需要输入您的FSA ID。没有FSA ID，您无法在移动应用程序上填写FAFSA表格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re a male between the ages of 18 and 25 and you haven t registered with the Selective Service System, select Yes when you re asked if you would like to be registered. Otherwise, you won t be eligible to receive federal student aid. This requirement applies to any person assigned the sex of male at birth.
source_blocks.text: 如果您是18至25岁之间的男性，并且尚未在兵役登记系统中注册，当被问及是否希望注册时，请选择“是”。否则，您将没有资格获得联邦学生援助。此要求适用于任何出生时被指定为男性的人。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The following tips apply whether you re filling out the form online or on the mobile app:
source_blocks.text: 以下提示适用于您在线或通过移动应用程序填写表格：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Near the beginning of the application, you ll create a save key, a temporary password that you ll use if you start your FAFSA form, save it without finishing it, then want to open it again later to finish it. One benefit of the save key is that students and parents can use this function to access the FAFSA form if they are completing the FAFSA in separate locations. (Unlike with the FSA ID, which needs to be kept private, it s okay to tell your parent what your save key is.) If you are applying for a summer session, contact the financial aid office at your college to find out which school year you should select when you complete your FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 在申请开始时，您将创建一个保存密钥，这是一个临时密码，如果您开始填写FAFSA表格但未完成并保存，之后想再次打开以完成它时使用。保存密钥的一个好处是，如果学生和家长在不同地点填写FAFSA，他们可以使用此功能访问FAFSA表格。（与需要保密的FSA ID不同，告诉您的父母您的保存密钥是可以的。） 如果您正在申请夏季学期，请联系您大学的财政援助办公室，以确定在填写FAFSA表格时应选择哪个学年。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you filled out a FAFSA form last year and want to renew it, select LOG IN on the FAFSA home page, select I am the student, enter your FSA ID, and be sure to select FAFSA RENEWAL once given the option. That way, many of the (nonfinancial) questions will be prefilled for you. Just be sure to update any information that has changed since last year.
source_blocks.text: 如果您去年填写了FAFSA表格并希望续签，请在FAFSA主页上选择“登录”，选择“我是学生”，输入您的FSA ID，并确保在出现选项时选择“FAFSA续签”。这样，许多（非财务）问题将为您预先填写。只需确保更新自去年以来发生的任何变化。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Only the student can start a FAFSA renewal using his or her FSA ID. If you re a dependent student and your parent helps you with your FAFSA form, you should start the FAFSA renewal, save it, and give the save key to your parent so he or she can access your FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 只有学生本人才能使用其 FSA ID 启动 FAFSA 续填。如果您是受抚养学生，且您的父母帮助您填写 FAFSA 表格，您应启动 FAFSA 续填，保存后，将保存密钥交给您的父母，以便他们访问您的 FAFSA 表格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re using the mobile app and log in as the student and are eligible for a FAFSA renewal, the renewal will automatically appear for you.
source_blocks.text: 如果您使用移动应用并以学生身份登录，且符合 FAFSA 续填资格，续填表格将自动为您显示。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Due to the coronavirus national emergency, processing of the FAFSA PDF may take longer than usual. We recommend filing your FAFSA form electronically to avoid processing delays.
source_blocks.text: 由于冠状病毒国家紧急状态，FAFSA PDF 的处理时间可能比平时更长。我们建议您以电子方式提交 FAFSA 表格，以避免处理延迟。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Listing Colleges and/or Career Schools
source_blocks.text: 列出学院和/或职业学校

source_blocks.source_text_en: While completing the FAFSA form, you must list at least one school to receive your information. The schools you list will use your FAFSA information to determine the types and amounts of aid you may receive. Use the Federal School Code Search to find the colleges you re interested in including on your FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 在填写 FAFSA 表格时，您必须至少列出一所学校以接收您的信息。您列出的学校将使用您的 FAFSA 信息来确定您可能获得的资助类型和金额。使用联邦学校代码搜索来查找您感兴趣并希望包含在 FAFSA 表格中的学院。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For purposes of federal student aid, it does not matter in what order you list the schools. However, to be considered for state aid, some states require you to list schools in a particular order (for instance, you might need to list a state school first). Find out whether your state has a requirement for the order in which you list schools on your FAFSA form
source_blocks.text: 就联邦学生资助而言，您列出学校的顺序无关紧要。但是，为了获得州资助的考虑，一些州要求您按特定顺序列出学校（例如，您可能需要先列出州内学校）。请了解您所在的州是否对在 FAFSA 表格上列出学校的顺序有要求。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can list up to 10 schools online or in the mobile app or up to four schools on a FAFSA PDF. (You can add more schools to your FAFSA form later.) Schools you list on the application will automatically receive your FAFSA results electronically.
source_blocks.text: 您可以在线或通过移动应用列出最多 10 所学校，或在 FAFSA PDF 上列出最多四所学校。（您之后可以在 FAFSA 表格中添加更多学校。）您在申请中列出的学校将自动以电子方式收到您的 FAFSA 结果。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: Schools will not be able to see which other schools you listed on your FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 注意：学校无法看到您在 FAFSA 表格上列出的其他学校。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You should add any school that you plan on applying to, even if you haven t been accepted yet. In most cases, once a school accepts you, they will then work on developing your aid offer.
source_blocks.text: 您应添加任何计划申请的学校，即使您尚未被录取。在大多数情况下，一旦学校录取您，他们就会着手制定您的资助方案。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Determining Your Dependency Status
source_blocks.text: 确定您的受抚养身份

source_blocks.source_text_en: The FAFSA form asks a series of questions that determine whether you are a dependent or independent student for purposes of applying for federal student aid. If you are a dependent student, you must report parent information, as well as your own information, on your application. If you re curious, you can find out now whether you re a dependent student.
source_blocks.text: FAFSA 表格会询问一系列问题，以确定您在申请联邦学生资助时是受抚养学生还是独立学生。如果您是受抚养学生，您必须在申请中报告父母信息以及您自己的信息。如果您好奇，现在就可以了解自己是否属于受抚养学生。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reporting Parents Information
source_blocks.text: 报告父母信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re a dependent student, you ll need to report parent information on your FAFSA form. Visit our page on reporting parent information to find out who counts as your parent, what to do if you don t live with your parents, and what to do if you don t have access to your parents financial information.
source_blocks.text: 如果您是受抚养学生，您需要在 FAFSA 表格上报告父母信息。请访问我们关于报告父母信息的页面，了解谁算作您的父母、如果您不与父母同住该怎么办，以及如果您无法获取父母的财务信息该怎么办。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your FAFSA information is safe with us! Is it safe with you? Read Federal Student Aid and Identity Theft to learn how we safeguard the personal information you report on fafsa.gov. We've also included some tips on what you can do (at home, online, or in the dorm) to keep your identity from being stolen.
source_blocks.text: 您的 FAFSA 信息在我们这里很安全！在您那里安全吗？阅读 联邦学生资助与身份盗窃，了解我们如何保护您在 fafsa.gov 上报告的个人信息。我们还提供了一些提示，告诉您（在家中、网上或宿舍里）可以采取哪些措施来防止身份被盗。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Providing Financial Information
source_blocks.text: 提供财务信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: The FAFSA form asks for financial information, including information from tax forms and balances of savings and checking accounts.
source_blocks.text: FAFSA 表格要求提供财务信息，包括税务表格中的信息以及储蓄和支票账户余额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The 2020 21 FAFSA form asks for 2018 tax information. If you re filling out the 2019 20 FAFSA form, you ll need your 2017 tax information.
source_blocks.text: 2020-21 FAFSA 表格要求提供 2018 年的税务信息。 如果您正在填写 2019-20 FAFSA 表格，您需要提供 2017 年的税务信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: If your family s financial situation has changed dramatically since you and/or your parents filed taxes, complete the FAFSA questions as required, submit the FAFSA form, then contact the school you plan to attend and discuss your situation with the financial aid office.
source_blocks.text: 注意：如果您和/或您的父母报税后，您家庭的财务状况发生了巨大变化，请按要求完成 FAFSA 问题，提交 FAFSA 表格，然后联系您计划就读的学校，并与财务援助办公室讨论您的情况。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What to Do If Your Parents (or Your) Marital Status Has Changed Since Taxes Were Filed
source_blocks.text: 如果您的父母（或您本人）在报税后婚姻状况发生变化该怎么办

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here are some tips for this type of situation using the example of the 2020 21 FAFSA form:
source_blocks.text: 以下是一些针对此类情况的提示，以2020-2021学年FAFSA表格为例：

source_blocks.source_text_en: The FAFSA form asks for marital status as of today (the day it s filled out). So if the student or parent is married now but wasn t in 2018 (and therefore didn t file taxes as married), the spouse s 2018 income will need to be added to the FAFSA form. Similarly, if the student or parent filed 2018 taxes as married but is no longer married when filling out the FAFSA form, the spouse s income will need to be subtracted. And if the student or parent was married when filing 2018 taxes, then got divorced and is now married to someone else, there s a bit more math to do: Subtract the ex s income, then add the new spouse s income.
source_blocks.text: FAFSA表格询问的是填写当天的婚姻状况。因此，如果学生或父母现在已婚，但在2018年未婚（因此未以已婚身份报税），则需要在FAFSA表格中添加配偶2018年的收入。 同样，如果学生或父母在2018年以已婚身份报税，但在填写FAFSA表格时已不再已婚，则需要减去配偶的收入。 如果学生或父母在2018年报税时已婚，随后离婚，现在又与其他人结婚，则需要进行更多计算：先减去前配偶的收入，再加上新配偶的收入。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The FAFSA help text covers all these situations in more detail as you re filling out the application.
source_blocks.text: FAFSA帮助文本在您填写申请时会更详细地涵盖所有这些情况。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Automatically Transferring Your Tax Information Using the Internal Revenue Service Data Retrieval Tool (IRS DRT)
source_blocks.text: 使用美国国税局数据检索工具（IRS DRT）自动转移您的税务信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: The IRS DRT automatically transfers tax information into the FAFSA form. Be sure to consider this option if it s offered to you. (If you got an extension on filing your taxes and didn t file until September or October, find out when your tax return information will likely be available using the IRS DRT.)
source_blocks.text: IRS DRT会自动将税务信息转移到FAFSA表格中。如果提供此选项，请务必考虑使用。（如果您申请了报税延期，直到9月或10月才报税，请了解您的纳税申报信息何时可能通过IRS DRT获取。）

source_blocks.source_text_en: Try This ResourceSimple Steps to Transfer Tax Information Into Your FAFSA Form graphic Explains how to use the IRS Data Retrieval Tool to transfer tax information into the FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 尝试此资源将税务信息转入FAFSA表格的简单步骤图形说明如何使用IRS数据检索工具将税务信息转入FAFSA表格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here s how the IRS DRT process works, assuming your tax information is available:
source_blocks.text: 以下是IRS DRT流程的工作原理，假设您的税务信息可用：

source_blocks.source_text_en: The IRS DRT takes you to the IRS website, where you ll need to provide your name and other information exactly as you provided it on your tax return. Some information will be prepopulated from your FAFSA form. At the IRS site, you ll see a page that indicates that your tax information is available. (For security and privacy protections, you won t see the actual information.) You can choose to import your information into the FAFSA form, or you can cancel your request and return to the FAFSA site. If you choose to import your information into the FAFSA form, you ll find that on the FAFSA site, instead of your tax information being displayed, you ll see Transferred from the IRS" in the appropriate fields. You won t be able to make changes to those answers.
source_blocks.text: IRS DRT会将您带到IRS网站，您需要提供与纳税申报表上完全一致的姓名和其他信息。部分信息将从您的FAFSA表格中预填。 在IRS网站上，您会看到一个页面，表明您的税务信息可用。（出于安全和隐私保护，您不会看到实际信息。）您可以选择将信息导入FAFSA表格，也可以取消请求并返回FAFSA网站。 如果您选择将信息导入FAFSA表格，您会发现FAFSA网站上不会显示您的税务信息，而是在相应字段中显示“已从IRS转移”。您将无法更改这些答案。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Using the IRS DRT saves you time and effort:
source_blocks.text: 使用IRS DRT可以节省您的时间和精力：

source_blocks.source_text_en: You don t have to find your tax records. You don t have to worry about making mistakes entering your tax information on your FAFSA form. You may not need to provide an IRS tax transcript or a signed copy of your income tax return if you re selected for verification.
source_blocks.text: 您无需查找税务记录。 您无需担心在FAFSA表格上输入税务信息时出错。 如果您被选中进行验证，您可能无需提供IRS税务记录或所得税申报表的签名副本。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can I change the tax return information that I transfer into the FAFSA form via the IRS DRT?
source_blocks.text: 我可以通过IRS DRT更改转入FAFSA表格的纳税申报信息吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: No. Information you transfer via the IRS DRT can t be changed. Remember, the information transferred is coming from your filed tax return, so it shouldn t need to be changed. If your financial situation has changed or you filed a 1040X amended return, contact your school s financial aid office to discuss whether it would be appropriate for the school to adjust the information on your FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 不能。通过IRS DRT转移的信息无法更改。请记住，转移的信息来自您已提交的纳税申报表，因此不应需要更改。如果您的财务状况发生变化或您提交了1040X修订申报表，请联系您学校的助学金办公室，讨论学校是否适合调整您FAFSA表格上的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If I ve transferred my tax return information into the FAFSA form via the IRS DRT, and then decide I want to enter the information manually instead, can I clear the information that was transferred via the DRT?
source_blocks.text: 如果我已通过IRS DRT将纳税申报信息转入FAFSA表格，但后来决定改为手动输入信息，我可以清除通过DRT转移的信息吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: We strongly discourage clearing the information. The IRS DRT remains the fastest, most accurate way to input your tax return information into the FAFSA form. Additionally, using the IRS DRT to enter your tax information into the FAFSA form may reduce the amount of paperwork you need to provide to your school later.
source_blocks.text: 我们强烈建议不要清除信息。IRS DRT仍然是向FAFSA表格输入纳税申报信息最快、最准确的方式。此外，使用IRS DRT将税务信息输入FAFSA表格可能会减少您日后需要向学校提供的文书工作。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If, despite this, you still want to clear the information transferred via the IRS DRT and enter your tax information manually and you haven t submitted the application or correction yet you can select the Reset FAFSA button at the top of the page (or in the menu at the upper right of the mobile app screen). Just know that by doing so, the entire application or correction will be cleared, and you will have to start the entire application or correction over again.
source_blocks.text: 尽管如此，如果您仍然希望清除通过IRS DRT转移的信息并手动输入税务信息，且尚未提交申请或更正，您可以选择页面顶部的“重置FAFSA”按钮（或在移动应用屏幕右上角的菜单中）。请注意，这样做将清除整个申请或更正，您将不得不重新开始整个申请或更正。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If I enter my tax information manually, will I be able to see it?
source_blocks.text: 如果我手动输入税务信息，我能看到它吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes. Tax return information that s entered manually will be visible on fafsa.gov, in the mobile app, and on your Student Aid Report.
source_blocks.text: 可以。手动输入的纳税申报信息将在fafsa.gov、移动应用和您的学生资助报告上可见。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Signing and Submitting the FAFSA Form
source_blocks.text: 签署并提交FAFSA表格

source_blocks.source_text_en: Before your FAFSA form can be processed, you ll need to sign and submit the application. Here are some tips as you finish your FAFSA form:
source_blocks.text: 在您的FAFSA表格得到处理之前，您需要签署并提交申请。以下是完成FAFSA表格时的一些提示：

source_blocks.source_text_en: To ensure the application functions properly, make sure the pop-up blocker in your browser allows pop-ups from fafsa.ed.gov. Learn how to enable pop-ups in your browser. Be sure to sign with your FSA ID (your username and password) so your FAFSA form will be processed as quickly as possible. (If you log in to the form by providing your FSA ID, you won t be asked for it again when it s time to sign. However, if you re providing parent information, one of your parents will be required to sign your application.) While your online FAFSA form will be processed much quicker if you (and your parent if you re a dependent student) sign your FAFSA form with your FSA ID, you have the option to print out, sign, and mail in a signature page to the address listed on the page. Learn more about printing a signature page. Once you see your confirmation page, you ll know you ve successfully submitted your FAFSA form. If you provided an email address on the form, you ll automatically receive the confirmation page by email. There are a few differences between the emailed confirmation and the one you ll see in the FAFSA form before exiting the application, so consider printing or saving your confirmation page before you exit. For example, the emailed confirmation won t include the college graduation, retention, and transfer rates for schools you listed on your FAFSA form. There are some states that have a partnership with our office that allows you to transfer your information directly into your state aid form (for example, New York residents can use this interface to link directly to the application for the Tuition Assistance Program [TAP]). When you fill out the FAFSA form, you ll have the option to apply with certain state financial aid forms. So, if you see a link from your FAFSA confirmation page to your state financial aid form, you should select it. The link will only appear on the confirmation page within the FAFSA form, so be sure to take advantage of it while you re still in the application. Your confirmation page offers the option for the parent information in your FAFSA form to be transferred automatically into another student s application. So if you have a sibling who needs to fill out a FAFSA form, be sure to use this option when you see your confirmation page. The link will only appear on the confirmation page within the FAFSA form, so be sure to take advantage of it while you re still in the application. Note: If you re filling out the FAFSA form on the myStudentAid app, your parent will only see this option if they sign and submit after you.
source_blocks.text: 为确保申请正常运行，请确保浏览器中的弹出窗口阻止程序允许来自fafsa.ed.gov的弹出窗口。了解如何在浏览器中启用弹出窗口。 请务必使用您的FSA ID（用户名和密码）签署，以便您的FAFSA表格尽快得到处理。（如果您通过提供FSA ID登录表格，签署时将不会再次要求您提供。但是，如果您提供家长信息，您的其中一位家长将被要求签署您的申请。） 虽然如果您（以及如果您是受抚养学生，您的家长）使用FSA ID签署FAFSA表格，在线FAFSA表格的处理速度会快得多，但您也可以选择打印、签署并邮寄签名页至页面上列出的地址。了解更多关于打印签名页的信息。 一旦您看到确认页面，您就知道已成功提交FAFSA表格。如果您在表格中提供了电子邮件地址，您将自动通过电子邮件收到确认页面。电子邮件确认与您在退出申请前在FAFSA表格中看到的确认之间存在一些差异，因此请考虑在退出前打印或保存确认页面。例如，电子邮件确认不会包含您在FAFSA表格中列出的学校的大学毕业率、保留率和转学率。 有些州与我们办公室建立了合作关系，允许您将信息直接转入州助学金表格（例如，纽约州居民可以使用此界面直接链接到学费援助计划[TAP]的申请）。填写FAFSA表格时，您将可以选择申请某些州财政援助表格。因此，如果您看到FAFSA确认页面到州财政援助表格的链接，您应选择它。该链接只会出现在FAFSA表格内的确认页面上，因此请务必在仍在申请中时利用它。 您的确认页面提供了将FAFSA表格中的家长信息自动转入另一名学生申请的选项。因此，如果您有兄弟姐妹需要填写FAFSA表格，请务必在看到确认页面时使用此选项。该链接只会出现在FAFSA表格内的确认页面上，因此请务必在仍在申请中时利用它。注意：如果您在myStudentAid应用程序上填写FAFSA表格，您的家长只有在您之后签署并提交时才会看到此选项。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Top FAFSA Tips
source_blocks.text: FAFSA重要提示

source_blocks.source_text_en: Read all questions and instructions carefully. Meet deadlines. Check your email (including spam) regularly for any messages from Federal Student Aid or your college.
source_blocks.text: 仔细阅读所有问题和说明。 遵守截止日期。 定期检查您的电子邮件（包括垃圾邮件），以获取联邦学生援助或您所在大学的任何消息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Taking the Next Steps
source_blocks.text: 后续步骤

source_blocks.source_text_en: Once you ve completed your FAFSA form, there are more steps you have to take before you receive financial aid. Make sure you know what happens after you submit your FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 完成FAFSA表格后，在获得财政援助之前，您还需要采取更多步骤。请确保您了解提交FAFSA表格后会发生什么。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Finding and Applying for Scholarships | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 寻找和申请奖学金 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: Find and apply for as many scholarships as you can it s free money for college or career school!
source_blocks.text: 尽可能多地寻找和申请奖学金——这是上大学或职业学校的免费资金！

source_blocks.source_text_en: Start researching early, and meet deadlines, and you may be on your way to scholarship success.
source_blocks.text: 尽早开始研究，并按时提交申请，你可能会在奖学金申请上取得成功。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Scholarships are gifts. They don't need to be repaid. There are thousands of them, offered by schools, employers, individuals, private companies, nonprofits, communities, religious groups, and professional and social organizations.
source_blocks.text: 奖学金是赠款，无需偿还。有数千种奖学金，由学校、雇主、个人、私营公司、非营利组织、社区、宗教团体以及专业和社会组织提供。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What kinds of scholarships are available?
source_blocks.text: 有哪些类型的奖学金？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Some scholarships for college are merit-based. You earn them by meeting or exceeding certain standards set by the scholarship-giver. Merit scholarships might be awarded based on academic achievement or on a combination of academics and a special talent, trait, or interest. Other scholarships are based on financial need.
source_blocks.text: 一些大学奖学金是基于成绩的。你通过达到或超过奖学金提供者设定的某些标准来获得它们。成绩奖学金可能基于学业成就或学业与特殊才能、特质或兴趣的结合来授予。其他奖学金则基于经济需求。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Many scholarships are geared toward particular groups of people; for instance, there are scholarships for women or graduate students. And some are available because of where you or your parent work, or because you come from a certain background (for instance, there are scholarships for military families).
source_blocks.text: 许多奖学金面向特定人群；例如，有面向女性或研究生的奖学金。还有一些奖学金是因为你或你父母的工作地点，或者因为你来自某个特定背景（例如，有面向军人家庭的奖学金）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: A scholarship might cover the entire cost of your tuition, or it might be a one-time award of a few hundred dollars. Either way, it s worth applying for, because it ll help reduce the cost of your education.
source_blocks.text: 奖学金可能覆盖你的全部学费，也可能是一次性几百美元的奖励。无论如何，都值得申请，因为它将有助于降低你的教育成本。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I find scholarships?
source_blocks.text: 如何找到奖学金？

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can learn about scholarships in several ways, including contacting the financial aid office at the school you plan to attend and checking information in a public library or online. But be careful. Make sure scholarship information and offers you receive are legitimate; and remember that you don't have to pay to find scholarships or other financial aid. Check out our information on how to avoid scams.
source_blocks.text: 你可以通过多种方式了解奖学金，包括联系你计划就读学校的财务援助办公室，以及在公共图书馆或网上查看信息。但要小心。确保你收到的奖学金信息和录取通知是合法的；并记住，你不必付费就能找到奖学金或其他财务援助。查看我们关于如何避免诈骗的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Try these free sources of information about scholarships:
source_blocks.text: 尝试这些免费的奖学金信息来源：

source_blocks.source_text_en: the financial aid office at a college or career school a high school or TRIO counselor the U.S. Department of Labor s FREE scholarship search tool your state grant agency your library s reference section foundations, religious or community organizations, local businesses, or civic groups organizations (including professional associations) related to your field of interest ethnicity-based organizations your employer or your parents employers
source_blocks.text: 大学或职业学校的财务援助办公室 高中或TRIO顾问 美国劳工部的免费奖学金搜索工具 你所在州的助学金机构 你图书馆的参考书区 基金会、宗教或社区组织、当地企业或公民团体 与你兴趣领域相关的组织（包括专业协会） 基于族裔的组织 你的雇主或你父母的雇主

source_blocks.source_text_en: When do I apply for scholarships?
source_blocks.text: 我什么时候申请奖学金？

source_blocks.source_text_en: That depends on each scholarship s deadline. Some deadlines are as early as a year before college starts, so if you re in high school now, you should be researching and applying for scholarships during the summer between your junior and senior years. But if you ve missed that window, don t give up! Look at scholarship information to see which ones you can still apply for now.
source_blocks.text: 这取决于每个奖学金的截止日期。有些截止日期早在大学开学前一年，所以如果你现在在读高中，你应该在高二和高三之间的暑假研究和申请奖学金。但如果你错过了那个时间窗口，不要放弃！查看奖学金信息，看看现在还有哪些你可以申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I apply for scholarships?
source_blocks.text: 我如何申请奖学金？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Each scholarship has its own requirements. The scholarship s website should give you an idea of who qualifies for the scholarship and how to apply. Make sure you read the application carefully, fill it out completely, and meet the application deadline.
source_blocks.text: 每个奖学金都有自己的要求。奖学金的网站应该会告诉你谁有资格获得该奖学金以及如何申请。确保你仔细阅读申请表，完整填写，并在申请截止日期前提交。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I get my scholarship money?
source_blocks.text: 我如何获得奖学金资金？

source_blocks.source_text_en: That depends on the scholarship. The money might go directly to your college, where it will be applied to any tuition, fees, or other amounts you owe, and then any leftover funds given to you. Or it might be sent directly to you in a check. The scholarship provider should tell you what to expect when it informs you that you ve been awarded the scholarship. If not, make sure to ask.
source_blocks.text: 这取决于奖学金。资金可能直接支付给你的大学，用于支付你欠下的任何学费、杂费或其他金额，然后剩余的资金会给你。或者可能以支票形式直接寄给你。奖学金提供者在通知你获得奖学金时，应该会告诉你预期情况。如果没有，一定要询问。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How does a scholarship affect my other student aid?
source_blocks.text: 奖学金如何影响我的其他学生资助？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A scholarship will affect your other student aid because all your student aid added together can t be more than your cost of attendance at your college or career school. So, you ll need to let your school know if you ve been awarded a scholarship so that the financial aid office can subtract that amount from your cost of attendance (and from certain other aid, such as loans, that you might have been offered). Then, any amount left can be covered by other financial aid for which you re eligible. Questions? Ask your financial aid office.
source_blocks.text: 奖学金会影响你的其他学生资助，因为你所有学生资助加起来不能超过你在大学或职业学校的出勤成本。因此，如果你获得了奖学金，你需要告知你的学校，以便经济援助办公室从你的出勤成本（以及你可能获得的其他某些援助，如贷款）中减去该金额。然后，剩余的任何金额可以由你有资格获得的其他经济援助来覆盖。有问题吗？请咨询你的经济援助办公室。

source_blocks.text: Gainful Employment Information

source_blocks.source_text_en: Generally, in order to be eligible for funding under the Higher Education Act Title IV student assistance programs, an educational program must lead to a degree at a non-profit or public institution or it must prepare students for "gainful employment in a recognized occupation." Therefore, with very few exceptions, any non-degree program offered by non-profit or public institutions and all educational programs offered at for-profit institutions must lead to gainful employment.
source_blocks.text: Generally, in order to be eligible for funding under the Higher Education Act Title IV student assistance programs, an educational program must lead to a degree at a non-profit or public institution or it must prepare students for "gainful employment in a recognized occupation." Therefore, with very few exceptions, any non-degree program offered by non-profit or public institutions and all educational programs offered at for-profit institutions must lead to gainful employment.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Subpart Q of the Student Assistance General Provisions establishes Debt-to-Earnings rates (D/E rates) to determine whether a gainful employment (GE) program prepares students for gainful employment in a recognized occupation. A D/E rate is based on the typical loan debt and earnings of a cohort of the program s former students who completed the program, usually those who completed during a two-year period concluding two years prior to the D/E rate calculation year. This delay is to account for the ramping up of the students earnings upon completion of the program.
source_blocks.text: Subpart Q of the Student Assistance General Provisions establishes Debt-to-Earnings rates (D/E rates) to determine whether a gainful employment (GE) program prepares students for gainful employment in a recognized occupation. A D/E rate is based on the typical loan debt and earnings of a cohort of the program s former students who completed the program, usually those who completed during a two-year period concluding two years prior to the D/E rate calculation year. This delay is to account for the ramping up of the students earnings upon completion of the program.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Two D/E rates, the Annual Earnings Rate and the Discretionary Income Rate, are calculated for each program as a measure of the ability of program completers to reasonably repay the educational debt incurred for their attendance in the program.
source_blocks.text: Two D/E rates, the Annual Earnings Rate and the Discretionary Income Rate, are calculated for each program as a measure of the ability of program completers to reasonably repay the educational debt incurred for their attendance in the program.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For the Annual Earnings Rate, the numerator is the calculated annual loan payment amount an estimate of the annual loan repayment amount based on the median educational debt of the members of the cohort. The denominator is the higher of the cohort s mean or median earnings obtained from the Social Security Administration (SSA). The Discretionary Income Rate uses the same annual loan payment amount in the numerator as the Annual Earnings Rate but the denominator is the higher of the mean or median earnings minus 150% of the poverty guideline.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Annual Earnings Rates of less than or equal to 8% are considered passing rates. Annual Earnings Rates greater than 8% but less than or equal to 12% are zone rates, and Annual Earnings Rates greater than 12% are failing rates. For the Discretionary Income Rate, rates less than or equal to 20% are passing rates, rates greater than 20% but less than or equal to 30% are zone rates, and rates greater than 30% are failing rates.

source_blocks.source_text_en: As described above, the SSA calculates and returns to the U.S. Department of Education (the Department) the mean and median annual earnings of a cohort of students who completed the GE program during a specified cohort period. At least 10 completers from a program must be matched for SSA to return mean and median earnings information for disclosure purposes, while there must be at least 30 students in the cohort sent to SSA for the Department to calculate D/E rates. In calculating a GE program's D/E rates, the Department uses the higher of the SSA-reported mean or median earnings. SSA does not provide the Department individual earnings data or the identity of any students.

source_blocks.source_text_en: To provide relief to student loan borrowers during the COVID-19 national emergency, federal student loan borrowers are automatically being placed in an administrative forbearance, which allows you to temporarily stop making your monthly loan payments. This suspension of payments will last from March 13, 2020, through Sept. 30, 2020, but you can still make payments if you choose.

If you re pursuing loan forgiveness, any period of deferment or forbearance likely will not count toward your forgiveness requirements. source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have a loan balance of \$30,000 and an interest rate of 6% and you are in forbearance for a year right after you enter repayment, \$1,800 in interest will accrue on your loans. source_blocks.source_text_en: Because interest accrues on your principal balance, capitalization will cause more interest to accrue over time than if you had paid the interest. It will also increase your monthly payment under most repayment plans. In this example, if you were on the Standard Repayment Plan, interest capitalization would increase your monthly payment by \$20 per month and increase the total amount that you would pay by about \$600.

source_blocks.source_text_en: To provide relief during the COVID-19 national emergency, the U.S. Department of Education (ED) has stopped collection activity on defaulted federally owned student loans and/or grant overpayments. In addition, interest is temporarily set at 0% on defaulted federally owned student aid debt. This 0% interest and stopped collections period will last from March 13, 2020, through Sept. 30, 2020. You can still make payments if you choose.

source_blocks.source_text_en: One way to get out of default is to repay the defaulted loan in full, but that's not a practical option for most borrowers. The two main ways to get out of default are loan rehabilitation and loan consolidation. While loan rehabilitation takes several months to complete, you can quickly apply for loan consolidation. However, loan rehabilitation provides certain benefits that are not available through loan consolidation. Take a look at the chart below to compare the benefits of loan rehabilitation versus the benefits of loan consolidation.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you rehabilitate a defaulted loan, the record of the default will be removed from your credit history. However, your credit history will still show late payments that were reported by your loan holder before the loan went into default. If you consolidate a defaulted loan, the record of the default (as well as late payments reported before the loan went into default) will remain in your credit history. Late payments will remain on your credit report for seven years from when they were first reported. It s important that you fully understand loan rehabilitation and loan consolidation before making your decision. Learn more about loan rehabilitation and loan consolidation.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Benefits of Loan Rehabilitation

source_blocks.source_text_en: When your loan is rehabilitated, the default status will be removed from your loan, and collection of payments through wage garnishment or Treasury offset will stop. You ll regain eligibility for benefits that were available on the loan before you defaulted, such as deferment, forbearance, a choice of repayment plans, and loan forgiveness, and you ll be eligible to receive federal student aid. Also, the record of default on the rehabilitated loan will be removed from your credit history. However, your credit history will still show late payments that were reported by your loan holder before the loan went into default.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your eligibility depends on your Expected Family Contribution, your year in school, your enrollment status, and the cost of attendance at the school you will be attending. The financial aid office at your college or career school will determine how much financial aid you are eligible to receive.
source_blocks.text: Your eligibility depends on your Expected Family Contribution, your year in school, your enrollment status, and the cost of attendance at the school you will be attending. The financial aid office at your college or career school will determine how much financial aid you are eligible to receive.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The financial aid staff starts by deciding upon your cost of attendance (COA) at that school. They then consider your Expected Family Contribution (EFC). They subtract your EFC from your COA to determine the amount of your financial need and therefore how much need-based aid you can get. To determine how much non-need-based aid you can get, the school takes your cost of attendance and subtracts any financial aid you ve already been awarded.

To determine how much non-need-based aid you can get, the school takes your cost of attendance and subtracts any financial aid you ve already been awarded.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What does cost of attendance (COA) mean?
source_blocks.text: What does cost of attendance (COA) mean?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your COA is the amount it will cost you to go to school. Most two-year and four-year colleges will calculate your COA to show your total cost for the school year (for instance, for the fall semester plus the spring semester). Schools with programs that last a different period of time (for instance, an 18-month certificate program) might give you a COA that covers a time period other than a year.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What s the Expected Family Contribution (EFC)?
source_blocks.text: What s the Expected Family Contribution (EFC)?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your EFC is an index number that college financial aid staff use to determine how much financial aid you would receive if you were to attend their school. The information you report on your FAFSA form is used to calculate your EFC.
source_blocks.text: Your EFC is an index number that college financial aid staff use to determine how much financial aid you would receive if you were to attend their school. The information you report on your FAFSA form is used to calculate your EFC.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The EFC is calculated according to a formula established by law. Your family's taxed and untaxed income, assets, and benefits (such as unemployment or Social Security) all could be considered in the formula. Also considered are your family size and the number of family members who will attend college or career school during the year. The EFC Formula guide shows exactly how an EFC is calculated.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your EFC is not the amount of money your family will have to pay for college, nor is it the amount of federal student aid you will receive. It is a number used by your school to calculate how much financial aid you are eligible to receive.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Need-based aid is financial aid that you can receive if you have financial need and meet other eligibility criteria. For instance, if your COA is \$16,000 and your EFC is 12000, your financial need is \$4,000; so you aren t eligible for more than \$4,000 in need-based aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How Financial Aid Works
source_blocks.text: 助学金如何运作

source_blocks.source_text_en: For most students planning to attend college or career school, financial aid is essential. We ll walk you through how financial aid works, resources to pay for college, and loan repayment options.
source_blocks.text: 对于大多数计划上大学或职业学校的学生来说，助学金至关重要。我们将向您介绍助学金如何运作、支付大学费用的资源以及贷款还款选项。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Start Planning Early
source_blocks.text: 尽早开始规划

source_blocks.source_text_en: Fill Out the FAFSA Form
source_blocks.text: 填写FAFSA表格

source_blocks.source_text_en: Review Your Aid Offer
source_blocks.text: 查看您的助学金通知

source_blocks.source_text_en: Get Your Aid
source_blocks.text: 获得您的助学金

source_blocks.source_text_en: Graduate and Start Repayment
source_blocks.text: 毕业并开始还款

source_blocks.source_text_en: Start Planning Early
source_blocks.text: 尽早开始规划

source_blocks.source_text_en: Plan how to pay for college before you start. Ask school counselors and the college financial aid office about state, college, and nonprofit grants and scholarships you can apply for. Be sure to meet application deadlines. Start saving before you get to college. Consider prepaid tuition and education savings (529) plans.
source_blocks.text: 在开始之前就计划如何支付大学费用。向学校辅导员和大学财务援助办公室咨询你可以申请的州、大学和非营利组织的助学金和奖学金。务必在申请截止日期前完成申请。在上大学之前就开始储蓄。考虑预付学费和教育储蓄（529）计划。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Fill Out the FAFSA Form
source_blocks.text: 填写FAFSA表格

source_blocks.source_text_en: Before each year of college, apply for federal grants, work-study, and loans with the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form. Your college uses your FAFSA data to determine your federal aid eligibility. Many states and colleges use FAFSA data to award their own aid. After submission, you ll receive your Student Aid Report.
source_blocks.text: 在大学每学年开始前，使用免费申请联邦学生援助（FAFSA）表格申请联邦助学金、勤工助学和贷款。你的大学会使用你的FAFSA数据来确定你是否有资格获得联邦援助。许多州和大学也使用FAFSA数据来发放他们自己的援助。提交后，你将收到学生援助报告。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Review Your Aid Offer
source_blocks.text: 查看你的援助通知

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your aid offer explains the types and amounts of aid a college is offering you, and your expected costs for the year. If you ve been accepted to multiple colleges, compare the costs and aid offers. Accept the aid from the school that's best for you and inform them of other sources of aid (such as scholarships) you expect to receive.
source_blocks.text: 你的援助通知说明了大学向你提供的援助类型和金额，以及你当年的预期费用。如果你被多所大学录取，请比较费用和援助通知。接受最适合你的学校的援助，并告知他们你预计会获得的其他援助来源（如奖学金）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Get Your Aid
source_blocks.text: 获得你的援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: Time to go to school! Your financial aid office will apply your aid to the amount you owe your school and send you the remaining balance to spend on other college costs. One of the requirements to maintain financial aid eligibility is that you must make satisfactory academic progress. And don t forget to complete a FAFSA form each year!
source_blocks.text: 是时候去上学了！你的财务援助办公室会将你的援助用于支付你欠学校的费用，并将剩余余额发放给你，用于其他大学开支。保持财务援助资格的要求之一是，你必须取得令人满意的学业进步。而且别忘了每年都要填写FAFSA表格！

source_blocks.source_text_en: Graduate and Start Repayment
source_blocks.text: 毕业并开始还款

source_blocks.source_text_en: As you prepare to graduate, get ready to repay your student loans. Good news! Federal student loan borrowers have a six-month grace period before you begin making payments. Use this time to get organized and choose a repayment plan. If you start falling behind on your payments, contact your loan servicer to discuss repayment options.
source_blocks.text: 当你准备毕业时，准备好偿还学生贷款。好消息！联邦学生贷款借款人有六个月的宽限期，之后你才开始还款。利用这段时间整理好事务并选择还款计划。如果你开始拖欠还款，请联系你的贷款服务机构讨论还款选项。

source_blocks.text: 查看学生援助报告

source_blocks.text: 领取援助

source_blocks.text: 从你的学校获取援助。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Renew Your FAFSA Form
source_blocks.text: 续签你的FAFSA表格

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reapply each year.
source_blocks.text: 每年重新申请。

source_blocks.text: 探索关于FAFSA表格的信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: The FAFSA form allows students to request federal grants, work-study, and loans, all in one application.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Beyond the FAFSA form, we encourage you to learn about and pursue financial aid resources that do not have to be repaid (grants and scholarships) from states, colleges, and nonprofit organizations.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you filed a FAFSA form using an incorrect SSN, you can correct your SSN by doing one of the following:
source_blocks.text: If you filed a FAFSA form using an incorrect SSN, you can correct your SSN by doing one of the following:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Recommended method: You can submit a new online FAFSA form. In many cases, this is the easiest and fastest option. Note: Submitting a new FAFSA form will change the date your FAFSA form was submitted and processed. Be sure to check your state or school deadlines, because your FAFSA submission date must meet those deadlines in order for you to qualify for state or school aid. You can ask the financial aid office at one of the schools listed on your Student Aid Report (SAR) to change your SSN for you. Least efficient method: You can change your SSN on your paper SAR, sign it, and mail it to the address provided on the SAR. This can take two to three weeks to process. Note: The SSN can t be changed through the paper SAR more than once.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Most information cannot be updated because it must be accurate as of the day you originally signed your FAFSA form. For example, if you spent some of your savings after filing the FAFSA form, you may not update your information to show a change in that amount. You should speak to the financial aid office at the school you plan to attend if there will be a significant change in your or your parent s income for the present year or if your family has other circumstances that cannot be reported on the FAFSA form.

If (and only if) you are selected for verification, you must update your FAFSA form if there is a change in the number of family members in your parents household or in your household. If the number of family members changes as a result of a change in your (the student s) marital status, you must speak to the financial aid office at the school you plan to attend to determine whether you may update the FAFSA form. source_blocks.source_text_en: After you submit your FAFSA form online or on the myStudentAid mobile app, you can check its status immediately. (Note: Only the student can check the status, because the FSA ID username and password are required to log in.) Here s how:
source_blocks.text: After you submit your FAFSA form online or on the myStudentAid mobile app, you can check its status immediately. (Note: Only the student can check the status, because the FSA ID username and password are required to log in.) Here s how:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Go to fafsa.gov or the myStudentAid mobile app and log in with your FSA ID username and password. The status of your application will be one of the following. - Processing: Your application is still processing. It typically takes three to five days, plus one additional business day to be made available to the schools you listed on the form. - Processed Successfully: Your application was processed successfully. No further action is needed. - Missing Signatures: Your application is missing the required signature(s). - Action Required: Your application requires further action. Contact your school to resolve the issue.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understand the Full Impact of Your FAFSA Application
source_blocks.text: Understand the Full Impact of Your FAFSA Application

source_blocks.source_text_en: Not only is your FAFSA form an application for federal student aid, it also is used in determining your eligibility for certain state and school financial aid.
source_blocks.text: Not only is your FAFSA form an application for federal student aid, it also is used in determining your eligibility for certain state and school financial aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your FAFSA information is shared with the colleges and/or career schools you list on the application. The financial aid office at a school uses your information to figure out how much aid you may receive at that school.
source_blocks.text: Your FAFSA information is shared with the colleges and/or career schools you list on the application. The financial aid office at a school uses your information to figure out how much aid you may receive at that school.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: The school might also have other forms for you to fill out to get school aid, so check with the financial aid office to be sure.
source_blocks.text: Note: The school might also have other forms for you to fill out to get school aid, so check with the financial aid office to be sure.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your information also goes to your state higher education agency, as well as to agencies of the states where your chosen schools are located. Many states have financial aid funds that they give out based on FAFSA information.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Review Your Student Aid Report (SAR)
source_blocks.text: Review Your Student Aid Report (SAR)

source_blocks.source_text_en: The SAR is a summary of the FAFSA data you submitted. You (the student) will get your SAR within three days to three weeks after you submit your FAFSA form. Look over your SAR carefully, make sure you didn t make a mistake on your FAFSA form, and make corrections to your FAFSA data if necessary. Find out more about the SAR, its purpose, how the method you use to file your FAFSA form determines when you ll get the SAR, and what you should do with the SAR.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What Not to Expect from the SAR
source_blocks.text: What Not to Expect from the SAR

source_blocks.source_text_en: The SAR won t tell you how much financial aid you ll get. Also, if you used the Internal Revenue Service Data Retrieval Tool (IRS DRT) when filling out your FAFSA form, the SAR won t show the details of your income and tax information.

source_blocks.source_text_en: So how do you find out how much aid you ll get?
source_blocks.text: So how do you find out how much aid you ll get?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you ve been accepted at a college or career school that you listed on your FAFSA form, the school will calculate your aid and send you an electronic or paper aid offer, sometimes called an award letter, telling you how much aid you re eligible for at the school. The timing of the aid offer varies from school to school and could be as early as winter (awarding for the fall) or as late as immediately before you start school. It depends on when you apply and how the school prefers to schedule awarding of aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Provide Required Verification
source_blocks.text: Provide Required Verification

source_blocks.source_text_en: You might see a note on your SAR saying you ve been selected for verification; or your school might contact you to inform you that you ve been selected. Verification is the process your school uses to confirm that the data reported on your FAFSA form is accurate. If you re selected for verification, your school will request additional documentation that supports the information you reported.
source_blocks.text: You might see a note on your SAR saying you ve been selected for verification; or your school might contact you to inform you that you ve been selected. Verification is the process your school uses to confirm that the data reported on your FAFSA form is accurate. If you re selected for verification, your school will request additional documentation that supports the information you reported.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Don t assume you re being accused of doing anything wrong. Some people are selected for verification at random; and some schools verify all students' FAFSA forms. All you need to do is provide the documentation your school asks for and be sure to do so by the school s deadline, or you won t be able to get financial aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: First, you ll need to understand the aid that s being offered. For instance, is it free money such as a grant or scholarship, or is it a loan that you ll have to pay back? Next, decide what aid you really need, and then respond to the school s aid offer within the deadline set by the school. Learn more about accepting aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn How Your Aid Is Paid Out

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you were offered financial aid and you accepted it, the financial aid staff at your college or career school will explain exactly how and when your aid will be paid out. They ll also tell you whether you need to fill out any more paperwork or meet other requirements. For instance, if you re receiving a federal student loan for the first time, you should expect to be required to sign a promissory note and go through entrance counseling. Be sure to keep in touch with your school s financial aid office so that you understand the whole process of receiving your aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I estimate my payment amount?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Use our Loan Simulator. Loan Simulator provides a comparison of estimated monthly payment amounts for all federal student loan repayment plans, including income-driven plans. This comparison is important because the income-driven plans may not provide you with the lowest payment amount based on your individual circumstances. Your payment may be lower under another repayment plan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How long will I be in repayment under each plan?
source_blocks.text: How long will I be in repayment under each plan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Income-driven repayment plans have different repayment periods.
source_blocks.text: Income-driven repayment plans have different repayment periods.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under all four plans, any remaining loan balance is forgiven if your federal student loans aren't fully repaid at the end of the repayment period. For any income-driven repayment plan, periods of economic hardship deferment, periods of repayment under certain other repayment plans, and periods when your required payment is zero will count toward your total repayment period. Whether you will have a balance left to be forgiven at the end of your repayment period depends on a number of factors, such as how quickly your income rises and how large your income is relative to your debt. Because of these factors, you may fully repay your loan before the end of your repayment period. Your loan servicer will track your qualifying monthly payments and years of repayment and will notify you when you are getting close to the point when you would qualify for forgiveness of any remaining loan balance.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re making payments under an income-driven repayment plan and also working toward loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program, you may qualify for forgiveness of any remaining loan balance after you've made 10 years of qualifying payments, instead of 20 or 25 years. Qualifying payments for the PSLF Program include payments made under any of the income-driven repayment plans.

To qualify, the payment you would be required to make under the PAYE or IBR plan (based on your income and family size) must be less than what you would pay under the Standard Repayment Plan with a 10-year repayment period.

To qualify, the payment you would be required to make under the PAYE or IBR plan (based on your income and family size) must be less than what you would pay under the Standard Repayment Plan with a 10-year repayment period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If the amount you would have to pay under the PAYE or IBR plan (based on your income and family size) is more than what you would have to pay under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan, you wouldn't benefit from having your monthly payment amount based on your income, so you don't qualify. Generally, you'll meet this requirement if your federal student loan debt is higher than your annual discretionary income or represents a significant portion of your annual income.

Generally, you'll meet this requirement if your federal student loan debt is higher than your annual discretionary income or represents a significant portion of your annual income.

source_blocks.source_text_en: In addition to meeting the requirement described above, to qualify for the PAYE Plan you must also be a new borrower. This means that you must have had no outstanding balance on a Direct Loan or FFEL Program loan when you received a Direct Loan or FFEL Program loan on or after Oct. 1, 2007, and you must have received a disbursement of a Direct Loan on or after Oct. 1, 2011.

source_blocks.text: ICR Plan

source_blocks.source_text_en: Any borrower with eligible federal student loans can make payments under this plan.
source_blocks.text: Any borrower with eligible federal student loans can make payments under this plan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: This plan is the only available income-driven repayment option for parent PLUS loan borrowers. Although PLUS loans made to parents can t be repaid under any of the income-driven repayment plans (including the ICR Plan), parent borrowers may consolidate their Direct PLUS Loans or Federal PLUS Loans into a Direct Consolidation Loan and then repay the new consolidation loan under the ICR Plan (though not under any other income-driven plan).

source_blocks.source_text_en: Will I always pay the same amount each month under an income-driven repayment plan?
source_blocks.text: Will I always pay the same amount each month under an income-driven repayment plan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: No. Under all of the income-driven repayment plans, your required monthly payment amount may increase or decrease if your income or family size changes from year to year. Each year you must recertify your income and family size. This means that you must provide your loan servicer with updated income and family size information so that your servicer can recalculate your payment. You must do this even if there has been no change in your income or family size.

Each year you must recertify your income and family size. You must do this even if there has been no change in your income or family size.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your loan servicer will send you a reminder notice when it s time for you to recertify. To recertify, you must submit another income-driven repayment plan application. On the application, you ll be asked to select the reason you re submitting the application. Respond that you are submitting documentation of your income for the annual recertification of your payment amount.

On the application, you ll be asked to select the reason you re submitting the application. Respond that you are submitting documentation of your income for the annual recertification of your payment amount.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Although you re required to recertify your income and family size only once each year, if your income or family size changes significantly before your annual certification date (for example, due to loss of employment), you can submit updated information and ask your servicer to recalculate your payment amount at any time. To do this, submit a new application for an income-driven repayment plan. When asked to select the reason for submitting the application, respond that you are submitting documentation early because you want your servicer to recalculate your payment immediately.

If you choose to wait, your current required monthly payment amount will remain the same until you provide the updated income information.

source_blocks.source_text_en: PAYE and IBR Plans
source_blocks.text: PAYE and IBR Plans

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under these plans, your monthly payment amount will be based on your income and family size when you first begin making payments, and at any time when your income is low enough that your calculated monthly payment amount would be less than the amount you would have to pay under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan.
source_blocks.text: Under these plans, your monthly payment amount will be based on your income and family size when you first begin making payments, and at any time when your income is low enough that your calculated monthly payment amount would be less than the amount you would have to pay under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your income ever increases to the point that your calculated monthly payment amount would be more than what you would have to pay under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan, you ll remain on the PAYE or IBR plan, but your payment will no longer be based on your income. Instead, your required monthly payment will be the amount you would pay under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan, based on the loan amount you owed when you first began repayment under the PAYE or IBR plan. Even if your income continues to increase, your monthly payment will never be more than the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan amount.

Instead, your required monthly payment will be the amount you would pay under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan, based on the loan amount you owed when you first began repayment under the PAYE or IBR plan. Even if your income continues to increase, your monthly payment will never be more than the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan amount.

source_blocks.source_text_en: During any period when your monthly payment is not based on your income, you still have the option of recertifying your income and family size. If you recertify and your income or family size changes so that your calculated monthly payment would once again be less than the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan amount, your servicer will recalculate your payment and you ll return to making payments that are based on your income.

source_blocks.source_text_en: REPAYE and ICR Plans
source_blocks.text: REPAYE and ICR Plans

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under the REPAYE and ICR Plans, your payment is always based on your income and family size, regardless of any changes in your income. This means that if your income increases over time, in some cases your payment may be higher than the amount you would have to pay under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan.

This means that if your income increases over time, in some cases your payment may be higher than the amount you would have to pay under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What will happen if I don t recertify my income and family size by the annual deadline?
source_blocks.text: What will happen if I don t recertify my income and family size by the annual deadline?

source_blocks.source_text_en: It s important for you to recertify your income and family size by the specified annual deadline. If you don t recertify your income by the deadline, the consequences vary depending on the plan.
source_blocks.text: It s important for you to recertify your income and family size by the specified annual deadline. If you don t recertify your income by the deadline, the consequences vary depending on the plan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under the REPAYE Plan, if you don t recertify your income by the annual deadline, you ll be removed from the REPAYE Plan and placed on an alternative repayment plan. Under this alternative repayment plan, your required monthly payment is not based on your income. Instead, your payment will be the amount necessary to repay your loan in full by the earlier of (a) 10 years from the date you begin repaying under the alternative repayment plan, or (b) the ending date of your 20- or 25-year REPAYE Plan repayment period. You may choose to leave the alternative repayment plan and repay under any other repayment plan for which you are eligible. Under the PAYE Plan, the IBR Plan, or the ICR Plan, if you don t recertify your income by the annual deadline, you ll remain on the same income-driven repayment plan, but your monthly payment will no longer be based on your income. Instead, your required monthly payment amount will be the amount you would pay under a Standard Repayment Plan with a 10-year repayment period, based on the loan amount you owed when you initially entered the income-driven repayment plan. You can return to making payments based on income if you provide your servicer with updated income information, and if your updated income still qualifies you to make payments based on income.

Under this alternative repayment plan, your required monthly payment is not based on your income. Instead, your payment will be the amount necessary to repay your loan in full by the earlier of (a) 10 years from the date you begin repaying under the alternative repayment plan, or (b) the ending date of your 20- or 25-year REPAYE Plan repayment period. You may choose to leave the alternative repayment plan and repay under any other repayment plan for which you are eligible. Under the PAYE Plan, the IBR Plan, or the ICR Plan, if you don t recertify your income by the annual deadline, you ll remain on the same income-driven repayment plan, but your monthly payment will no longer be based on your income. Instead, your required monthly payment amount will be the amount you would pay under a Standard Repayment Plan with a 10-year repayment period, based on the loan amount you owed when you initially entered the income-driven repayment plan. You can return to making payments based on income if you provide your servicer with updated income information, and if your updated income still qualifies you to make payments based on income.

source_blocks.source_text_en: In addition to the consequences described above, if you don t recertify your income by the annual deadline under the REPAYE, PAYE, and IBR plans, any unpaid interest will be capitalized (added to the principal balance of your loans). This will increase the total cost of your loans over time, because you will then pay interest on the increased loan principal balance.

This will increase the total cost of your loans over time, because you will then pay interest on the increased loan principal balance.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under all of the income-driven repayment plans, if you don t recertify your family size each year, you ll remain on the same repayment plan, but your servicer will assume that you have a family size of one. If your actual family size is larger, but your servicer assumes a family size of one because you didn t recertify your family size, this could result in an increased monthly payment amount or (for the PAYE and IBR plans) loss of eligibility to make payments based on income.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Is an income-driven repayment plan right for me?
source_blocks.text: Is an income-driven repayment plan right for me?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Income-driven repayment plans usually lower your federal student loan payments. However, whenever you make lower payments or extend your repayment period, you will likely pay more in interest over time sometimes significantly more. In addition, under current Internal Revenue Service rules, you may be required to pay income tax on any amount that's forgiven if you still have a remaining balance at the end of your repayment period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I decide which income-driven repayment plan to choose?
source_blocks.text: How do I decide which income-driven repayment plan to choose?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you ve decided that an income-driven repayment plan is right for you, you ll want to choose the plan that provides the most benefit to you based on your individual circumstances. Although all four income-driven plans allow you to make a monthly payment based on your income, the plans differ in terms of who qualifies, how much you have to pay each month, the length of the repayment period, and the types of loans that can be repaid under the plan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have only Direct Loans, you can choose from all four income-driven repayment plans. If you re not sure which plan to choose, you have the option of requesting the income-driven plan that provides the lowest payment amount. Your servicer will determine which plans you qualify for and will then place you on the plan with the lowest monthly payment.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have FFEL Program loans, your only income-driven repayment plan option is the IBR Plan. However, if you consolidate your FFEL Program loans into a Direct Consolidation Loan, you ll then have access to the REPAYE, PAYE, and ICR plans. Find out more about loan consolidation.

source_blocks.text: How do I apply for an income-driven repayment plan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Before you apply for an income-driven repayment plan, contact your loan servicer if you have any questions. Your loan servicer will help you decide whether one of these plans is right for you.
source_blocks.text: Before you apply for an income-driven repayment plan, contact your loan servicer if you have any questions. Your loan servicer will help you decide whether one of these plans is right for you.

source_blocks.source_text_en: To apply, you must submit an application called the Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request. You can submit the application online or on a paper form, which you can get from your loan servicer. The application allows you to select an income-driven repayment plan by name, or to request that your loan servicer determine what income-driven plan or plans you qualify for, and to place you on the income-driven plan with the lowest monthly payment amount.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The IT Dashboard was launched on June 1, 2009, to provide Federal agencies and the public with the ability to view details of Federal Information Technology (IT) investments online and to track their progress over time. The IT Dashboard displays data received from agency IT Portfolio and Business Case reports, including general information on over 7,000 Federal IT investments and detailed data for over 700 of those investments that agencies classify as "major."
