source_blocks.source_text_en: Lifecycle Management Methodology
source_blocks.text: 生命周期管理方法论

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Lifecycle Management Methodology comprises a comprehensive process for managing information technology projects from vision to retirement. The methodology is composed of eight distinct stages, each of which guides project managers through the LMM process by identifying a core/minimum set of deliverables to be created in order to ensure a project's viability. This methodology promotes an incremental and iterative approach that fosters the development of complex solutions by breaking them down into small, manageable phases. The intent of implementing and following the LMM is to maximize project outcomes and minimize the risks traditionally associated with IT solution development projects.
source_blocks.text: 生命周期管理方法论包含了一个全面的流程，用于管理信息技术项目从愿景到退役的全过程。该方法论由八个不同的阶段组成，每个阶段通过确定要创建的核心/最低限度的可交付成果集来指导项目经理完成LMM流程，以确保项目的可行性。该方法论提倡增量式和迭代式的方法，通过将复杂解决方案分解为小而可管理的阶段来促进其开发。实施并遵循LMM的目的是最大化项目成果，并最小化传统上与IT解决方案开发项目相关的风险。

source_blocks.source_text_en: This section of the IT Standards Library highlights federal organizations involved in establishing and coordinating the implementation of federal laws, regulations, standards and guidelines applicable to information and information technology management. The standards and guidelines they promulgate apply to all federal agencies and departments. Entities seeking to do business with Federal Student Aid must be cognizant of and apply them.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. Office of Management and Budget's (OMB) predominant mission is to assist the President in overseeing the preparation of the federal budget and to supervise its administration in Executive Branch agencies.
source_blocks.text: 美国管理和预算办公室（OMB）的主要使命是协助总统监督联邦预算的编制，并监督其在行政分支机构中的执行。

source_blocks.source_text_en: OMB oversees and coordinates the Administration's procurement, financial management, information, and regulatory policies, and issues associated instructions to federal agencies.
source_blocks.text: OMB监督并协调政府的采购、财务管理、信息和监管政策，并向联邦机构发布相关指示。

source_blocks.text: 管理和预算办公室

source_blocks.source_text_en: National Institute of Standards and Technology Resources
source_blocks.text: 国家标准与技术研究院资源

source_blocks.source_text_en: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is a non-regulatory federal agency within the U.S. Department of Commerce. NIST's mission is to promote U.S. innovation and industrial competitiveness by advancing measurement science, standards, and technology in ways that enhance economic security and improve our quality of life. The NIST website offers many valuable resources.
source_blocks.text: 国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）是美国商务部下属的一个非监管性联邦机构。NIST的使命是通过推进测量科学、标准和技术，以增强经济安全并提高我们的生活质量，从而促进美国的创新和工业竞争力。NIST网站提供了许多有价值的资源。

source_blocks.source_text_en: NIST's work in the area of information security is of particular interest and relevance to the work of Federal Student Aid. The Federal Information Security Management Act of 2002 (FISMA) charged NIST with developing and issuing standards, guidelines, and other publications to assist federal agencies in implementing the FISMA and in managing cost-effective programs to protect their information and information systems. NIST's Computer Security Resource Center offers extensive resources on this subject matter.
source_blocks.text: NIST在信息安全领域的工作对联邦学生援助的工作特别感兴趣且具有相关性。2002年《联邦信息安全管理法案》（FISMA）责成NIST制定和发布标准、指南及其他出版物，以协助联邦机构实施FISMA并管理具有成本效益的计划，以保护其信息和信息系统。NIST的计算机安全资源中心提供了关于此主题的广泛资源。

source_blocks.source_text_en: National Institute of Standards and Technology Federal Information Security Management Act of 2002 Computer Security Resource Center
source_blocks.text: 国家标准与技术研究院 2002年《联邦信息安全管理法案》 计算机安全资源中心

source_blocks.source_text_en: U.S. General Services Administration Office of Government-wide Policy
source_blocks.text: 美国总务管理局政府范围内政策办公室

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. General Services Administration's (GSA) government-wide policymaking authority covers the areas of personal and real property, travel and transportation, information technology, regulatory information and use of federal advisory committees, and is carried out by GSA's Office of Governmentwide Policy (OGP).
source_blocks.text: 美国总务管理局（GSA）的政府范围内政策制定权限涵盖个人和不动产、旅行和交通、信息技术、监管信息及联邦咨询委员会的使用等领域，并由GSA的政府范围内政策办公室（OGP）执行。

source_blocks.source_text_en: OGP provides leadership in the development of a policy environment and key enablers for electronic government, and supports OMB in the implementation of various E-Gov initiatives to standardize and streamline government processes.
source_blocks.text: OGP在制定电子政务的政策环境和关键推动因素方面发挥领导作用，并支持OMB实施各项电子政务倡议，以标准化和简化政府流程。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Among other initiatives, OGP sponsors http://www.section508.gov, a website devoted to disseminating information regarding Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. Section 508 of the Act requires federal agencies to make their electronic and information technology accessible to people with disabilities.
source_blocks.text: 在其他倡议中，OGP赞助了http://www.section508.gov，这是一个专门传播关于经修订的1973年《康复法案》第508条信息的网站。该法案第508条要求联邦机构使其电子和信息技术对残障人士可访问。

source_blocks.text: 政府范围内政策办公室 Section508.gov

source_blocks.source_text_en: While completing the FAFSA form, you must list at least one college to receive your information.
source_blocks.text: While completing the FAFSA form, you must list at least one college to receive your information.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The schools you list will use your FAFSA information to determine the types and amounts of aid you may receive.
source_blocks.text: The schools you list will use your FAFSA information to determine the types and amounts of aid you may receive.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The information you report on the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form is sent to each school you list. (Use the Federal School Code Search to find the colleges you re interested in including on your FAFSA form.) You don t need to apply for admission to a school before you list it on your FAFSA form; you can list all the schools to which you have applied or might apply. source_blocks.source_text_en: Loan Repayment Checklist | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: Loan Repayment Checklist | Federal Student Aid

source_blocks.source_text_en: Are you a federal student loan borrower? Are you confused about the student loan repayment process?
source_blocks.text: Are you a federal student loan borrower? Are you confused about the student loan repayment process?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Don t let the student loan repayment process overwhelm you. Use this checklist to help you manage and repay your federal student loans.
source_blocks.text: Don t let the student loan repayment process overwhelm you. Use this checklist to help you manage and repay your federal student loans.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Be an informed borrower by learning about your loans and what to do for a smooth repayment experience. As you work through this checklist, you ll find out how to make payments and figure out which repayment plan is best for you; and you ll know what to do if you re having trouble making payments or think you might be eligible for loanforgiveness.
source_blocks.text: Be an informed borrower by learning about your loans and what to do for a smooth repayment experience. As you work through this checklist, you ll find out how to make payments and figure out which repayment plan is best for you; and you ll know what to do if you re having trouble making payments or think you might be eligible for loanforgiveness.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Remember: You never have to pay for help with your student loans!
source_blocks.text: Remember: You never have to pay for help with your student loans!

source_blocks.source_text_en: Before You Graduate or Leave School
source_blocks.text: Before You Graduate or Leave School

source_blocks.source_text_en: Review your federal student loan history. Get your loan history by logging in to "My Federal Student Aid" you ll need to create an FSA ID if you don t already have one. As you review your information, note the following:
source_blocks.text: Review your federal student loan history. Get your loan history by logging in to "My Federal Student Aid" you ll need to create an FSA ID if you don t already have one. As you review your information, note the following:

source_blocks.source_text_en: The current loan balance and interest rate for each loan The loan type (depending on when you went to school and what loan programs your school participated in, you may have loans from different federal student loan programs; the types of loans you received can affect what benefits are available to you) The name of the loan servicer for each loan (a loan servicer is a company that handles the billing and other services on your loans; generally, you ll have one servicer for all your federal student loans, but there is a chance you could have more than one)
source_blocks.text: The current loan balance and interest rate for each loan The loan type (depending on when you went to school and what loan programs your school participated in, you may have loans from different federal student loan programs; the types of loans you received can affect what benefits are available to you) The name of the loan servicer for each loan (a loan servicer is a company that handles the billing and other services on your loans; generally, you ll have one servicer for all your federal student loans, but there is a chance you could have more than one)

source_blocks.source_text_en: Get to know your loan servicer. Your servicer helps you with your student loans for FREE! It s important that you know who your loan servicer is and how to contact them because you will eventually be making your loan payments to your servicer. Take this opportunity to save your servicer s phone number in your phone.
source_blocks.text: Get to know your loan servicer. Your servicer helps you with your student loans for FREE! It s important that you know who your loan servicer is and how to contact them because you will eventually be making your loan payments to your servicer. Take this opportunity to save your servicer s phone number in your phone.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Create an online account on your servicer s website. You can find the most detailed and up-to-date information about your loans, make your payments, and manage your loans (for example, change repayment plans or apply for a deferment) on your loan servicer s website. When you create your account, be sure your contact information is correct.
source_blocks.text: Create an online account on your servicer s website. You can find the most detailed and up-to-date information about your loans, make your payments, and manage your loans (for example, change repayment plans or apply for a deferment) on your loan servicer s website. When you create your account, be sure your contact information is correct.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete mandatory exit counseling. All federal student loan borrowers must complete exit counseling. Exit counseling provides important information you need to help you prepare for repayment of your loans. Check with your school to find out how they want you to complete exit counseling. Schools have different requirements.
source_blocks.text: Complete mandatory exit counseling. All federal student loan borrowers must complete exit counseling. Exit counseling provides important information you need to help you prepare for repayment of your loans. Check with your school to find out how they want you to complete exit counseling. Schools have different requirements.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you can afford it, make loan payments while you re in school, especially if your loans are accruing interest. Making payments early can reduce the interest you pay and the cost of your loan over time.
source_blocks.text: If you can afford it, make loan payments while you re in school, especially if your loans are accruing interest. Making payments early can reduce the interest you pay and the cost of your loan over time.

source_blocks.source_text_en: After You Graduate or Leave School
source_blocks.text: After You Graduate or Leave School

source_blocks.source_text_en: Know when you have to start making payments. For most loans, you ll have six months or nine months for Federal Perkins Loans after you graduate, leave school, or drop below half-time enrollment before you must begin making your loan payments. Take this time to make a plan for repayment.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Create a budget. Create a budget to determine how much you can realistically afford to pay monthly toward your student loans. Get help creating a budget.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Consider loan consolidation. A Direct Consolidation Loan allows you to combine all of your federal student loans into one loan with one monthly payment. Loan consolidation can be helpful if you have multiple servicers, loans from the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program, or Federal Perkins Loans. Loan consolidation can increase your chances of qualifying for an affordable repayment plan and loan forgiveness options, but it may not be the best option for you. Learn more about loan consolidation.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Set a goal for repayment. After you know how much you can afford to pay each month, set a goal for repaying your loans. To begin setting your goal, ask and answer this question: Do I want to repay my loans quickly, or do I want to pay as little as possible per month? You can t choose both options. Any time you lower your payment, you ll be in repayment for a longer time and you ll pay more interest on your loans.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you want to pay your loans off quickly and you can afford to do it, select the Standard Repayment Plan. Unless you consolidate, your loans will be paid off after 10 years of payments.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program: You may qualify for this loan forgiveness program if you are employed by a government or a not-for-profit organization. source_blocks.source_text_en: When It s Time to Start Making Payments
source_blocks.text: When It s Time to Start Making Payments

source_blocks.source_text_en: Make on-time payments to your loan servicer. Your loan servicer will provide you with a loan repayment schedule that tells you when your first payment is due, the number and frequency of payments, and the amount of each payment. Contact your loan servicer if you haven t received this information.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Make repayment simple and save on interest enroll in automatic debit. Once you enroll, your payments will be automatically taken from your bank account each month. source_blocks.source_text_en: Know your options if you can t make your loan payment. If you don t pay the full amount due on time or if you start missing payments even one your loan will be considered delinquent, and late fees may be charged to you. If you can t make your payments, contact your loan servicer immediately for help. Your servicer can offer you temporary or long-term options, such as changing repayment plans, deferment, forbearance, or loan consolidation. Get details about what to do if you are having trouble making your payments.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Who s My Student Loan Servicer?
source_blocks.text: 谁是我的学生贷款服务商？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn about the role that student loan servicers play in the repayment process and which servicer handles your federal student loans.
source_blocks.text: 了解学生贷款服务商在还款过程中扮演的角色，以及哪家服务商负责处理你的联邦学生贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What Loan Servicers Do
source_blocks.text: 贷款服务商做什么

source_blocks.source_text_en: A loan servicer is a company that we assign to handle the billing and other services on your federal student loan on our behalf, at no cost to you. Your loan servicer will work with you on repayment options (such as income-driven repayment plans and loan consolidation) and will assist you with other tasks related to your federal student loans.
source_blocks.text: 贷款服务商是我们指派代表我们处理你的联邦学生贷款账单和其他服务的公司，对你免费。你的贷款服务商会与你合作制定还款方案（如收入驱动还款计划和贷款合并），并协助你处理与联邦学生贷款相关的其他任务。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Keep your contact information up to date so your loan servicer can help you stay on track with repaying your loans. If your circumstances change at any time during your repayment period, your loan servicer will be able to help.
source_blocks.text: 保持你的联系信息最新，以便你的贷款服务商能帮助你按时还款。如果在还款期间的任何时候你的情况发生变化，你的贷款服务商将能够提供帮助。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Never pay an outside company for help with your federal student loans. Your loan servicer will help you for FREE. Contact your servicer to apply for income-driven repayment plans, student loan forgiveness, and more.
source_blocks.text: 切勿为联邦学生贷款寻求外部公司的付费帮助。你的贷款服务商会免费为你提供帮助。联系你的服务商以申请收入驱动还款计划、学生贷款减免等。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Loan Servicer Assignment
source_blocks.text: 贷款服务商分配

source_blocks.source_text_en: We will assign your loan to a loan servicer after your loan amount is first disbursed (paid out). Your loan servicer will contact you after that.
source_blocks.text: 在你的贷款金额首次发放（支付）后，我们会将你的贷款分配给贷款服务商。之后，你的贷款服务商会与你联系。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Identifying Your Servicer
source_blocks.text: 识别你的服务商

source_blocks.source_text_en: The following are loan servicers for loans that the U.S Department of Education (ED) owns. To find out who your loan servicer is, call the Federal Student Aid Information Center (FSAIC) at 1-800-433-3243.
source_blocks.text: 以下是美国教育部（ED）拥有的贷款的贷款服务商。要了解你的贷款服务商是谁，请致电联邦学生援助信息中心（FSAIC），电话：1-800-433-3243。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Whom to Contact for Loan Information
source_blocks.text: 贷款信息联系谁

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your loan is for the current or upcoming school year, contact your school s financial aid office directly for information about
source_blocks.text: 如果你的贷款是针对当前或即将到来的学年，请直接联系你学校的财务援助办公室以获取以下信息：

source_blocks.source_text_en: loan status, the timeframes for cancelling all or part of your loan or loan disbursement, and loan disbursement amounts and timing.
source_blocks.text: 贷款状态， 取消全部或部分贷款或贷款发放的时间范围，以及 贷款发放金额和时间。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Only your school's financial aid office can provide this information.
source_blocks.text: 只有你学校的财务援助办公室能提供这些信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your loan was disbursed in a past school year and you re still in school, keep your contact information up to date with your school and contact your loan servicer when you
source_blocks.text: 如果你的贷款是在过去的学年发放的，而你仍在就读，请保持你的联系信息在学校最新，并在以下情况时联系你的贷款服务商：

source_blocks.source_text_en: withdraw, graduate, drop below half-time enrollment, or stop going to school.
source_blocks.text: 退学， 毕业， 注册状态降至半日制以下，或 停止上学。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re no longer in school, contact your loan servicer when you
source_blocks.text: 如果你不再就读，请在以下情况时联系你的贷款服务商：

source_blocks.source_text_en: change your name, address, or phone number; need help making your loan payment; have a question about your bill; or have other questions about your student loan.
source_blocks.text: 更改您的姓名、地址或电话号码； 需要帮助偿还贷款； 对账单有疑问；或 有其他关于学生贷款的问题。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Contact Information for Loans Not Owned by ED
source_blocks.text: 非教育部拥有的贷款的联系信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have FFEL Program loans that are not owned by ED, contact your servicer for details about repayment options and tools. Not sure who your servicer is? Look for the most recent communication from the entity sending you bills for your loan payments.
source_blocks.text: 如果您有非教育部拥有的联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划贷款，请联系您的贷款服务机构，了解还款选项和工具的详细信息。不确定您的服务机构是谁？请查找最近发送给您贷款还款账单的实体发来的通信。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have Federal Perkins Loans that are not owned by ED, contact the school where you received your Federal Perkins Loan for details about repaying your loan. Your school may be the servicer for your loan.
source_blocks.text: 如果您有非教育部拥有的联邦帕金斯贷款，请联系您获得联邦帕金斯贷款的学校，了解还款详情。您的学校可能是您贷款的服务机构。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have HEAL Program loans and you re not in default, contact your loan servicer for help with account-related questions. Use the contact information your loan servicer provided to you. Not sure who your servicer is? Look for the most recent communication from the entity sending you bills for your loan payments.
source_blocks.text: 如果您有卫生教育援助贷款（HEAL）计划贷款且未违约，请联系您的贷款服务机构，获取与账户相关问题的帮助。请使用您的贷款服务机构提供的联系信息。不确定您的服务机构是谁？请查找最近发送给您贷款还款账单的实体发来的通信。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have HEAL Program loans and you re in default, contact the Debt Collection Center for help with account-related questions:
source_blocks.text: 如果您有卫生教育援助贷款（HEAL）计划贷款且已违约，请联系债务催收中心，获取与账户相关问题的帮助：

source_blocks.source_text_en: For mail sent via U.S. Postal Service:
source_blocks.text: 通过美国邮政服务寄送邮件：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Accounting Services, Debt Collection Center Mailstop 10230B 7700 Wisconsin Avenue, Suite 8-8110D Bethesda, MD 20857
source_blocks.text: 会计服务部，债务催收中心 Mailstop 10230B 7700 Wisconsin Avenue, Suite 8-8110D Bethesda, MD 20857

source_blocks.source_text_en: For mail sent via UPS or FedEx:
source_blocks.text: 通过UPS或FedEx寄送邮件：

source_blocks.source_text_en: HHS Program Support Center Accounting Services, Debt Collection Center Mailstop Seventh Floor 7700 Wisconsin Avenue, Suite 8-8110D Bethesda, MD 20814Phone: 301-492-4664
source_blocks.text: HHS项目支持中心 会计服务部，债务催收中心 Mailstop 第七层 7700 Wisconsin Avenue, Suite 8-8110D Bethesda, MD 20814电话：301-492-4664

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understanding Loan Transfers
source_blocks.text: 了解贷款转移

source_blocks.source_text_en: In some cases, we need to transfer loans from one servicer to another servicer. If we transfer your federal student loans from one servicer to another servicer, your loans will still be owned by ED. The transfer to another servicer simply means that a new servicer will provide the support you need to fully repay your loans.
source_blocks.text: 在某些情况下，我们需要将贷款从一个服务机构转移到另一个服务机构。如果我们把您的联邦学生贷款从一个服务机构转移到另一个服务机构，您的贷款仍归教育部所有。转移到另一个服务机构仅意味着新的服务机构将为您提供全额偿还贷款所需的支持。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here s what you should expect if your loan is transferred to a new servicer:
source_blocks.text: 如果您的贷款被转移到新的服务机构，您应该预期以下情况：

source_blocks.source_text_en: You will receive an email or a letter from your assigned servicer to inform you about the transfer. You will receive a welcome letter from the new servicer after the new servicer receives your loans. This notice will provide you with the contact information for the new servicer and inform you of actions that you may need to take. All of your loan information will be transferred from your assigned servicer to your new servicer, but you may only be able to see online information that covers the period since your new servicer took your loans over. There will be no change in the terms of your loans. Your previous loan servicer and new loan servicer will work together to make sure that all payments you make during the transfer process are credited to your loan account with the new servicer.
source_blocks.text: 您将收到指定服务机构发送的电子邮件或信件，告知您转移事宜。 新服务机构收到您的贷款后，您将收到其欢迎信。此通知将提供新服务机构的联系信息，并告知您可能需要采取的行动。 您的所有贷款信息将从指定服务机构转移到新服务机构，但您可能只能看到新服务机构接管您的贷款后的在线信息。 您的贷款条款不会发生变化。 您之前的贷款服务机构和新的贷款服务机构将合作，确保您在转移过程中支付的所有款项都计入您在新服务机构的贷款账户。

source_blocks.source_text_en: After you receive the welcome letter from your new servicer, you should do the following:
source_blocks.text: 收到新服务机构的欢迎信后，您应该执行以下操作：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Begin sending your loan payments to your new servicer. If you use a bank or bill paying service to make your loan payments, update the new servicer s contact information with the bank or bill paying service. Follow the new servicer s instructions for creating an online account so that you can more easily communicate with the new servicer and keep track of your loan account.
source_blocks.text: 开始向新服务机构发送贷款还款。如果您使用银行或账单支付服务进行贷款还款，请更新银行或账单支付服务中新服务机构的联系信息。 按照新服务机构的指示创建在线账户，以便更轻松地与新服务机构沟通并跟踪您的贷款账户。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Avoid Paying for Federal Student Loan Assistance
source_blocks.text: 避免为联邦学生贷款援助付费

source_blocks.source_text_en: You don t have to pay to receive help with loan services such as consolidating your federal student loans or applying for an income-driven repayment plan.
source_blocks.text: 您无需付费即可获得贷款服务方面的帮助，例如合并联邦学生贷款或申请收入驱动还款计划。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are contacted by a company asking you to pay enrollment, subscription, or maintenance fees to enroll you in a federal repayment plan or forgiveness program, you should walk away.
source_blocks.text: 如果有人联系你，要求你支付注册费、订阅费或维护费，以便让你参加联邦还款计划或免除计划，你应该离开。

source_blocks.source_text_en: These services and more can be completed by your servicer for free!
source_blocks.text: 这些服务及更多服务都可以由你的服务商免费完成！

source_blocks.source_text_en: Want to learn more? Read our blog post called Don t Be Fooled: You Never Have to Pay for Student Loan Help.
source_blocks.text: 想了解更多？请阅读我们的博客文章《别被骗了：你永远不必为助学贷款帮助付费》。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal student loans for college or career school are an investment in your future.
source_blocks.text: Federal student loans for college or career school are an investment in your future.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You must repay your loan, so be sure you understand your options and responsibilities.
source_blocks.text: You must repay your loan, so be sure you understand your options and responsibilities.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you apply for financial aid, you may be offered loans as part of your school s financial aid offer. A loan is money you borrow and must pay back with interest.
source_blocks.text: If you apply for financial aid, you may be offered loans as part of your school s financial aid offer. A loan is money you borrow and must pay back with interest.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you decide to take out a loan, make sure you understand who is making the loan and the terms and conditions of the loan. Student loans can come from the federal government, from private sources such as a bank or financial institution, or from other organizations. Loans made by the federal government, called federal student loans, usually have more benefits than loans from banks or other private sources. Learn more about the differences between federal and private student loans.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What types of federal student loans are available?
source_blocks.text: What types of federal student loans are available?

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. Department of Education s federal student loan program is the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program. Under this program, the U.S. Department of Education is your lender. There are four types of Direct Loans available:
source_blocks.text: The U.S. Department of Education s federal student loan program is the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program. Under this program, the U.S. Department of Education is your lender. There are four types of Direct Loans available:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct Subsidized Loans are loans made to eligible undergraduate students who demonstrate financial need to help cover the costs of higher education at a college or career school. Direct Unsubsidized Loans are loans made to eligible undergraduate, graduate, and professional students, but eligibility is not based on financial need. Direct PLUS Loans are loans made to graduate or professional students and parents of dependent undergraduate students to help pay for education expenses not covered by other financial aid. Eligibility is not based on financial need, but a credit check is required. Borrowers who have an adverse credit history must meet additional requirements to qualify. Direct Consolidation Loans allow you to combine all of your eligible federal student loans into a single loan with a single loan servicer.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How much money can I borrow in federal student loans?
source_blocks.text: How much money can I borrow in federal student loans?

source_blocks.source_text_en: It depends on whether you re an undergraduate student, a graduate or professional student, or a parent.
source_blocks.text: It depends on whether you re an undergraduate student, a graduate or professional student, or a parent.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are an undergraduate student, the maximum amount you can borrow each year in Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans ranges from \$5,500 to \$12,500 per year, depending on what year you are in school and your dependency status. If you are a graduate or professional student, you can borrow up to \$20,500 each year in Direct Unsubsidized Loans. Direct PLUS Loans can also be used for the remainder of your college costs, as determined by your school, not covered by other financial aid. If you are a parent of a dependent undergraduate student, you can receive a Direct PLUS Loan for the remainder of your child s college costs, as determined by his or her school, not covered by other financial aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Remember, you can borrow less than your school offers and can request more loan funds later if you need to. You should borrow only what you need.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Why should I take out federal student loans?
source_blocks.text: Why should I take out federal student loans?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal student loans are an investment in your future. You should not be afraid to take out federal student loans, but you should be smart about it.
source_blocks.text: Federal student loans are an investment in your future. You should not be afraid to take out federal student loans, but you should be smart about it.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal student loans offer many benefits compared to other options you may consider when paying for college:
source_blocks.text: Federal student loans offer many benefits compared to other options you may consider when paying for college:

source_blocks.source_text_en: The interest rate on federal student loans is fixed and usually lower than that on private loans and much lower than that on a credit card! You don t need a credit check or a cosigner to get most federal student loans. You don t have to begin repaying your federal student loans until after you leave college or drop below half-time. If you demonstrate financial need, the government pays the interest on some loan types while you are in school and during some periods after school. Federal student loans offer flexible repayment plans and options to postpone your loan payments if you re having trouble making payments. If you work in certain jobs, you may be eligible to have a portion of your federal student loans forgiven if you meet certain conditions.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What should I consider when taking out federal student loans?
source_blocks.text: What should I consider when taking out federal student loans?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Before you take out a loan, it s important to understand that a loan is a legal obligation that makes you responsible for repaying the amount you borrow with interest. Even though you don t have to begin repaying your federal student loans right away, you shouldn t wait to understand your responsibilities as a borrower. Get the scoop: Watch this video about responsible borrowing or browse the tips below it.

Even though you don t have to begin repaying your federal student loans right away, you shouldn t wait to understand your responsibilities as a borrower. Get the scoop: Watch this video about responsible borrowing or browse the tips below it.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Be a responsible borrower.
source_blocks.text: Be a responsible borrower.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Keep track of how much you re borrowing. Think about how the amount of your loans will affect your future finances, and how much you can afford to repay. Your student loan payments should be only a small percentage of your salary after you graduate, so it s important not to borrow more than you need for your school-related expenses. Research starting salaries in your field. Ask your school for starting salaries of recent graduates in your field of study to get an idea of how much you are likely to earn after you graduate. You can also use the U.S. Department of Labor's Occupational Outlook Handbook or career search tool to research careers and salaries. Understand the terms of your loan and keep copies of your loan documents. When you sign your promissory note, you are agreeing to repay the loan according to the terms of the note even if you don t complete your education, can t get a job after you complete the program, or you didn t like the education you received. Make payments on time. You are required to make payments on time even if you don t receive a bill, repayment notice, or a reminder. You must pay the full amount required by your repayment plan, as partial payments do not fulfill your obligation to repay your student loan on time. Keep in touch with your loan servicer. Notify your loan servicer when you graduate; withdraw from school; drop below half-time status; transfer to another school; or change your name, address, or Social Security number. You also should contact your servicer if you re having trouble making your scheduled loan payments. Your servicer has several options available to help you keep your loan in good standing.

source_blocks.text: How do I get a federal student loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: To apply for a federal student loan, you must first complete and submit a Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form. Based on the results of your FAFSA form, your college or career school will send you a financial aid offer, which may include federal student loans. Your school will tell you how to accept all or a part of the loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Enrollment in an income-driven repayment plan is good for one year. Before the year is over, you need to recertify your income and family size to stay on the plan. Your federal loan servicer will notify you when it is time to recertify. If you can t afford your current income-driven payments because you ve had a drop in income, you can recertify early to have your new income taken into account right away.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Master Promissory Note (MPN) for Graduate/Professional Students
source_blocks.text: 研究生/专业学生主本票（MPN）

source_blocks.source_text_en: The MPN is a legal document in which you promise to repay your loan(s) and any accrued interest and fees to the U.S. Department of Education. It also explains the terms and conditions of your loan(s).Graduate/professional students may be eligible for both Direct Unsubsidized Loans and Direct PLUS Loans, which have different MPNs. You may receive more than one loan under an MPN over a period of up to 10 years to pay for your educational costs, as long as the school is authorized to use the MPN in this way and chooses to do so. Your school will tell you which loans, if any, you are eligible to receive.

Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program. Some schools may have a different process for obtaining the additional information needed to process your Direct PLUS Loan application.

You will have an opportunity to complete the Direct PLUS Loan MPN after you complete the Direct PLUS Loan Request.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct PLUS Loans are federal loans that parents of dependent undergraduate students can use to help pay for college or career school.
source_blocks.text: Direct PLUS Loans are federal loans that parents of dependent undergraduate students can use to help pay for college or career school.

source_blocks.source_text_en: PLUS loans can help pay for education expenses not covered by other financial aid.
source_blocks.text: PLUS loans can help pay for education expenses not covered by other financial aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. Department of Education makes Direct PLUS Loans to eligible parents through schools participating in the Direct Loan Program. (We also offer PLUS loans for graduate or professional students.)
source_blocks.text: The U.S. Department of Education makes Direct PLUS Loans to eligible parents through schools participating in the Direct Loan Program. (We also offer PLUS loans for graduate or professional students.)

source_blocks.source_text_en: A Direct PLUS Loan is commonly referred to as a parent PLUS loan when made to a parent borrower.
source_blocks.text: A Direct PLUS Loan is commonly referred to as a parent PLUS loan when made to a parent borrower.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Looking to apply? Use the online application to apply for a parent PLUS loan.
source_blocks.text: Looking to apply? Use the online application to apply for a parent PLUS loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Important: Most schools require you to submit the PLUS loan application online, although some schools have different application processes.
source_blocks.text: Important: Most schools require you to submit the PLUS loan application online, although some schools have different application processes.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: Before you apply for a PLUS loan, make sure your child has already filled out the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Am I eligible for a parent PLUS loan?
source_blocks.text: Am I eligible for a parent PLUS loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: To receive a parent PLUS loan, you must
source_blocks.text: To receive a parent PLUS loan, you must

source_blocks.source_text_en: be the biological or adoptive parent (or in some cases, the stepparent) of a dependent undergraduate student enrolled at least half-time at an eligible school; not have an adverse credit history (unless you meet certain additional requirements); and meet the general eligibility requirements for federal student aid. (Your child must also meet these requirements.)

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: Grandparents (unless they have legally adopted the dependent student) and legal guardians are not eligible to receive parent PLUS loans, even if they have had primary responsibility for raising the student.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is the current interest rate?
source_blocks.text: What is the current interest rate?

source_blocks.source_text_en: For Direct PLUS Loans first disbursed on or after July 1, 2019, and before July 1, 2020, the interest rate is 7.08%. This is a fixed interest rate for the life of the loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How much can I borrow?
source_blocks.text: How much can I borrow?

source_blocks.source_text_en: The maximum PLUS loan amount you can borrow is the cost of attendance at the school your child will attend minus any other financial assistance your child receives. The cost of attendance is determined by the school.
source_blocks.text: The maximum PLUS loan amount you can borrow is the cost of attendance at the school your child will attend minus any other financial assistance your child receives. The cost of attendance is determined by the school.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Do I have to make payments on my loan while my child is still in school?
source_blocks.text: Do I have to make payments on my loan while my child is still in school?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you request a deferment, you will not need to make payments while your child is enrolled at least half-time and for an additional six months after your child graduates, leaves school, or drops below half-time enrollment. If the school your child is attending requires you to submit your request for a parent PLUS loan at StudentAid.gov, you ll have the option of requesting a deferment as part of the loan request process. You can also contact your loan servicer to request a deferment.
source_blocks.text: If you request a deferment, you will not need to make payments while your child is enrolled at least half-time and for an additional six months after your child graduates, leaves school, or drops below half-time enrollment. If the school your child is attending requires you to submit your request for a parent PLUS loan at StudentAid.gov, you ll have the option of requesting a deferment as part of the loan request process. You can also contact your loan servicer to request a deferment.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you do not request a deferment, you will be expected to begin making payments after the loan is fully disbursed (paid out).
source_blocks.text: If you do not request a deferment, you will be expected to begin making payments after the loan is fully disbursed (paid out).

source_blocks.source_text_en: During any period when you re not required to make payments, interest will accrue on your loan. You may choose to pay the accrued interest or allow the interest to be capitalized (added to your loan principal balance) when you have to start making payments. Your loan servicer will notify you when your first payment is due.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can I still receive a parent PLUS loan if I have an adverse credit history?
source_blocks.text: Can I still receive a parent PLUS loan if I have an adverse credit history?

source_blocks.source_text_en: A credit check will be performed during the application process. If you have an adverse credit history, you may still receive a parent PLUS loan through one of these two options:
source_blocks.text: A credit check will be performed during the application process. If you have an adverse credit history, you may still receive a parent PLUS loan through one of these two options:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Obtaining an endorser who does not have an adverse credit history. An endorser is someone who agrees to repay the parent PLUS loan if you do not repay it. The endorser cannot be the child on whose behalf you are borrowing. Documenting to the satisfaction of the U.S. Department of Education that there are extenuating circumstances relating to your adverse credit history.

The endorser cannot be the child on whose behalf you are borrowing. source_blocks.source_text_en: With either option 1 or option 2, you also must complete credit counseling for parent PLUS loan borrowers.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are unable to obtain a parent PLUS loan, your child may be eligible for additional unsubsidized loans. Your child should contact the school s financial aid office for more information.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I apply for a parent PLUS loan?
source_blocks.text: How do I apply for a parent PLUS loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Go to the online Direct PLUS Loan Application for Parents.
source_blocks.text: Go to the online Direct PLUS Loan Application for Parents.

This site has a list of schools that participate in the Direct Loan Program. When you select your child s school from the list, the site will tell you if the school has a different application process. In that case, check with the school s financial aid office to find out how to request a parent PLUS loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What additional steps must I take to receive my loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are eligible for a parent PLUS loan, you will be required to sign a Direct PLUS Loan Master Promissory Note (MPN), agreeing to the terms of the loan. Contact the financial aid office at the school your child is planning to attend for details regarding the process at that school.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re taking out parent PLUS loans for more than one child, you ll need to sign separate Direct PLUS Loan MPNs for the loans you receive for each child.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Other than interest, is there a charge for this loan?
source_blocks.text: Other than interest, is there a charge for this loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes, there is a loan fee on all Direct PLUS Loans. The loan fee is a percentage of the loan amount and is proportionately deducted from each loan disbursement. The percentage varies depending on when the loan is first disbursed, as shown in the chart below.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How will I receive my loan?
source_blocks.text: How will I receive my loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: The school will first apply parent PLUS loan funds to the student s school account to pay for tuition, fees, room and board, and other school charges. If any loan funds remain, your child s school will give them to you to help pay other education expenses for the student. With your authorization, the school can pay the remaining loan funds directly to the student. Get more information about receiving aid.

source_blocks.text: What happens after I receive my loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: After you receive your parent PLUS loan, you will be contacted by your loan servicer (you will repay your loan to the loan servicer). Your loan servicer will provide regular updates on the status of your parent PLUS loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What types of loan repayment plans are available?
source_blocks.text: What types of loan repayment plans are available?

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I have trouble repaying my loan?
source_blocks.text: What if I have trouble repaying my loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are unable to make your scheduled loan payments, contact your loan servicer immediately. Your servicer can help you understand your options for keeping your loan in good standing. For example, you may wish to change your repayment plan to lower your monthly payment or request a deferment or forbearance that allows you to temporarily stop or lower the payments on your loan.Learn more about deferment and forbearance options.

source_blocks.source_text_en: As a parent PLUS loan borrower, can I transfer responsibility for repaying the loan to my child?
source_blocks.text: As a parent PLUS loan borrower, can I transfer responsibility for repaying the loan to my child?

source_blocks.source_text_en: No, a Direct PLUS Loan made to a parent cannot be transferred to the child. You, the parent borrower, are legally responsible for repaying the loan.
source_blocks.text: No, a Direct PLUS Loan made to a parent cannot be transferred to the child. You, the parent borrower, are legally responsible for repaying the loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can I cancel the loan if I decide that I don t need it or if I need less than the amount offered?
source_blocks.text: Can I cancel the loan if I decide that I don t need it or if I need less than the amount offered?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes. Before your loan money is disbursed, you may cancel all or part of your loan at any time by notifying your child s school. After your loan is disbursed, you may cancel all or part of the loan within certain time frames. Your promissory note and additional information you ll receive from the school will explain the procedures and time frames for canceling your loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can my loan ever be forgiven (canceled) or discharged?
source_blocks.text: Can my loan ever be forgiven (canceled) or discharged?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under certain conditions, you may be eligible to have all or part of your loan forgiven (canceled) or discharged. Find out about loan forgiveness, cancellation, and discharge.
source_blocks.text: Under certain conditions, you may be eligible to have all or part of your loan forgiven (canceled) or discharged. Find out about loan forgiveness, cancellation, and discharge.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are seeking Public Service Loan Forgiveness, you will need to repay your loans under an income-driven repayment plan. The Income-Contingent Repayment Plan is the only income-driven repayment plan available to parent PLUS borrowers, and to repay your parent PLUS loans under the Income-Contingent Repayment Plan, you must first consolidate the loans into a Direct Consolidation Loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may be eligible to have all or a portion of your Federal Perkins Loan canceled (based on your employment or volunteer service) or discharged (under certain conditions).

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal Perkins Loancancellation is based on eligible employment or eligible volunteer service and the length of time that you were in such a position. Discharge of your Perkins Loan may occur under certain circumstances.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Perkins Loan Teacher Cancellation
source_blocks.text: Perkins Loan Teacher Cancellation

source_blocks.source_text_en: What are the eligibility requirements?
source_blocks.text: What are the eligibility requirements?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You qualify for cancellation of up to 100 percent of a Federal Perkins Loan if you have served full-time in a public or nonprofit elementary or secondary school system as a
source_blocks.text: You qualify for cancellation of up to 100 percent of a Federal Perkins Loan if you have served full-time in a public or nonprofit elementary or secondary school system as a

source_blocks.source_text_en: teacher in a school serving students from low-income families; special education teacher, including teachers of infants, toddlers, children, or youth with disabilities; or teacher in the fields of mathematics, science, foreign languages, or bilingual education, or in any other field of expertise determined by a state education agency to have a shortage of qualified teachers in that state.
source_blocks.text: teacher in a school serving students from low-income families; special education teacher, including teachers of infants, toddlers, children, or youth with disabilities; or teacher in the fields of mathematics, science, foreign languages, or bilingual education, or in any other field of expertise determined by a state education agency to have a shortage of qualified teachers in that state.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Eligibility for teacher cancellation is based on the duties presented in an official position description, not on the position title. To receive a cancellation, you must be directly employed by the school system. There is no provision for canceling Federal Perkins Loans for teaching in postsecondary schools.
source_blocks.text: Eligibility for teacher cancellation is based on the duties presented in an official position description, not on the position title. To receive a cancellation, you must be directly employed by the school system. There is no provision for canceling Federal Perkins Loans for teaching in postsecondary schools.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note that you also qualify for deferment while you re performing teaching service that qualifies for cancellation. Contact your college or your college s Perkins Loan servicer for information on applying for deferment.
source_blocks.text: Note that you also qualify for deferment while you re performing teaching service that qualifies for cancellation. Contact your college or your college s Perkins Loan servicer for information on applying for deferment.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Who is considered a teacher?
source_blocks.text: Who is considered a teacher?

source_blocks.source_text_en: A teacher is someone (including for example, a school librarian or guidance counselor) who provides elementary or secondary school students with direct services directly related to classroom teaching.
source_blocks.text: A teacher is someone (including for example, a school librarian or guidance counselor) who provides elementary or secondary school students with direct services directly related to classroom teaching.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You do not need to be certified or licensed to receive cancellation benefits. However, your employing school must consider you to be a full-time professional for the purposes of salary, tenure, retirement benefits, etc. If you are a supervisor, administrator, researcher, or curriculum specialist, you are not considered a teacher unless you primarily provide direct and personal educational services to students.
source_blocks.text: You do not need to be certified or licensed to receive cancellation benefits. However, your employing school must consider you to be a full-time professional for the purposes of salary, tenure, retirement benefits, etc. If you are a supervisor, administrator, researcher, or curriculum specialist, you are not considered a teacher unless you primarily provide direct and personal educational services to students.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How long must I teach?
source_blocks.text: How long must I teach?

source_blocks.source_text_en: For each full academic year (or its equivalent) of full-time teaching service, you are eligible to have a portion of your loan canceled. There is no requirement that you must teach a given number of hours a day to qualify as a full-time teacher; the employing school is responsible for making that decision.
source_blocks.text: For each full academic year (or its equivalent) of full-time teaching service, you are eligible to have a portion of your loan canceled. There is no requirement that you must teach a given number of hours a day to qualify as a full-time teacher; the employing school is responsible for making that decision.

source_blocks.source_text_en: An academic year or its equivalent for cancellation purposes is defined as one complete school year or two half-years that are from different school years. The two half-years must be complete and consecutive, excluding summer sessions, and must generally fall within a 12-month period.
source_blocks.text: An academic year or its equivalent for cancellation purposes is defined as one complete school year or two half-years that are from different school years. The two half-years must be complete and consecutive, excluding summer sessions, and must generally fall within a 12-month period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Teaching Part-time at Multiple Schools
source_blocks.text: Teaching Part-time at Multiple Schools

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can have your loan canceled if you are simultaneously teaching part-time in two or more schools if an official at one of the schools where you taught certifies that you taught full-time for a full academic year.
source_blocks.text: You can have your loan canceled if you are simultaneously teaching part-time in two or more schools if an official at one of the schools where you taught certifies that you taught full-time for a full academic year.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Teaching at a Private School
source_blocks.text: Teaching at a Private School

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your loan can be canceled for services performed in a private school if the private school has established its nonprofit status with the Internal Revenue Service, and if the school is providing elementary and/or secondary education according to state law.
source_blocks.text: Your loan can be canceled for services performed in a private school if the private school has established its nonprofit status with the Internal Revenue Service, and if the school is providing elementary and/or secondary education according to state law.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Teaching at a Preschool or Prekindergarten Program
source_blocks.text: Teaching at a Preschool or Prekindergarten Program

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your loan can be canceled only if the state considers such a program to be a part of its elementary education program. A low-income-school-directory designation that includes prekindergarten or kindergarten does not suffice for a state determination of program eligibility.
source_blocks.text: Your loan can be canceled only if the state considers such a program to be a part of its elementary education program. A low-income-school-directory designation that includes prekindergarten or kindergarten does not suffice for a state determination of program eligibility.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Teaching at Low-income Schools
source_blocks.text: Teaching at Low-income Schools

source_blocks.source_text_en: A cancellation based on teaching in a school serving students from low-income families will be granted only if you taught in an eligible school as determined by the state education agency. To be considered a low-income school, the school must be in a school district that qualified for federal Title I funds in the year for which the cancellation is sought. Also, more than 30 percent of the school s enrollment must be made up of children in the Title I program.
source_blocks.text: A cancellation based on teaching in a school serving students from low-income families will be granted only if you taught in an eligible school as determined by the state education agency. To be considered a low-income school, the school must be in a school district that qualified for federal Title I funds in the year for which the cancellation is sought. Also, more than 30 percent of the school s enrollment must be made up of children in the Title I program.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Each year, the U.S. Department of Education (ED) publishes a list of low-income elementary and secondary schools. To find out if a school is classified as a low-income school, check our online database for the year(s) you have been employed as a teacher. Questions about the inclusion or omission of a particular school must be directed to the state education agency contact in the state where the school is located and not to ED.

To find out if a school is classified as a low-income school, check our online database for the year(s) you have been employed as a teacher. Questions about the inclusion or omission of a particular school must be directed to the state education agency contact in the state where the school is located and not to ED.

source_blocks.source_text_en: All elementary and secondary schools operated by the Bureau of Indian Education (BIE) or operated on Indian reservations by Indian tribal groups under contract with BIE qualify as schools serving low-income students.
source_blocks.text: All elementary and secondary schools operated by the Bureau of Indian Education (BIE) or operated on Indian reservations by Indian tribal groups under contract with BIE qualify as schools serving low-income students.

source_blocks.source_text_en: NOTE: If you have had a portion of your loan canceled for teaching at a low-income elementary or secondary school in one year, you can continue to have portions of your loan canceled for teaching at that school even if it is not listed as a low-income school in later years. Under certain circumstances, the institution that holds your Perkins Loan may permit retroactive cancellation if you can demonstrate that you qualified for cancellation in a prior year. However, the institution may not refund payments made during such a retroactive period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Teaching at an Educational Service Agency
source_blocks.text: Teaching at an Educational Service Agency

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you teach at an educational service agency, your teaching service may qualify for cancellation if the period of qualifying service includes Aug. 14, 2008, or begins on or after that date.
source_blocks.text: If you teach at an educational service agency, your teaching service may qualify for cancellation if the period of qualifying service includes Aug. 14, 2008, or begins on or after that date.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Teaching Special Education
source_blocks.text: Teaching Special Education

source_blocks.source_text_en: You must have an official at the public or other nonprofit elementary or secondary school certify that you are a full-time special education teacher of infants, toddlers, children, or youth with disabilities either on the deferment/cancellation form or on an official letter from the school bearing the school's seal or letterhead.
source_blocks.text: You must have an official at the public or other nonprofit elementary or secondary school certify that you are a full-time special education teacher of infants, toddlers, children, or youth with disabilities either on the deferment/cancellation form or on an official letter from the school bearing the school's seal or letterhead.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you provide one of the services listed below, you qualify as a teacher only if you are licensed, certified, or registered by the appropriate state education agency for that area in which you are providing related special educational services, and the services you provide are part of the educational curriculum for handicapped children.
source_blocks.text: If you provide one of the services listed below, you qualify as a teacher only if you are licensed, certified, or registered by the appropriate state education agency for that area in which you are providing related special educational services, and the services you provide are part of the educational curriculum for handicapped children.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The services are
source_blocks.text: The services are

source_blocks.source_text_en: speech and language pathology and audiology, physical therapy, occupational therapy, psychological and counseling services, and recreational therapy.
source_blocks.text: speech and language pathology and audiology, physical therapy, occupational therapy, psychological and counseling services, and recreational therapy.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Teaching in a Designated Subject Shortage Area
source_blocks.text: Teaching in a Designated Subject Shortage Area

source_blocks.source_text_en: This cancellation is based on full-time teaching if there is a shortage of teachers in your subject area. Each year the state education agency determines any subject shortage areas in the elementary and secondary schools within the state. Check with your local school system or state education agency to find out if your subject-matter area has been so designated. If you teach full-time in science, mathematics, foreign language, or bilingual education, you qualify for cancellation even if the state has not designated one of these subject areas as a shortage area. For a borrower to be considered as teaching in a field of expertise, the majority of classes taught must be in that field of expertise.

source_blocks.source_text_en: In addition to teaching, the following employment or service may qualify you for a full or partial Perkins Loan cancellation depending on the type of loan you have and the date of the loan:

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is a Direct PLUS Loan Application for Graduate/Professional Students?
source_blocks.text: 什么是研究生/专业学生直接PLUS贷款申请？

source_blocks.source_text_en: This is a request for supplemental information in connection with your application for a Federal Direct PLUS Loan (Direct PLUS Loan) through the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program. Some schools may have a different process for obtaining the additional information needed to process your Direct PLUS Loan application.
source_blocks.text: 这是与您通过威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款（直接贷款）计划申请联邦直接PLUS贷款（直接PLUS贷款）相关的补充信息请求。一些学校可能有不同的流程来获取处理您的直接PLUS贷款申请所需的额外信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The information that you provide will be sent to the school that you select. The school you select will use the information collected to determine your eligibility for a Direct PLUS Loan and process your application.
source_blocks.text: 您提供的信息将发送给您选择的学校。您选择的学校将使用收集的信息来确定您是否有资格获得直接PLUS贷款并处理您的申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Before you can receive a Direct PLUS Loan, you must complete a Direct PLUS Loan Master Promissory Note (Direct PLUS Loan MPN), which explains all of the terms and conditions of Direct PLUS Loans and constitutes your legally binding agreement to repay all Direct PLUS Loans that you receive under the Direct PLUS Loan MPN. You will have an opportunity to complete the Direct PLUS Loan MPN after you complete the Direct PLUS Loan Request.
source_blocks.text: 在您获得直接PLUS贷款之前，您必须完成直接PLUS贷款主本票（直接PLUS贷款MPN），该本票解释了直接PLUS贷款的所有条款和条件，并构成您偿还根据直接PLUS贷款MPN获得的所有直接PLUS贷款的法律约束协议。在您完成直接PLUS贷款请求后，您将有机会完成直接PLUS贷款MPN。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Direct PLUS Loan Application allows you to authorize the school to use your loan funds to satisfy other educationally related charges after tuition and fees, and room and board have been paid. You are not required to provide this authorization.
source_blocks.text: 直接PLUS贷款申请允许您授权学校在支付学费和杂费以及食宿费后，使用您的贷款资金来支付其他与教育相关的费用。您不需要提供此授权。

source_blocks.source_text_en: BEFORE YOU CONTINUE: If you have placed a security freeze on your credit file, you must lift or remove the freeze at each credit bureau before you continue. Your application will not be processed if you have a security freeze.
source_blocks.text: 在您继续之前：如果您已在信用档案上设置了安全冻结，您必须在继续之前解除或移除每个信用机构的安全冻结。如果您有安全冻结，您的申请将不会被处理。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Thinking about college, career school, or graduate school? There s so much to consider when it comes to getting ready for college: where to go, what to study, how to apply, how to pay for it all, and more.
source_blocks.text: 正在考虑上大学、职业学院或研究生院？为大学做准备需要考虑的事情太多了：去哪里、学什么、如何申请、如何支付所有费用等等。

source_blocks.source_text_en: It s never too early or too late to explore your options for college or career school. We ll walk through some key steps in preparing for college and provide resources that can help you along the way. You ll have to take the time to research and understand your options, but you don t have to do it alone. We re here to help students make informed decisions and find out what they need to do!
source_blocks.text: 探索大学或职业学院的选择永远不会太早或太晚。我们将逐步介绍为大学做准备的一些关键步骤，并提供沿途可以帮助你的资源。你需要花时间研究和了解你的选择，但你不必独自完成。我们在这里帮助学生做出明智的决定，并找出他们需要做什么！

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here s a simple equation: a college or career school education = more money, more job options, and more freedom. As you ll see from the chart below, as you get more education, you make more money.

source_blocks.source_text_en: A college education is a long-term investment. With careful planning, you can find the school and funding options that work best for your situation and put you on the path to success.
source_blocks.text: 大学教育是一项长期投资。通过仔细规划，你可以找到最适合你情况的学校和资助选项，并让你走上成功之路。

source_blocks.source_text_en: A college or career school education can give you the skills needed to pursue a career that really interests you. Love working with animals? Or how about computers? Find possible careers to match your interests.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Whether you re in high school now, in elementary or middle school, out of school, or perhaps never finished school, there are a number of steps you can take to get college ready. Our checklists will walk you through the steps you can take to find and get into the college or career school that s right for you and help you learn how to prepare financially. Review our checklists now!
source_blocks.text: 无论你现在是高中生、小学生、初中生、已辍学，还是从未完成学业，都有许多步骤可以帮助你为上大学做好准备。我们的清单将引导你完成寻找并进入适合你的大学或职业学院，以及学习如何做好财务准备的步骤。现在就查看我们的清单吧！

source_blocks.source_text_en: You have a variety of college options, from two-year community and junior colleges, to four-year colleges and universities, to technical, vocational, and trade schools. source_blocks.text: 你有多种大学选择，从两年制社区学院和初级学院，到四年制学院和大学，再到技术、职业和贸易学校。获取关于选择学校时需要考虑的事项的建议，并使用我们的免费大学搜索工具来找到符合你兴趣、职业目标和财务状况的学校。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Program Reviews
source_blocks.text: 项目审查

source_blocks.source_text_en: As part of its oversight duties, Federal Student Aid (FSA) routinely conducts program reviews to confirm that a school meets FSA requirements for institutional eligibility, financial responsibility, and administrative capability. During a program review, reviewers evaluate the school s compliance with FSA requirements, assess liabilities for errors in performance, and identify actions the school must take to improve its future administrative capabilities.
source_blocks.text: 作为其监督职责的一部分，联邦学生援助（FSA）定期进行项目审查，以确认学校是否符合FSA关于机构资格、财务责任和行政能力的要求。在项目审查期间，审查员评估学校对FSA要求的遵守情况，评估绩效错误的责任，并确定学校为改善其未来行政能力必须采取的行动。

source_blocks.source_text_en: After completing a program review, Federal Student Aid issues a Final Program Review Determination (FPRD), which is a report that includes each finding identified in the program review report, the school's response, and the Department s final determination. The FPRD also identifies liabilities, if any, calculated based on the findings of the program review; provides instructions for the payment of liabilities, as appropriate; notifies the institution of its right to appeal the existence and amount of any liabilities identified, as appropriate; and closes the program review, if appropriate. The FPRD may or may not require additional action by the institution.
source_blocks.text: 完成项目审查后，联邦学生援助发布最终项目审查决定（FPRD），该报告包括项目审查报告中确定的每项发现、学校的回应以及教育部的最终决定。FPRD还根据项目审查的发现确定任何责任（如有）；提供支付责任的说明（如适用）；通知机构其对任何已确定责任的存在和金额提出上诉的权利（如适用）；并在适当时结束项目审查。FPRD可能要求也可能不要求机构采取额外行动。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Future FPRDs will be posted regularly.
source_blocks.text: 未来的FPRD将定期发布。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Below are the Final Program Review Determinations and Expedited Determination Letters issued in
source_blocks.text: 以下是发布的最终项目审查决定和快速决定函：

source_blocks.source_text_en: To access all documents associated with focused-Clery Act reviews, visit the "Clery Act Reports" page. To locate Final Program Review Determinations from completed third-party servicer program reviews, visit the "Third-party Servicer Program Reviews" page. An overview of the top program review and audit findings by fiscal year is also available. These annual reports detail by frequency the most common findings identified in the annual compliance audits conducted by independent auditors, and identified through program reviews conducted by the Department of Education at institutions of higher education.
source_blocks.text: 要访问与重点Clery Act审查相关的所有文件，请访问“Clery Act报告”页面。要查找已完成第三方服务商项目审查的最终项目审查决定，请访问“第三方服务商项目审查”页面。还提供了按财政年度划分的主要项目审查和审计发现概述。这些年度报告按频率详细列出了独立审计师进行的年度合规审计中发现的最常见发现，以及教育部在高等教育机构进行的项目审查中发现的发现。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Qualifying for PSLF
source_blocks.text: Qualifying for PSLF

source_blocks.source_text_en: To qualify for PSLF, you must
source_blocks.text: To qualify for PSLF, you must

source_blocks.source_text_en: be employed by a U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government or not-for-profit organization; work full-time for that agency or organization; have Direct Loans (or consolidate other federal student loans into a Direct Loan); repay your loans under an income-driven repayment plan; and make 120 qualifying payments.
source_blocks.text: be employed by a U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government or not-for-profit organization; work full-time for that agency or organization; have Direct Loans (or consolidate other federal student loans into a Direct Loan); repay your loans under an income-driven repayment plan; and make 120 qualifying payments.

source_blocks.source_text_en: To ensure you re on the right track, you should submit a Public Service Loan Forgiveness: Employment Certification Form annually or when you change employers. We ll use the information you provide on the form to let you know if you are making qualifying PSLF payments. This will help you determine if you re on the right track as early as possible.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Qualifying Employment
source_blocks.text: Qualifying Employment

source_blocks.source_text_en: Qualifying employment for the PSLF Program isn t about the specific job that you do for your employer. Instead, it s about who your employer is. Employment with the following types of organizations qualifies for PSLF:
source_blocks.text: Qualifying employment for the PSLF Program isn t about the specific job that you do for your employer. Instead, it s about who your employer is. Employment with the following types of organizations qualifies for PSLF:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Government organizations at any level (U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal) Not-for-profit organizations that are tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code
source_blocks.text: Government organizations at any level (U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal) Not-for-profit organizations that are tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code

source_blocks.source_text_en: Serving as a full-time AmeriCorps or Peace Corps volunteer also counts as qualifying employment for the PSLF Program.
source_blocks.text: Serving as a full-time AmeriCorps or Peace Corps volunteer also counts as qualifying employment for the PSLF Program.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The following types of employers do not qualify for PSLF:
source_blocks.text: The following types of employers do not qualify for PSLF:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Labor unions Partisan political organizations For-profit organizations, including for-profit government contractors
source_blocks.text: Labor unions Partisan political organizations For-profit organizations, including for-profit government contractors

source_blocks.source_text_en: Contractors: You must be directly employed by a qualifying employer for your employment to count toward PSLF. If you re employed by an organization that is doing work under a contract with a qualifying employer, it is your employer s status not the status of the organization that your employer has a contract with that determines whether your employment qualifies for PSLF. For example, if you re employed by a for-profit contractor that is doing work for a qualifying employer, your employment does not count toward PSLF.

If you re employed by an organization that is doing work under a contract with a qualifying employer, it is your employer s status not the status of the organization that your employer has a contract with that determines whether your employment qualifies for PSLF. For example, if you re employed by a for-profit contractor that is doing work for a qualifying employer, your employment does not count toward PSLF.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Other types of not-for-profit organizations: If you work for a not-for-profit organization that is not tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, it can still be considered a qualifying employer if it provides certain types of qualifying public services. However, in our experience, few organizations meet these criteria.

However, in our experience, few organizations meet these criteria.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Full-time Employment
source_blocks.text: Full-time Employment

source_blocks.source_text_en: For PSLF, you re generally considered to work full-time if you meet your employer s definition of full-time or work at least 30 hours per week, whichever is greater.
source_blocks.text: For PSLF, you re generally considered to work full-time if you meet your employer s definition of full-time or work at least 30 hours per week, whichever is greater.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are employed in more than one qualifying part-time job at the same time, you will be considered full-time if you work a combined average of at least 30 hours per week with your employers.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are employed by a not-for-profit organization, time spent on religious instruction, worship services, or any form of proselytizing may not be counted toward meeting the full-time employment requirement.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Eligible Loans
source_blocks.text: Eligible Loans

source_blocks.source_text_en: Any loan received under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program qualifies for PSLF.
source_blocks.text: Any loan received under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program qualifies for PSLF.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Loans from these federal student loan programs don't qualify for PSLF: the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program and the Federal Perkins Loan (Perkins Loan) Program. However, they may become eligible if you consolidate them into a Direct Consolidation Loan.
source_blocks.text: Loans from these federal student loan programs don't qualify for PSLF: the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program and the Federal Perkins Loan (Perkins Loan) Program. However, they may become eligible if you consolidate them into a Direct Consolidation Loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Student loans from private lenders do not qualify for PSLF.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you consolidate your loans, only qualifying payments that you make on the new Direct Consolidation Loan can be counted toward the 120 payments required for PSLF. Any payments you made on the loans before you consolidated them don t count.
