source_blocks.source_text_en: Qualifying Payments
source_blocks.text: Qualifying Payments

source_blocks.source_text_en: A qualifying monthly payment is a payment that you make
source_blocks.text: A qualifying monthly payment is a payment that you make

source_blocks.source_text_en: after Oct. 1, 2007; under a qualifying repayment plan; for the full amount due as shown on your bill; no later than 15 days after your due date; and while you are employed full-time by a qualifying employer.
source_blocks.text: after Oct. 1, 2007; under a qualifying repayment plan; for the full amount due as shown on your bill; no later than 15 days after your due date; and while you are employed full-time by a qualifying employer.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can make qualifying monthly payments only during periods when you re required to make a payment. Therefore, you can t make a qualifying monthly payment while your loans are in
source_blocks.text: You can make qualifying monthly payments only during periods when you re required to make a payment. Therefore, you can t make a qualifying monthly payment while your loans are in

source_blocks.source_text_en: an in-school status, the grace period, a deferment, or a forbearance.
source_blocks.text: an in-school status, the grace period, a deferment, or a forbearance.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you want to make qualifying payments, but you re in a deferment or forbearance, contact your federal student loan servicer to waive the deferment or forbearance.
source_blocks.text: If you want to make qualifying payments, but you re in a deferment or forbearance, contact your federal student loan servicer to waive the deferment or forbearance.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your 120 qualifying monthly payments don t need to be consecutive. For example, if you have a period of employment with a nonqualifying employer, you will not lose credit for prior qualifying payments you made.
source_blocks.text: Your 120 qualifying monthly payments don t need to be consecutive. For example, if you have a period of employment with a nonqualifying employer, you will not lose credit for prior qualifying payments you made.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The best way to ensure that you are making on-time, complete payments is to sign up for automatic debit with your loan servicer.
source_blocks.text: The best way to ensure that you are making on-time, complete payments is to sign up for automatic debit with your loan servicer.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can I qualify sooner by making higher monthly payments?
source_blocks.text: Can I qualify sooner by making higher monthly payments?

source_blocks.source_text_en: No. If you make a monthly payment for more than the amount you are required to pay, you should keep in mind that you can receive credit for only one payment per month, no matter how much you pay. You can t qualify for PSLF faster by making larger payments.
source_blocks.text: No. If you make a monthly payment for more than the amount you are required to pay, you should keep in mind that you can receive credit for only one payment per month, no matter how much you pay. You can t qualify for PSLF faster by making larger payments.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you want to pay more than your required monthly payment amount, you should contact your servicer and ask that the extra amount not be applied to cover future payments. Otherwise, you may end up being paid ahead, and you can t receive credit for a qualifying PSLF payment during a month when no payment is due.

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are special rules that allow borrowers who are AmeriCorps or Peace Corps volunteers to use their Segal Education Award or Peace Corps transition payment to make a single lump-sum payment that may count for up to 12 qualifying PSLF payments.
source_blocks.text: There are special rules that allow borrowers who are AmeriCorps or Peace Corps volunteers to use their Segal Education Award or Peace Corps transition payment to make a single lump-sum payment that may count for up to 12 qualifying PSLF payments.

source_blocks.source_text_en: In addition, borrowers who have lump-sum payments made on their behalf under a student loan repayment program administered by the U.S. Department of Defense may also receive credit for more than one qualifying PSLF payment.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Qualifying Repayment Plans
source_blocks.text: Qualifying Repayment Plans

source_blocks.source_text_en: Qualifying repayment plans include all of the income-driven repayment (IDR) plans (plans that base your monthly payment on your income).
source_blocks.text: Qualifying repayment plans include all of the income-driven repayment (IDR) plans (plans that base your monthly payment on your income).

source_blocks.source_text_en: While payments made under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan are qualifying payments, you would have to change to an IDR plan to benefit from PSLF. Under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan, your loans will be paid in full once you have made the 120 qualifying PSLF payments and there will be no balance to forgive. Before you change to an IDR plan, however, you should understand that your payment may increase under these plans depending on your income and the amount that you owe. If this is the case for you, and you do not wish to pay this higher amount, then the PSLF Program may not benefit you.

source_blocks.source_text_en: PSLF Process
source_blocks.text: PSLF Process

source_blocks.source_text_en: Because you have to make 120 qualifying monthly payments, it will take at least 10 years before you can qualify for PSLF.
source_blocks.text: Because you have to make 120 qualifying monthly payments, it will take at least 10 years before you can qualify for PSLF.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Important: You must be working for a qualifying employer at the time you submit the application for forgiveness and at the time the remaining balance on your loan is forgiven.
source_blocks.text: Important: You must be working for a qualifying employer at the time you submit the application for forgiveness and at the time the remaining balance on your loan is forgiven.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are working toward PSLF, you should complete and submit the Public Service Loan Forgiveness: Employment Certification Form (often referred to as the ECF) annually or when you change employers.
source_blocks.text: If you are working toward PSLF, you should complete and submit the Public Service Loan Forgiveness: Employment Certification Form (often referred to as the ECF) annually or when you change employers.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have made 120 qualifying payments, you should fill out and submit the Public Service Loan Forgiveness: Application for Forgiveness (PSLF application).

source_blocks.source_text_en: Either way, we ll use the information you provide on the form to let you know if you are making qualifying PSLF payments. This will help you determine if you re on the right track as early as possible.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Questions and Answers About FAFSA Completion Data
source_blocks.text: 关于FAFSA完成数据的问答

source_blocks.source_text_en: Below are questions we ve heard about the Completion by High School and Public School District"\>data we provide on FAFSA completion by high school.
source_blocks.text: 以下是我们听到的关于我们提供的高中和公立学区FAFSA完成数据的问题。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Basics
source_blocks.text: 基本信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: Missing or Duplicate High Schools
source_blocks.text: 缺失或重复的高中

source_blocks.source_text_en: Low Completion Totals
source_blocks.text: 完成总数较低

source_blocks.source_text_en: Technical and Analytical
source_blocks.text: 技术和分析

source_blocks.source_text_en: Basics
source_blocks.text: 基本信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is the source of data?
source_blocks.text: 数据的来源是什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: The source of the data is the U.S. Department of Education's Central Processing System.
source_blocks.text: 数据的来源是美国教育部中央处理系统。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What years of Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) submission and completion data are available?
source_blocks.text: 哪些年份的免费申请联邦学生援助（FAFSA）提交和完成数据可用？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal Student Aid releases data for the current 2018 19 cycle and provides a side-by-side comparison of the previous 2017 18 cycle. We also have an archive that contains data files from the 2017 18 cycle comparing it to the past 2016 17 cycle. Each file has the previous cycle data through the same date in the prior year as well as the 6-month and 12-month numbers for the previous cycle.
source_blocks.text: 联邦学生援助发布了当前2018-19周期的数据，并提供与上一2017-18周期的并排比较。我们还有一个档案，包含2017-18周期的数据文件，与过去的2016-17周期进行比较。每个文件都包含上一周期截至前一年同期的数据，以及上一周期的6个月和12个月数字。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Only numbers of submitted and completed FAFSA forms are available. No personally identifiable information for any FAFSA filer will be shared through this process. Email us at HSFAFSA@ed.gov if you see data that is inaccurate and/or you have suggestions for improvement. We welcome your input.
source_blocks.text: 只有提交和完成的FAFSA表格数量可用。不会通过此过程共享任何FAFSA申请人的个人身份信息。如果您看到不准确的数据和/或有改进建议，请发送电子邮件至HSFAFSA@ed.gov。我们欢迎您的意见。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is the difference between a submitted and a completed FAFSA form?
source_blocks.text: 提交的FAFSA表格和完成的FAFSA表格有什么区别？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Submitted applications reflect all FAFSA forms submitted by students at that high school. These applications, however, can be subsequently rejected by the Central Processing System if they are missing key pieces of information. The applications that are not rejected are referred to as completed applications. Completed applications, therefore, are a subset of all submitted applications. If a FAFSA form is submitted but not complete, the student will receive an email from the Department of Education asking him or her to correct the FAFSA form. A completed FAFSA form is necessary to determine eligibility for federal student aid and often other forms of financial aid.
source_blocks.text: 提交的申请反映了该高中学生提交的所有FAFSA表格。然而，如果这些申请缺少关键信息，中央处理系统随后可能会拒绝它们。未被拒绝的申请称为已完成的申请。因此，已完成的申请是所有已提交申请的子集。如果FAFSA表格已提交但未完成，学生将收到教育部的电子邮件，要求他或她更正FAFSA表格。完成FAFSA表格是确定联邦学生援助和其他形式财政援助资格所必需的。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How often will the FAFSA submission data be updated?
source_blocks.text: FAFSA提交数据多久更新一次？

source_blocks.source_text_en: From October through June, data releases are weekly. For the remainder of the calendar year, data releases occur every other Friday. (For high schools to track their progress, Federal Student Aid regularly updates estimates for the first 12 months of an application cycle. As of the 2017 18 FAFSA cycle, this is extended to the first 15 months of the application cycle and will cover October of one year through December of the following year.)
source_blocks.text: 从十月到六月，数据每周发布。在日历年的剩余时间内，数据每两周发布一次（每隔一个周五）。（为了让高中跟踪他们的进展，联邦学生援助定期更新申请周期前12个月的估计。截至2017-18 FAFSA周期，这延长到申请周期的前15个月，并将涵盖一年十月至次年十二月。）

source_blocks.source_text_en: Missing or Duplicate High Schools
source_blocks.text: 缺失或重复的高中

source_blocks.source_text_en: Why isn't my high school listed in these data files?
source_blocks.text: 为什么我的高中没有列在这些数据文件中？

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are two primary reasons that you may not see your school on the list.
source_blocks.text: 您可能看不到您学校在名单上有两个主要原因。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your school will not appear on the report if there are fewer than five completed applications. Your school may appear on the report, but it may be listed under an alternative name. Since school names are inherently student-reported, the reported name can vary considerably. In aggregating the data, our standard practice is to report the school name that is most commonly reported by applicants. It is possible this name is different than your formal school name. As a result, it is important to look for other variations of your school name and city.
source_blocks.text: 如果完成的申请少于五份，您的学校将不会出现在报告中。 您的学校可能会出现在报告中，但可能以另一个名称列出。由于学校名称本质上是学生自行报告的，报告的名称可能会有很大差异。在汇总数据时，我们的标准做法是报告申请人最常报告的学校名称。这个名称可能与您学校的正式名称不同。因此，重要的是查找您学校名称和城市的其他变体。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You do not need to request to be added to the list. Once a high school shows at least five completed FAFSA forms, their submission and completion totals will appear in the database.
source_blocks.text: 您无需请求添加到列表中。一旦一所高中显示至少五份完成的FAFSA表格，其提交和完成总数将出现在数据库中。

source_blocks.source_text_en: I cannot find my high school within the FAFSA form's high school search results. What could be causing this? How do I go about getting my school included?
source_blocks.text: 我在FAFSA表格的高中搜索结果中找不到我的高中。可能是什么原因？我该如何让我的学校被收录？

source_blocks.source_text_en: With a few exceptions (discussed below), most high schools should be contained in our database on the FAFSA form. If you can t find your school, double-check your spelling of the city and school name, and then try your search again. Also, consider alternate names or cities that may be used. Sometimes the official location of the school reported to us is a suburb within a larger city, or vice-versa. If after trying various possibilities you still cannot find your institution, you may still continue forward by clicking next. Despite being unable to find your school, the information you type in will still be captured and recorded, so be sure the spelling is correct.
source_blocks.text: 除少数例外（下文讨论），大多数高中都应包含在我们的FAFSA表格数据库中。如果您找不到您的学校，请仔细检查城市和学校名称的拼写，然后再次尝试搜索。同时，考虑可能使用的替代名称或城市。有时，学校向我们报告的官方位置是大城市内的郊区，反之亦然。如果在尝试各种可能性后仍然找不到您的学校，您仍然可以通过点击“下一步”继续前进。尽管无法找到您的学校，您输入的信息仍将被捕获和记录，因此请确保拼写正确。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For public schools, our database should contain every high school in the nation, unless the school was opened, merged, or otherwise changed its name within the past year or two. If you fit into one of these categories, your school may not be listed within the current FAFSA form, but will be listed on future FAFSA forms.
source_blocks.text: 对于公立学校，我们的数据库应包含全国每一所高中，除非学校在过去一两年内新开设、合并或更改了名称。如果您属于这些类别之一，您的学校可能不会出现在当前的FAFSA表格中，但会出现在未来的FAFSA表格中。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For private schools, our database contains every high school that has participated in the U.S. Department of Education's Private School Survey. Visit the National Center for Education Statistics if your private school would like more information. If your private school only recently participated in the survey, your school may not be listed within the current FAFSA form, but will be listed on future FAFSA forms.
source_blocks.text: 对于私立学校，我们的数据库包含所有参与美国教育部私立学校调查的高中。如果您的私立学校想了解更多信息，请访问国家教育统计中心。如果您的私立学校最近才参与调查，您的学校可能不会出现在当前的FAFSA表格中，但会出现在未来的FAFSA表格中。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Why do there appear to be duplicates of the same school?
source_blocks.text: 为什么同一所学校似乎有重复？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Since these school names are inherently student-reported, the reported name can vary considerably. In aggregating the data, our standard practice is to report the school name that is most commonly reported by applicants.
source_blocks.text: 由于这些学校名称本质上是学生自行报告的，报告的名称可能会有很大差异。在汇总数据时，我们的标准做法是报告申请人最常报告的学校名称。

source_blocks.source_text_en: However, when we are unable to determine if school name variations are referring to the same school, we err on the side of caution and do not aggregate the data to a single record and applicant count. In that instance, it may appear that there are duplicates of the same school. Email us at HSFAFSA@ed.gov if you believe your school has been listed more than once.
source_blocks.text: 然而，当我们无法确定学校名称变体是否指同一所学校时，我们会谨慎行事，不将数据汇总到单一记录和申请人数量。在这种情况下，可能看起来有同一所学校的重复。如果您认为您的学校被多次列出，请发送电子邮件至HSFAFSA@ed.gov。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Low Completion Totals
source_blocks.text: 完成总数较低

source_blocks.source_text_en: Why is my number of FAFSA submissions or completions lower than I think it should be?
source_blocks.text: 为什么我的FAFSA提交或完成数量低于我认为应有的数量？

source_blocks.source_text_en: While we know that many high schools inadvertently overestimate their FAFSA completion rates, one reason your rates may be lower than expected is because your school could be listed more than once. This happens if students entered your school name in different ways on the FAFSA form. For instance, if some students listed "John Doe High School" and other students listed "Doe High School," then your high school could be listed in more than one place. Please look for alternate names for your school. Email us at HSFAFSA@ed.gov if you find your school has been listed more than once.
source_blocks.text: 虽然我们知道许多高中无意中高估了他们的FAFSA完成率，但您的完成率可能低于预期的一个原因是您的学校可能被多次列出。如果学生在FAFSA表格上以不同方式输入了您学校的名称，就会发生这种情况。例如，如果一些学生列出了“John Doe高中”，而其他学生列出了“Doe高中”，那么您的高中可能会被列在多个地方。请查找您学校的替代名称。如果您发现您的学校被多次列出，请发送电子邮件至HSFAFSA@ed.gov。

source_blocks.source_text_en: I am a high school counselor or college access professional. What resources do you have to help increase FAFSA completion totals?
source_blocks.text: 我是一名高中辅导员或大学入学专业人士。你们有哪些资源可以帮助提高FAFSA完成总数？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal Student Aid s Financial Aid Toolkit provides federal student aid information and outreach tools for counselors, college access professionals, nonprofit mentors, and others. The site helps counselors understand the basics of federal student aid, provides tips on hosting events (along with sample PowerPoint presentations), provides suggested messages for social media and email outreach, and helps find other training opportunities.
source_blocks.text: 联邦学生援助的财务援助工具包为辅导员、大学入学专业人士、非营利导师和其他人提供联邦学生援助信息和外展工具。该网站帮助辅导员了解联邦学生援助的基础知识，提供举办活动的提示（以及示例PowerPoint演示文稿），提供社交媒体和电子邮件外展的建议信息，并帮助寻找其他培训机会。

source_blocks.source_text_en: I am a counselor at a high school with a lot of students age 20 or older. Why are my numbers so low?
source_blocks.text: 我是一所高中有很多20岁或以上学生的辅导员。为什么我的数字这么低？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Because there is no question on the FAFSA form that asks if an applicant is a high school senior, we must use several criteria to identify those applicants that are likely high school seniors. In this instance, the bulk of the students would likely not satisfy the age criteria requiring applicants to be less than 20 years of age at the cutoff date. Also, students must also be receiving their high school diploma, as opposed to a GED or other program, to fit this definition of a high school senior.
source_blocks.text: 由于FAFSA表格上没有询问申请人是否为高中毕业班学生的问题，我们必须使用多个标准来识别那些可能是高中毕业班的申请人。在这种情况下，大部分学生可能不满足年龄标准，即申请人在截止日期时年龄必须小于20岁。此外，学生还必须获得高中文凭，而不是GED或其他课程，才符合高中毕业班的定义。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Technical and Analytical
source_blocks.text: 技术与分析

source_blocks.source_text_en: The totals reported last year are different from the numbers reported now about last year. What is causing this?
source_blocks.text: 去年报告的总数与现在关于去年的报告数字不同。这是什么原因造成的？

source_blocks.source_text_en: There could be several causes for this, including the possibility that your institution is listed more than once in the data using alternate variations of the school's name or city. One other cause is a change we made in 2017 to our definition of a high school senior, which now aligns with other data we publicly release. In past years, we used proxies to determine whether an applicant was a first-time filer; we now use true first-time filer status as one criterion for being a senior. While this impacts a relatively small number of applicants, if your total decreased compared to what we reported last year, then this may mean there were applicants that had applied in a previous year.
source_blocks.text: 可能的原因有几种，包括你的机构可能以学校名称或城市的不同变体在数据中被多次列出。另一个原因是我们2017年对高中毕业班学生定义所做的更改，现在这一定义与我们公开发布的其他数据保持一致。在过去的几年里，我们使用代理指标来确定申请人是否为首次提交者；现在我们使用真正的首次提交者状态作为毕业班学生的一个标准。虽然这影响的申请人数量相对较少，但如果你的总数与去年报告的数字相比有所下降，那么这可能意味着有申请人在前一年已经申请过。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can I add up all the submitted applications from a single state file to calculate a state total? What about adding up all the submitted applications from a single city?
source_blocks.text: 我可以将单个州文件中的所有已提交申请相加来计算州总数吗？那么将单个城市中的所有已提交申请相加呢？

source_blocks.source_text_en: The answer to both questions is no. The official location of a school (or the location most commonly reported by students) may actually be a suburb falling within a larger city's limits. For example, adding up all the applications reported under "New York City" would exclude any institutions reported being within "Queens" or even within "Jamaica," a smaller neighborhood within the New York City Borough of Queens.
source_blocks.text: 这两个问题的答案都是否定的。学校的官方位置（或学生最常报告的位置）实际上可能是位于更大城市范围内的郊区。例如，将“纽约市”下报告的所有申请相加，将排除任何报告为位于“皇后区”甚至“牙买加”的机构，后者是纽约市皇后区内一个较小的社区。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Any analysis must also consider the impact of withholding the totals or names of schools with fewer than five completed applications. At its most basic level, summing the number of applications reported in these files always underestimates the number of applications. If an institution is reported as having "\<5" completed applications, one cannot assume there were zero applications. Further, the totals for some schools are never made public because their class sizes essentially preclude them from having enough completed applications to ever be disclosed publicly. Because this impacts some areas more than others, be sure to consider these and other factors when conducting any analyses.
source_blocks.text: 任何分析还必须考虑隐瞒少于五份已完成申请的学校总数或名称的影响。在最基本的层面上，将这些文件中报告的申请数量相加总是低估了申请数量。如果某机构被报告为有“\<5”份已完成申请，不能假设申请数为零。此外，一些学校的总数从未公开，因为其班级规模基本上使其无法拥有足够多的已完成申请来公开披露。由于这对某些地区的影响大于其他地区，在进行任何分析时，请务必考虑这些因素和其他因素。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Why do some districts appear in white on the maps?
source_blocks.text: 为什么地图上有些学区显示为白色？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Districts are listed as missing/insufficient data if any of the following conditions are true:
source_blocks.text: 如果满足以下任一条件，学区将被列为缺失/数据不足：

source_blocks.source_text_en: The regulatory adjusted cohort graduation rate is missing (e.g., if districts merged or a new district was created after 2009 10). A district has fewer than 15 students in the regulatory adjusted cohort graduation rate data. There s an unpredicted increase in the number of district graduating seniors (e.g., a dramatic increase in the graduation rate, or if two districts merge under one district's name). A district has fewer than 10 projected graduates. A district has fewer than five completed FAFSA forms. The National Center Education Statistics Local Education Agency (LEA) code does not match the LEA code found in the Tiger/Line shapefile for the state.
source_blocks.text: 监管调整后的队列毕业率缺失（例如，如果学区合并或在2009-10学年之后创建了新学区）。 学区的监管调整后队列毕业率数据中少于15名学生。 学区毕业班学生数量出现不可预测的增长（例如，毕业率急剧上升，或两个学区合并为一个学区的名称）。 学区预计毕业生少于10人。 学区完成的FAFSA表格少于五份。 国家教育统计中心地方教育机构（LEA）代码与该州Tiger/Line形状文件中找到的LEA代码不匹配。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Depending on what materials are available at your school and for your courses, you may have several lower-cost options to obtain your books:

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your course uses a hard-copy textbook, consider buying a used copy or renting your textbook from a bookstore or online. If you purchase your textbook, consider reselling that textbook, if allowed, when you are done with the course. Even with new textbooks, you may be able to save money by shopping around. If your course uses paid online content, your school may have negotiated a deal with the publisher that will allow you online access at a fraction of the cost you would pay for a physical book. The paid online content may also come with study tools and other content in addition to the textbook.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Have you been told you can t get federal student aid any longer?
source_blocks.text: Have you been told you can t get federal student aid any longer?

source_blocks.source_text_en: In most circumstances, there are things you can do to get back your eligibility for financial aid.
source_blocks.text: In most circumstances, there are things you can do to get back your eligibility for financial aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You might lose federal student aid eligibility for a number of reasons. For instance, you might no longer meet one of the basic eligibility criteria, or you might have changed majors and no longer be enrolled in a program that makes you eligible to receive a specific type of funding (for instance, a Teacher Education Assistance for College and Higher Education [TEACH] Grant). We recommend you talk to your financial aid office about those and any other circumstances that cause you to lose eligibility.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Meanwhile, below we provide some tips on how to get your eligibility back if you find yourself in one of the following situations:

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I defaulted on my student loan but now I want to get more federal student aid?
source_blocks.text: What if I defaulted on my student loan but now I want to get more federal student aid?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You ll need to get out of default before you can receive aid again.
source_blocks.text: You ll need to get out of default before you can receive aid again.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if my grades slipped, or I haven t completed enough credits, and my financial aid office told me I can t get federal student aid?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You need to make satisfactory academic progress in college or career school in order to keep getting federal student aid. Talk to your school about whether you can appeal the decision that made you ineligible to continue receiving federal student aid.
source_blocks.text: You need to make satisfactory academic progress in college or career school in order to keep getting federal student aid. Talk to your school about whether you can appeal the decision that made you ineligible to continue receiving federal student aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I was an eligible noncitizen but my status expired or was revoked?
source_blocks.text: What if I was an eligible noncitizen but my status expired or was revoked?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You ll need to reinstate the status that made you an eligible noncitizen, or become a citizen or permanent resident, before you can receive federal student aid. For information about reinstating your status or becoming a citizen, contact U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you ve lost eligibility due to a conviction for a drug offense, and you are not scheduled to regain eligibility this academic year, it is possible to regain eligibility early.
source_blocks.text: If you ve lost eligibility due to a conviction for a drug offense, and you are not scheduled to regain eligibility this academic year, it is possible to regain eligibility early.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I m incarcerated?
source_blocks.text: What if I m incarcerated?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your incarceration affects your eligibility for different types of aid in different ways. If you are ineligible for a particular type of student aid due to your incarceration, you ll need to wait until you re released before you can get that type of aid.
source_blocks.text: Your incarceration affects your eligibility for different types of aid in different ways. If you are ineligible for a particular type of student aid due to your incarceration, you ll need to wait until you re released before you can get that type of aid.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I accidentally received more federal student loan or grant money than I was supposed to?
source_blocks.text: What if I accidentally received more federal student loan or grant money than I was supposed to?

source_blocks.source_text_en: In certain cases, you ll need to repay the amount that was beyond the maximum that you were allowed to receive. You can either repay the excess all at once, or you can make arrangements to repay it a bit at a time. Once you ve repaid or made arrangements to repay the excess, you ll be able to receive additional federal student aid (assuming you haven t reached the maximum amounts for all programs for which you are otherwise eligible). In other cases, your financial aid office might be able to adjust the amount of money you ll be getting from another federal student aid program to make up for the excess you received. If you have questions about repaying aid or getting additional aid, talk to the financial aid staff at your school.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Reporting Parent Information | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 报告家长信息 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: Dependent students must report their parents information, as well as their own, on the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form.
source_blocks.text: 受抚养学生必须在其联邦学生援助免费申请（FAFSA）表格上报告其家长信息以及自己的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Find out who counts as your parent when you file your FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 了解在提交FAFSA表格时，谁算作你的家长。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are considered a dependent student for FAFSA purposes, you will need to provide information about your legal parent(s) on the application. A legal parent is your biological or adoptive parent, or your legal parent as determined by the state (for example, if the parent is listed on your birth certificate). If you have a stepparent currently married to your legal parent, you generally also must provide information about him or her.
source_blocks.text: 如果你出于FAFSA目的被视为受抚养学生，你需要在申请中提供关于你的法定家长的信息。法定家长是指你的亲生父母或养父母，或由州确定的法定家长（例如，如果家长列在你的出生证明上）。如果你有一位目前与你法定家长结婚的继父/继母，你通常也必须提供关于他/她的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: View text-only version
source_blocks.text: 查看纯文本版本

source_blocks.source_text_en: Who is my parent according to the FAFSA form?
source_blocks.text: 根据FAFSA表格，谁是我的家长？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you need to report parent information, here are some guidelines to help you:
source_blocks.text: 如果你需要报告家长信息，以下是一些指导原则可以帮助你：

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your legal parents (your biological and/or adoptive parents, or parents as determined by the state [e.g., a parent listed on your birth certificate]) are married to each other, answer the questions about both of them, regardless of whether your parents are of the same or opposite sex. If your legal parents are not married to each other and live together, answer the questions about both of them, regardless of whether your parents are of the same or opposite sex. If your legal parent is widowed or was never married, answer the questions about that parent.
source_blocks.text: 如果你的法定家长（你的亲生父母和/或养父母，或由州确定的家长 [例如，列在你出生证明上的家长]）彼此结婚，请回答关于他们双方的问题，无论你的家长是同性还是异性。 如果你的法定家长未彼此结婚但住在一起，请回答关于他们双方的问题，无论你的家长是同性还是异性。 如果你的法定家长丧偶或从未结婚，请回答关于该家长的问题。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if my parents are divorced or separated?
source_blocks.text: 如果我的父母离婚或分居怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: In this case, how you fill out the FAFSA form depends on whether your parents live together or not.
source_blocks.text: 在这种情况下，你如何填写FAFSA表格取决于你的父母是否住在一起。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Keep the following in mind as you read this section:
source_blocks.text: 在阅读本节时，请记住以下几点：

source_blocks.source_text_en: For FAFSA purposes, your married parents are separated if they are considered legally separated by a state, or if they are legally married but have chosen to live separate lives, including living in separate households, as though they were not married. When two married persons live as a married couple but are separated by physical distance (or have separate households), they are considered married for FAFSA purposes.
source_blocks.text: 出于FAFSA目的，如果你的已婚父母被州视为合法分居，或者他们合法结婚但选择分开生活，包括住在不同的家庭中，就像他们未结婚一样，则他们被视为分居。 当两个已婚人士作为已婚夫妇生活但因物理距离（或有不同的家庭）而分开时，出于FAFSA目的，他们被视为已婚。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Divorced or Separated Parents Who Do Not Live Together
source_blocks.text: 不住在一起的离婚或分居父母

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your parents are divorced or separated and don t live together, answer the questions about the parent with whom you lived more during the past 12 months.
source_blocks.text: 如果你的父母离婚或分居且不住在一起，请回答关于在过去12个月中你与之居住时间较长的家长的问题。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you lived the same amount of time with each divorced or separated parent, give answers about the parent who provided more financial support during the past 12 months or during the most recent 12 months that you actually received support from a parent.
source_blocks.text: 如果你与每位离婚或分居的父母居住的时间相同，请提供关于在过去12个月中或在你实际从家长那里获得支持的最远12个月中提供更多经济支持的家长的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Divorced or Separated Parents Who Live Together
source_blocks.text: 住在一起的离婚或分居父母

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your divorced parents live together, you ll indicate their marital status as Unmarried and both legal parents living together," and you will answer questions about both of them on the FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 如果你的离婚父母住在一起，你将在FAFSA表格上表明他们的婚姻状况为“未婚且双方法定家长住在一起”，并回答关于他们双方的问题。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your separated parents live together, you ll indicate their marital status as Married or remarried" (NOT Divorced or separated"), and you will answer questions about both of them on the FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 如果你的分居父母住在一起，你将在FAFSA表格上表明他们的婚姻状况为“已婚或再婚”（而非“离婚或分居”），并回答关于他们双方的问题。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I have a stepparent?
source_blocks.text: 如果我有继父或继母怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have a stepparent who is married to the legal parent whose information you re reporting, you must provide information about that stepparent as well.
source_blocks.text: 如果你有一个继父或继母，且该继父或继母与你正在报告其信息的法定父母结婚，则你也必须提供该继父或继母的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: EXCEPTION: The FAFSA form asks about your parents education level. For these two questions, your parents are considered to be your birth parents or adoptive parents your stepparent is not your parent in these questions.
source_blocks.text: 例外：FAFSA表格询问你父母的教育水平。对于这两个问题，你的父母被视为你的亲生父母或养父母，继父或继母不视为你的父母。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Including your stepparent s information on the FAFSA form helps create an accurate picture of your family s total financial strength.
source_blocks.text: 在FAFSA表格中包含继父或继母的信息有助于准确反映你家庭的总经济实力。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if my stepparent is widowed?
source_blocks.text: 如果我的继父或继母丧偶怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your stepparent was married to your parent but is now widowed, that stepparent doesn t count as a parent on your FAFSA form unless he or she has legally adopted you.
source_blocks.text: 如果你的继父或继母曾与你的父母结婚但现在丧偶，除非他或她已合法收养你，否则该继父或继母在FAFSA表格中不计为你的父母。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if my parents are in a same-sex marriage?
source_blocks.text: 如果我的父母是同性婚姻怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Same-sex couples must report their marital status as married if they were legally married in a state or other jurisdiction (foreign country), without regard to where they live or where the student will be going to school.
source_blocks.text: 同性伴侣如果在某个州或其他司法管辖区（外国）合法结婚，则必须报告其婚姻状况为已婚，无论他们居住在哪里或学生将去哪里上学。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The FAFSA questions use gender-neutral terminology for married parents ( Parent 1 (father/mother/stepparent)" and Parent 2 (father/mother/stepparent)" instead of mother" and father"). It does not matter which parent completes which set of questions.
source_blocks.text: FAFSA问题对已婚父母使用性别中立的术语（“父母1（父亲/母亲/继父或继母）”和“父母2（父亲/母亲/继父或继母）”，而不是“母亲”和“父亲”）。哪一方填写哪组问题并不重要。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I live with someone other than my parents?
source_blocks.text: 如果我和父母以外的人住在一起怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: It doesn t matter if you don t live with your parent or parents; you still must report information about them. The following people are not your parents unless they have legally adopted you: grandparents, foster parents, legal guardians, older brothers or sisters, uncles or aunts, and widowed stepparents.
source_blocks.text: 即使你不与父母同住，你仍然必须报告他们的信息。以下人员除非已合法收养你，否则不视为你的父母：祖父母、寄养父母、法定监护人、哥哥姐姐、叔叔阿姨以及丧偶的继父或继母。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What kind of information must my parents provide for the FAFSA form?
source_blocks.text: 我的父母必须为FAFSA表格提供哪些信息？

source_blocks.source_text_en: For each parent, you ll report similar information to that you report for yourself: basic information about your parent s identity (e.g., name, date of birth, and Social Security number if he or she has one); living situation (e.g., marital status, state of residence, household size); and financial circumstances (e.g., tax information, certain assets, certain untaxed income). Learn more about the types of information you and your parents will report on the FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 对于每位父母，你需要报告与你为自己报告类似的信息：关于你父母身份的基本信息（例如姓名、出生日期和社会安全号码，如果有）；居住情况（例如婚姻状况、居住州、家庭人数）；以及财务状况（例如税务信息、某些资产、某些未征税收入）。了解更多关于你和你的父母将在FAFSA表格上报告的信息类型。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I'm unable to provide parent information due to special circumstances?
source_blocks.text: 如果我因特殊情况无法提供父母信息怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: In situations such as the ones below, you may be able to submit your FAFSA form without parent information despite being considered a dependent student:
source_blocks.text: 在以下情况下，即使你被视为受抚养学生，也可能无需父母信息即可提交FAFSA表格：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your parents are incarcerated. You have left home due to an abusive family environment. You do not know where your parents are and are unable to contact them (and you have not been adopted). You are older than 21 but not yet 24, are unaccompanied, and are either homeless or self-supporting and at risk of being homeless.
source_blocks.text: 你的父母被监禁。 你因家庭虐待环境而离家。 你不知道父母的下落且无法联系他们（且你未被收养）。 你年龄超过21岁但未满24岁，无人陪伴，并且无家可归或自食其力且面临无家可归的风险。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are filling out the FAFSA form online or on the myStudentAid app, you will be asked whether you are able to provide information about your parents. If you are not, you will have the option to indicate that you have special circumstances that make you unable to get your parents information. You will then be able to submit your application without entering data about your parents.
source_blocks.text: 如果你在线或通过myStudentAid应用程序填写FAFSA表格，系统会询问你是否能够提供父母信息。如果不能，你可以选择表明你有特殊情况导致无法获取父母信息。然后你可以在不输入父母数据的情况下提交申请。

source_blocks.source_text_en: However, it is important for you to understand the following:
source_blocks.text: 然而，你需要了解以下重要事项：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Although your FAFSA form will be submitted, it will not be fully processed. You will not receive an Expected Family Contribution (EFC) and must immediately contact the financial aid office at the college or career school you plan to attend. The financial aid staff may ask for additional information to determine whether you can be considered independent and have an EFC calculated without parent data. Gather as much written evidence of your situation as you can. Written evidence may include court or law enforcement documents; letters from a clergy member, school counselor or social worker; and/or any other relevant data that explains your special circumstance. The financial aid office s decision about your dependency status is final and cannot be appealed to the U.S. Department of Education.
source_blocks.text: 尽管您的FAFSA表格将被提交，但不会得到完全处理。您将不会收到预期家庭贡献（EFC），并且必须立即联系您计划就读的学院或职业学校的财政援助办公室。 财政援助工作人员可能会要求提供额外信息，以确定您是否可以被视为独立学生，并在没有家长数据的情况下计算EFC。尽可能多地收集您情况的书面证据。书面证据可能包括法院或执法文件；神职人员、学校辅导员或社会工作者的信件；和/或任何其他解释您特殊情况的有关数据。 财政援助办公室关于您依赖状态的决定是最终的，不能向美国教育部提出上诉。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if my parents are unwilling to provide their information on my FAFSA form?
source_blocks.text: 如果我的父母不愿意在FAFSA表格上提供他们的信息怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can t be considered independent of your parents just because they refuse to help you with the FAFSA form. Still, we do understand that in some cases, the parents are not supporting the dependent student at all and refuse to provide their information on the student s application. If you re in that situation, here s the process for filling out the FAFSA form online (or on the myStudentAid app):
source_blocks.text: 仅仅因为您的父母拒绝帮助您填写FAFSA表格，您就不能被视为独立于父母的学生。尽管如此，我们确实理解在某些情况下，父母完全不支持受抚养学生，并拒绝在学生的申请中提供他们的信息。如果您处于这种情况，以下是在线（或通过myStudentAid应用程序）填写FAFSA表格的流程：

source_blocks.source_text_en: When the FAFSA form asks you to provide information about your parents, select the I am unable to provide information about my parent(s) option. (If you are using the myStudentAid app, you will need to select the Learn more link when you get to the point in the app where it tells you that it looks like parent information is required to calculate your EFC.) You will then be provided with an explanation of what s considered a special circumstance. After reading through the options, select the one that says you don t have a special circumstance but you still can t provide parent information. (If you are using the myStudentAid app, you will need to select the option indicating that you d like to be considered for an unsubsidized loan.) The application explains that if your parents don t support you and refuse to provide their information on the application, you may submit your FAFSA form without their information. However, you won t be able to get any federal student aid other than an unsubsidized loan and even that might not happen. The decision is up to the financial aid office at the college or career school you plan to attend. If you agree to this, you may submit your FAFSA form without parent information. Your FAFSA information will be sent to the colleges you list, but you won t get an EFC. You must immediately contact your school s financial aid office to discuss the possibility of getting an unsubsidized loan. The financial aid office may ask for a written statement from your parents, indicating that they refuse to provide their information on the FAFSA form and that they no longer support you. (Forms of support include allowing you to live in their home, including you on their car or health insurance, providing a car to drive on a regular basis, and payment of your tuition or fees.) The financial aid office will look at your situation and decide whether you may receive an unsubsidized loan. That decision is final and cannot be appealed to the U.S. Department of Education.
source_blocks.text: 当FAFSA表格要求您提供有关父母的信息时，请选择“我无法提供有关我父母的信息”选项。（如果您使用myStudentAid应用程序，当您到达应用程序中提示您需要父母信息来计算您的EFC时，您需要选择“了解更多”链接。） 然后，您将看到关于什么构成特殊情况的说明。阅读完选项后，选择表明您没有特殊情况但仍无法提供父母信息的选项。（如果您使用myStudentAid应用程序，您需要选择表明您希望被考虑获得无补贴贷款的选项。） 应用程序说明，如果您的父母不支持您并拒绝在申请中提供他们的信息，您可以在没有他们信息的情况下提交FAFSA表格。但是，除了无补贴贷款外，您将无法获得任何其他联邦学生援助，甚至可能无法获得无补贴贷款。决定权在您计划就读的学院或职业学校的财政援助办公室。如果您同意这一点，您可以在没有父母信息的情况下提交FAFSA表格。 您的FAFSA信息将发送给您列出的学院，但您不会收到EFC。 您必须立即联系您学校的财政援助办公室，讨论获得无补贴贷款的可能性。财政援助办公室可能会要求您的父母提供书面声明，表明他们拒绝在FAFSA表格上提供信息，并且不再支持您。（支持形式包括允许您住在他们家中、将您纳入他们的汽车或健康保险、定期提供汽车供您驾驶，以及支付您的学费或杂费。） 财政援助办公室将审查您的情况，并决定您是否可以获得无补贴贷款。该决定是最终的，不能向美国教育部提出上诉。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re considering following this process, think about this first: If you submit your FAFSA form without parent information, you will not receive an EFC. Some state- or school-based aid programs look at the EFC in order to determine your eligibility for their funds; because you won t have an EFC, you won t be considered for those aid programs. You could be giving up a chance at many sources of aid. So encourage your parents to provide their information doing so won t require them to support you in any way, it ll just help you be considered for as many sources of financial aid as possible.
source_blocks.text: 如果您正在考虑遵循此流程，请先考虑这一点：如果您在没有父母信息的情况下提交FAFSA表格，您将不会收到EFC。一些州或学校为基础的援助项目会查看EFC以确定您是否有资格获得他们的资金；因为您不会有EFC，您将不会被考虑参加这些援助项目。您可能会放弃许多援助来源的机会。因此，请鼓励您的父母提供他们的信息——这样做不会要求他们以任何方式支持您，只会帮助您尽可能多地获得财政援助来源的考虑。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if my parents are concerned about providing their information because of their citizenship status?
source_blocks.text: 如果我的父母因为他们的公民身份状况而担心提供信息怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your parents citizenship status does not affect your eligibility for federal student aid. In fact, the FAFSA form doesn t even ask about your parents status.
source_blocks.text: 您父母的公民身份状况不会影响您获得联邦学生援助的资格。事实上，FAFSA表格甚至不会询问您父母的身份状况。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How should we report information about my noncitizen parents on my FAFSA form?
source_blocks.text: 我们应该如何在FAFSA表格上报告我非公民父母的信息？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here are some tips for students with noncitizen parents:
source_blocks.text: 以下是一些针对父母为非公民的学生的提示：

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your parent does not have a Social Security number (SSN), you should enter all zeroes for him or her on the FAFSA form where it asks for that information. Do NOT enter a Taxpayer Identification Number in the SSN field. If your parent doesn t have an SSN, he or she won t be able to create an FSA ID (which requires an SSN) and therefore won t be able to sign your FAFSA form electronically (either online or via the myStudentAid app). From the online form (you can t print a signature page from the app), you ll need to select the option to print a signature page when you get to the end of the application. Print the page, have your parent sign it, and then mail it to the address indicated so that your FAFSA form can be processed. If your parent doesn't live in the U.S., select "Foreign Country" from the dropdown box for the question that asks about the parents' state of legal residence. If your parents live and file taxes in a foreign country and don t file U.S. taxes, you ll have the opportunity to indicate that they have filed their taxes. - Then, when the FAFSA form asks whether your parents filed a Puerto Rican or foreign tax return, you should select Yes." - Convert the amounts on the foreign tax return into U.S. dollars as directed by the FAFSA help and hints. - If your parents live in one of the Freely Associated States, they should enter the Amount of Wages Earned from their Freely Associated States tax form in the field where the FAFSA form asks for adjusted gross income. If your parent doesn t file taxes at all, select Not going to file" for the question that asks whether the parent(s) have filed taxes. Then you ll be asked for information about how much your parent earned from work, rather than being asked for information about specific items on the tax form.
source_blocks.text: 如果您的父母没有社会安全号码（SSN），您应该在FAFSA表格上要求该信息的地方为他或她输入全零。不要在SSN字段中输入纳税人识别号。 如果您的父母没有SSN，他或她将无法创建FSA ID（这需要SSN），因此将无法以电子方式签署您的FAFSA表格（无论是在线还是通过myStudentAid应用程序）。从在线表格（您无法从应用程序打印签名页），您需要在应用程序结束时选择打印签名页的选项。打印该页面，让您的父母签名，然后邮寄到指示的地址，以便您的FAFSA表格得到处理。 如果您的父母不住在美国，请在询问父母合法居住州的问题的下拉框中选择“外国”。 如果您的父母在外国居住并报税，且不提交美国税款，您将有机会表明他们已经提交了税款。 - 然后，当FAFSA表格询问您的父母是否提交了波多黎各或外国纳税申报表时，您应选择“是”。 - 按照FAFSA帮助和提示的指示，将外国纳税申报表上的金额转换为美元。 - 如果您的父母居住在自由联合国家之一，他们应在FAFSA表格要求调整后总收入的地方输入其自由联合国家税表上的工资收入金额。 如果您的父母根本不报税，请在选择父母是否已提交税款的选项中选择“不打算报税”。然后，您将被要求提供有关您的父母从工作中赚取多少的信息，而不是被要求提供税表上特定项目的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Standard Plan | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 标准还款计划 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Standard Repayment Plan is the basic repayment plan for loans from the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program and Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program.
source_blocks.text: 标准还款计划是威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款（直接贷款）计划和联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划下贷款的基本还款计划。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Payments are fixed and made for up to 10 years (between 10 and 30 years for consolidation loans).
source_blocks.text: 还款金额固定，最长还款期为10年（合并贷款为10至30年）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: This repayment plan saves you money over time because your monthly payments may be slightly higher than payments made under other plans, but you ll pay off your loan in the shortest time. For this reason, you will pay the least amount of interest over the life of your loan.
source_blocks.text: 该还款计划从长远来看能为您节省资金，因为您的每月还款额可能略高于其他计划下的还款额，但您将在最短时间内还清贷款。因此，在整个贷款期限内，您支付的利息总额将是最少的。

source_blocks.source_text_en: When it comes time to repay your loans, you have the option to choose a repayment plan. If you don t choose a different repayment plan, your loan servicer, the company that handles the billing and other services on your federal education loan, will place you on the Standard Repayment Plan.
source_blocks.text: 当需要偿还贷款时，您可以选择还款计划。如果您未选择其他还款计划，您的贷款服务机构（负责处理您的联邦教育贷款账单及其他服务的公司）将为您安排标准还款计划。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Eligible Federal Loans
source_blocks.text: 符合条件的联邦贷款

source_blocks.source_text_en: The following loans from the Direct Loan Program and the FFEL Program are eligible for the Standard Repayment Plan:
source_blocks.text: 以下来自直接贷款计划和FFEL计划的贷款符合标准还款计划的条件：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct Subsidized Loans Direct Unsubsidized Loans Direct PLUS Loans Direct Consolidation Loans Subsidized Federal Stafford Loans Unsubsidized Federal Stafford Loans FFEL PLUS Loans
source_blocks.text: 直接补贴贷款 直接非补贴贷款 直接PLUS贷款 直接合并贷款 补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款 非补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款 FFEL PLUS贷款

source_blocks.source_text_en: FFEL Consolidation Loans
source_blocks.text: FFEL合并贷款

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note that no new loans have been made under the FFEL Program since July 1, 2010.
source_blocks.text: 请注意，自2010年7月1日起，FFEL计划下不再发放新贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Monthly Payments for Federal Education Loans Except Consolidation Loans
source_blocks.text: 联邦教育贷款（合并贷款除外）的每月还款额

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under this plan, your monthly payments are a fixed amount of at least \$50 each month and made for up to 10 years for all loan types except Direct Consolidation Loans and FFEL Consolidation Loans.
source_blocks.text: 在此计划下，您的每月还款额为固定金额，每月至少50美元，最长还款期为10年，适用于除直接合并贷款和FFEL合并贷款以外的所有贷款类型。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Monthly Payments for Consolidation Loans
source_blocks.text: 合并贷款的每月还款额

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under this plan, your monthly payments are
source_blocks.text: 在此计划下，您的每月还款额为

source_blocks.source_text_en: a fixed amount of at least \$50 each month and made for a period of between 10 and 30 years for Direct Consolidation Loans and FFEL Consolidation Loans.
source_blocks.text: 每月固定金额至少50美元，并且 直接合并贷款和FFEL合并贷款的还款期为10至30年。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have a Direct Consolidation Loan or FFEL Consolidation Loan, the length of your repayment period will depend on the amount of your total education loan indebtedness. This total education loan indebtedness includes the amount of your consolidation loan and your other student loan debt. Other student loan debt includes any federal student loans that are not included in the consolidation loan, as well as private education loans that are not eligible for consolidation.
source_blocks.text: 如果您有直接合并贷款或FFEL合并贷款，您的还款期长度将取决于您的总教育贷款债务金额。此总教育贷款债务包括您的合并贷款金额和其他学生贷款债务。其他学生贷款债务包括未纳入合并贷款的任何联邦学生贷款，以及不符合合并条件的私人教育贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The maximum amount of other student loan debt that may be considered in determining your repayment period may not exceed the loan amount you are consolidating.
source_blocks.text: 在确定您的还款期时，可考虑的其他学生贷款债务的最高金额不得超过您正在合并的贷款金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To include other student loan debt in the determination of the repayment period for your Direct Consolidation Loan, be sure to list those loans on your consolidation application in the section for listing loans that you do not want to consolidate, but want considered in the determination of your repayment period.
source_blocks.text: 要将其他学生贷款债务纳入直接合并贷款还款期的确定中，请务必在合并申请中列出这些贷款，在用于列出您不希望合并但希望纳入还款期确定范围的贷款的栏目中填写。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The chart below shows the maximum repayment period for a Direct Consolidation Loan or FFEL Consolidation Loan under the Standard Repayment Plan depending on total education loan indebtedness.
source_blocks.text: 下表显示了在标准还款计划下，直接合并贷款或FFEL合并贷款根据总教育贷款债务额确定的最长还款期。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Using Loan Simulator to Estimate Your Eligibility and Payment Amount Under the Standard Repayment Plan
source_blocks.text: 使用贷款模拟器估算您在标准还款计划下的资格和还款金额

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your loan servicer can help you choose a loan repayment plan that s best for you. Before you contact your loan servicer to discuss repayment plans, use our Loan Simulator to get an early look at what repayment plans you may be eligible for and to receive a comparison of estimated monthly payment amounts for all federal student loan repayment plans. This comparison is important because the Standard Plan may not provide you with the lowest payment amount based on your individual circumstances. You may find that your payment will be lower under another repayment plan.
source_blocks.text: 您的贷款服务机构可以帮助您选择最适合您的贷款还款计划。在联系您的贷款服务机构讨论还款计划之前，请使用我们的贷款模拟器提前了解您可能有资格获得的还款计划，并获取所有联邦学生贷款还款计划的预计月还款金额比较。这一比较很重要，因为根据您的个人情况，标准计划可能无法为您提供最低的还款金额。您可能会发现，在其他还款计划下，您的还款金额会更低。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Staying Eligible | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 保持资格 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you want to keep receiving your federal student aid, make sure you stay eligible.
source_blocks.text: 如果你想继续获得联邦学生援助，请确保你保持资格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You ll need to continue to meet the basic eligibility criteria, make satisfactory academic progress, and fill out the FAFSA form every year.
source_blocks.text: 你需要继续满足基本资格标准，取得令人满意的学业进步，并每年填写FAFSA表格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Once you ve filled out your Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form and received your grant, loan, or work-study funds to help you pay for college or career school, make sure you stay eligible throughout the academic year and in subsequent years.
source_blocks.text: 一旦你填写了联邦学生援助免费申请（FAFSA）表格，并获得了助学金、贷款或勤工助学资金来帮助你支付大学或职业学校的费用，请确保你在整个学年及以后的年份中保持资格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Continue to Meet Basic Eligibility Criteria
source_blocks.text: 继续满足基本资格标准

source_blocks.source_text_en: Remember, the basic eligibility criteria that allow you to get federal student aid continue to apply throughout the time you re receiving aid not just when you first fill out the FAFSA form and are awarded aid.
source_blocks.text: 请记住，允许你获得联邦学生援助的基本资格标准在你接受援助的整个期间都适用，而不仅仅是在你首次填写FAFSA表格并获得援助时。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Make Satisfactory Academic Progress
source_blocks.text: 取得令人满意的学业进步

source_blocks.source_text_en: You need to make satisfactory academic progress in order to continue receiving federal student aid. In other words, you have to make good enough grades, and complete enough classes (credits, hours, etc.), to keep moving toward successfully completing your degree or certificate in a time period that s acceptable to your school.
source_blocks.text: 你需要取得令人满意的学业进步才能继续获得联邦学生援助。换句话说，你必须取得足够好的成绩，并完成足够的课程（学分、学时等），以便在你学校可接受的时间范围内，持续朝着成功完成学位或证书的目标前进。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Each school has a satisfactory academic progress policy for financial aid purposes; to see your school s, you can check your school s website or ask someone at the financial aid office. Your school s policy will tell you
source_blocks.text: 每所学校都有针对经济援助目的的学业进步满意政策；要查看你学校的政策，你可以查看学校网站或咨询经济援助办公室的人员。你学校的政策将告诉你：

source_blocks.source_text_en: what grade-point average (or equivalent standard) you need to maintain; how quickly you need to be moving toward graduation (for instance, how many credits you should have successfully completed by the end of each year); how an incomplete class, withdrawal, repeated class, change of major, or transfer of credits from another school affects your satisfactory academic progress; how often your school will evaluate your progress; what will happen if you fail to make satisfactory academic progress when your school evaluates you; whether you are allowed to appeal your school s decision that you haven t made satisfactory academic progress (reasons for appeal usually include the death of a member of your family, your illness or injury, or other special circumstances); and how you can regain eligibility for federal student aid.
source_blocks.text: 你需要保持的绩点（或同等标准）； 你需要以多快的速度朝着毕业前进（例如，每年结束时你应该成功完成多少学分）； 未完成的课程、退课、重修课程、更换专业或从其他学校转学分如何影响你的学业进步满意状态； 你的学校多久评估一次你的进步； 如果你的学校评估时你未能取得令人满意的学业进步，会发生什么； 你是否被允许对学校关于你未取得满意学业进步的决定提出申诉（申诉理由通常包括家庭成员去世、你的疾病或受伤，或其他特殊情况）；以及 你如何重新获得联邦学生援助的资格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Fill Out the FAFSA Form Each Year
source_blocks.text: 每年填写FAFSA表格

source_blocks.source_text_en: When you fill out the FAFSA form, you are applying for aid for a specific year. In order to receive aid the next year, you ll need to submit that next year s FAFSA form. Luckily, the FAFSA website makes it easy for you by allowing you to submit a Renewal FAFSA form that remembers certain information you reported the year before and places it in your new FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: 当你填写FAFSA表格时，你是在申请特定年度的援助。为了在接下来的一年获得援助，你需要提交下一年的FAFSA表格。幸运的是，FAFSA网站让你轻松做到这一点，它允许你提交一份续填FAFSA表格，该表格会记住你上一年报告的某些信息，并将其放入你的新FAFSA表格中。

source_blocks.source_text_en: After you submit your Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form, you ll get a Student Aid Report that summarizes the information you provided on your application.
source_blocks.text: After you submit your Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form, you ll get a Student Aid Report that summarizes the information you provided on your application.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Review your Student Aid Report carefully to make sure it s correct and complete.
source_blocks.text: Review your Student Aid Report carefully to make sure it s correct and complete.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your Student Aid Report (SAR) is a paper or electronic document that gives you some basic information about your eligibility for federal student aid as well as listing your answers to the FAFSAquestions.
source_blocks.text: Your Student Aid Report (SAR) is a paper or electronic document that gives you some basic information about your eligibility for federal student aid as well as listing your answers to the FAFSAquestions.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How and when will I get my SAR?
source_blocks.text: How and when will I get my SAR?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Whether you receive your SAR online or on paper depends on whether you provide an email address on your FAFSA form.
source_blocks.text: Whether you receive your SAR online or on paper depends on whether you provide an email address on your FAFSA form.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you provide a valid email address, you ll receive an email from noreply@FAFSA.gov with instructions on how to access an online copy of your SAR.
source_blocks.text: If you provide a valid email address, you ll receive an email from noreply@FAFSA.gov with instructions on how to access an online copy of your SAR.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you don't provide a valid email address on your FAFSA form, you will receive either a SAR or a SAR Acknowledgement via postal mail.
source_blocks.text: If you don't provide a valid email address on your FAFSA form, you will receive either a SAR or a SAR Acknowledgement via postal mail.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The SAR lists your FAFSA information and provides space for you to make corrections. You will receive a paper SAR if you file a paper FAFSA form and don t provide an email address. The SAR Acknowledgement lists your FAFSA information, but you ll need to make any corrections at fafsa.gov. You ll receive a SAR Acknowledgement if you file an electronic FAFSA form and don t provide an email address.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have an FSA ID (username and password) and your FAFSA information has been processed, you can log in at fafsa.gov to view SAR information regardless of whether you filled out the FAFSA form online, on the myStudentAid app, or on a FAFSA PDF or whether you provided an email address or not.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What information does a SAR contain?
source_blocks.text: What information does a SAR contain?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your application is complete, an Expected Family Contribution (EFC) will display in the upper right-hand corner of your SAR. If your application is incomplete, your SAR will not include an EFC, but it will tell you what you need to do to resolve any issues.
source_blocks.text: If your application is complete, an Expected Family Contribution (EFC) will display in the upper right-hand corner of your SAR. If your application is incomplete, your SAR will not include an EFC, but it will tell you what you need to do to resolve any issues.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The SAR also contains a four-digit Data Release Number (DRN), which appears on the first page in the upper right corner of the paper SAR and SAR Acknowledgement. On the electronic SAR, the DRN is located in the box that contains the Application Receipt date, below the EFC. You will need the DRN if you choose to allow your college or career school to change certain information on your FAFSA form.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What am I supposed to do with my SAR?
source_blocks.text: What am I supposed to do with my SAR?

source_blocks.source_text_en: When you get your SAR, review it carefully to make sure it s correct and complete. The school(s) you listed on your FAFSA form will use your information to determine your eligibility for federal and possibly nonfederal financial aid. A school may ask you to verify the accuracy of your FAFSA data, so you need to be sure the information is correct.
source_blocks.text: When you get your SAR, review it carefully to make sure it s correct and complete. The school(s) you listed on your FAFSA form will use your information to determine your eligibility for federal and possibly nonfederal financial aid. A school may ask you to verify the accuracy of your FAFSA data, so you need to be sure the information is correct.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you don t have any changes to make to the information listed on your SAR, just keep it for your records.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Student Loan Consolidation | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 学生贷款合并 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: Consolidating your federal education loans can simplify your payments, but it also can result in the loss of some benefits.
source_blocks.text: 合并您的联邦教育贷款可以简化您的还款，但也可能导致某些福利的丧失。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn about consolidation so you can weigh the pros and cons and decide whether a Direct Consolidation Loan is right for you.
source_blocks.text: 了解合并，以便您权衡利弊，决定直接合并贷款是否适合您。

source_blocks.source_text_en: A Direct Consolidation Loan allows you to consolidate (combine) multiple federal education loans into one loan. The result is a single monthly payment instead of multiple payments. Loan consolidation can also give you access to additional loan repayment plans and forgiveness programs.
source_blocks.text: 直接合并贷款允许您将多笔联邦教育贷款合并（组合）为一笔贷款。结果是每月只需支付一次，而不是多次支付。贷款合并还可以让您获得额外的还款计划和免除计划。

source_blocks.source_text_en: There is no application fee to consolidate your federal education loans into a Direct Consolidation Loan.
source_blocks.text: 将您的联邦教育贷款合并为直接合并贷款无需申请费。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may be contacted by private companies that offer to help you apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan, for a fee. These companies have no affiliation with the U.S. Department of Education (ED) or ED s consolidation loan servicers. There s no need to pay anyone for assistance in getting a Direct Consolidation Loan. The application process is easy and free.
source_blocks.text: 您可能会被提供有偿帮助您申请直接合并贷款的私营公司联系。这些公司与美国教育部（ED）或其合并贷款服务机构没有任何关联。无需付费请人帮助您获得直接合并贷款。申请过程简单且免费。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Should I consolidate my loans?
source_blocks.text: 我应该合并我的贷款吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: The answer depends on your individual circumstances.
source_blocks.text: 答案取决于您的个人情况。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Pros
source_blocks.text: 优点

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you currently have federal student loans that are with different loan servicers, consolidation can greatly simplify loan repayment by giving you a single loan with just one monthly bill. Consolidation can lower your monthly payment by giving you a longer period of time (up to 30 years) to repay your loans. If you consolidate loans other than Direct Loans, consolidation may give you access to additional income-driven repayment plan options and Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF). (Direct Loans are from the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan Program.) You ll be able to switch any variable-rate loans you have to a fixed interest rate.
source_blocks.text: 如果您目前有由不同贷款服务机构服务的联邦学生贷款，合并可以通过为您提供一笔贷款和一张月度账单来大大简化贷款还款。 合并可以通过给您更长的时间（最长30年）来偿还贷款，从而降低您的每月还款额。 如果您合并除直接贷款以外的贷款，合并可能使您获得额外的收入驱动还款计划和公共服务贷款免除（PSLF）。（直接贷款来自威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款计划。） 您可以将任何浮动利率贷款转换为固定利率。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Cons
source_blocks.text: 缺点

source_blocks.source_text_en: Because consolidation usually increases the period of time you have to repay your loans, you will likely make more payments and pay more in interest than would be the case if you didn t consolidate. When you consolidate your loans, any outstanding interest on the loans that you consolidate becomes part of the original principal balance on your consolidation loan, which means that interest may accrue on a higher principal balance than might have been the case if you had not consolidated. Consolidation may also cause you to lose certain borrower benefits such as interest rate discounts, principal rebates, or some loan cancellation benefits that are associated with your current loans. If you re paying your current loans under an income-driven repayment plan, or if you ve made qualifying payments toward Public Service Loan Forgiveness, consolidating your current loans will cause you to lose credit for any payments made toward income-driven repayment plan forgiveness or PSLF.
source_blocks.text: 由于合并通常会增加您偿还贷款的时间，您可能会比不合并时支付更多的款项和更多的利息。 当您合并贷款时，您所合并贷款上的任何未偿利息都会成为您合并贷款原始本金余额的一部分，这意味着利息可能会在比未合并时更高的本金余额上产生。 合并也可能导致您失去与当前贷款相关的某些借款人福利，如利率折扣、本金回扣或某些贷款取消福利。 如果您目前正在按收入驱动还款计划偿还贷款，或者您已经为公共服务贷款免除进行了符合条件的还款，合并您当前的贷款将导致您失去对收入驱动还款计划免除或PSLF的任何还款信用。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If consolidation would cause you to lose the benefits associated with some of your current loans and you are working toward earning those benefits, you should not include those loans in your new Direct Consolidation Loan. When you apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan, you don t have to consolidate all of your eligible loans.
source_blocks.text: 如果合并会导致您失去与当前某些贷款相关的福利，并且您正在努力获得这些福利，则不应将这些贷款纳入您的新直接合并贷款中。当您申请直接合并贷款时，您不必合并所有符合条件的贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For example, if you have both Direct Loans and other types of federal student loans, and you have been making payments toward PSLF on your Direct Loans, you should not consolidate your Direct Loans along with your other loans. Similarly, if you have Federal Perkins Loans and you are employed in an occupation that would qualify you for Perkins Loan cancellation benefits, you should not include your Perkins Loans when you consolidate. Leaving out your Direct Loans or Perkins Loans will preserve the benefits on those loans.
source_blocks.text: 例如，如果您同时拥有直接贷款和其他类型的联邦学生贷款，并且您一直在为您的直接贷款进行PSLF还款，则不应将您的直接贷款与其他贷款一起合并。同样，如果您有联邦帕金斯贷款，并且您从事的职业使您有资格获得帕金斯贷款取消福利，则您在合并时不应包括您的帕金斯贷款。将您的直接贷款或帕金斯贷款排除在外将保留这些贷款的福利。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you want to lower your monthly payment amount but are concerned about the impact of loan consolidation, you might want to consider deferment or forbearance as options for short-term payment relief, or consider switching to an income-driven repayment plan for longer-term payment relief.
source_blocks.text: 如果您想降低每月还款额，但担心贷款合并的影响，您可能要考虑延期还款或暂缓还款作为短期还款减免的选项，或者考虑转为收入驱动还款计划以获得长期还款减免。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Once your loans are combined into a Direct Consolidation Loan, they cannot be removed. The loans that were consolidated are paid off and no longer exist.
source_blocks.text: 一旦您的贷款合并为直接合并贷款，就无法移除。被合并的贷款已还清，不再存在。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What types of loans can be consolidated?
source_blocks.text: 哪些类型的贷款可以合并？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Most federal student loans, including the following, are eligible for consolidation:
source_blocks.text: 大多数联邦学生贷款，包括以下类型，都有资格合并：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Subsidized Federal Stafford Loans Unsubsidized and Nonsubsidized Federal Stafford Loans PLUS loans from the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program Supplemental Loans for Students Federal Perkins Loans Nursing Student Loans Nurse Faculty Loans Health Education Assistance Loans Health Professions Student Loans Loans for Disadvantaged Students Direct Subsidized Loans Direct Unsubsidized Loans Direct PLUS Loans FFEL Consolidation Loans and Direct Consolidation Loans (only under certain conditions) Federal Insured Student Loans Guaranteed Student Loans National Direct Student Loans National Defense Student Loans Parent Loans for Undergraduate Students Auxiliary Loans to Assist Students
source_blocks.text: 补贴性联邦斯塔福德贷款 非补贴性及无补贴性联邦斯塔福德贷款 联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划下的PLUS贷款 学生补充贷款 联邦帕金斯贷款 护理学生贷款 护士教师贷款 健康教育援助贷款 卫生专业学生贷款 贫困学生贷款 直接补贴贷款 直接非补贴贷款 直接PLUS贷款 FFEL合并贷款和直接合并贷款（仅在特定条件下） 联邦保险学生贷款 担保学生贷款 国家直接学生贷款 国防学生贷款 本科生家长贷款 辅助学生贷款

source_blocks.source_text_en: Private education loans are not eligible for consolidation, but for some Direct Consolidation Loan repayment plans, the total amount of your education loan debt including any private education loans determines how long you have to repay your Direct Consolidation Loan.
source_blocks.text: 私人教育贷款不符合合并条件，但对于某些直接合并贷款还款计划，您的教育贷款债务总额（包括任何私人教育贷款）决定了您需要多长时间偿还您的直接合并贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct PLUS Loans received by parents to help pay for a dependent student s education cannot be consolidated together with federal student loans that the student received.
source_blocks.text: 家长为帮助支付受抚养学生的教育而获得的直接PLUS贷款不能与学生获得的联邦学生贷款合并。

source_blocks.source_text_en: When can I consolidate my loans?
source_blocks.text: 我何时可以合并我的贷款？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Generally, you are eligible to consolidate after you graduate, leave school, or drop below half-time enrollment.
source_blocks.text: 一般来说，您在毕业、离开学校或注册状态降至半日制以下后，即有资格进行合并。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What are the requirements to consolidate a loan?
source_blocks.text: 合并贷款需要满足哪些要求？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here are some of the eligibility requirements for receiving a Direct Consolidation Loan:
source_blocks.text: 以下是获得直接合并贷款的一些资格要求：

source_blocks.source_text_en: The loans you consolidate must be in repayment or in the grace period. Generally, you cannot consolidate an existing consolidation loan unless you include an additional eligible loan in the consolidation. Under certain circumstances, you may reconsolidate an existing FFEL Consolidation Loan without including any additional loans.\ If you want to consolidate a defaulted loan, you must either make satisfactory repayment arrangements (defined as three consecutive monthly payments) on the loan before you consolidate, or you must agree to repay your new Direct Consolidation Loan under the - Income-Based Repayment Plan, - Pay As You Earn Repayment Plan, - Revised Pay As You Earn Repayment Plan, or - Income-Contingent Repayment Plan. If you want to consolidate a defaulted loan that is being collected through garnishment of your wages, or that is being collected in accordance with a court order after a judgment was obtained against you, you cannot consolidate the loan unless the wage garnishment order has been lifted or the judgment has been vacated.
source_blocks.text: 您要合并的贷款必须处于还款期或宽限期。 通常，除非您在合并中包含另一笔符合条件的贷款，否则您不能合并现有的合并贷款。 在某些情况下，您可以在不包含任何额外贷款的情况下重新合并现有的FFEL合并贷款。\ 如果您想合并违约贷款，您必须在合并前对贷款做出满意的还款安排（定义为连续三个月按时还款），或者您必须同意在新的直接合并贷款下还款，采用以下计划之一： - 基于收入的还款计划， - 按收入还款计划， - 修订版按收入还款计划，或 - 收入条件还款计划。 如果您想合并一笔违约贷款，而该贷款正通过工资扣押方式追收，或根据对您作出的判决后按法院命令追收，则除非工资扣押令已被解除或判决已被撤销，否则您不能合并该贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: \You may be able to reconsolidate an existing
source_blocks.text: \您可能能够重新合并现有的

source_blocks.source_text_en: delinquent or defaulted FFEL Consolidation Loan and repay your new Direct Consolidation Loan under an income-driven repayment plan; FFEL Consolidation Loan in order to qualify for the PSLF Program; or FFEL Consolidation Loan to use the no accrual of interest benefit for active duty service members, which states that you re not required to pay the interest that accrues during periods of qualifying active duty military service (for up to 60 months) on the portion of a Direct Consolidation Loan that repaid a Direct Loan Program or FFEL Program loan first disbursed on or after Oct. 1, 2008.
source_blocks.text: 拖欠或违约的FFEL合并贷款，并在新的直接合并贷款下按收入驱动还款计划还款； FFEL合并贷款，以便符合PSLF计划的资格；或 FFEL合并贷款，以利用现役军人免计利息的福利，该福利规定，在符合条件的现役军事服务期间（最长60个月），您无需支付直接合并贷款中用于偿还直接贷款计划或FFEL计划贷款（首次发放日期在2008年10月1日或之后）部分所产生的利息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is the interest rate on a consolidation loan?
source_blocks.text: 合并贷款的利率是多少？

source_blocks.source_text_en: A Direct Consolidation Loan has a fixed interest rate for the life of the loan. The fixed rate is the weighted average of the interest rates on the loans being consolidated, rounded up to the nearest one-eighth of one percent. There is no cap on the interest rate of a Direct Consolidation Loan.
source_blocks.text: 直接合并贷款在贷款期限内采用固定利率。固定利率是所合并贷款利率的加权平均值，向上取整至最接近的八分之一百分点。直接合并贷款的利率没有上限。

source_blocks.source_text_en: When do I begin repayment?
source_blocks.text: 我何时开始还款？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Repayment of a Direct Consolidation Loan will begin within 60 days after the loan is disbursed (paid out). Your loan servicer will let you know when the first payment is due.
source_blocks.text: 直接合并贷款的还款将在贷款发放（支付）后60天内开始。您的贷款服务商将告知您首次还款的到期日。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If any of the loans you want to consolidate are still in the grace period, you have the option of indicating on your Direct Consolidation Loan application that you want the servicer that is processing your application to delay the consolidation of your loans until closer to the grace period end date. If you select this option, you won t have to begin making payments on your new Direct Consolidation Loan until closer to the end of the grace period on your current loans.
source_blocks.text: 如果您要合并的任何贷款仍处于宽限期，您可以选择在直接合并贷款申请中注明，希望处理您申请的服务商将贷款合并推迟至接近宽限期结束日期。如果您选择此选项，您将无需在当前贷款的宽限期接近结束前开始支付新的直接合并贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Are there different repayment plans?
source_blocks.text: 是否有不同的还款计划？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Borrowers have different needs, so there are several repayment plans including income-driven repayment plans, which base your monthly payment amount on your income and family size. You ll select a repayment plan when you apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan. Learn about repayment plans.
source_blocks.text: 借款人有不同的需求，因此有几种还款计划，包括基于收入的还款计划，该计划根据您的收入和家庭规模确定每月还款金额。您在申请直接合并贷款时将选择还款计划。了解还款计划。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan?
source_blocks.text: 我如何申请直接合并贷款？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan. You can complete and submit the application online, or you can download and print a paper application for submission by U.S. mail.
source_blocks.text: 申请直接合并贷款。您可以在线填写并提交申请，或者下载并打印纸质申请表，通过美国邮政寄送。

source_blocks.source_text_en: After you submit your application electronically or by mailing a paper application, the consolidation servicer you selected will complete the actions required to consolidate your eligible loans. The consolidation servicer will be your point of contact for any questions you may have related to your consolidation application.
source_blocks.text: 在您通过电子方式提交申请或邮寄纸质申请后，您选择的合并服务机构将完成合并您符合条件的贷款所需的操作。合并服务机构将是您就合并申请相关问题联系的主要联系人。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Unless the loans you want to consolidate are in a deferment, forbearance, or grace period, it s important for you to continue making payments on those loans until your consolidation servicer tells you that they have been paid off by your new Direct Consolidation Loan.
source_blocks.text: 除非您想要合并的贷款处于延期还款、暂缓还款或宽限期，否则在合并服务机构通知您这些贷款已被新的直接合并贷款还清之前，您需要继续偿还这些贷款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Whom do I contact if I have questions about consolidation?
source_blocks.text: 如果我对合并有疑问，应该联系谁？

source_blocks.source_text_en: This depends on where you are in the consolidation process.
source_blocks.text: 这取决于您在合并过程中的阶段。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To ask questions about consolidating your loans before you apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan, contact the Student Loan Support Center at 1-800-557-7394.
source_blocks.text: 在申请直接合并贷款之前，如需咨询合并贷款的问题，请联系学生贷款支持中心，电话：1-800-557-7394。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To request technical assistance while you are logged in and completing the Federal Direct Consolidation Loan Application and Promissory Note online, either complete and submit the feedback form or contact the Student Loan Support Center at 1-800-557-7394.
source_blocks.text: 在您登录并在线填写联邦直接合并贷款申请表和本票时，如需技术帮助，请填写并提交反馈表，或联系学生贷款支持中心，电话：1-800-557-7394。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To ask questions after you have submitted your Federal Direct Consolidation Loan Application and Promissory Note, contact the servicer for your new Direct Consolidation Loan. If you submitted your application online, your consolidation servicer s contact information was provided at the end of the online process. If you submitted a paper application by U.S. mail, your consolidation servicer s contact information was available when you downloaded or printed the paper application.
source_blocks.text: 在您提交联邦直接合并贷款申请表和本票后，如有疑问，请联系您新的直接合并贷款的服务机构。如果您在线提交申请，您的合并服务机构的联系信息将在在线流程结束时提供。如果您通过美国邮政提交纸质申请，您的合并服务机构的联系信息在您下载或打印纸质申请表时即可获得。
