source_blocks.source_text_en: Student Loan Deferment | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 学生贷款延期偿还 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: Student loan deferment allows you to temporarily stop making payments.
source_blocks.text: 学生贷款延期偿还允许您暂时停止还款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Find out if a deferment is the best option for your situation.
source_blocks.text: 了解延期偿还是否是您情况下的最佳选择。

source_blocks.source_text_en: With deferment, you won t have to make a payment. However, you probably won t be making any progress toward forgiveness or paying back your loan. As an alternative, consider income-driven repayment.
source_blocks.text: 延期偿还期间，您无需还款。但是，您可能不会在贷款减免或偿还贷款方面取得任何进展。作为替代方案，请考虑收入驱动型还款计划。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Get Relief With Lower Payments on an Income-Driven Repayment Plan
source_blocks.text: 通过收入驱动型还款计划获得较低还款额的救济

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re having trouble repaying your loans due to circumstances that may continue for an extended period, or if you re unsure when you ll be able to afford to make your monthly loan payments again, a better option might be to consider changing to an income-driven repayment plan. Income-driven repayment plans base your monthly payments on your income and family size. In some cases, your payment could be as low as \$0 per month. Income-driven plans can also provide loan forgiveness if your loan isn t paid in full after 20 or 25 years.
source_blocks.text: 如果您因可能持续较长时间的情况而难以偿还贷款，或者您不确定何时能够再次负担得起每月贷款还款，更好的选择可能是考虑转为收入驱动型还款计划。收入驱动型还款计划根据您的收入和家庭规模计算每月还款额。在某些情况下，您的还款额可能低至每月0美元。收入驱动型计划还可以在您的贷款在20或25年后未还清时提供贷款减免。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Always contact your student loan servicer immediately if you re having trouble making your student loan payments.
source_blocks.text: 如果您在偿还学生贷款方面遇到困难，请务必立即联系您的学生贷款服务机构。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re seeking Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) or income-driven repayment forgiveness, in most cases deferment will not allow you to make progress toward forgiveness.
source_blocks.text: 如果您正在寻求公共服务贷款减免（PSLF）或收入驱动型还款减免，在大多数情况下，延期偿还不会让您在减免方面取得进展。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Be Aware That Interest Might Accrue During Deferment
source_blocks.text: 请注意延期偿还期间可能会产生利息

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re granted a deferment, you might still be responsible for paying the interest that accrues during the deferment period. The table below shows when you are responsible for paying the interest and when you are not responsible based on loan type.
source_blocks.text: 如果您获得延期偿还，您可能仍需负责支付延期偿还期间产生的利息。下表根据贷款类型显示了您何时负责支付利息以及何时不负责。

source_blocks.source_text_en: When you are responsible for paying the interest on your loans during a deferment, you can either pay the interest as it accrues, or you can allow it to accrue and be capitalized (added to your loan principal balance) at the end of the deferment period. If you don t pay the interest on your loan and allow it to be capitalized, the total amount you repay over the life of your loan may be higher. Unpaid interest is capitalized only on Direct Loans and FFEL Program loans. Unpaid interest is never capitalized on Perkins Loans.
source_blocks.text: 当您在延期偿还期间负责支付贷款利息时，您可以选择在利息产生时支付，或者允许其累积并在延期偿还期结束时资本化（添加到您的贷款本金余额中）。如果您不支付贷款利息并允许其资本化，您在贷款期限内偿还的总金额可能会更高。未付利息仅在直接贷款和联邦家庭教育贷款计划贷款上资本化。珀金斯贷款上的未付利息永远不会资本化。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Request a Deferment
source_blocks.text: 申请延期偿还

source_blocks.source_text_en: Most deferments are not automatic you need to submit a request to your student loan servicer, often on a form. Also, for most deferments, you must provide your student loan servicer with documentation to show that you meet the eligibility requirements for the deferment. Learn more about requirements and how to access request forms.
source_blocks.text: 大多数延期偿还并非自动生效——您需要向您的学生贷款服务机构提交申请，通常是通过表格。此外，对于大多数延期偿还，您必须向您的学生贷款服务机构提供文件，以证明您符合延期偿还的资格要求。了解更多关于要求以及如何获取申请表格的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understand Eligibility for a Deferment
source_blocks.text: 了解延期偿还的资格

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are a variety of circumstances that may qualify you for a deferment on your federal student loan.
source_blocks.text: 有多种情况可能使您有资格获得联邦学生贷款的延期偿还。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Cancer Treatment Deferment
source_blocks.text: 癌症治疗延期偿还

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may qualify for this deferment while you are undergoing cancer treatment and for the six-month period after your treatment ends.
source_blocks.text: 在接受癌症治疗期间以及治疗结束后的六个月内，您可能有资格获得此延期偿还。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete the Cancer Treatment Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 填写癌症治疗延期偿还申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Economic Hardship Deferment
source_blocks.text: 经济困难延期还款

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may qualify for this deferment if you
source_blocks.text: 如果您符合以下条件，您可能有资格获得此延期还款：

source_blocks.source_text_en: are receiving a means-tested benefit, like welfare (e.g., Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)); work full-time but have earnings that are below 150% of the poverty guideline for your family size and state of residence; or are serving in the Peace Corps.
source_blocks.text: 正在领取基于经济状况调查的福利，如公共援助（例如，贫困家庭临时援助（TANF））； 全职工作但收入低于您家庭规模和居住州贫困指南的150%；或 正在和平队服役。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can only receive this deferment for up to three years.
source_blocks.text: 您最多只能获得此延期还款三年。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete the Economic Hardship Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 填写经济困难延期还款申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Graduate Fellowship Deferment
source_blocks.text: 研究生奖学金延期还款

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may qualify for this deferment if you are enrolled in an approved graduate fellowship program. A graduate fellowship program is generally a program that provides financial support to graduate students to pursue graduate studies and research. Most graduate fellowship programs are for doctoral students, but some are available to master s degree students.
source_blocks.text: 如果您被录取到经批准的研究生奖学金项目，您可能有资格获得此延期还款。研究生奖学金项目通常是为研究生提供经济支持以进行研究生学习和研究的项目。大多数研究生奖学金项目面向博士生，但有些也面向硕士生。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete the Graduate Fellowship Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 填写研究生奖学金延期还款申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: In-School Deferment
source_blocks.text: 在校延期还款

source_blocks.source_text_en: You are eligible for this deferment if you re enrolled at least half-time at an eligible college or career school. If you re a graduate or professional student who received a Direct PLUS Loan, you qualify for an additional six months of deferment after you cease to be enrolled at least half-time.
source_blocks.text: 如果您在符合条件的学院或职业学校至少半日制注册，您就有资格获得此延期还款。如果您是获得直接PLUS贷款的研究生或专业学生，您在停止至少半日制注册后，有资格获得额外六个月的延期还款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Important! If you are enrolled in an eligible college or career school at least half-time, in most cases your loan will be placed into a deferment automatically based on enrollment information reported by your school, and your loan servicer will notify you that the deferment has been granted. If you enroll at least half-time but do not automatically receive a deferment, you should contact the school where you are enrolled. Your school will then report information about your enrollment status so that your loan can be placed into deferment.
source_blocks.text: 重要！如果您在符合条件的学院或职业学校至少半日制注册，在大多数情况下，您的贷款将根据您学校报告的注册信息自动进入延期还款状态，您的贷款服务机构将通知您延期还款已获批准。如果您至少半日制注册但没有自动获得延期还款，您应联系您注册的学校。您的学校随后将报告有关您注册状态的信息，以便您的贷款可以进入延期还款状态。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete the In-School Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 填写在校延期还款申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: In-school deferment is generally automatic, so in most cases it isn t necessary to complete the In-School Deferment Request. However, if you re enrolled at least half-time but do not automatically receive a deferment, you can either ask your school to report your enrollment information, as explained above, or complete the In-School Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 注意：在校延期还款通常是自动的，因此在大多数情况下无需填写在校延期还款申请表。但是，如果您至少半日制注册但没有自动获得延期还款，您可以按照上述说明要求您的学校报告您的注册信息，或填写在校延期还款申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Military Service and Post-Active Duty Student Deferment
source_blocks.text: 兵役和现役后学生延期还款

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may be eligible for this deferment if
source_blocks.text: 如果您符合以下条件，您可能有资格获得此延期还款：

source_blocks.source_text_en: you are on active duty military service in connection with a war, military operation, or national emergency; or you ve completed qualifying active duty service and any applicable grace period. This deferment ends when you resume enrollment in an eligible college or career school on at least a half-time basis or 13 months following the completion date of active duty service and any applicable grace period, whichever is earlier.
source_blocks.text: 您正在与战争、军事行动或国家紧急状态相关的现役军事服役中；或 您已完成符合条件的现役服役以及任何适用的宽限期。此延期还款在您以至少半日制身份重新注册到符合条件的学院或职业学校时结束，或在现役服役完成日期及任何适用宽限期后13个月结束，以较早者为准。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete the Military Service and Post-Active Duty Student Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 填写兵役和现役后学生延期还款申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Parent PLUS Borrower Deferment
source_blocks.text: 家长PLUS借款人延期还款

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may qualify for this deferment if you re a parent who received a Direct PLUS Loan to help pay for your child s education, and the student you took the loan out for is enrolled at least half-time at an eligible college or career school. You can also receive a deferment for an additional six months after the student ceases to be enrolled at least half-time.
source_blocks.text: 如果您是家长，为了帮助支付孩子的教育费用而获得了Direct PLUS贷款，并且您为其贷款的学生至少在半日制就读于符合条件的学院或职业学校，则您可能有资格获得此延期。在学生不再至少半日制就读后，您还可以额外获得六个月的延期。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete the Parent PLUS Borrower Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 填写家长PLUS借款人延期申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: As an alternative to completing the Parent PLUS Borrower Deferment Request, if the school your child is attending requires you to complete a Direct PLUS Loan Request, you can request this deferment when you submit the Direct PLUS Loan Request. Check with your child s school.
source_blocks.text: 注意：作为填写家长PLUS借款人延期申请表的替代方案，如果您孩子就读的学校要求您填写Direct PLUS贷款申请表，您可以在提交Direct PLUS贷款申请表时请求此延期。请咨询您孩子所在的学校。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Rehabilitation Training Deferment
source_blocks.text: 康复培训延期

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may qualify for this deferment if you re enrolled in an approved rehabilitation training program that is designed to provide vocational, drug abuse, mental health, or alcohol abuse rehabilitation treatment.
source_blocks.text: 如果您参加了一个经批准的康复培训项目，该项目旨在提供职业、药物滥用、心理健康或酒精滥用康复治疗，则您可能有资格获得此延期。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete the Rehabilitation Training Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 填写康复培训延期申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Unemployment Deferment
source_blocks.text: 失业延期

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may be eligible for this deferment if you receive unemployment benefits or you are seeking and unable to find full-time employment. You can receive this deferment for up to three years.
source_blocks.text: 如果您领取失业救济金，或者您正在寻找全职工作但未能找到，则您可能有资格获得此延期。您最多可以获得三年的此延期。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Complete the Unemployment Deferment Request.
source_blocks.text: 填写失业延期申请表。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you received federal student loans before July 1, 1993, you might be eligible for additional deferments. For more information about these deferments, contact your loan servicer.
source_blocks.text: 如果您在1993年7月1日之前获得了联邦学生贷款，您可能有资格获得额外的延期。有关这些延期的更多信息，请联系您的贷款服务机构。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Loan Types Eligible for Deferment
source_blocks.text: 符合延期条件的贷款类型

source_blocks.source_text_en: All the deferments are available to Direct Loan, FFEL Program loan, and Perkins Loan borrowers.
source_blocks.text: 所有延期均适用于直接贷款、FFEL计划贷款和珀金斯贷款借款人。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you received a Perkins Loan, you may also be eligible for a deferment while you are working toward cancellation on your Perkins Loan. Get contact information regarding your Perkins Loan.
source_blocks.text: 如果您获得了珀金斯贷款，您也可能有资格在努力争取珀金斯贷款取消期间获得延期。获取有关您珀金斯贷款的联系信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: In most cases, Perkins Loan recipients who receive a deferment will receive a six-month post-deferment grace period that begins on the date they no longer meet the deferment eligibility requirements. No payments are required during the post-deferment grace period.
source_blocks.text: 在大多数情况下，获得延期的珀金斯贷款借款人将获得六个月的延期后宽限期，该宽限期从他们不再满足延期资格要求之日起开始。在延期后宽限期内无需还款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You MUST continue making payments on your student loan(s) until you have been notified that your request for deferment has been granted. If you stop paying and your deferment is not approved, your loan(s) will become delinquent and you may go into default.
source_blocks.text: 在收到您的延期请求已获批准的通知之前，您必须继续偿还您的学生贷款。如果您停止还款且您的延期未获批准，您的贷款将逾期，并且您可能会违约。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Student loan forbearance allows you to temporarily stop making payments.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Find out if a forbearance is the best option for your situation.

source_blocks.source_text_en: With forbearance, you won t have to make a payment, or you can temporarily make a smaller payment. However, you probably won t be making any progress toward forgiveness or paying back your loan. As an alternative, consider income-driven repayment.

source_blocks.source_text_en: NEW: Automatic Suspension of Monthly Payments as a Result of the COVID-19 National Emergency
source_blocks.text: NEW: Automatic Suspension of Monthly Payments as a Result of the COVID-19 National Emergency

source_blocks.source_text_en: To provide relief to student loan borrowers during the COVID-19 national emergency, federal student loan borrowers are automatically being placed in an administrative forbearance, which allows you to temporarily stop making your monthly loan payments. This suspension of payments will last from March 13, 2020, through Sept. 30, 2020, but you can still make payments if you choose.
source_blocks.text: To provide relief to student loan borrowers during the COVID-19 national emergency, federal student loan borrowers are automatically being placed in an administrative forbearance, which allows you to temporarily stop making your monthly loan payments. This suspension of payments will last from March 13, 2020, through Sept. 30, 2020, but you can still make payments if you choose.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Have questions? Find out what loans qualify and get additional information about this forbearance and other student loan flexibilities due to the COVID-19 national emergency.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Get Relief With Lower Payments on an Income-Driven Repayment Plan
source_blocks.text: Get Relief With Lower Payments on an Income-Driven Repayment Plan

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re having trouble repaying your loans due to circumstances that may continue for an extended period, or if you re unsure when you ll be able to afford to make your monthly loan payments again, a better option might be to change to an income-driven repayment plan. Income-driven repayment plans base your monthly payments on your income and family size. In some cases, your payment could be as low as \$0 per month. They can also provide loan forgiveness if your loan is not paid in full after 20 or 25 years.

Unpaid interest is capitalized only on Direct Loans and Federal Family Education Loan FFEL Program loans. Unpaid interest is never capitalized on Federal Perkins Loans.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Most types of forbearance are not automatic you need to submit a request to your student loan servicer, often using a form. Also, for some types of forbearance, you must provide your student loan servicer with documentation to show that you meet the eligibility requirements for the forbearance you are requesting. Learn more about requirements and how to access request forms.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understand Eligibility for a Forbearance
source_blocks.text: Understand Eligibility for a Forbearance

source_blocks.source_text_en: There are two main types of forbearance: general and mandatory.

source_blocks.source_text_en: General Forbearance
source_blocks.text: General Forbearance

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your loan servicer decides whether to grant a request for a general forbearance. For this reason, a general forbearance is sometimes called a discretionary forbearance.
source_blocks.text: Your loan servicer decides whether to grant a request for a general forbearance. For this reason, a general forbearance is sometimes called a discretionary forbearance.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can request a general forbearance if you are temporarily unable to make your scheduled monthly loan payments for the following reasons:
source_blocks.text: You can request a general forbearance if you are temporarily unable to make your scheduled monthly loan payments for the following reasons:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Financial difficulties Medical expenses Change in employment Other reasons acceptable to your loan servicer

source_blocks.source_text_en: Loan Programs Eligible for General Forbearance
source_blocks.text: Loan Programs Eligible for General Forbearance

source_blocks.source_text_en: General forbearances are available for Direct Loans, Federal Family Education (FFEL) Program loans, and Perkins Loans.
source_blocks.text: General forbearances are available for Direct Loans, Federal Family Education (FFEL) Program loans, and Perkins Loans.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Duration of a General Forbearance
source_blocks.text: Duration of a General Forbearance

source_blocks.source_text_en: For loans made under all three programs, a general forbearance may be granted for no more than 12 months at a time. If you re still experiencing a hardship when your current forbearance expires, you may request another general forbearance. However, there is a cumulative limit on general forbearances of three years.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you meet the eligibility requirements for a mandatory forbearance, your loan servicer is required to grant the forbearance. You may be eligible for a mandatory forbearance in the following circumstances.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Once you graduate, drop below half-time enrollment, or leave school, your federal student loan goes into repayment. However, if you have a Direct Subsidized, Direct Unsubsidized, or Federal Family Education Loan, you have a six-month grace period before you are required to start making regular payments. source_blocks.source_text_en: The Grace Period
source_blocks.text: The Grace Period

source_blocks.source_text_en: For most federal student loan types, after you graduate, leave school, or drop below half-time enrollment, you have a six-month grace period (sometimes nine months for Perkins Loans) before you must begin making payments. This grace period gives you time to get financially settled and to select your repayment plan. Not all federal student loans have a grace period. Note that for most loans, interest accrues during your grace period. You can choose to pay the interest that accrues during your grace period. This prevents that interest from being added to the principal balance (also known as interest capitalization).

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans have a six-month grace period before payments are due. PLUS loans do not have a grace period; but if you received a PLUS loan as a graduate or professional student, you ll automatically get a six-month deferment after you graduate, leave school, or drop below half-time enrollment. No payments are required during this six-month deferment period. If you re a parent borrower who took out a PLUS loan to pay for your child s education, you can request a six-month deferment after your child graduates, leaves school, or drops below half-time enrollment. Contact your loan servicer for more information. If you received a Federal Perkins Loan, check with the school where you received your loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Active duty military If you are called to active military duty for more than 30 days before the end of your grace period, you will receive the full six-month grace period when you return from active duty. Returning to school before the end of your loan s grace period If you reenroll in school at least half-time before the end of your grace period, you will receive the full six-month grace period when you stop attending school or drop below half-time enrollment. Loan consolidation If you consolidate your loans during your grace period, you give up the remainder of your grace period and begin repayment after your Direct Consolidation Loan is processed (unless you request to have the processing of your consolidation loan delayed until closer to the end of your grace period).

source_blocks.source_text_en: The U.S. Department of Education offers low-interest loans to eligible students to help cover the cost of college or career school.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Students may be eligible to receive subsidized and unsubsidized loans based on their financial need.
source_blocks.text: Students may be eligible to receive subsidized and unsubsidized loans based on their financial need.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Subsidized and unsubsidized loans are federal student loans for eligible students to help cover the cost of higher education at a four-year college or university, community college, or trade, career, or technical school. The U.S. Department of Education offers eligible students at participating schools Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans. (Some people refer to these loans as Stafford Loans or Direct Stafford Loans.)

The U.S. Department of Education offers eligible students at participating schools Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans. (Some people refer to these loans as Stafford Loans or Direct Stafford Loans.)

source_blocks.source_text_en: What s the difference between Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans?
source_blocks.text: What s the difference between Direct Subsidized Loans and Direct Unsubsidized Loans?

source_blocks.source_text_en: In short, Direct Subsidized Loans have slightly better terms to help out students with financial need.
source_blocks.text: In short, Direct Subsidized Loans have slightly better terms to help out students with financial need.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here s a quick overview of Direct Subsidized Loans:
source_blocks.text: Here s a quick overview of Direct Subsidized Loans:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct Subsidized Loans are available to undergraduate students with financial need. Your school determines the amount you can borrow, and the amount may not exceed your financial need. The U.S. Department of Education pays the interest on a Direct Subsidized Loan - while you re in school at least half-time, - for the first six months after you leave school (referred to as a grace period\), and - during a period of deferment (a postponement of loan payments).

source_blocks.source_text_en: \Note: If you received a Direct Subsidized Loan that was first disbursed between July 1, 2012, and July 1, 2014, you will be responsible for paying any interest that accrues during your grace period. If you choose not to pay the interest that accrues during your grace period, the interest will be added to your principal balance.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here s a quick overview of Direct Unsubsidized Loans:
source_blocks.text: Here s a quick overview of Direct Unsubsidized Loans:

source_blocks.source_text_en: Direct Unsubsidized Loans are available to undergraduate and graduate students; there is no requirement to demonstrate financial need. Your school determines the amount you can borrow based on your cost of attendance and other financial aid you receive. You are responsible for paying the interest on a Direct Unsubsidized Loan during all periods. If you choose not to pay the interest while you are in school and during grace periods and deferment or forbearance periods, your interest will accrue (accumulate) and be capitalized (that is, your interest will be added to the principal amount of your loan).

source_blocks.source_text_en: Am I eligible for a Direct Subsidized Loan or a Direct Unsubsidized Loan?
source_blocks.text: Am I eligible for a Direct Subsidized Loan or a Direct Unsubsidized Loan?

source_blocks.source_text_en: To receive either type of loan, you must be enrolled at least half-time at a school that participates in the Direct Loan Program. Generally, you must also be enrolled in a program that leads to a degree or certificate awarded by the school. Direct Subsidized Loans are available only to undergraduate students who have financial need. Direct Unsubsidized Loans are available to both undergraduates and graduate or professional degree students. You are not required to show financial need to receive a Direct Unsubsidized Loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: To apply for a Direct Loan, you must first complete and submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form. source_blocks.source_text_en: Is there a time limit on how long I can receive loans?
source_blocks.text: Is there a time limit on how long I can receive loans?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are a first-time borrower on or after July 1, 2013, there is a limit on the maximum period of time (measured in academic years) that you can receive Direct Subsidized Loans. This time limit does not apply to Direct Unsubsidized Loans or Direct PLUS Loans. If this limit applies to you, you may not receive Direct Subsidized Loans for more than 150 percent of the published length of your program. This is called your maximum eligibility period. Your maximum eligibility period is generally based on the published length of your current program. You can usually find the published length of any program of study in your school s catalog.
source_blocks.text: If you are a first-time borrower on or after July 1, 2013, there is a limit on the maximum period of time (measured in academic years) that you can receive Direct Subsidized Loans. This time limit does not apply to Direct Unsubsidized Loans or Direct PLUS Loans. If this limit applies to you, you may not receive Direct Subsidized Loans for more than 150 percent of the published length of your program. This is called your maximum eligibility period. Your maximum eligibility period is generally based on the published length of your current program. You can usually find the published length of any program of study in your school s catalog.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For example, if you are enrolled in a four-year bachelor s degree program, the maximum period for which you can receive Direct Subsidized Loans is six years (150 percent of 4 years = 6 years). If you are enrolled in a two-year associate degree program, the maximum period for which you can receive Direct Subsidized Loans is three years (150 percent of 2 years = 3 years).
source_blocks.text: For example, if you are enrolled in a four-year bachelor s degree program, the maximum period for which you can receive Direct Subsidized Loans is six years (150 percent of 4 years = 6 years). If you are enrolled in a two-year associate degree program, the maximum period for which you can receive Direct Subsidized Loans is three years (150 percent of 2 years = 3 years).

source_blocks.source_text_en: Because your maximum eligibility period is based on the length of your current program of study, your maximum eligibility period can change if you change to a program that has a different length. Also, if you receive Direct Subsidized Loans for one program and then change to another program, the Direct Subsidized Loans you received for the earlier program will generally count toward your new maximum eligibility period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Did you know that the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) provides tax benefits for education?
source_blocks.text: 您知道美国国税局（IRS）为教育提供税收优惠吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: The tax benefits can be used to get back some of the money you spend on tuition or loan interest or to maximize your college savings.
source_blocks.text: 这些税收优惠可用于收回您为学费或贷款利息支付的部分资金，或最大化您的大学储蓄。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Read IRS Publication 970, Tax Benefits for Education to see which federal income tax benefits might apply to your situation. Here are some highlights:
source_blocks.text: 阅读 IRS出版物970，教育税收优惠，了解哪些联邦所得税优惠可能适用于您的情况。以下是一些要点：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Tax Credits for Higher Education Expenses
source_blocks.text: 高等教育费用税收抵免

source_blocks.source_text_en: Two tax credits help offset the costs (tuition, fees, books, supplies, equipment) of college or career school by reducing the amount of your income tax:
source_blocks.text: 两项税收抵免通过减少您的所得税金额来帮助抵消大学或职业学校的费用（学费、杂费、书本费、用品费、设备费）：

source_blocks.source_text_en: The American Opportunity Credit allows you to claim up to \$2,500 per student per year for the first four years of school as the student works toward a degree or similar credential. The Lifetime Learning Credit allows you to claim up to \$2,000 per student per year for any college or career school tuition and fees, as well as for books, supplies, and equipment that were required for the course and had to be purchased from the school.
source_blocks.text: 美国机会税收抵免允许您在每个学生攻读学位或类似证书的前四年内，每年为每位学生申请最高 \$2,500 的抵免。 终身学习税收抵免允许您每年为每位学生申请最高 \$2,000 的抵免，用于任何大学或职业学校的学费和杂费，以及课程要求且必须从学校购买的书本、用品和设备。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Even if you normally wouldn t file a tax return because of your income level, be sure to do so! If you don t, you ll miss out on tax credits that would put money in your pocket.
source_blocks.text: 即使您因收入水平通常不需要报税，也请务必报税！如果您不报税，您将错失能让钱进入您口袋的税收抵免。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Coverdell Education Savings Account
source_blocks.text: Coverdell教育储蓄账户

source_blocks.source_text_en: A Coverdell Education Savings Account allows up to \$2,000 a year to be put aside for a student s education expenses (elementary, secondary, or college or career school).
source_blocks.text: Coverdell教育储蓄账户允许每年为学生的教育费用（小学、中学或大学或职业学校）预留最高 \$2,000。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Qualified Tuition Programs (QTPs; also known as 529 Plans)
source_blocks.text: 合格学费计划（QTP；也称为529计划）

source_blocks.source_text_en: A QTP/529 plan is established by a state or school so that you can either prepay or save up to pay education-related expenses. Once you re in college or career school and you withdraw money from your account to pay your education expenses, the money you withdraw will not be taxed. Learn more about state 529 plans. To find out whether the college you plan to attend participates in a QTP, ask the financial aid or admissions staff.
source_blocks.text: QTP/529计划由州或学校设立，以便您可以预付或储蓄以支付教育相关费用。一旦您进入大学或职业学校，并从您的账户中提取资金以支付教育费用，您提取的资金将不会被征税。了解更多关于州529计划的信息。要了解您计划就读的大学是否参与QTP，请咨询经济援助或招生工作人员。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Student Loan Interest Deduction
source_blocks.text: 学生贷款利息扣除

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can take a tax deduction for the interest paid on student loans that you took out for yourself, your spouse, or your dependent. This benefit applies to all loans (not just federal student loans) used to pay for higher education expenses. The maximum deduction is \$2,500 a year.
source_blocks.text: 您可以为您自己、您的配偶或您的受抚养人申请的学生贷款所支付的利息进行税收扣除。此优惠适用于所有用于支付高等教育费用的贷款（不仅仅是联邦学生贷款）。最高扣除额为每年 \$2,500。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Using IRA Withdrawals for College Costs
source_blocks.text: 使用IRA取款支付大学费用

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may withdraw from an IRA to pay higher education expenses for yourself, your spouse, your child, or your grandchild. You will owe federal income tax on the amount withdrawn, but won't be subject to the early withdrawal penalty.
source_blocks.text: 您可以从IRA中提取资金，为您自己、您的配偶、您的子女或您的孙子女支付高等教育费用。 您将需要对提取的金额缴纳联邦所得税，但不会受到提前取款罚款的影响。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Wondering whether you can get your federal student loans forgiven for your service as a teacher?
source_blocks.text: Wondering whether you can get your federal student loans forgiven for your service as a teacher?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn about the forgiveness program to see whether you qualify.
source_blocks.text: Learn about the forgiveness program to see whether you qualify.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Under the Teacher Loan Forgiveness Program, if you teach full-time for five complete and consecutive academic years in a low-income school or educational service agency, and meet other qualifications, you may be eligible for forgiveness of up to \$17,500 on your Direct Subsidized and Unsubsidized Loans and your Subsidized and Unsubsidized Federal Stafford Loans.
source_blocks.text: Under the Teacher Loan Forgiveness Program, if you teach full-time for five complete and consecutive academic years in a low-income school or educational service agency, and meet other qualifications, you may be eligible for forgiveness of up to \$17,500 on your Direct Subsidized and Unsubsidized Loans and your Subsidized and Unsubsidized Federal Stafford Loans.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have a Direct Consolidation Loan or a Federal Consolidation Loan, you may be eligible for forgiveness of the outstanding portion of the consolidation loan that repaid an eligible Direct Subsidized Loan, Direct Unsubsidized Loan, Subsidized Federal Stafford Loan, or Unsubsidized Federal Stafford Loan.
source_blocks.text: If you have a Direct Consolidation Loan or a Federal Consolidation Loan, you may be eligible for forgiveness of the outstanding portion of the consolidation loan that repaid an eligible Direct Subsidized Loan, Direct Unsubsidized Loan, Subsidized Federal Stafford Loan, or Unsubsidized Federal Stafford Loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What are the eligibility requirements?
source_blocks.text: What are the eligibility requirements?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You must not have had an outstanding balance on Direct Loans or Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program loans as of Oct. 1, 1998, or on the date that you obtained a Direct Loan or FFEL Program loan after Oct. 1, 1998. You must have been employed as a full-time, highly qualified teacher for five complete and consecutive academic years, and at least one of those years must have been after the 1997 98 academic year. You must have been employed at an elementary school, secondary school, or educational service agency that serves low-income students (a "low-income school or educational service agency"). The loan(s) for which you are seeking forgiveness must have been made before the end of your five academic years of qualifying teaching service.

The loan(s) for which you are seeking forgiveness must have been made before the end of your five academic years of qualifying teaching service.

To find out if your school or educational service agency is classified as low-income, search the directory database for the years you have been employed as a teacher. If the TCLI Directory is not available before May 1 of any year, the previous year s directory may be used for that year.

source_blocks.text: Can I receive loan forgiveness under both the Teacher Loan Forgiveness Program and the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can potentially receive forgiveness under both the Teacher Loan Forgiveness Program and the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program, but not for the same period of teaching service. For example, if you complete five consecutive years of qualifying teaching and receive forgiveness of your Direct Loans under the Teacher Loan Forgiveness Program, any payments you made on your Direct Loans during that five-year period cannot be counted toward the required 120 monthly payments for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program. source_blocks.source_text_en: The Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended (HEA), allows institutions of higher education to outsource any aspect of the institution s participation in federal student aid programs, including, but not limited to, services and functions necessary
source_blocks.text: The Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended (HEA), allows institutions of higher education to outsource any aspect of the institution s participation in federal student aid programs, including, but not limited to, services and functions necessary

source_blocks.source_text_en: for the institution to remain eligible to participate in the federal student aid programs, to determine a student s eligibility for federal student aid, to account for federal student aid funds, to deliver federal student aid to students, or to perform any other aspect of the administration of the federal student aid programs.

source_blocks.source_text_en: A third-party servicer may be an individual, a state, or a private, profit or non-profit organization that enters into a contract with an eligible institution to administer, through manual or automated processing, any aspect of the institution s participation in any federal student aid programs. When contracting with an institution, a third-party servicer and/or its contractors must comply with the various Title IV requirements applicable to its servicing agreement with the school. A third-party servicer is jointly and severally liable with the institution for any violation of Title IV requirements resulting from the functions performed by the third-party servicer.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Title IV regulations authorize the U.S. Department of Education (ED) to provide oversight of third-party servicers. As part of its oversight duties, Federal Student Aid (FSA) routinely conducts program reviews to confirm that third-party servicers and the schools that they contract with meet FSA requirements for institutional eligibility, financial responsibility, and administrative capability. During program reviews, reviewers evaluate the third-party servicers and schools compliance with FSA requirements, assess liabilities for errors in performance, and identify actions the third-party servicers and their partner schools must take to improve future administrative capabilities.

source_blocks.source_text_en: VA Documentation
source_blocks.text: VA Documentation

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re a veteran, you can qualify for a TPD discharge by providing documentation from the VA that shows you have received a VA disability determination because you (1) have a service-connected disability that is 100 percent disabling; or (2) are totally disabled based on an individual unemployability rating.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re eligible for Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income, you can qualify for a TPD discharge if you provide a copy of your SSA notice of award or Benefits Planning Query showing that your next scheduled disability review will be five to seven years or more from the date of your last SSA disability determination.

source_blocks.text: How do I apply for a TPD discharge?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You need to complete a TPD discharge application and send it, along with any required documentation of your eligibility for discharge, to Nelnet, the TPD discharge servicer. The TPD discharge application applies to all of your federal student loans and TEACH Grant service obligations. Nelnet assists us in administering the TPD discharge process and communicates with borrowers and TEACH Grant recipients on our behalf concerning TPD discharge requests.

The TPD discharge application applies to all of your federal student loans and TEACH Grant service obligations. Nelnet assists us in administering the TPD discharge process and communicates with borrowers and TEACH Grant recipients on our behalf concerning TPD discharge requests.

source_blocks.source_text_en: To learn more about applying for a TPD discharge and to obtain a TPD discharge application, visit our TPD Discharge website at disabilitydischarge.com and select "Application Process."

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can let Nelnet know that you want to apply and request a TPD discharge application by phone or email. If you do, any required payments on your federal student loans will stop for 120 days to give you time to submit your application and any required supporting documentation.

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can contact Nelnet by email at disabilityinformation@nelnet.net and by phone at 1-888-303-7818 Monday Friday from 7 a.m. 2 a.m. Eastern time (ET), and Saturday from 8 a.m. 7 p.m. ET. For additional ways to contact Nelnet, and to get more information about applying for a TPD discharge, visit our TPD discharge website.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can a representative apply on my behalf and help me throughout the TPD discharge process?
source_blocks.text: Can a representative apply on my behalf and help me throughout the TPD discharge process?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes, you can designate an individual or organization to complete and submit your TPD discharge application on your behalf, and assist you throughout the discharge process. To designate a representative, you and your representative must complete an Applicant Representative Designation form. Nelnet must receive and process this form before working with your representative. You must submit this form even if your representative already has a power of attorney to act on your behalf in other matters.

source_blocks.text: What happens after I submit a TPD discharge application?

source_blocks.source_text_en: After your application is received, Nelnet will explain the process for the review of your application. You won't be required to make any payments on your loans while your discharge application is being reviewed.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What happens if my TPD discharge request is approved?
source_blocks.text: What happens if my TPD discharge request is approved?

source_blocks.source_text_en: This depends on the type of documentation you submitted to show us that you qualified for a TPD discharge.

source_blocks.text: If we determine that you are totally and permanently disabled based on documentation from the VA, Nelnet will

source_blocks.source_text_en: notify you that your loans and/or TEACH Grant service obligation have been discharged and instruct your loan holders to return any loan payments received on or after the effective date of the VA s disability determination to the person who made the payments.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If we determine that you are totally and permanently disabled based on SSA documentation or a physician's certification, Nelnet will
source_blocks.text: If we determine that you are totally and permanently disabled based on SSA documentation or a physician's certification, Nelnet will

source_blocks.source_text_en: notify you that your loans and/or TEACH Grant service obligation have been discharged; instruct your loan holders to return any loan payments received after the date Nelnet received the SSA documentation or the date the physician certified your discharge application to the person who made the payments; and notify you that you will be subject to a three-year postdischarge monitoring period that begins on the date the discharge is approved, and that your obligation to repay your loans or complete your TEACH Grant service obligation will be reinstated if you don t meet certain requirements at any time during this monitoring period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What requirements do I have to meet during the three-year postdischarge monitoring period?
source_blocks.text: What requirements do I have to meet during the three-year postdischarge monitoring period?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your obligation to repay your loans or complete your TEACH Grant service obligation will be reinstated if, at any time during the three-year postdischarge monitoring period, you receive
source_blocks.text: Your obligation to repay your loans or complete your TEACH Grant service obligation will be reinstated if, at any time during the three-year postdischarge monitoring period, you receive

source_blocks.source_text_en: annual earnings from employment that exceed the poverty guideline amount for a family of two in your state, regardless of your actual family size; a new federal student loan under the Direct Loan Program or a new TEACH Grant; another disbursement (payment) of a Direct Loan or a TEACH Grant that was first disbursed (paid out) before your discharge was approved, and the new disbursement has not been returned to the loan holder or (for a TEACH Grant) to us within 120 days of the disbursement date; or a notice from the SSA stating that you are no longer disabled, or that your next scheduled disability review will no longer be five to seven years from the date of your last SSA disability determination.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: During the postdischarge monitoring period, Nelnet will require you to submit documentation of your annual earnings from employment on a form that Nelnet will provide. If you don't submit this form with the required documentation of your income, your obligation to repay your loans or complete your TEACH Grant service obligation will be reinstated.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The poverty guideline amounts are updated annually by the Department of Health and Human Services. Nelnet will notify you of the current poverty guideline amounts during each year of the postdischarge monitoring period.
source_blocks.text: The poverty guideline amounts are updated annually by the Department of Health and Human Services. Nelnet will notify you of the current poverty guideline amounts during each year of the postdischarge monitoring period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For detailed information regarding the three-year postdischarge monitoring period requirements, visit the TPD Discharge website at disabilitydischarge.com and select Monitoring Period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you're a veteran whose TPD discharge application is approved based on documentation from the VA, you aren't subject to a postdischarge monitoring period.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What happens if my obligation to repay my loans or satisfy my TEACH Grant service obligation is reinstated?
source_blocks.text: What happens if my obligation to repay my loans or satisfy my TEACH Grant service obligation is reinstated?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You will again be responsible for repaying your loans in accordance with the terms of the promissory note that you signed, or satisfying your TEACH Grant service obligation in accordance with the terms of the TEACH Grant Agreement to Serve that you completed.
source_blocks.text: You will again be responsible for repaying your loans in accordance with the terms of the promissory note that you signed, or satisfying your TEACH Grant service obligation in accordance with the terms of the TEACH Grant Agreement to Serve that you completed.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you applied for a discharge of loans, your loans will be returned to the status they were in before you applied for discharge. This means that if a loan was in default before you applied for a TPD discharge, it will be returned to default status.
source_blocks.text: If you applied for a discharge of loans, your loans will be returned to the status they were in before you applied for discharge. This means that if a loan was in default before you applied for a TPD discharge, it will be returned to default status.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your obligation to repay your loans or complete your TEACH Grant service obligation is reinstated, Nelnet will explain the reason for the reinstatement and provide information about what you can do if you have questions about the reinstatement or if you believe the reinstatement was based on incorrect information.
source_blocks.text: If your obligation to repay your loans or complete your TEACH Grant service obligation is reinstated, Nelnet will explain the reason for the reinstatement and provide information about what you can do if you have questions about the reinstatement or if you believe the reinstatement was based on incorrect information.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What happens if my TPD discharge request is denied?
source_blocks.text: What happens if my TPD discharge request is denied?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If we determine that you don t qualify for a TPD discharge, Nelnet will
source_blocks.text: If we determine that you don t qualify for a TPD discharge, Nelnet will

source_blocks.source_text_en: notify you of the reason for the denial of your discharge application; explain that you may ask us to reevaluate your discharge application if you provide new information that supports your eligibility for discharge within 12 months of the date you are notified that your discharge application has been denied; explain that if you don t request reevaluation of your discharge application within 12 months of the date you re notified that your discharge application has been denied, and you still want us to reevaluate your eligibility, you must submit a new TPD discharge application with new information about your disabling condition that was not provided with your prior discharge application; explain that you re again responsible for repaying your loans, and that your loan holder will notify you when your first payment is due; and explain that if you applied for a discharge of a TEACH Grant service obligation, you re again responsible for meeting the terms and conditions of the service obligation.

source_blocks.source_text_en: I received a TPD discharge but want to go back to school. Can I take out more student loans or TEACH Grants?
source_blocks.text: I received a TPD discharge but want to go back to school. Can I take out more student loans or TEACH Grants?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes, but with some conditions.
source_blocks.text: Yes, but with some conditions.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you received a TPD discharge based on VA documentation, SSA documentation, or a physician s certification, you must
source_blocks.text: If you received a TPD discharge based on VA documentation, SSA documentation, or a physician s certification, you must

source_blocks.source_text_en: give your school a letter from a physician stating that you are once again able to engage in substantial gainful activity, and sign a statement acknowledging that you can't get a TPD discharge of the new loan or TEACH Grant based on a disabling condition that already exists when you receive the new loan or TEACH Grant, unless that condition substantially deteriorates in the future.
source_blocks.text: give your school a letter from a physician stating that you are once again able to engage in substantial gainful activity, and sign a statement acknowledging that you can't get a TPD discharge of the new loan or TEACH Grant based on a disabling condition that already exists when you receive the new loan or TEACH Grant, unless that condition substantially deteriorates in the future.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you received a TPD discharge based on SSA documentation or a physician s certification and your three-year postdischarge period hasn t ended, you must also resume repayment on your previously discharged loans or acknowledge that you are once again responsible for meeting the terms and conditions of your TEACH Grant service obligation.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If my loan is discharged due to TPD, do I have to pay taxes on the discharged loan amount?
source_blocks.text: If my loan is discharged due to TPD, do I have to pay taxes on the discharged loan amount?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Because of a change in federal law related to the taxability of loan amounts discharged due to TPD, the answer depends on when you received the discharge.
source_blocks.text: Because of a change in federal law related to the taxability of loan amounts discharged due to TPD, the answer depends on when you received the discharge.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you received a TPD discharge of a loan before Jan. 1, 2018, the loan amount discharged may be considered income for federal tax purposes under Internal Revenue Service (IRS) rules. If you received a TPD discharge of a loan during the period from Jan. 1, 2018 to Dec. 31, 2025, the discharged loan amount won t be considered income for federal tax purposes.
source_blocks.text: If you received a TPD discharge of a loan before Jan. 1, 2018, the loan amount discharged may be considered income for federal tax purposes under Internal Revenue Service (IRS) rules. If you received a TPD discharge of a loan during the period from Jan. 1, 2018 to Dec. 31, 2025, the discharged loan amount won t be considered income for federal tax purposes.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For purposes of determining whether a loan amount discharged due to TPD may be treated as taxable income for federal tax purposes, the date you are considered to have received the discharge is different depending on how you qualified for the discharge.
source_blocks.text: For purposes of determining whether a loan amount discharged due to TPD may be treated as taxable income for federal tax purposes, the date you are considered to have received the discharge is different depending on how you qualified for the discharge.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re a veteran who showed that you re totally and permanently disabled based on a disability determination by the VA, you re considered to have received the discharge for federal tax purposes on the date we approve the discharge.
source_blocks.text: If you re a veteran who showed that you re totally and permanently disabled based on a disability determination by the VA, you re considered to have received the discharge for federal tax purposes on the date we approve the discharge.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you showed that you re totally and permanently disabled based on documentation from the SSA or a physician s certification (meaning that you re subject to a three-year postdischarge monitoring period), you re considered to have received the discharge for federal tax purposes at the end of the postdischarge monitoring period. For example, if your discharge was approved in July 2017, you would not be considered to have received the discharge for federal tax purposes until July 2020, at the end of the three-year postdischarge monitoring period. Therefore, the IRS would not consider the discharged loan amount to be taxable income for federal tax purposes.
source_blocks.text: If you showed that you re totally and permanently disabled based on documentation from the SSA or a physician s certification (meaning that you re subject to a three-year postdischarge monitoring period), you re considered to have received the discharge for federal tax purposes at the end of the postdischarge monitoring period. For example, if your discharge was approved in July 2017, you would not be considered to have received the discharge for federal tax purposes until July 2020, at the end of the three-year postdischarge monitoring period. Therefore, the IRS would not consider the discharged loan amount to be taxable income for federal tax purposes.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you receive a Form 1099-C, you should keep the form for your records, but you do not need to include it when filing your federal tax return. For additional information, visit irs.gov.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Loan amounts discharged due to TPD may still be considered income for state tax purposes. If you receive a TPD discharge of a federal student loan, you may want to consult with your state tax office or a tax professional before you file your state tax return.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Understanding College Costs | Federal Student Aid
source_blocks.text: 了解大学费用 | 联邦学生援助

source_blocks.source_text_en: College and career school costs can vary significantly from school to school.
source_blocks.text: 大学和职业学校的费用可能因学校而异，差异很大。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn about college costs and get tips on how to lower costs when you go to school.
source_blocks.text: 了解大学费用，并获取如何在上学期间降低费用的建议。

source_blocks.source_text_en: The cost of college can include a variety of items including some you might not expect. By understanding college costs, you can compare schools and explore options for how to lower your costs.
source_blocks.text: 大学费用可能包括各种项目，其中一些可能出乎你的意料。通过了解大学费用，你可以比较学校，并探索如何降低费用的选项。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is included in the cost of college?
source_blocks.text: 大学费用包括哪些内容？

source_blocks.source_text_en: College costs include more than tuition and room and board. Here are common costs:
source_blocks.text: 大学费用不仅包括学费和食宿费。以下是常见的费用：

source_blocks.source_text_en: Make sure colleges and career schools give you a clear statement of their tuition and fees.
source_blocks.text: 确保大学和职业学校向你提供其学费和杂费的清晰说明。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How can I lower the cost of college?
source_blocks.text: 我如何降低大学费用？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here are some suggestions on how you might be able to lower the cost of college. For many of these suggestions, you ll want to follow up with the colleges or career schools you are interested in to get additional details.
source_blocks.text: 以下是一些关于如何降低大学费用的建议。对于许多建议，你可能需要向你感兴趣的大学或职业学校咨询以获取更多详细信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Set a budget and stick to it! Having a budget will help you compare anticipated college or career school expenses against your potential available income and financial aid. You also can use a budget to compare costs between different schools. Learn about budgeting.
source_blocks.text: 制定预算并坚持执行！制定预算将帮助你比较预期的大学或职业学校开支与潜在的可支配收入和财政援助。你也可以使用预算来比较不同学校之间的费用。了解如何制定预算。

source_blocks.source_text_en: College or career school costs can vary significantly and there are many schools with affordable tuition and generous financial assistance. Make sure to research all schools that may meet your academic and financial needs. To find colleges or career schools, use our college search tool, College Navigator.
source_blocks.text: 大学或职业学校的费用可能差异很大，而且有许多学校提供负担得起的学费和慷慨的财政援助。确保研究所有可能满足你学术和经济需求的学校。要查找大学或职业学校，请使用我们的大学搜索工具 College Navigator。

source_blocks.source_text_en: You may be able to get school credit based on your knowledge or life experiences, and you can manage your course work to reduce costs. - Ask your school whether it s possible to test out of any classes. If you don t take a class, you may not have to pay for the credits. - Some colleges give credit for life experiences, thereby reducing the number of credits needed for graduation. - Most schools charge a set price for a specific number of credits taken in a semester. If academically possible, take the maximum number of credits allowed. This strategy reduces the amount of time needed to graduate. - Some schools offer combined degree programs or three-year programs that allow you to take all of the courses needed for graduation in three years, instead of four, thereby eliminating one year's educational expenses.
source_blocks.text: 你可能能够根据你的知识或生活经历获得学校学分，并且你可以管理你的课程作业以降低成本。 - 询问你的学校是否有可能免修某些课程。如果你不修课程，你可能不必支付这些学分。 - 一些大学会为生活经历提供学分，从而减少毕业所需的学分数。 - 大多数学校对一学期内修读的特定学分数收取固定费用。如果学业上可行，请修读允许的最大学分数。这一策略减少了毕业所需的时间。 - 一些学校提供联合学位课程或三年制课程，允许你在三年内修完毕业所需的所有课程，而不是四年，从而省去一年的教育费用。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Colleges and career schools may offer discounts on tuition if - you are a child of an alumnus or alumna (i.e., if your parent went to the school); - more than one family member is enrolled at the school; - you are a student government leader or the editor of the college newspaper or yearbook; - you are an older student; - your family s main wage earner is unemployed; or - you or a member of your family works at the school.
source_blocks.text: 大学和职业学校可能会提供学费折扣，如果 - 你是校友的子女（即，如果你的父母曾就读于该校）； - 多个家庭成员在同一所学校就读； - 你是学生会领袖或大学报纸或年鉴的编辑； - 你是年龄较大的学生； - 你家庭的主要收入来源者失业；或 - 你或你的家庭成员在该校工作。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Housing costs can add up. Here are some tips for reducing your housing costs: - If you go to a college or career school near home, consider living with your parents or other family.
source_blocks.text: 住房费用可能会增加。以下是一些降低住房费用的建议： - 如果你就读的大学或职业学校离家近，考虑与父母或其他家人同住。

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you live off-campus, consider sharing a house or apartment with multiple housemates to cut down the cost of rent, and carpool to save on gas and parking. - Most colleges and universities sponsor resident advisor programs that offer reduced tuition or reduced room and board costs if you work in a residence hall. You may be eligible for health care benefits including the following: - Most young adults can stay on their parents family plan until they turn 26, even if they are married or still living with their parents. - If you have been uninsured because of a pre-existing condition, you may be eligible to join the Pre-Existing Condition Insurance Plan. - If you are in a new insurance plan, insurance companies cannot charge you a deductible or copays for recommended or preventive services such as flu shots or other immunizations. You can work part-time to pay part of your costs. Be sure your work and school schedules don t conflict and that you have enough time for studying. Here are a couple of options: - The Federal Work-Study Program provides an opportunity to earn money while going to school. Ask schools if they participate in the program. - Cooperative education programs allow students to alternate between working full-time and studying full-time. - Most schools have placement offices that help students find employment and personnel offices that hire students to work on campus. Taking small steps can add up. For example, you can lower the cost of textbooks if you buy used books or rent textbooks (if you won t need the books once you finish the class).
source_blocks.text: 如果你住在校外，考虑与多位室友合租房屋或公寓以降低租金成本，并拼车以节省油费和停车费。 - 大多数学院和大学提供宿舍助理项目，如果你在宿舍楼工作，可以获得学费减免或食宿费用减免。 你可能符合享受医疗保健福利的资格，包括以下内容： - 大多数年轻人可以留在父母的家庭计划中直到年满26岁，即使他们已经结婚或仍与父母同住。 - 如果你因已有病症而一直没有保险，你可能符合加入已有病症保险计划的资格。 - 如果你加入新的保险计划，保险公司不能就推荐或预防性服务（如流感疫苗或其他免疫接种）向你收取免赔额或共付额。 你可以兼职工作以支付部分费用。确保你的工作和学校时间表不冲突，并且你有足够的时间学习。以下是一些选择： - 联邦勤工俭学计划提供了上学期间赚钱的机会。询问学校是否参与该计划。 - 合作教育项目允许学生交替进行全职工作和全日制学习。 - 大多数学校设有就业办公室，帮助学生找工作，以及人事办公室，雇用学生在校园内工作。 积少成多。例如，如果你购买二手书或租用教科书（如果你完成课程后不再需要这些书），你可以降低教科书成本。

source_blocks.source_text_en: A credit card can help you build a credit history, if you use it wisely. But use it for emergencies only and don t spend more than you can afford to pay. If you decide to get a credit card, make sure you understand the terms.
source_blocks.text: 如果你明智地使用信用卡，它可以帮助你建立信用记录。但只应在紧急情况下使用，并且不要花费超过你负担得起的金额。如果你决定办理信用卡，请确保你了解相关条款。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How can I compare the costs of colleges?
source_blocks.text: 如何比较大学的费用？

source_blocks.source_text_en: You can find information about whether the cost of a college is low, medium, or high by using the College Scorecard. Keep in mind that a higher-priced school might have more financial aid available to help you pay for your education, so take a look at the school s net price if you want an idea of how much it might cost you after financial aid is taken into account.
source_blocks.text: 你可以通过使用大学记分卡来查找大学费用是低、中还是高的信息。请记住，价格较高的学校可能有更多的经济援助来帮助你支付教育费用，因此如果你想了解在考虑经济援助后可能需要支付多少费用，可以查看学校的净价格。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Automatic Administrative Forbearance and Temporary 0% Interest as a Result of the COVID-19 National Emergency
source_blocks.text: Automatic Administrative Forbearance and Temporary 0% Interest as a Result of the COVID-19 National Emergency

source_blocks.source_text_en: To provide relief to student loan borrowers during the COVID-19 national emergency, federal student loan borrowers are automatically being placed in an administrative forbearance, which allows you to temporarily stop making your monthly loan payments. In addition, interest is being temporarily set at 0% on federal student loans. This 0% interest and suspension of payments will last from March 13, 2020, through Sept. 30, 2020, but you can still make payments if you choose.

source_blocks.source_text_en: The first day after you miss a student loan payment, your loan becomes past due, or delinquent. Your loan account remains delinquent until you repay the past due amount or make other arrangements, such as deferment or forbearance, or changing repayment plans.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are delinquent on your student loan payment for 90 days or more, your loan servicer will report the delinquency to the three major national credit bureaus. source_blocks.source_text_en: Understanding Default
source_blocks.text: Understanding Default

source_blocks.source_text_en: If your loan continues to be delinquent, the loan may go into default. The point when a loan is considered to be in default varies depending on the type of loan you received.
source_blocks.text: If your loan continues to be delinquent, the loan may go into default. The point when a loan is considered to be in default varies depending on the type of loan you received.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For a loan made under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan Program or the Federal Family Education Loan Program, you re considered to be in default if you don t make your scheduled student loan payments for at least 270 days.
source_blocks.text: For a loan made under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan Program or the Federal Family Education Loan Program, you re considered to be in default if you don t make your scheduled student loan payments for at least 270 days.

source_blocks.source_text_en: For a loan made under the Federal Perkins Loan Program, the holder of the loan may declare the loan to be in default if you don t make your scheduled payment by the due date. Find out where to go for information about your Perkins Loan.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you defaulted on any of your federal student loans, contact the organization that notified you of the default as soon as possible so you can explain your situation fully and discuss your options. If you make repayment arrangements soon enough after your loan has gone into default, you may be able to resolve the default quickly. Learn more about getting out of default.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Consequences of Default
source_blocks.text: Consequences of Default

source_blocks.source_text_en: The consequences of defaulting can not only impact your ability to borrow but can impact your finances as well. Consequences include the following:
source_blocks.text: The consequences of defaulting can not only impact your ability to borrow but can impact your finances as well. Consequences include the following:

source_blocks.source_text_en: The entire unpaid balance of your loan and any interest you owe becomes immediately due (this is called "acceleration"). You can no longer receive deferment or forbearance, and you lose eligibility for other benefits, such as the ability to choose a repayment plan. You lose eligibility for additional federal student aid. The default is reported to credit bureaus, damaging your credit rating and affecting your ability to buy a car or house or to get a credit card. It may take years to reestablish a good credit record. You may not be able to purchase or sell assets such as real estate. Your tax refunds and federal benefit payments may be withheld and applied toward repayment of your defaulted loan (this is called Treasury offset ). Your wages may be garnished. This means your employer may be required to withhold a portion of your pay and send it to your loan holder to repay your defaulted loan. Your loan holder can take you to court. You may be charged court costs, collection fees, attorney s fees, and other costs associated with the collection process. Your school may withhold your academic transcript until your defaulted student loan is satisfied. The academic transcript is the property of the school, and it is the school's decision not the U.S. Department of Education s or your loan holder s whether to release the transcript to you.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do I apply for unpaid refund discharge?

source_blocks.source_text_en: If the school that you attended is still open, you should contact that school and attempt to resolve the issue with the school before applying for an unpaid refund discharge. source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal Work-Study jobs help students earn money to pay for college or career school.
source_blocks.text: Federal Work-Study jobs help students earn money to pay for college or career school.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Undergraduate and graduate students with work-study jobs will work part-time on or off campus while enrolled.
source_blocks.text: Undergraduate and graduate students with work-study jobs will work part-time on or off campus while enrolled.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Federal Work-Study provides part-time jobs for undergraduate and graduate students with financial need, allowing them to earn money to help pay education expenses. The program encourages community service work and work related to the student s course of study.
source_blocks.text: Federal Work-Study provides part-time jobs for undergraduate and graduate students with financial need, allowing them to earn money to help pay education expenses. The program encourages community service work and work related to the student s course of study.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Here s a quick overview of Federal Work-Study:
source_blocks.text: Here s a quick overview of Federal Work-Study:

source_blocks.source_text_en: It provides part-time employment while you are enrolled in school. It s available to undergraduate, graduate, and professional students with financial need. It s available to full-time or part-time students. It s administered by schools participating in the Federal Work-Study Program. Check with your school's financial aid office to find out if your school participates.
source_blocks.text: It provides part-time employment while you are enrolled in school. It s available to undergraduate, graduate, and professional students with financial need. It s available to full-time or part-time students. It s administered by schools participating in the Federal Work-Study Program. Check with your school's financial aid office to find out if your school participates.

source_blocks.source_text_en: What kinds of jobs are there?
source_blocks.text: What kinds of jobs are there?

source_blocks.source_text_en: The Federal Work-Study Program emphasizes employment in civic education and work related to your course of study whenever possible.
source_blocks.text: The Federal Work-Study Program emphasizes employment in civic education and work related to your course of study whenever possible.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Are jobs on campus or off campus?
source_blocks.text: Are jobs on campus or off campus?

source_blocks.source_text_en: Both. If you work on campus, you ll usually work for your school. If you work off campus, your employer will usually be a private nonprofit organization or a public agency, and the work performed must be in the public interest.
source_blocks.text: Both. If you work on campus, you ll usually work for your school. If you work off campus, your employer will usually be a private nonprofit organization or a public agency, and the work performed must be in the public interest.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Some schools might have agreements with private for-profit employers for work-study jobs. These jobs must be relevant to your course of study (to the maximum extent possible). If you attend a proprietary school (i.e., a for-profit institution), there may be further restrictions on the types of jobs you can be assigned.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you re interested in getting a Federal Work-Study job while you re enrolled in college or career school, make sure you apply for aid early. Funds are limited.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How much can I earn?
source_blocks.text: How much can I earn?

source_blocks.source_text_en: You ll earn at least the current federal minimum wage. However, you may earn more depending on the type of work you do and the skills required for the position.
source_blocks.text: You ll earn at least the current federal minimum wage. However, you may earn more depending on the type of work you do and the skills required for the position.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Your total work-study award depends on
source_blocks.text: Your total work-study award depends on

source_blocks.source_text_en: when you apply, your level of financial need, and your school s funding level.

source_blocks.source_text_en: How will I be paid?
source_blocks.text: How will I be paid?

source_blocks.source_text_en: How you re paid depends partly on whether you re an undergraduate or graduate student.
source_blocks.text: How you re paid depends partly on whether you re an undergraduate or graduate student.

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you are an undergraduate student, you're paid by the hour. If you are a graduate or professional student, you're paid by the hour or by salary, depending on the work you do. Your school must pay you at least once a month. Your school must pay you directly unless you request that the school - send your payments directly to your bank account or - use the money to pay for your education-related institutional charges such as tuition, fees, and room and board.

source_blocks.source_text_en: Can I work as many hours as I want?
source_blocks.text: Can I work as many hours as I want?

source_blocks.source_text_en: No. The amount you earn can t exceed your total Federal Work-Study award. When assigning work hours, your employer or your school s financial aid office will consider your class schedule and your academic progress.

source_blocks.source_text_en: About VA disability ratings
source_blocks.text: 关于VA伤残等级

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn about VA disability ratings and how we assign your rating. If you have more than one service-connected condition, use our disability rating calculator or the ratings table to find your VA combined disability rating.
source_blocks.text: 了解VA伤残等级以及我们如何为您评定等级。如果您有多个与服务相关的疾病，请使用我们的伤残等级计算器或等级表来查找您的VA综合伤残等级。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Loading the disability rating calculator Sorry, this is taking longer than expected.
source_blocks.text: 正在加载伤残等级计算器 抱歉，这比预期花费的时间更长。

source_blocks.source_text_en: We re sorry. Something went wrong when we tried to load the disability rating calculator.Please try refreshing your browser in a few minutes.
source_blocks.text: 我们很抱歉。加载伤残等级计算器时出现了问题。请几分钟后尝试刷新浏览器。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How we assign VA disability ratings
source_blocks.text: 我们如何评定VA伤残等级

source_blocks.source_text_en: What is a disability rating?
source_blocks.text: 什么是伤残等级？

source_blocks.source_text_en: We assign you a disability rating based on the severity of your disability. We express this rating as a percentage, representing how much your disability decreases your overall health and ability to function.
source_blocks.text: 我们根据您伤残的严重程度为您评定伤残等级。我们将此等级表示为百分比，代表您的伤残在多大程度上降低了您的整体健康和功能能力。

source_blocks.source_text_en: We then use your disability rating to determine your disability compensation rate, so we can calculate how much money you ll receive from us each month. We also use your disability rating to help determine your eligibility for other benefits, like VA health care.
source_blocks.text: 然后，我们使用您的伤残等级来确定您的伤残补偿率，以便计算您每月将从我们这里获得的金额。我们还使用您的伤残等级来帮助确定您是否有资格获得其他福利，如VA医疗保健。

source_blocks.source_text_en: What does VA use to decide my disability rating?
source_blocks.text: VA用什么来决定我的伤残等级？

source_blocks.source_text_en: We base your rating on:
source_blocks.text: 我们根据以下内容评定您的等级：

source_blocks.source_text_en: The evidence you give us (like a doctor s report or medical test results), and The results of your VA claim exam (also called a compensation and pension, or C&P, exam), if we determine you need this exam, and Other information we may get from other sources (like federal agencies)
source_blocks.text: 您提供给我们的证据（如医生报告或医学检测结果），以及 您的VA索赔检查（也称为补偿和养老金，或C&P检查）的结果（如果我们确定您需要此检查），以及 我们可能从其他来源（如联邦机构）获得的其他信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: What if I have more than one disability?
source_blocks.text: 如果我有多个伤残怎么办？

source_blocks.source_text_en: We use a method called the whole person theory to determine what we call your combined disability rating. We do this to make sure that your total VA disability rating doesn t add up to more than 100%. That s because a person can t be more than 100% able-bodied.
source_blocks.text: 我们使用一种称为整体人理论的方法来确定我们所说的您的综合伤残等级。我们这样做是为了确保您的总VA伤残等级不会加起来超过100%。那是因为一个人不可能超过100%的健康。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Read below to find out more about how we calculate your combined disability rating.
source_blocks.text: 请阅读下文，了解更多关于我们如何计算您的综合伤残等级的信息。

source_blocks.source_text_en: How do ratings work for a disability I had before entering the service that got worse because of my service?
source_blocks.text: 对于我在服役前就有的伤残，但因服役而加重，等级如何计算？

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you get disability benefits for a preservice disability, we base your monthly compensation amount on the level of aggravation. Level of aggravation means how much worse your preservice disability got because of your military service.
source_blocks.text: 如果您因服役前伤残而获得伤残福利，我们根据加重程度确定您的每月补偿金额。加重程度意味着您的服役前伤残因您的军事服务而恶化的程度。

source_blocks.source_text_en: For example: If you had an illness or injury (also known as a condition) that was rated as 10% disabling when you entered the military, and it became 20% disabling due to the effects of your service, then the level of aggravation would be 10%.
source_blocks.text: 例如：如果您在入伍时有一种疾病或伤害（也称为一种状况）被评定为10%致残，并且由于您的服务影响而变为20%致残，那么加重程度将是10%。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Is there anything else, other than my disability rating, that may affect the amount of compensation I receive?
source_blocks.text: 除了我的伤残等级外，还有其他因素可能影响我获得的赔偿金额吗？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Yes. We may increase or decrease your compensation amount in certain situations.
source_blocks.text: 是的。在某些情况下，我们可能会增加或减少您的赔偿金额。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Learn more about compensation rates
source_blocks.text: 了解更多关于赔偿率的信息

source_blocks.source_text_en: What happens after I get my disability rating?
source_blocks.text: 在我获得伤残等级后会发生什么？

source_blocks.source_text_en: Find out what to expect after you get your rating
source_blocks.text: 了解获得评级后会发生什么

source_blocks.source_text_en: How we determine combined VA disability ratings
source_blocks.text: 我们如何确定合并的VA伤残等级

source_blocks.source_text_en: If you have more than one disability, we use the combined ratings table below to calculate your combined disability rating.
source_blocks.text: 如果您有多个伤残，我们使用下面的合并等级表来计算您的合并伤残等级。

source_blocks.source_text_en: To make this table easier to use online, we ve separated it into smaller tables, based on the percentage of the most severe, or highest rated, disability. You can also download the full combined ratings table (PDF).
source_blocks.text: 为了使此表在线上更易于使用，我们根据最严重或最高等级的伤残百分比将其分成较小的表格。您也可以下载完整的合并等级表（PDF）。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Note: If you have 2 disabilities, each rated at 10% disabling, your combined disability rating is 19%.
source_blocks.text: 注意：如果您有2项伤残，每项评级为10%致残，您的合并伤残等级为19%。

source_blocks.source_text_en: Combined ratings table (not rounded)
source_blocks.text: 合并等级表（未四舍五入）
